# Build a Tape integration with OAuth

> Connect each of your product's users to their Tape account from your backend, with a "Sign in with Tape" button or a sync, and keep the connection healthy.

Connect each of your product's users to their own Tape account from your backend.

This guide is for integrations and partners registered by Tape. It covers a product with a *backend*, such as a "Sign in with Tape" button, a sync, or any integration that keeps working while the user is away. It builds on [the authorization flow](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow).

Do you call the API directly from your own code, including on a user's behalf? You don't need any of this. Use a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens).

## Step 1: Request a client

Ask Tape for a [confidential client](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/clients#a-client-registered-by-tape) with exact `https` redirect URIs.

Mention whether your app keeps *one* connection per Tape user. With that setting, a new sign-in replaces that Tape user's previous connection, even when it comes from a different account in your product. Two of your accounts linked to the same Tape user can't both stay connected.

A confidential client registered by Tape has no yearly reconnect. Its connections last as long as you refresh them at least once every 90 days.

## Step 2: Start the sign-in

Start every sign-in from an endpoint on your backend:

1.  Create a fresh `state` and PKCE `code_verifier`. Use PKCE even though your client has a secret.
2.  Store both in a short-lived, `HttpOnly`, `Secure` cookie, set on the user's browser by this endpoint.
3.  Redirect the browser to the [authorization endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow#2-send-the-user-to-tape), and request every scope your integration needs.

Tape shows the consent screen on every sign-in, including when the user already approved your app.

> Bind the sign-in to the browser, not to `state`
> 
> On the callback, read `state` and the verifier from the cookie, and compare. Never look up a pending sign-in by the `state` value alone. Otherwise an attacker can have their own sign-in completed in a victim's browser, which links the *victim's* Tape account to the attacker's account in your product.

## Step 3: Handle the callback

1.  Check `state` against the cookie, and `iss` against `https://api.tapeapp.com`.
2.  Exchange the code *once*. [Never retry a code exchange](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow#5-exchange-the-code-for-tokens): a code presented twice disconnects the connection it created.
3.  **Key the account on `tape_user_id`** from the token response, and store `tape_organization_id` beside it. A person who belongs to two Tape organizations is two Tape users, with two IDs.
4.  Read `scope` from the token response to learn what the user granted.
5.  **Overwrite the stored token pair on every sign-in.** If your client keeps one connection per user, the new sign-in replaced the old connection, and the old tokens stop working.

Need the user's name, email, or organization name? Call [`GET /v1/user`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-the-current-user) with the new access token.

## Step 4: Keep the connection alive

-   **Refresh when the access token expires,** or when the API answers `401`. A confidential client keeps the refresh token from the code exchange for the whole connection. Refresh responses contain no new refresh token, so don't overwrite the stored one with an empty value.
-   **Refresh at least once every 90 days,** or the connection expires.
-   **On `invalid_grant`, re-read before giving up.** Another sign-in may have replaced the stored tokens while your refresh was in flight. Re-read the stored pair, and retry once if it changed. Only when Tape refuses the current pair, mark the account as disconnected and ask the user to sign in again.

## Step 5: Let the user disconnect

When the user disconnects Tape in your product, [revoke the refresh token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow#disconnecting). That ends the connection in Tape as well, instead of leaving it to expire.

Users can also disconnect your app in Tape, under **Preferences** → **Connections**. Your next refresh then fails with `invalid_grant`.

## Libraries

Tape is an OAuth 2.1 authorization server, not an OpenID Connect provider. It publishes an [OAuth metadata document](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview#endpoints) but no OpenID configuration, and issues no ID token. Configure libraries for plain OAuth.

### Auth.js (`NextAuth`)

```js
{
  id: 'tape',
  name: 'Tape',
  type: 'oauth',
  issuer: 'https://api.tapeapp.com',
  clientId: process.env.TAPE_CLIENT_ID,
  clientSecret: process.env.TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET,
  authorization: {
    url: 'https://api.tapeapp.com/oauth/authorize',
    params: { scope: 'apps:read records:read records:edit' },
  },
  token: 'https://api.tapeapp.com/oauth/token',
  userinfo: 'https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/user',
  checks: ['pkce', 'state'],
  profile(profile) {
    return { id: String(profile.user_id), name: profile.name, email: profile.email };
  },
}
```

-   **Set `issuer`.** Tape sends `iss` on the callback. Without a configured issuer, the check fails.
-   **Store the tokens on every sign-in.** Auth.js doesn't update a stored account when the same user signs in again. Write the new token pair in the `events.signIn` callback.
-   **NextAuth v4 with the Prisma adapter** writes every field of the token response to the account. Add `tape_user_id Int?` and `tape_organization_id Int?` to the `Account` model, or the first sign-in fails.
-   **Auth.js v5** stores only the standard token fields. To keep the Tape IDs, add the same two columns and return them from the provider's `account(tokens)` callback. Return the standard fields there too (`access_token`, `refresh_token`, `expires_at`, `scope`, `token_type`), because that callback replaces the default one.
-   **For a public client**, set `client: { token_endpoint_auth_method: 'none' }`.

### `openid-client`

Discover the server as OAuth, not as OpenID Connect:

```js
import * as client from 'openid-client';

const config = await client.discovery(
  new URL('https://api.tapeapp.com'),
  process.env.TAPE_CLIENT_ID,
  process.env.TAPE_CLIENT_SECRET,
  undefined,
  { algorithm: 'oauth2' },
);
```

### `requests-oauthlib` (Python)

```python
import base64, hashlib, os, secrets
from requests_oauthlib import OAuth2Session

os.environ['OAUTHLIB_RELAX_TOKEN_SCOPE'] = '1'

def tape_session(state=None):
    return OAuth2Session(
        client_id,
        redirect_uri='https://app.example.com/oauth/callback',
        scope=['apps:read', 'records:read', 'records:edit'],
        state=state,
    )

# Start the sign-in
verifier = secrets.token_urlsafe(64)
challenge = base64.urlsafe_b64encode(hashlib.sha256(verifier.encode()).digest()).rstrip(b'=').decode()
url, state = tape_session().authorization_url(
    'https://api.tapeapp.com/oauth/authorize',
    code_challenge=challenge,
    code_challenge_method='S256',
)
# Store state and verifier in the cookie, then redirect the browser to url.

# On the callback, after checking state and iss:
token = tape_session(state=state_from_cookie).fetch_token(
    'https://api.tapeapp.com/oauth/token',
    authorization_response=callback_url,
    code_verifier=verifier_from_cookie,
    client_secret=client_secret,
)
```

-   **Set `OAUTHLIB_RELAX_TOKEN_SCOPE`.** requests-oauthlib raises an error when the granted scopes differ from the requested ones, for example when Tape ignores a requested `offline_access`. It checks again on every refresh.
-   **Create the PKCE verifier yourself.** The session's `pkce=` option keeps the verifier only on the session object that built the authorization URL. A callback handled in a separate request can't use it.
-   **Authenticate on refresh.** `refresh_token()` sends no client credentials by default. Pass `auth=(client_id, client_secret)` for a confidential client, or `client_id=client_id` for a public one. You can also set them once in `auto_refresh_kwargs`.
-   **For a public client**, pass `include_client_id=True` to `fetch_token`.

### `Spring Security`

When a refresh fails with `invalid_grant`, the default failure handler of Spring Security removes the stored authorized client. That may be the newer one another sign-in stored a moment ago. Call `OAuth2AuthorizedClientManager.authorize()` without a pre-loaded authorized client, so it reads the current tokens before giving up.

# Pagination

> Use a cursor to page through endpoints that return long collections.

Use a `cursor` to page through endpoints that return long collections.

Many collection endpoints are *cursor-paginated*. Each response carries a `cursor`. Pass it back to fetch the next page. Some collection endpoints don't paginate. See [Non-paginated collections](#non-paginated-collections).

## Requests

Cursor-paginated endpoints accept these parameters:

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | `string` (optional) | A `cursor` from a previous response, used to request the next page. Treat it as opaque. Omit it (default) to start from the beginning. |
| `limit` | `integer` (optional) | The maximum number of items to return in the page. The response may contain fewer. Defaults and maximums vary per endpoint. |

> What are the default and maximum for `limit`?
> 
> `50` / `500` is the common case, for example for the record listing and filter endpoints and the automation run endpoints. It isn't universal: record comments cap at `100`, and related records default to `1000`. Each endpoint page states its own default and maximum.

> Where do the parameters go?
> 
> For `GET` endpoints, pass `cursor` and `limit` in the *query string*. For `POST` endpoints, pass them in the request *body*.
> 
> The exception: the record [filter](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-filtered-records-for-an-app) endpoint uses `POST` but reads `cursor` and `limit` from the *query string*. The [related records](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-related-records-for-a-set-of-records) endpoint reads only `limit` there and has no pagination. When in doubt, follow the example on the endpoint's own page.

## Responses

A cursor-paginated response contains these properties:

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `total` | `integer` | The number of items that match the request across all pages. Tape measures it when you request the first page. Treat it as an approximate snapshot, not a live count. |
| `cursor` | `string` | An opaque cursor that points at the last item on this page. Pass it back as the `cursor` parameter to fetch the next page. Some endpoints return `null` at the end. |
| *`collection`* | `array` | The page of results. The property is named for the resource, such as `records`, `comments` or `automation_runs`. It's *not* a generic `results`. |

A response looks like this (here the collection is `records`):

```json
{
  "total": 128,
  "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...",
  "records": [
    { "record_id": 2 },
    { "record_id": 3 }
  ]
}
```

For example, request the next page of [records of a database app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-records-for-an-app) with `GET /v1/record/app/1?limit=50&cursor=eyJhbGci...`.

## Walk the whole collection

Repeat the request with the `cursor` from the previous response until a page has *fewer items than `limit`*, or `cursor` is `null`. Without `limit`, compare with the endpoint's default.

> Paging search or shared records?
> 
> Several endpoints return a cursor even on the last page, so a short page marks the end. [Search](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/search#pagination) and [shared records](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-shared-records) are the exception: page them until `cursor` is `null`. A full page can be the last one, and a search page can be short and still not be the last.

## Non-paginated collections

Some endpoints return their *entire* collection in one response and accept no `cursor` or `limit`. They typically return `{ "total": <n>, "<collection>": [ ... ] }`, and sometimes only the array. Their resource pages document this.

Don't assume a collection endpoint is pageable unless its page documents `cursor` and `limit`.

# Personal access tokens

> Named API credentials that you limit to specific capabilities, workspaces, and apps, and revoke one by one.

A personal access token (PAT) is a named credential for one integration that can only do what you allow it to.

Unlike the [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key), which can do everything your account can do, a token carries two grants:

-   **Capabilities:** what the token may do, for example read records. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   **Content access:** which workspaces and apps the token may reach.

Tokens start with the prefix `tape_pat_`.

Use a personal access token when you call the API directly, for yourself or to act in Tape on a user's behalf. [OAuth](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview) is mainly for MCP clients and for integrations registered by Tape. See [Which credential to use](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#which-credential-to-use).

> Can a token reach more than you can?
> 
> A token's access is your own permissions, narrowed by its capabilities and again by its content access. Granting a capability never reaches beyond what you can reach yourself. When you lose access to a workspace, every token you own loses it too.

## Create a token

1.  Select your profile picture, then select **Preferences**.
2.  In the settings window, select **Developer** (under **Features**).
3.  Under **Personal access tokens (PATs)**, select **New token**.

![Developer page in the settings window with the New token button](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/developer-new-token-988178e3a3fafc65b0b0cc06f1a768e8.png)

4.  Enter a **Token name**, for example "Monthly sales report".
5.  Under **Content access**, keep **All** or select only the workspaces and apps the integration needs.
6.  Under **Capabilities**, keep **All** or select only what the integration needs, for example **Read records**.
7.  Select **Create token** and copy the token.

![New personal access token dialog with one workspace and the capability Read records](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/new-token-dialog-ef7422cf400c95911d7ed57c025bdf45.png)

> Tape shows the token only once
> 
> Copy the token right away and store it in a safe place, such as your integration's secret store. Tape keeps only a hash, so it can't show the value again. If you lose it, revoke the token and create a new one.

The token list then shows only the first and last few characters of each token.

> Need different capabilities or content access?
> 
> You can rename a token later. To change its capabilities or content access, create a new token and revoke the old one.

## Use a token

Send the token as a bearer token, the same way as a user API key:

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer tape_pat_0a1b2c3d..."
```

A personal access token works for the Developer API (`/v1/*`) only. It can't create or manage personal access tokens; you do that in Tape while signed in.

## Content access

When you create a token, you choose its reach:

| Content access | What the token can reach |
| --- | --- |
| **All** | Every workspace and app you can reach, including ones created later. |
| **Only some** | Clear **All** and select the workspaces and apps the token may reach. |

A selected *workspace* includes every app in it, also apps added later. A selected app does *not* include its workspace. See [Limits](#limits) for how many you can select.

### General behavior

-   A request for a resource outside the token's content access returns `404`, as if the resource didn't exist.
-   List endpoints return `200` with fewer results. This applies to [`GET /v1/app`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app), [`GET /v1/workspace/org`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/workspace), `GET /v1/automation/org`, the automation run history, and [search](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/search).
-   Some endpoints name the resource in the request body: `workspace_id` when you create an app, `record_id`s when you batch-update record permissions, and `trigger_workflow_def_id` when you generate an automation weblink. Tape checks these against the token's content access too.
-   Creating a workspace requires a token with **All**. A new top-level workspace has no parent that content access could name.

> Content access limits a credential, not your data
> 
> Content access doesn't isolate data, hide data from you, or change anyone's permissions.
> 
> Related records of a record in a selected app come back as read-only previews (ID, title, creation date, app, and workspace), even from apps the token didn't select. The previews stay within your own permissions.

## Revoke a token

Revoke a token in the same **Developer** section. Revocation applies from the next request on.

Revoking one token doesn't affect your other tokens, your user API key, or your account. Revoked tokens stay in the list, so you keep a record of what existed.

> Webhooks outlive the token that created them
> 
> A webhook created through the API keeps delivering after you revoke the token that created it. Delete those webhooks separately.

## Limits

| Limit | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Active tokens per user | 20 |
| Selected workspaces per token | 50 |
| Selected apps per token | 50 |
| Token name length | 500 characters |

## Rate limits

A personal access token has no rate limit budget of its own. Your user API key, all your tokens and your [OAuth](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview) connections share one per-user budget, so more tokens don't mean more throughput. See [Request limits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits).

## Attribution

A token acts as you. Records it creates or changes show you as the author, and it sends emails on your behalf. To show an integration under its own name, create a dedicated user for it and create the token from that account.

## Keep tokens safe

-   **Never commit a token** to source control or put it in a client-side app. A token in a browser bundle is public.
-   **Use one token per integration**, so you can revoke one without breaking another.
-   **Grant the fewest capabilities that work.** A reporting integration needs only read capabilities.
-   **Select only the workspaces and apps the integration needs.**
-   Secret-scanning tools recognize the `tape_pat_` prefix, so they can spot a leaked token.
-   If a token may have leaked, revoke it first and investigate afterwards.

## Next steps

-   [Quickstart](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/getting-started): retrieve your first record with a token.
-   [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities): the capability each endpoint needs.
-   [Request limits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits): the per-user budget all your tokens share.
-   [Authentication](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication): compare tokens with OAuth and the user API key.
-   In the Help Center: [Personal access tokens](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18449281-personal-access-tokens)

# Request limits

> Handle rate limits and size limits so your integration keeps working under load.

Handle rate limits and size limits so your integration keeps working under load.

## Rate limits

A rate-limited request returns HTTP status `429` with the error code `user_too_many_requests`.

The base rate limit is an average of 3 requests per second. Short bursts above the average are allowed.

Handle `429` responses and slow down your following requests. After a `429`, wait the number of seconds in the `Retry-After` header before you retry.

A common pattern is one or more queues for pending requests. Keep sending from the queue as long as Tape doesn't respond with `429`.

> Rate limits may change
> 
> Tape plans to adjust rate limits to balance demand and reliability. Tape may also introduce distinct rate limits for organizations on different pricing plans.

### Rate limit credits

Tape enforces rate limits with credits:

-   Each user has 2,000 credits per minute. After the minute, the credits refill.
-   A request costs 10 credits by default. Expensive requests cost more, for example creating a record or creating, updating or deleting an app. Some endpoint pages list their cost. The `X-Retry-Cost` header shows the cost of every request.
-   All credentials of a user share the same budget: the user API key, every [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) they own, and every app or MCP client they connected with [OAuth](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview). More tokens don't mean more throughput.
-   A request that authenticates but lacks a capability, or falls outside a token's content access, still costs credits. Tape checks both after rate limiting.

Coming from the [Podio API](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/coming-from-podio)? Tape counts credits per minute, not calls per hour.

### Rate limit headers

Tape sends rate limit headers *with every response*. Use them to slow down before you hit the limit. These are the response headers of a valid request:

```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Retry-After: 57
X-RateLimit-Limit: 2000
X-Retry-Remaining: 1990
X-Retry-Cost: 10
X-Retry-Reset: 2022-03-01 12:00:00
X-RateLimit-Scope: user
```

| HTTP header | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `X-RateLimit-Limit` | Total credits per time interval. | `2000` |
| `X-Retry-Remaining` | Credits left in this time interval. | `1980` |
| `X-Retry-Cost` | Credits the current request used. | `10` |
| `X-Retry-Reset` | Date and time at which the credits reset. | `2022-03-01 12:00:00` |
| `Retry-After` | Seconds left in this interval until the credits reset. | `60` |
| `X-RateLimit-Scope` | Which budget the request counts against: `user` for a user's credentials, `workflow` for an automation API key. | `user` |

> Which timezone does `X-Retry-Reset` use?
> 
> `X-Retry-Reset` uses the format `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, the same datetime format as the rest of the API, with no `Z` suffix and no numeric offset. Unlike the temporal properties in response bodies, it's a header and has no local counterpart: *it's in UTC*. See [Date & timezone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone).

When you exceed the rate limit, the error response body also contains all rate limit information:

```json
{
  "status_code": 429,
  "endpoint": "/v1/record/123",
  "error_code": "user_too_many_requests",
  "error_message": "Too many requests (0/2000 credits left) for user with ID 1, retry after 58 seconds (2022-03-01 12:00:00). Your current request costs 10 credits. Check https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits for more info",
  "retry_after": 58,
  "rate_limit": 2000,
  "rate_limit_remaining": 0,
  "rate_limit_cost": 10,
  "rate_limit_reset": "2022-03-01 12:00:00"
}
```

### Tips for reducing API usage

-   Avoid API requests inside loops. Load a collection of objects in one request instead of one object per request.
-   Cache results where you can.
-   Don't poll for changed data. Use [webhooks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/webhook) to react to changes.
-   Log your requests to see how many you make.

### Getting more credits

Need more credits per time interval, for example for a large partner integration? Ask the [Tape team](mailto:team@tapeapp.com) to raise your limit.

## Size limits

Tape limits the size of some parameters. A request above a limit returns HTTP status `400` with the error code `validation`. The `error_message` property says which limit applies.

Stay below the size limits in your integration. Add test data with deliberately large parameters to your test suite to check that you handle the errors.

For example, if your integration copies a URL from another system into a Tape record, plan for URLs above the length limit. Log the error, alert the user who set up the integration, or take another action.

# App

> Use these endpoints to create, read, update and delete the apps of a workspace.

Use these endpoints to create, read, update and delete the apps of a workspace.

An *app* belongs to exactly one workspace. A database app holds records of one kind. To find an app by name across all workspaces, use the [Search resource](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/search).

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> Endpoints that read apps need `apps:read`. Endpoints that change apps need `apps:edit`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

> Where do I find the app ID and field IDs?
> 
> In Tape, open the app menu (**Follow, export and more…**) and select **Developer**. It shows the **Workspace ID**, the **App ID** and, for each field, its **Field ID** and **External ID** (the field's slug). Through the API, [Retrieve all available apps](#retrieve-all-available-apps) returns every `app_id`, and [Retrieve a single app](#retrieve-a-single-app) returns the `field_id` and `slug` of every field.

## The app object

[Retrieve a single app](#retrieve-a-single-app), [Create an app](#create-an-app) and [Update an app](#update-an-app) return the full app object with all its fields:

*App*

```json
{
  "app_id": 1,
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "workspace_name": "CRM",
  "slug": "contacts",
  "external_id": "contacts",
  "name": "Contacts",
  "record_name": "Contact",
  "item_name": "Contact",
  "type": "database",
  "description": "A simple contact app.",
  "position": 0,
  "config": {
    "description": "A simple contact app.",
    "item_name": "Contact",
    "name": "Contacts",
    "icon": {
      "type": "graphic",
      "id": "contacts"
    },
    "item_icon": {
      "type": "graphic",
      "id": "person"
    }
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "slug": "name",
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Name",
        "slug": "name",
        "external_id": "name",
        "description": "The full name of the contact.",
        "show_description": true,
        "required": true,
        "always_hidden": false,
        "hidden_if_empty": false,
        "primary": true,
        "settings": {
          "formatted": false,
          "format": "plain"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The list endpoints [Retrieve apps for a workspace](#retrieve-apps-for-a-workspace) and [Retrieve all available apps](#retrieve-all-available-apps) return a preview of each app: the same properties without `fields`, and `config` without `icon` and `item_icon`.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | number | The app ID. | `1` |
| `workspace_id` | number | The workspace the app belongs to. | `1` |
| `workspace_name` | string | Name of that workspace. | `"CRM"` |
| `slug` | string | Slug of the app, unique in its workspace. | `"contacts"` |
| `external_id` | string | *Deprecated.* Same as `slug`. | `"contacts"` |
| `name` | string | Name of the app. | `"Contacts"` |
| `record_name` | string | Name of one record, for example `Contact`. | `"Contact"` |
| `item_name` | string | *Deprecated.* Same as `record_name`. | `"Contact"` |
| `type` | `"database"` | `"dashboard"` | `"form"` | The kind of app. Untyped and legacy apps return `"database"`. | `"database"` |
| `description` | string | Description of the app. Missing when the app has no description. | `"A simple contact app."` |
| `position` | number | Position of the app in its workspace. | `0` |
| `config` | object | Copy of `description`, `item_name` and `name`, plus `icon` and `item_icon` when set. See [Icon](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/icon). | `{ "name": "Contacts", "item_name": "Contact" }` |
| `fields` | array | Every field of the app, in the order of the app. See [The field object](#the-field-object). | `[{ "field_id": 1, … }]` |

### The field object

Each entry in `fields` describes one field. The format of `config.settings` depends on the field type. See [Fields](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview).

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field_id` | number | The field ID. | `1` |
| `slug` | string | Slug of the field, unique in its app. Use it as a key in the `fields` of a record. | `"name"` |
| `external_id` | string | *Deprecated.* Same as `slug`. | `"name"` |
| `label` | string | Name of the field. | `"Name"` |
| `field_type` | string | The field type. It tells single and multi fields apart, for example `single_category` and `multi_category`. | `"single_text"` |
| `type` | string | The data type, the same for single and multi fields. Prefer `field_type`. | `"text"` |
| `config.label` | string | Same as `label`. | `"Name"` |
| `config.slug` | string | Same as `slug`. | `"name"` |
| `config.external_id` | string | *Deprecated.* Same as `slug`. | `"name"` |
| `config.description` | string | Help text of the field. Missing when the field has none. | `"The full name of the contact."` |
| `config.show_description` | boolean | `true` if records show the help text. A new `single_text` or `multi_text` field with a `description` gets `true`, a new field of another type gets `false`. For updates, see [Fields](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview). | `true` |
| `config.required` | boolean | `true` if every record needs a value. | `true` |
| `config.always_hidden` | boolean | `true` if every record hides the field. | `false` |
| `config.hidden_if_empty` | boolean | `true` if records hide the field while it has no value. | `false` |
| `config.primary` | boolean | `true` for the primary field. Its value names each record. Some database apps have no primary field. | `true` |
| `config.settings` | object | Settings of the field type. | `{ "formatted": false, "format": "plain" }` |

## Retrieve apps for a workspace

Use this endpoint to list all apps of one workspace.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/workspace/{workspace_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/workspace/200 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 2,
  "apps": [
    {
      "app_id": 1,
      "workspace_id": 200,
      "name": "Tasks",
      "record_name": "Task",
      "slug": "tasks",
      "type": "database",
      "config": {
        "item_name": "Task",
        "name": "Tasks"
      }
    },
    {
      "app_id": 2,
      "workspace_id": 200,
      "name": "Projects",
      "record_name": "Project",
      "slug": "projects",
      "type": "database",
      "config": {
        "item_name": "Project",
        "name": "Projects"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The example lists the apps of the workspace with ID `200`, without their fields. To read the fields, retrieve the app by its ID.

**Requirements:** `apps:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Retrieve all available apps

Use this endpoint to list the apps of all workspaces you have access to.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 3,
  "apps": [
    {
      "app_id": 1,
      "workspace_id": 200,
      "workspace_name": "Task management",
      "name": "Tasks",
      "record_name": "Task",
      "slug": "tasks",
      "type": "database",
      "config": {
        "item_name": "Task",
        "name": "Tasks"
      }
    },
    {
      "app_id": 2,
      "workspace_id": 200,
      "workspace_name": "Task management",
      "name": "Projects",
      "record_name": "Project",
      "slug": "projects",
      "type": "database",
      "config": {
        "item_name": "Project",
        "name": "Projects"
      }
    },
    {
      "app_id": 3,
      "workspace_id": 300,
      "workspace_name": "CRM",
      "name": "Contacts",
      "record_name": "Contact",
      "slug": "contacts",
      "type": "database",
      "config": {
        "item_name": "Contact",
        "name": "Contacts"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Every app carries `workspace_id` and `workspace_name`. The response doesn't contain the fields.

**Requirements:** `apps:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Retrieve a single app

Use this endpoint to read one app together with all its fields.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/{app_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "app_id": 1,
  "workspace_id": 200,
  "name": "Tasks",
  "record_name": "Task",
  "slug": "tasks",
  "type": "database",
  "config": {
    "item_name": "Task",
    "name": "Tasks"
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "slug": "full_name",
      "external_id": "full_name",
      "label": "Full Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Full Name",
        "show_description": false,
        "required": false,
        "primary": true,
        "settings": {
          "formatted": false,
          "format": "plain"
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The response is the full [app object](#the-app-object), with every field of the app.

**Requirements:** `apps:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

## Retrieve views for an app

Use this endpoint to list the public views of an app.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/{app_id}/views`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/1/views \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "views": [
    {
      "id": 500,
      "view_id": 500,
      "name": "Open Tasks",
      "app_id": 1,
      "is_default": true,
      "layout": "list",
      "private": false
    },
    {
      "id": 501,
      "view_id": 501,
      "name": "Completed Tasks",
      "app_id": 1,
      "is_default": false,
      "layout": "table",
      "private": false
    }
  ],
  "total": 2
}
```

Each entry is a *preview* with the ID, name, layout and default flag of the view. To read the full definition of a view, or to create, update, promote or delete views, use the [View resource](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/view).

**Requirements:** `apps:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

## Create an app

Use this endpoint to create an app in a workspace, with or without fields.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/ \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "workspace_id": 1,
    "name": "Contacts",
    "item_name": "Contact",
    "description": "A simple contact app.",
    "icon": {
      "id": "contacts",
      "type": "graphic"
    },
    "item_icon": {
      "id": "person",
      "type": "graphic"
    },
    "fields": [
      {
        "field_type": "single_text",
        "config": {
          "label": "Name",
          "description": "The full name of the contact.",
          "required": true
        }
      },
      {
        "field_type": "multi_text",
        "config": {
          "label": "Notes",
          "description": "Notes about the contact.",
          "required": false
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "name": "Contacts",
  "item_name": "Contact",
  "description": "A simple contact app.",
  "icon": {
    "id": "contacts",
    "type": "graphic"
  },
  "item_icon": {
    "id": "person",
    "type": "graphic"
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Name",
        "description": "The full name of the contact.",
        "required": true
      }
    },
    {
      "field_type": "multi_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Notes",
        "description": "Notes about the contact.",
        "required": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "app_id": 1,
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "slug": "contacts",
  "external_id": "contacts",
  "name": "Contacts",
  "record_name": "Contact",
  "item_name": "Contact",
  "type": "database",
  "description": "A simple contact app.",
  "position": 0,
  "config": {
    "description": "A simple contact app.",
    "item_name": "Contact",
    "name": "Contacts",
    "icon": {
      "type": "graphic",
      "id": "contacts"
    },
    "item_icon": {
      "type": "graphic",
      "id": "person"
    }
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 10,
      "external_id": "name",
      "slug": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Name",
        "slug": "name",
        "external_id": "name",
        "description": "The full name of the contact.",
        "show_description": true,
        "required": true,
        "always_hidden": false,
        "hidden_if_empty": false,
        "primary": true,
        "settings": {
          "formatted": false
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "field_id": 20,
      "external_id": "notes",
      "slug": "notes",
      "label": "Notes",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "multi_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Notes",
        "slug": "notes",
        "external_id": "notes",
        "description": "Notes about the contact.",
        "show_description": true,
        "required": false,
        "always_hidden": false,
        "hidden_if_empty": false,
        "primary": false,
        "settings": {
          "formatted": true
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The example creates a contacts app in the workspace with ID `1`. The app gets a `single_text` field "Name" and a `multi_text` field "Notes".

The response has status `201` and contains the new app with all its fields.

**General behavior**

-   Tape creates the fields in the order of the `fields` array.
-   Set the record name with `item_name`. The response returns it as `record_name`.
-   Without `position`, the new app goes after the last app of the workspace.

> Workspace has 500 apps?
> 
> A workspace holds at most 500 apps. Further create requests then return an error. Delete an existing app to create a new one.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and a workspace role that may edit apps in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `workspace_id` | `integer` | Required. ID of the workspace to create the app in. |
| `name` | `string` | Required. Name of the app. |
| `item_name` | `string` | Name of one record, for example `Contact` (default: the app `name`). |
| `description` | `string` | Description of the app. |
| `position` | `number` | Position of the app in the workspace, the same `position` value apps return (default: after the last app of the workspace). |
| `fields` | `Array` | Fields to create with the app, in this order. See [Fields](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview). |
| `icon` | `object` | Icon of the app. See [Icon](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/icon). |
| `item_icon` | `object` | Icon of the records. See [Icon](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/icon). |

## Update an app

Use this endpoint to rename an app, change its icons, or add, change and delete fields.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": [
      {
        "field_type": "single_text",
        "config": {
          "label": "First Name",
          "description": "The first name of the contact.",
          "required": true
        }
      },
      {
        "field_type": "single_text",
        "config": {
          "label": "Last Name",
          "description": "The last name of the contact.",
          "required": true
        }
      }
    ],
    "fields_to_delete": [
      {
        "field_id": 10
      }
    ]
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "First Name",
        "description": "The first name of the contact.",
        "required": true
      }
    },
    {
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Last Name",
        "description": "The last name of the contact.",
        "required": true
      }
    }
  ],
  "fields_to_delete": [
    {
      "field_id": 10
    }
  ]
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "app_id": 1,
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "slug": "contacts",
  "name": "Contacts",
  "record_name": "Contact",
  "item_name": "Contact",
  "type": "database",
  "description": "A simple contact app.",
  "position": 0,
  "config": {
    "description": "A simple contact app.",
    "item_name": "Contact",
    "name": "Contacts",
    "icon": {
      "type": "graphic",
      "id": "contacts"
    }
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 20,
      "external_id": "notes",
      "slug": "notes",
      "label": "Notes",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "multi_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Notes",
        "slug": "notes",
        "description": "Notes about the contact.",
        "show_description": true,
        "required": false,
        "always_hidden": false,
        "hidden_if_empty": false,
        "primary": true,
        "settings": {
          "formatted": true
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "field_id": 30,
      "external_id": "first_name",
      "slug": "first_name",
      "label": "First Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "First Name",
        "slug": "first_name",
        "description": "The first name of the contact.",
        "show_description": true,
        "required": true,
        "always_hidden": false,
        "hidden_if_empty": false,
        "primary": false,
        "settings": {
          "formatted": false
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "field_id": 40,
      "external_id": "last_name",
      "slug": "last_name",
      "label": "Last Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Last Name",
        "slug": "last_name",
        "description": "The last name of the contact.",
        "show_description": true,
        "required": true,
        "always_hidden": false,
        "hidden_if_empty": false,
        "primary": false,
        "settings": {
          "formatted": false
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The example updates the contacts app from [Create an app](#create-an-app). It deletes the "Name" field and adds two `single_text` fields, "First Name" and "Last Name". The "Notes" field is in neither `fields` nor `fields_to_delete`, so it stays unchanged.

The response contains the updated app with all its fields.

**General behavior**

-   Send only the properties you want to change.
-   A field in `fields` with a `field_id` updates that existing field. A field without `field_id` creates a new field. Tape adds new fields after the existing ones, in the order of the array.
-   To delete a field, add it to `fields_to_delete` with its `field_id`. This also deletes its values in every record. Entries copied from the app's `fields` property work too.
-   Fields that are in neither array stay unchanged.
-   To delete options of a category or status field, send `options_to_delete` in the `config.settings` of that field. See [Category](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/category#app-update) and [Status](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/status#app-update).
-   Want to make sure a request never deletes anything? Set `reject_deletions` to `true`.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and **Full access** to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

With `reject_deletions=true`, a request that deletes a field (`fields_to_delete`) or an option (`options_to_delete`) returns `400` with `deletions_rejected`. Tape applies nothing from that request, not even the other changes in the body:

```json
{
  "status_code": 400,
  "endpoint": "/v1/app/1",
  "error_code": "deletions_rejected",
  "error_message": "This request asks for something to be deleted ('fields_to_delete' names 1 field(s)), and it was sent with 'reject_deletions=true'. Nothing was applied — not the deletions, and not the rest of the body. Remove the deletion from the request, or send it without 'reject_deletions'."
}
```

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reject_deletions` | `boolean` | Reject the request with `400` (`deletions_rejected`) if it deletes a field (`fields_to_delete`) or an option (`options_to_delete`). Nothing is applied then (default: `false`). |

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Name of the app. |
| `item_name` | `string` | Name of one record, for example `Contact`. |
| `description` | `string` | Description of the app. |
| `fields` | `Array` | Fields to create or update. A field with `field_id` is updated, a field without one is created. See [Fields](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview). |
| `fields_to_delete` | `Array` | Fields to delete, each with its `field_id`. |
| `icon` | `object` | Icon of the app. See [Icon](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/icon). |
| `item_icon` | `object` | Icon of the records. See [Icon](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/icon). |

## Update an app's field order

Use this endpoint to change the order of the fields in an app.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/{app_id}/fields/order`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/1/fields/order \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": [
      {
        "field_id": 20
      },
      {
        "field_id": 30
      },
      {
        "field_id": 40
      }
    ]
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 20
    },
    {
      "field_id": 30
    },
    {
      "field_id": 40
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
{
  "app_id": 1,

  "name": "Contacts",
  "record_name": "Contact",

  "type": "database",
  "description": "A simple contact app.",
  "position": 0,
  "config": {
    "description": "A simple contact app.",
    "item_name": "Contact",
    "name": "Contacts",
    "icon": {
      "type": "graphic",
      "id": "contacts"
    }
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 20,
      "external_id": "notes",
      "slug": "notes",
      "label": "Notes",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "multi_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "Notes",
        "slug": "notes",
        "description": "Notes about the contact.",
        "show_description": true,
        "required": false,
        "always_hidden": false,
        "hidden_if_empty": false,
        "primary": true,
        "settings": {
          "formatted": true
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "field_id": 30,
      "external_id": "first_name",
      "slug": "first_name",
      "label": "First Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "label": "First Name",
        "slug": "first_name",
        "description": "The first name of the contact.",
        "show_description": true,
        "required": true,
        "always_hidden": false,
        "hidden_if_empty": false,

        }

```

The example moves the `notes` field of the contacts app to the first position.

The response contains the app with its fields in the new order.

**General behavior**

-   Identify each field by its `field_id`.
-   To set the complete order, list all fields of the app.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and **Full access** to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fields` | `Array` | Fields in the new order, each with its `field_id`. |

## Delete an app

Use this endpoint to delete an app.

`DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "app_id": 1
}
```

> Can you undo deleting an app?
> 
> No. Deleting an app also deletes all its records and fields.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and **Full access** to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

# Automation run

> List and retrieve Tape automation runs and their step logs through the Developer API.

Use these endpoints to list the runs of your automations and to read a single run with its step logs.

An automation run is one execution of an automation. You see the runs of automations in workspaces you *administer*.

The listings leave out simulation runs, which you create when you test an automation in the editor or [simulate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution#simulate-an-automation) it through the API. The [per-automation listing](#list-runs-for-an-automation) includes them, and you can retrieve any of them by ID.

> Which credential and capability do I need?
> 
> All endpoints on this page need `automations:read` ([Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities)) and a credential that acts for a user: a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens), an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview) or a [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key).
> 
> An automation API key has no workspace role to check and returns `401` with the message `Automation runs can only be listed with a user API key.` (or `... retrieved with ...` for a single run). The message names only the user API key, but a personal access token or an OAuth access token works too.

## List automation runs

Use this endpoint to list the runs you may see, newest first.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "status": ["completed"],
    "limit": 2
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "status": ["completed"],
  "limit": 2
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 37,
  "automation_runs": [
    {
      "id": "9001",
      "automation_id": 88,
      "automation_name": "Notify on new lead",
      "automation_revision_id": "3",
      "app_id": 42,
      "app_name": "Leads",
      "workspace_id": 7,
      "status": "completed",
      "type": "regular",
      "created_at": "2024-01-18 08:12:04",
      "created_at_utc": "2024-01-18 07:12:04",
      "completed_at": "2024-01-18 08:12:09",
      "completed_at_utc": "2024-01-18 07:12:09",
      "num_consumed_actions": 2,
      "failure_reason": null,
      "error_message": null,
      "triggered_on_record_id": 5001,
      "triggered_on_record_revision_id": 4,
      "triggered_by_automation_id": null
    },
    {
      "id": "8974",
      "automation_id": 88,
      "automation_name": "Notify on new lead",
      "automation_revision_id": "3",
      "app_id": 42,
      "app_name": "Leads",
      "workspace_id": 7,
      "status": "completed",
      "type": "regular",
      "created_at": "2024-01-17 22:47:51",
      "created_at_utc": "2024-01-17 21:47:51",
      "completed_at": "2024-01-17 22:47:55",
      "completed_at_utc": "2024-01-17 21:47:55",
      "num_consumed_actions": 1,
      "failure_reason": null,
      "error_message": null,
      "triggered_on_record_id": 4987,
      "triggered_on_record_revision_id": 1,
      "triggered_by_automation_id": 71
    }
  ],
  "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ3b3JrZmxvd1J1bklkIjo4OTc0LCJleHAiOjE2NTA2MTg3Nzh9.iY5TnLSBDGCnFXbStcrLPTmP6MATnS_JKywbvC4tx3g"
}
```

The example asks for the 2 most recent successful runs.

The example comes from a user whose timezone is one hour ahead of UTC. Each plain timestamp is in that timezone, and its `_utc` twin is the same instant in UTC. The example is shortened: every run also carries `filtering_at`, `started_at`, their `_utc` twins, `execution_duration_ms` and `waiting_duration_ms`.

**Response fields**

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `total` | `integer` | Number of runs that match the filters, across all pages. See [Pagination](#pagination). | `37` |
| `automation_runs` | `array` | The page itself. Each entry is a run. See [The run object](#the-run-object). | `[{ "id": "9001", … }]` |
| `cursor` | `string` | Cursor of the last run on this page. Send it back to get the next page. `null` on the last page. | `"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."` |

**General behavior**

-   The response contains one page of runs, without logs.
-   All body parameters are optional. An empty object `{}` lists every run you may see. A request without a body returns `400`.
-   An ID that *exists but that you don't administer* returns `404`. This applies to an app, an automation or a workspace, including one in another organization.
-   A *completely unknown* ID is handled differently per filter. An unknown `app_ids` or `workspace_ids` value returns `404`.
-   An unknown `automation_ids` value is a *filter, not a lookup*. An ID that never existed, or a soft-deleted automation whose runs you would otherwise see, matches no runs. The response is `200` with an empty list, not `404`.
-   Don't use this endpoint to test whether an automation exists. Use `GET /v1/automation/{id}`, which returns `404` in those cases.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the workspaces whose runs you list. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | `string` | Cursor of the previous page. Can't be combined with the filters below. See [Pagination](#pagination). |
| `limit` | `integer` | Page size. Between `1` and `500`. Defaults to `50`. |
| `app_ids` | `integer[]` | Only runs of automations that belong to these apps. Max 100 IDs. Only database apps can have automations. |
| `automation_ids` | `integer[]` | Only runs of these automations. Max 100 IDs. |
| `workspace_ids` | `integer[]` | Only runs of automations in these workspaces. Max 100 IDs. |
| `status` | `string[]` | Only runs in these statuses. One or more of `pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`. |
| `created_at_from` | `string` | Only runs created at or after this instant, read in your timezone. Inclusive. See [Filtering by date](#filtering-by-date). |
| `created_at_to` | `string` | Only runs created at or before this instant, read in your timezone. Inclusive. See [Filtering by date](#filtering-by-date). |
| `created_at_from_utc` | `string` | Same bound as `created_at_from`, read as UTC. Wins over `created_at_from` when you send both. See [Filtering by date](#filtering-by-date). |
| `created_at_to_utc` | `string` | Same bound as `created_at_to`, read as UTC. Wins over `created_at_to` when you send both. See [Filtering by date](#filtering-by-date). |

### The run object

Each entry in `automation_runs` has these fields. So does the `automation_run` you get when you retrieve a single run.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | ID of the run. A 64-bit integer, returned as a string so that every language can handle it safely. | `"9001"` |
| `automation_id` | `integer` | The automation this run executed. | `88` |
| `automation_name` | `string` | Name of the automation. | `"Notify on new lead"` |
| `automation_revision_id` | `string` | The revision of the automation this run executed. A 64-bit integer, returned as a string. | `"3"` |
| `app_id` | `integer` | The app the automation belongs to. | `42` |
| `app_name` | `string` | Name of that app. | `"Leads"` |
| `workspace_id` | `integer` | The workspace the app belongs to. | `7` |
| `status` | `string` | See [Statuses](#statuses). | `"completed"` |
| `type` | `string` | Execution kind of the run. One of `regular`, `manual`, `simulation`. | `"regular"` |
| `created_at` | `string` | When the run was created (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`), in your timezone. | `"2024-01-18 08:12:04"` |
| `created_at_utc` | `string` | Same instant as `created_at`, in UTC. | `"2024-01-18 07:12:04"` |
| `filtering_at` | `string` | `null` | When the filtering of the run was scheduled (enqueued), in your timezone. `null` before then. | `"2024-01-18 08:12:04"` |
| `filtering_at_utc` | `string` | `null` | Same instant as `filtering_at`, in UTC. | `"2024-01-18 07:12:04"` |
| `started_at` | `string` | `null` | When the run started executing (entered `running`), in your timezone. `null` before then. | `"2024-01-18 08:12:05"` |
| `started_at_utc` | `string` | `null` | Same instant as `started_at`, in UTC. | `"2024-01-18 07:12:05"` |
| `completed_at` | `string` | `null` | When the run finished (reached a final status), in your timezone. `null` while the run is `pending` or `running`. | `"2024-01-18 08:12:09"` |
| `completed_at_utc` | `string` | `null` | Same instant as `completed_at`, in UTC. | `"2024-01-18 07:12:09"` |
| `execution_duration_ms` | `integer` | `null` | How long the run executed, in milliseconds. `null` until the run completes. | `4000` |
| `waiting_duration_ms` | `integer` | `null` | How long the run waited (scheduled) before it started executing, in milliseconds. `null` until the run starts. | `1000` |
| `num_consumed_actions` | `integer` | Number of action credits this run consumed. | `2` |
| `failure_reason` | `string` | `null` | Why the run failed, if it did. One of `filters_setup_failed`, `filters_failed`, `actions_setup_failed`, `actions_failed`, `actions_timeout`, `actions_resource_limit_exceeded`, `exit_on_purpose`. `null` for any run that has not failed. | `null` |
| `error_message` | `string` | `null` | Readable error detail for a failed run. `null` otherwise. | `null` |
| `triggered_on_record_id` | `integer` | `null` | The record this run executed on. `null` if no record triggered the run. | `5001` |
| `triggered_on_record_revision_id` | `integer` | `null` | The revision of that record. `null` if no record triggered the run. | `4` |
| `triggered_by_automation_id` | `integer` | `null` | The automation that started this run, if another automation called it. `null` otherwise. | `null` |

Timestamps use the [Tape API datetime format](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone) `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, with no `T` separator, no `Z` suffix and no milliseconds. Each plain field is in your timezone, and its `_utc` twin carries the same instant in UTC. Use the plain field for display and the `_utc` field for comparing, sorting and storing.

### Statuses

| Status | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `pending` | The run is scheduled and has not started executing yet. |
| `running` | The run is executing. |
| `completed` | The run finished successfully. |
| `failed` | The run finished with an error. |
| `cancelled` | The run was cancelled before it could finish. |

### Filtering by date

Use `created_at_from` and `created_at_to` to list only runs whose `created_at` falls within a window. Both bounds are *inclusive*, and you can send either one on its own.

Both use the format of `created_at` and are read in your timezone, so you can send a value from a response back as a bound.

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "created_at_from": "2024-01-18 00:00:00",
    "created_at_to": "2024-01-18 23:59:59"
  }'
```

Computing the bounds yourself? Use `created_at_from_utc` and `created_at_to_utc` instead. They take the same format, read as UTC, and pair with the `created_at_utc` of a run.

A wall-clock time in your timezone is ambiguous when daylight saving time ends. If you send both versions of a bound, the `_utc` version wins.

-   `created_at_from` never reaches back beyond the 30 days Tape keeps runs. An older value counts as the start of that window, so you can safely send an open lower bound.
-   `created_at_to` has no such limit.
-   The lower bound must be at or before the upper bound. Otherwise the request returns `400`.

### Pagination

Results are [paginated](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/pagination) with a cursor. To get the next page, send the `cursor` from the previous response *on its own*. You can add `limit`:

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
  }'
```

The cursor carries the filters of the first page, so don't send them again. A request with a `cursor` and any of `app_ids`, `automation_ids`, `workspace_ids`, `status`, `created_at_from`, `created_at_to`, `created_at_from_utc` or `created_at_to_utc` returns `400`.

Runs come *newest first*, in descending order of run ID. When `cursor` is `null`, you have reached the end of the list.

> Why does the number of runs differ from `total`?
> 
> Tape counts `total` once, when you request the first page, and keeps it for the rest of the walk. Automations keep running and old runs leave the 30-day window while you page through, so the runs you receive may differ slightly from `total`.

> How long are runs kept?
> 
> Only runs from the last 30 days are available. Older runs can't be listed or retrieved. Tape doesn't return runs of deleted automations.

## List runs for an app

Use this endpoint to list the runs of all automations of one app, newest first.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/app/{app_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/app/42 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "limit": 2
  }'
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 37,
  "automation_runs": [
    {
      "id": "9001",
      "automation_id": 88,
      "automation_name": "Notify on new lead",
      "automation_revision_id": "3",
      "app_id": 42,
      "app_name": "Leads",
      "workspace_id": 7,
      "status": "completed",
      "type": "regular",
      "created_at": "2024-01-18 08:12:04",
      "created_at_utc": "2024-01-18 07:12:04",
      "completed_at": "2024-01-18 08:12:09",
      "completed_at_utc": "2024-01-18 07:12:09",
      "num_consumed_actions": 2,
      "failure_reason": null,
      "error_message": null,
      "triggered_on_record_id": 5001,
      "triggered_on_record_revision_id": 4,
      "triggered_by_automation_id": null
    }
  ],
  "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
}
```

This variant of [List automation runs](#list-automation-runs) is locked to the app in the path. The body carries [pagination](#pagination) only: `cursor` and `limit`.

Each entry is a [run object](#the-run-object).

**General behavior**

-   The filters and date bounds of the general list are *not* accepted here. Any other body property returns `400`.
-   Simulation runs are left out, as in the general list.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. The app must be a database app.

**Errors**

-   An `app_id` that is not available to you returns `404`, the same as a missing ID. This is the [protection against probing IDs](#retrieve-an-automation-run) of all endpoints here.
-   An ID of an app that is not a database app returns `400`, because only database apps can have automations.

## List runs for a workspace

Use this endpoint to list the runs of all automations in one workspace, newest first.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/workspace/{workspace_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/workspace/7 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "limit": 2
  }'
```

As in [List runs for an app](#list-runs-for-an-app), the body carries pagination only (`cursor`, `limit`), simulation runs are left out, and the response has the same shape.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

A `workspace_id` that is not available to you returns `404`. You can't tell it apart from a missing one.

## List runs for an automation

Use this endpoint to list the runs of one automation, newest first.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/automation/{automation_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/automation/88 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "limit": 2
  }'
```

The body carries pagination only (`cursor`, `limit`). The response has the same shape as in [List runs for an app](#list-runs-for-an-app).

After a [manual run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution#run-an-automation) or a [simulation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution#simulate-an-automation), find your run by `triggered_on_record_id` and `type` (`manual` or `simulation`).

> Why do I see simulation runs here?
> 
> This listing matches the run history of an automation in Tape, so it includes *simulation runs*. They count in `total` and appear in `automation_runs`.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the automation's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

An `automation_id` that is missing, deleted or not one you administer returns the same `404`.


To find `automation_run_id`, use the `id` of a run from a listing. The run has the same fields as [a run in a listing](#the-run-object), plus a `logs` array.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the automation's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A run that is not available to you returns `404`: it doesn't exist, was deleted, is older than 30 days, or belongs to a workspace you don't administer. Tape IDs are unique across all organizations, so one `404` for every case keeps anyone from probing which run IDs exist.
-   An automation API key returns `401`.
-   A run ID that is not an integer returns `400`.

### The log object

A run is a sequence of *steps*: the trigger that started it, the filter that decided whether to go on, and one entry per executed action. This is the same view of a run as under **Automations** → **Runs** in Tape and in its export (**Export runs**), not the raw internal event stream.

> Missing the step of an action?
> 
> A `completed` run does *not* guarantee a `success` step for every top-level action. Control-flow containers (`conditional`, `for_loop`) log only their *nested* actions, and a *deactivated* action (`deactivate: true`) logs *no* entry, not even a `skipped` one. Some actions finish without a step, for example a skipped `authenticated_http_call`, `collected_records_collect_referenced_records`, or a `referenced_records_update` on a record without related records in its app. Match on the `action_id` you expect: a missing step doesn't prove that the run failed.

> Don't see all steps of a run yet?
> 
> The trigger and filter steps are there from the start. Tape buffers the action steps, so they arrive *after* the run reaches its final status. When you poll, wait for the step of your `action_id`, not for `logs.length > 0`.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Stable ID of the step within its run. A durable handle, not a position. See below. | `"9042-action-a1b2c3-1"` |
| `type` | `string` | `trigger`, `filter`, `action` or `exception`. | `"action"` |
| `status` | `string` | Outcome of the step: `in_progress`, `success`, `failure`, `skipped` or `cancelled`. | `"success"` |
| `label` | `string` | Readable description of the step, as in the run log in Tape, for example `"When a record is created triggered by Record ID 5001"` or `"Send an email"`. An action with a custom name in the editor shows that name. | `"Send an email"` |
| `messages` | `array` | The messages the step logged. Each has a `message` and a `level` (`info`, `warn`, `error`, `success` or `null`). A message starts with its time in UTC, `[HH:mm:ss.SSS]`. | `[{ "message": "[07:12:06.310] Action execution started.", "level": null }]` |
| `action_id` | `string` | `null` | The automation action this step executed. `null` for `trigger`, `filter` and `exception` steps. | `"a1b2c3"` |
| `record_id` | `integer` | `null` | The record this step acted on, if it acted on one. `null` otherwise. | `5001` |
| `logged_at` | `string` | When the step was logged (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`), in your timezone. | `"2024-01-18 08:12:07"` |
| `logged_at_utc` | `string` | Same instant as `logged_at`, in UTC. | `"2024-01-18 07:12:07"` |

The trigger step has the ID `"{run_id}-trigger"` and the filter step `"{run_id}-filter"`. An action step also carries the execution it belongs to: `"{run_id}-action-{action_id}-{execution_id}"`. An action inside a loop runs more than once, and each execution is its own step. An action that changes several records in one execution, such as `collected_records_update`, writes one step per record with the same `id`. Tell them apart by `record_id`.

Tape adds an `exception` step when a run failed and no single step recorded the failure.

> When is a step `skipped`?
> 
> When the run did not execute it on purpose. That is the *trigger* step of a manual or simulation run, and the *filter* step of a simulation run. In a simulation, the steps of actions that change records, such as `record_create` or `current_record_update`, read `skipped` too. Other action steps of a simulation, for example `custom_variable` or `send_email`, read `success`, but the simulation still has no side effects. A regular run produces no `skipped` steps.

> Why are labels and messages in English?
> 
> `type`, `status` and `level` are stable values for machines and are never translated. `label` and `message` are prose, and this endpoint returns them in English, whatever the language of the user behind the credential.

## Validation errors

A malformed body returns a `400` validation error. For example, a `cursor` sent together with a filter:

*Response*

```json
{
  "status_code": 400,
  "endpoint": "/v1/automation-run",
  "error_code": "input_validation",
  "error_message": "Invalid input: data must match exactly one schema in oneOf ([...])"
}
```

The same applies to:

-   a `limit` outside `1`–`500`;
-   a filter array with more than 100 IDs;
-   an unknown `status` or an unknown body property;
-   a date bound that is not a valid `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` datetime;
-   a run ID that is not an integer.

A lower date bound later than the upper bound also returns `400`. The message names the fields you sent, for example `created_at_from_utc` if you used the UTC version:

*Response*

```json
{
  "status_code": 400,
  "endpoint": "/v1/automation-run",
  "error_code": "validation",
  "error_message": "\"created_at_from\" must be before or equal to \"created_at_to\"."
}
```

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for the full list of error codes.

## Rate limit credits

Each listing endpoint costs `2x` the base credits: the general list and the variants per app, per workspace and per automation. Retrieving a single run costs `1x`. See [Request limits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits) for how rate limiting works.

# Automation usage report

> Retrieve your organization's automation consumption, with actions consumed and run outcomes, aggregated into time buckets.

Use this endpoint to see how many actions and automation runs your organization used, per hour, day, week, month or year.

The report covers the organization of your credential. You can't read the usage of another organization.

## Retrieve an automation usage report

Use this endpoint to get usage buckets for your organization, newest first.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-usage-report`

*Request*

```shell
curl -G https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-usage-report \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=30" \
  --data-urlencode "interval_resolution=daily"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "organization_id": 1337,
  "usage_reports": [
    {
      "organization_id": 1337,
      "from": "2024-01-18 08:12:04",
      "from_utc": "2024-01-18 08:12:04",
      "to": "2024-01-18 22:47:51",
      "to_utc": "2024-01-18 22:47:51",
      "num_consumed_actions": 320,
      "num_succeeded_runs": 540,
      "num_failed_runs": 12,
      "num_cancelled_runs": 3
    },
    {
      "organization_id": 1337,
      "from": "2024-01-17 00:03:11",
      "from_utc": "2024-01-17 00:03:11",
      "to": "2024-01-17 23:58:40",
      "to_utc": "2024-01-17 23:58:40",
      "num_consumed_actions": 412,
      "num_succeeded_runs": 690,
      "num_failed_runs": 20,
      "num_cancelled_runs": 5
    },
    {
      "organization_id": 1337,
      "from": "2024-01-15 09:30:00",
      "from_utc": "2024-01-15 09:30:00",
      "to": "2024-01-15 17:05:22",
      "to_utc": "2024-01-15 17:05:22",
      "num_consumed_actions": 88,
      "num_succeeded_runs": 130,
      "num_failed_runs": 4,
      "num_cancelled_runs": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

The example requests the 30 most recent daily buckets.

The response has no bucket for 2024-01-16, because nothing ran that day.

**General behavior**

-   Buckets come *newest first* (by bucket start), up to `limit`.
-   Tape returns only buckets with activity. Periods without activity don't appear as empty buckets.
-   Bucket boundaries follow the calendar in UTC. `weekly` uses the ISO week: a week starts on Monday at `00:00` UTC.
-   A personal access token limited to some apps still returns the totals of the whole organization. The report has no per-app breakdown.

> Don't see the latest activity?
> 
> A background job builds the report from regular snapshots. The newest bucket can lag behind live activity until the job runs again. Use the endpoint for usage history, not for live metering.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Errors**

A missing, out-of-range or non-integer `limit`, or an unknown `interval_resolution`, returns `400` with `validation`. For example, `limit=250` returns:

*Response*

```json
{
  "status_code": 400,
  "endpoint": "/v1/automation-usage-report",
  "error_code": "validation",
  "error_message": "Query param \"limit\" must be between 0 and 100, got 250."
}
```

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `integer` | Yes | Number of buckets to return, from `0` to `100`. `0` returns an empty list. |
| `interval_resolution` | `string` | Yes | Size of a bucket. One of `hourly`, `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly` or `yearly`. |

**Response fields**

Each entry in `usage_reports` describes one time bucket:

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `organization_id` | `integer` | The organization of the report. | `1337` |
| `from` | `string` | Start of the earliest reporting interval with activity in the bucket, in UTC (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`). Can be later than the start of the calendar bucket. | `"2024-01-18 08:12:04"` |
| `from_utc` | `string` | Same value as `from`, in UTC. | `"2024-01-18 08:12:04"` |
| `to` | `string` | End of the latest reporting interval with activity in the bucket, in UTC (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`). Can be earlier or later than the end of the calendar bucket. | `"2024-01-18 22:47:51"` |
| `to_utc` | `string` | Same value as `to`, in UTC. | `"2024-01-18 22:47:51"` |
| `num_consumed_actions` | `integer` | Action credits consumed in the bucket. | `320` |
| `num_succeeded_runs` | `integer` | Automation runs that finished successfully (status `completed`). | `540` |
| `num_failed_runs` | `integer` | Automation runs that finished with a failed status. | `12` |
| `num_cancelled_runs` | `integer` | Automation runs that finished with a cancelled status. | `3` |

The top-level `organization_id` repeats the organization of every bucket. `from` and `to` stay in UTC, unlike most dates in the API, because they define the UTC buckets. They use the format described in [Date & timezone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone): no `T` separator, no `Z` suffix, no milliseconds.

## Rate limit credits

Each request to this endpoint costs `2x` the base credits. See [Request limits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits) for how credits work.
