# Action examples

> Copy-paste config for the most common Tape automation actions — records, email, HTTP, code, control flow, and collections.

Use these examples to copy a working `config` for the most common automation actions.

Each example is the *smallest `config`* that Tape saves, validates and runs for that [action type](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions). [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) returns the full `config_schema` of every action type. Build against it for the complete list of fields.

How to read the examples:

-   Put these objects into the `actions` array when you [create or update](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage) an automation.
-   Node `id`s are *left out*. Tape creates them. Stable `id`s appear only where an action nests other actions.
-   `group` *follows from `type`* and is optional on input. It's shown to make the examples clearer.
-   Values that pull in live record data are [dynamic values](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values), an *array* (template or code). Plain settings, such as an `app_id` or a boolean, are scalars. Each example says which is which.
-   All config enum values are *lower-case*, for example `http_call_type: "post"`, `weblink_expiration: "never"`, `exit_type: "success"`, and on `collect_referenced_records` both `ref_collection_defs[].direction` (`outgoing`, `incoming`, `both`) and `match_type` (`all`, `filtered`). Send them as the `config_schema` lists them.

## Create a record — `record_create`

Creates a record in a database app. Without `field_assignments`, it creates an *empty* record.

```json
{
  "type": "record_create",
  "group": "action",
  "config": {
    "app_id": 12345,
    "silent": false,
    "trigger_other_flows": false
  }
}
```

-   `app_id`: the target database app. Send it in every config. The schema doesn't mark it as required, and validation doesn't report it when it's missing. Without it, the action saves but Tape skips it when the automation runs.
-   `field_assignments`: `[]` is accepted in every case. A filled assignment has the same shape as in [Update the current record](#update-the-current-record--current_record_update) below.
-   `trigger_other_flows` is the option **Trigger automations** in the automation editor. `false` keeps the new record from starting other automations. Keep it at `false` to avoid a loop when this automation triggers on the same database app.
-   All three keys are plain scalars, with no dynamic-value arrays.

![Settings of the action that creates a record, with the options Silent, Trigger automations and Trigger webhooks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/create-record-settings-342936401ceecf2b64510b5a4bcc10ee.png)

## Update the current record — `current_record_update`

Updates the record the run works on, with a list of `field_assignments`.

```json
{
  "type": "current_record_update",
  "group": "action",
  "config": {
    "field_assignments": [],
    "silent": false
  }
}
```

-   `field_assignments` (optional): left out or `[]` is a valid update that *changes no field value* and still logs success. The record's `last_modified_on` and `last_modified_by` still change.
-   A filled assignment is a *typed object per field type*, with lower-case `field_type` and `assignment_type` values (for example `single_text` and `set`) plus any nested match or search conditions in the public [filter tree](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters). `meta/action` describes the items only loosely. [`current_record_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-update) shows filled assignments to copy.
-   It targets the *current record*, with no `app_id` (that's `referenced_records_update`) and no `record_collection` (that's `collected_records_update`). It needs a trigger with a record, such as `record_created`. With no trigger, or with `periodic` or `webhook_received`, `validate` reports `action_invalid`. See [Trigger context](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#trigger-context).
-   `silent`, `trigger_webhooks`, `trigger_other_flows` and `author_id` are optional. `trigger_webhooks` and `trigger_other_flows` are the options **Trigger webhooks** and **Trigger automations** in the editor. Without `author_id`, the automation itself is the author.

## Run code — `custom_code`

Runs your own code in the automation sandbox. This is the most self-contained action: no referenced entities and no external service.

```json
{
  "type": "custom_code",
  "group": "action",
  "config": {
    "code": ["const sum = 1 + 1;"]
  }
}
```

-   `code` (*required*): a *code dynamic value*, an array of literal strings mixed with variable references that pull in record data. Value references aren't allowed here. See [Dynamic values](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values). Tape also accepts a plain string and turns it into an array.
-   `custom_variable_defs` left out means the script declares no variables for later actions.

## Declare a variable — `custom_variable`

Computes a value and stores it in a declared variable that later actions can reference.

```json
{
  "type": "custom_variable",
  "group": "action",
  "config": {
    "custom_variable_defs": [{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Result" }],
    "assignment_code": ["1 + 1"]
  }
}
```

-   `custom_variable_defs`: the *declaration*. Each entry is `{ "custom_type", "label" }`. `custom_type` is one of `any`, `single_file`, `multi_file`, `single_link`, `html_table_rows`. Later actions reference the variable with `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type", "label" }`.
-   `assignment_code`: a *code dynamic value* (array) that computes the value. Tape evaluates it as one *expression*: write `1 + 1`, *not* `return 1 + 1;`. A top-level `return` fails when the automation runs. See [`custom_variable`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/custom-variable).
-   [`custom_code`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/custom-code) is different: its `code` is a block of statements. Don't use a top-level `return` there either. Tape runs the code of all actions as one script, so a `return` stops every later action.

> Why does my action save but do nothing?
> 
> With an empty or missing `custom_variable_defs`, this action still *validates and saves*. When the automation runs, Tape skips it without a per-action log. The same happens to a `for_loop` without `iterable` and to an `authenticated_http_call` without `authentication_provider_id`.

## Send an email — `send_email`

Sends one email from the automation.

```json
{
  "type": "send_email",
  "group": "action",
  "config": {
    "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "subject": ["Email from the automation"],
    "message_body": ["<p>Sent by the send_email automation action.</p>"]
  }
}
```

-   `to_address` and `subject` are *required*. `message_body` is *optional*. Without it, Tape sends the email with an empty body.
-   All three are *template dynamic values* (arrays). The HTML body comes back unchanged.
-   Without `smtp_account_id`, Tape uses the organization's *default* SMTP account. Set an ID only if you need a specific account. [`send_email`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/send-email) shows where to find it.

## Make an HTTP request — `http_call`

Sends an HTTP request from the automation sandbox.

```json
{
  "type": "http_call",
  "group": "action",
  "config": {
    "http_call_type": "get",
    "http_call_url": ["https://tapeapp.com/"]
  }
}
```

-   `http_call_type` (*required*): a lower-case enum scalar, one of `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch`, `delete`.
-   `http_call_url` (*required*): a *template dynamic value* (array), so you can put record data into the URL.
-   Requests leave from Tape's worker IP addresses and are subject to network restrictions. See [Troubleshooting › IP addresses](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18448976-automation-ip-addresses). Tape refuses private and internal hosts.

## Branch on a condition — `conditional`

A control-flow action. It runs its nested `action_rows` (the then-branch) only when `condition` is true.

```json
{
  "type": "conditional",
  "group": "control_flow",
  "config": {
    "condition": {
      "operator": "and",
      "rows": [
        { "id": "cond-leaf", "code": ["true"] }
      ]
    },
    "action_rows": [
      {
        "id": "then-1",
        "type": "custom_code",
        "group": "action",
        "config": { "code": ["const a = 1;"] }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

-   The branch structure lives *inside `config`*: `condition`, `action_rows` and the optional `else_action_rows`. Like every action, a `conditional` keeps its whole shape in `config`. See [`conditional`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/conditional).
-   `condition` is a filter group. The row above is a *script condition*, with `code` instead of `subject`, `operator` and `value`.
-   `action_rows` is the then-branch, with full nested action nodes. Add `else_action_rows` inside `config` for an else-branch. Leave it out to switch the else-branch off.

## Loop over items — `for_loop`

A control-flow action. It runs its nested `action_rows` (the loop body) once for each item of an iterable.

```json
{
  "type": "for_loop",
  "group": "control_flow",
  "config": {
    "iterable": {
      "kind": "variable",
      "source": "action",
      "action_type": "record_collection",
      "app_id": 12345
    },
    "action_rows": [
      {
        "id": "loop-body",
        "type": "custom_code",
        "group": "action",
        "config": { "code": ["const x = 1;"] }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

-   The loop lives *inside `config`*: `iterable` (what to loop over), `action_rows` (the body), and the optional `break_condition` and `continue_condition`.
-   The [`iterable`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/for-loop) is a `record_collection` from an earlier `collect_*` action, a multi-value field or a custom variable. Without an iterable, the loop body doesn't run. [The collection pattern](#collect-and-update-a-collection--collect_app_records--collected_records_update) shows how to create and reference a collection. On its own, the example doesn't validate (`action_variable_missing`): put a `collect_app_records` action before it.

## Collect and update a collection — `collect_app_records` → `collected_records_update`

The collection pattern: a *collect* action earlier in the list creates a `record_collection`, and a later action references it. Order matters. The action that creates the collection comes first.

```json
{
  "actions": [
    {
      "id": "collect",
      "type": "collect_app_records",
      "group": "action",
      "config": { "app_id": 12345 }
    },
    {
      "type": "collected_records_update",
      "group": "action",
      "config": {
        "record_collection": {
          "kind": "variable",
          "source": "action",
          "action_type": "record_collection",
          "app_id": 12345
        },
        "field_assignments": [],
        "silent": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

-   `record_collection` is an *object reference*, never a string. Tape resolves it by `action_type` and `app_id` to the nearest earlier action that creates such a collection. It doesn't name the `id` of the collect action.
-   Every action that uses a collection takes the same reference shape: `filter_record_collection`, `sort_record_collection`, `collected_records_comment_create`, the `iterable` of a `for_loop`, and so on.

# Advanced / sandbox

> The sandbox endpoints behind a Tape automation's call-automation and generate-weblink actions.

Use these endpoints to call an automation on a record or to create a weblink that runs an automation when someone selects it.

Both endpoints are the *engine behind specific automation actions*: an automation uses them during its run to call another automation or to hand out a weblink. To start an automation from your own code, use [manual-run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution#run-an-automation) instead. It works with every trigger and on a paused automation.

| Endpoint | Action behind it |
| --- | --- |
| [`POST /v1/automation/{automation_id}/trigger`](#call-an-automation) | **Call automation**: `current_record_call_automation`, `collected_records_call_automation` |
| [`POST /v1/automation/weblink/generate`](#generate-a-weblink) | **Generate weblink**: `current_record_generate_automation_weblink` |

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> Both endpoints need **Run automations** (`automations:run`). They work with a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens), an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview), a [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key) or an automation API key. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

> How do these endpoints differ from the rest of the resource?
> 
> -   They also accept an automation API key. Apart from [discovery](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery), the rest of the resource doesn't.
> -   They report a missing or unavailable automation or record as `400` (validation error), *not* with the [`404` collapse](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#the-404-collapse) of the other endpoints. Only an automation outside a personal access token's content access returns `404`.
> -   Each request costs `1x` base credits.
> -   The legacy paths `POST /v1/workflow/{automation_id}/trigger` and `POST /v1/workflow/weblink/generate` stay as *deprecated* aliases for older integrations. Use `/v1/automation/…`.

## Call an automation

Use this endpoint to run an automation on a record. The **Call automation** actions use it.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}/trigger`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/88/trigger \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{ "trigger_on_record_id": 5001 }'
```

The response is `202` with an empty body `{}`. Like [manual-run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution), the call is asynchronous and returns *no run ID*. Poll [Automation run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation-run) for the result.

**General behavior**

-   The target automation needs an [`automation_called`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers) trigger.
-   Tape applies the target's filter. A record that doesn't match creates no run.
-   `202` means Tape *accepted* the call, not that it created a run. The call still answers `202` and creates *no run* when the target doesn't fire:
    -   its trigger isn't `automation_called`,
    -   its filter rejects the record, or
    -   it's *paused or broken*. New automations start paused, so [activate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage) the target first.

**Requirements:** `automations:run`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Errors**

-   A malformed body, an automation or record that doesn't exist or that you can't access, or a record outside the automation's app returns `400`.
-   A request without a credential returns `401`.
-   A token without `automations:run` returns `403`.
-   An automation outside your personal access token's content access returns `404`.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger_on_record_id` | `integer` | yes | The record to run the automation on. |
| `triggered_by_record_id` | `integer` | no | The record that started the call. |
| `triggered_by_workflow_def_id` | `integer` | no | The automation that started the call. |
| `trigger_with_arguments` | `object` | no | Values for the automation's custom input variables, keyed by *internal variable name*. See the note below. |
| `is_manual_run` | `boolean` | no | Defaults to `false`. |
| `is_simulation` | `boolean` | no | Defaults to `false`. |

> How do I build a `trigger_with_arguments` key?
> 
> Each key is the automation's *internal variable name*. Tape builds it from the label you declared:
> 
> 1.  Lower-case the label.
> 2.  Replace every character outside `0-9`, `a-z`, `A-Z`, `_` and `$` with an underscore.
> 3.  Put `var_` in front.
> 
> Tape doesn't trim the label, so spaces at the start or end become underscores. A variable of type *file* adds `_<selected_property>` at the end.
> 
> | Declared label | Argument key |
> | --- | --- |
> | `note` | `var_note` |
> | `My Variable` | `var_my_variable` |
> | `My-Variable-2` | `var_my_variable_2` |
> | `My%Variable` | `var_my_variable` |
> | `' My variable '` (spaces at start and end) | `var__my_variable_` |
> 
> A key that matches no declared variable is *accepted without an error*: the schema is open, the variable resolves to `null` and the run goes on. If an argument seems to have no effect, check the key first.

## Generate a weblink

Use this endpoint to create a public weblink that runs a `weblink_clicked` automation on a record when someone selects it. The **Generate weblink** action uses it.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/weblink/generate`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/weblink/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "trigger_workflow_def_id": 91,
    "trigger_on_record_id": 5001,
    "expiration_type": "ONE_WEEK"
  }'
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "trigger_token": "3f2b1c94-7d6e-4a51-9b0f-2c8e5d41a7b3",
  "trigger_client_url": "https://weblink.tapeapp.com/trigger/3f2b1c94-7d6e-4a51-9b0f-2c8e5d41a7b3"
}
```

**Key fields**

-   `trigger_token`: a UUID.
-   `trigger_client_url`: `<weblink-client-base>/trigger/<trigger_token>`. The host depends on the environment, in production `https://weblink.tapeapp.com`. Treat the whole URL as *opaque*: hand it out as is, and don't build or parse it yourself.

**General behavior**

-   The response is `201`. The endpoint is *synchronous*. Only the run that a later click starts is asynchronous.
-   Send `trigger_workflow_def_id` and `trigger_on_record_id` in every request. The endpoint needs the automation to fire and the record to scope the weblink to.
-   You need view access to the record.

**Requirements:** `automations:run`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Errors**

-   A malformed body, an automation or record that doesn't exist or that you can't access, or a target that isn't a `weblink_clicked` automation returns `400`.
-   A request without a credential returns `401`.
-   A token without `automations:run` returns `403`.
-   An automation outside your personal access token's content access returns `404`.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger_workflow_def_id` | `integer` | yes | The `weblink_clicked` automation the weblink fires. |
| `trigger_on_record_id` | `integer` | yes | The record the weblink belongs to. |
| `triggered_by_record_id` | `integer` | no | The record that started the generation. |
| `triggered_by_workflow_def_id` | `integer` | no | The automation that started the generation. |
| `trigger_with_arguments` | `object` | no | Arguments the weblink carries into the run, keyed by *internal variable name*, as for [Call an automation](#call-an-automation). |
| `expiration_type` | `string` | no | One of `NEVER`, `ONE_DAY`, `ONE_WEEK`, `ONE_MONTH`, `ONE_YEAR`. |
| `expire_after_first_click` | `boolean` | no | Make the weblink invalid after its first click. |
| `is_manual_run` | `boolean` | no | Defaults to `false`. |
| `is_simulation` | `boolean` | no | Defaults to `false`. |

> Why does the action use a different expiration key?
> 
> `expiration_type` with upper-case values (`NEVER`, `ONE_DAY`, …) belongs to *this endpoint's* body. The `current_record_generate_automation_weblink` *action* uses `weblink_expiration` with *lower-case* values (`never`, `one_day`, `one_week`, `one_month`, `one_year`) and also has `on_click`. Don't copy the endpoint's key or casing into an action config.

# Discovery

> Discover the live Automation catalog — trigger types, action types, and filter operators, each with the config schema to build against.

Use these endpoints to read the live catalog of trigger types, action types and filter operators that automations are built from.

Each entry in the catalog comes with the `config` it accepts. Build against it instead of hard-coding the list: new types show up here without an API change.

**General behavior**

-   The catalog is the same for everyone. The endpoints have no workspace scope.
-   Each successful `200` response can be cached for an hour (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`).
-   Each request costs `1x` base credits.

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> All three endpoints need **Read automations** (`automations:read`). They work with a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens), an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview), a [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key) or an automation API key. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

## List trigger types

Use this endpoint to list every public trigger type with its config schema.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/meta/trigger`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/meta/trigger \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "triggers": [
    {
      "type": "record_created",
      "label": "Record created",
      "description": "Triggers when a record is created in the app.",
      "config_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {},
        "additionalProperties": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Each entry is `{ type, label, description?, config_schema }`. See the [trigger types](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers).

A `config_schema` property with `"readOnly": true` marks a field Tape sets itself, for example the `webhook_url` of a `webhook_received` trigger. Tape returns it when you read a config and rejects it on write, so remove it before you send one.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

## List action types

Use this endpoint to list every public action type with its group and config schema.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/meta/action`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/meta/action \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

The response is `200` with `{ "actions": [ … ] }`.

Each entry is `{ type, group, label, description?, config_schema }`. `group` is `action` or `control_flow`. See the [action types](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions).

**Requirements:** `automations:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

## List filter operators

Use this endpoint to list the filter operators for one *field type*. The operators differ per type.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/meta/filter?field_type={field_type}`

*Request*

```shell
curl "https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/meta/filter?field_type=number" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "field_type": "number",
  "operators": [
    { "operator": "is", "label": "Is", "value_arity": "single" },
    { "operator": "greater_than", "label": "Greater than", "value_arity": "single" },
    { "operator": "is_empty", "label": "Is empty", "value_arity": "none" }
  ]
}
```

`field_type` is required, for example `single_text` or `number`. A missing or unknown value returns `400`. [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app) returns the `field_type` of each field.

Each entry is `{ operator, label, description?, value_arity }`. See [Filters](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) for the full set of operators and the tagged value union.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

## Errors

-   [List filter operators](#list-filter-operators) without a `field_type`, or with an unknown one, returns `400`.
-   A request without a credential returns `401`.
-   A token without `automations:read` returns `403`.

See [Errors & broken reasons](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors) for the Automation API and [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Dynamic values & references

> How Tape automation values reference live record and run data — the dynamic-value array and reference model.

Use dynamic values to pull live record and run data into the config of a trigger, an action or a filter.

A *dynamic value* is an ordered *array* that mixes *literal strings* with *references*. Tape uses a literal string as is. It resolves a reference against the triggering record and the run when the automation runs.

An email subject "Hi {first name}!" looks like this:

*A dynamic value*

```json
[
  "Hi ",
  { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 42, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
  "!"
]
```

-   A value with only a literal is a one-element array: `["shipped"]`.
-   A config key with a plain scalar type, such as a number, a boolean or an ID, is *not* wrapped in an array. Only template and code keys are.
-   A config slot that holds one reference and no template takes the reference *alone*, as a bare object instead of an array: the `iterable` of a `for_loop`, the `record_collection` of a collection action, or a sort key. Example: `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 87 }`. See [Action examples](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/action-examples) for the collect and consume pattern.

## Two flavors

| Flavor | Contains | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Template** | Literals and *any* reference (variable or value) | Text and template fields, filter `text` values |
| **Code** | Literals and *variable* references only (no constant `value` references) | Number and code expressions, filter `number` values, date offsets |

## References

Every reference has a `kind`. It can also have a **`property`**, for example the `email` of a user reference or the `start_date_utc` of a date. Without `property`, the reference returns its whole default value.

### `kind: "variable"` — live data, by `source`

| `source` | Extra fields | Points to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `field` | `field_id`, `field_type`, `previous`, `collection`, `triggering` | A field's value on the record. |
| `trigger` | `trigger_type` (plus `key_path` and `data_type` for `webhook_payload_property`) | The trigger's output. |
| `action` | `action_type`, `app_id?` | The output of an earlier action. |
| `global` | `global_type` | A value for the whole automation. |
| `meta` | `meta_type`, `app_id`, `previous`, `collection`, `triggering` | Record metadata. |
| `custom` | `custom_type`, `label` | A variable you declared, or the output of `http_call`, `create_pdf`, `rollup_iterable_values` or `current_record_generate_automation_weblink`. |

To find a `field_id`, see [Find the app ID and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

**Allowed values** (the complete lists):

-   `global_type`: `current_date`, `current_datetime`, `current_time`, `current_automation`, `current_automation_run`, `actions_left_in_hour`, `most_recent_error`
-   `trigger_type`: `webhook_payload`, `webhook_payload_property`, `webhook_file_collection`, `periodic_execution_datetime`, `periodic_next_execution_datetime`, `weblink_click_count`, `weblink_created_at`, `record_comment_or_reply_id`, `record_comment_or_reply_content`, `record_comment_or_reply_created_by`, `record_comment_or_reply_attachments`, `record_comment_or_reply_entity_type`
-   `meta_type`: `record_id`, `record_url`, `app_record_id`, `revision`, `created_at`, `last_modified_at`, `created_by`, `last_modified_by`, `all_comments`
-   `action_type`: `record_collection`, `created_record`, `file_collection`
-   `custom_type`: `any`, `single_file`, `multi_file`, `single_link`, `html_table_rows`

A reference with `action_type: "created_record"`, the `app_id` of the new record and `"property": "id"` returns the ID of the record that [`record_create`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/record-create) created.

### `kind: "value"` — a fixed entity or constant, by `value_type`

| `value_type` | Extra fields | `property` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `option` | `field_id`, `option_id` | Optional |
| `user` | `user_id` | Optional |
| `record` | `record_id` | Optional |
| `pdf` | none | Required (`page_number` or `page_count`) |
| `date` | none | Required (`current_date` or `current_datetime`) |
| `time` | none | Required (`current_time`) |

## Write and read dynamic values

-   **`property` values come from the stored value.** They can look different from the label in Tape. A status option is sent as `completed`, a checklist assignee as `assign_user_formatted`.
-   **Tape doesn't check referenced IDs when you write.** A well-formed ID that doesn't exist or belongs to someone else passes here. It shows up when you [validate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) or activate. Some references and plain config IDs are only checked when the automation runs.
-   **Tape checks the *structure* of a reference when you write.** An unrecognized discriminator returns `400`: an unknown `source` on a `kind: "variable"` reference, an unknown `value_type` on a `kind: "value"` reference, or a `field` reference without `field_type`. `previous`, `collection` and `triggering` are optional on write and default to `false`.
-   **A `meta` reference needs `app_id`,** the app of the record it reads. For the current record, that's the automation's app. Tape saves a reference without `app_id`, but `validate` reports `action_variable_missing` and activation fails.
-   **`meta` references keep `previous`, `collection` and `triggering` on write,** like `field` references. A read returns these flags *only when they're `true`*, so a plain `meta` reference reads back without them. Collection actions use a collection-scoped meta reference (`collection: true`, with `app_id`). A `sort_record_collection` sort key needs one. A meta reference without `collection` fails validation there.
-   **One reference loses data in v1.** Custom variables of type `html_table_rows` don't keep their inner template when you read and write them back.
-   **Template and code members accept a plain string on write.** It's short for a one-element literal array: `"application/json"` equals `["application/json"]`. A read returns them *wrapped in an array*. This also applies to nested template members, for example each `http_call_headers[].value` and the template and code strings inside `field_assignments`. A written config doesn't come back byte for byte for these fields, so don't compare write and read.
-   **Three flags set which value a `field` reference returns:**
    -   `previous: true` reads the value *before* the triggering change.
    -   `triggering: true` points to the record that fired the trigger.
    -   `collection: true` reads the value *of each collected record* in an earlier collection, which is what collection actions use. With `false`, it reads the current record.

# Run & simulate

> Run and simulate a Tape automation against a record, and validate a definition — including the asynchronous run model.

Use these endpoints to run an automation for real, simulate it without side effects, and validate its definition.

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> Run and simulate need **Run automations** (`automations:run`), validate needs **Read automations** (`automations:read`). All three need the **Admin** role in the app's workspace and work with a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens), an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview) or a [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key). See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

## The run body is trigger-aware

Manual run and simulate share one body. Send the payload that the automation's *trigger* expects. The automation in the path already fixes the trigger, so you don't name it again.

| Trigger | Body |
| --- | --- |
| Record-based (`record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted`, `date_field_arrived`, `record_comment_or_reply_created`, `automation_called`, `weblink_clicked`) | `{ "record_id": <id> }` |
| `webhook_received` | `{ "webhook_payload": <object or string> }` *or* `{ "use_last_received_webhook_payload": true }` |
| `periodic`, or no trigger | `{}` |

A well-formed body that doesn't match the automation's *actual* trigger returns `400`.

> Does a paused automation still run?
> 
> Yes. Manual run and simulate use the automation's *stored definition, whether it's paused or not*, so you can test without setting it live. Only a *broken* definition returns `409`.
> 
> The [call automation endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/advanced) works differently: it creates *no run* for a paused target and reports no error.

> Why is there no run ID in the response?
> 
> Both endpoints queue the work for a background worker and answer `202` with a fixed message. A manual run creates its run only after the record passes the filter. A simulation skips the filter. To see the result, poll [List runs for an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation-run#list-runs-for-an-automation) and match `triggered_on_record_id` to your record. `type` tells real and simulation runs apart (`manual` or `simulation`).

> When do run logs show up?
> 
> A run's per-action `logs` arrive *after* the run reaches a final status (`completed` or `failed`). The trigger and filter steps are there from the start.
> 
> -   Poll for the *specific* log entry you need. Don't wait for `logs.length > 0`, which can return before an action's entry is in.
> -   Some successful steps write no per-action `success` entry: the control-flow containers (`conditional`, `for_loop`), `collected_records_collect_referenced_records` and `create_pdf`. For those, a final `completed` without a setup failure is the success signal.
> -   An action with `deactivate: true` writes no entry. Tape removes it before the run starts, so it's *missing* from the log, not listed as `skipped`. See [Automation run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation-run) for how the two differ and when `skipped` appears.

## Run an automation

Use this endpoint to run an automation on a record, with *real side effects*.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}/manual-run`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/manual-run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{ "record_id": 5001 }'
```

*Response*

```json
{ "message": "Use the automation-run API to poll the run. Based on queueing and limitations, this may be delayed." }
```

To find `automation_id`, see [List automations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#list-automations). In the automation editor, it's the number after `/edit-workflow/` in the address.

To check the run, follow step 3 of [Run an existing automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/overview#run-an-existing-automation).

**General behavior**

-   This is the API version of **Manual run** in the automation editor, for one record. See [Execution types](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/execution-types).
-   Tape queues the run with at-least-once delivery. One request can run the automation more than once.
-   Tape applies the filter. A record that doesn't match creates no run.
-   Each request costs `1x` base credits. A real run also uses automation *action credits*, reported as `num_consumed_actions`.
-   `record_id` must point to a *live* record in the automation's app. A deleted record, a record in another database app or an unknown ID returns `404` before Tape schedules the run.
-   To test `current_record_restore`, delete the record *within* the run: put a `current_record_delete` step before it.

> Why does my comment automation create no run?
> 
> For a `record_comment_or_reply_created` automation, a manual run uses the record's *most recent* comment or reply as the current comment. A record *without* comments or replies creates *no run*. The endpoint still answers `202`.

**Requirements:** `automations:run`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   An automation ID that isn't an integer, or a body that doesn't match the trigger, returns `400`.
-   A credential that doesn't act on behalf of a user returns `401`.
-   A token without `automations:run` returns `403`.
-   An automation or record that isn't available to you returns `404`.
-   A broken automation returns `409`.

## Simulate an automation

Use this endpoint to run the automation's stored definition as a dry run, with *no side effects*.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}/simulate`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/simulate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{ "record_id": 5001 }'
```

The response is the same `202` with `{ "message": … }` as for [Run](#run-an-automation), with no run ID.

**General behavior**

-   A simulation creates a *simulation* run every time. Most run lists leave it out. [List runs for an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation-run#list-runs-for-an-automation) shows it, and you can retrieve it by ID.
-   The body is the same as for [Run](#run-an-automation). Each request costs `1x` base credits.
-   You also need view access to the target record.

**Requirements:** `automations:run`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

The same causes as for [Run](#run-an-automation) return `400`, `401`, `403`, `404` and `409`.

## Validate an automation

Use this endpoint to check whether the current definition can run.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}/validate`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/validate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "valid": false,
  "errors": [
    { "code": "action_app_missing", "message": "An action references an app that no longer exists.", "action_id": "a1b2c3", "app_id": 42, "deactivated": false }
  ]
}
```

**Key fields**

-   `valid`: `true` when no error sits in an active part of the automation. An entry with `deactivated: true` doesn't count.
-   `errors`: one entry per fault. Each entry has the same shape and the same [broken-reason codes](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors) as `broken_reason` on the automation object.

**General behavior**

-   No request body.
-   Tape computes a fresh verdict. It can differ from the stored `broken` flag, because create and update don't store a new verdict.

> What does `validate` check?
> 
> `validate` checks *meaning*, not syntax: whether a stored definition still points to things that exist and can be reached. Typical faults are a deleted field or app, a removed connection, or an action that uses a collection no earlier action creates. These faults can appear *after* a successful save, without any change to the definition.
> 
> Payload *format* is checked earlier. Create and update reject a [malformed body](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#what-returns-400-in-a-definition-body) with `400`, for example an unknown enum value, a broken dynamic-value reference or a tree nested too deep.

> Does `valid: true` mean the run succeeds?
> 
> Not necessarily. `validate` checks the *listed* faults, and some references only for presence. For example, Tape only checks that the `app_view_id` of a `collect_app_view_records` action isn't empty, so a wrong view ID fails only when the automation *runs*.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   An automation ID that isn't an integer returns `400`.
-   A credential that doesn't act on behalf of a user returns `401`.
-   A token without `automations:read` returns `403`.
-   An automation that isn't available to you returns `404`.

# Manage automations

> Create, retrieve, list, update, replace the trigger, activate, pause, and delete Tape automations through the Developer API.

Use these endpoints to create, read, list, change, activate, pause and delete automations.

Every endpoint returns the [automation object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/object), wrapped as `{ automation }`, except the list endpoints.

> Which credential and capability do I need?
> 
> All endpoints on this page need a credential that acts on behalf of a user: a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens), an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview) or a [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key). Retrieve and list need `automations:read`, all other endpoints need `automations:edit` (see [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities)).
> 
> You need the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Automations you can't use return the same `404`. See [Authentication and permissions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/overview#authentication-and-permissions).

## Create an automation

Use this endpoint to create an automation in an app.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/app/87 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "name": "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead",
    "trigger": { "type": "record_created", "config": {} }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "name": "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead",
  "trigger": { "type": "record_created", "config": {} }
}
```

The response is `201` with the new automation.

**General behavior**

-   A new automation starts *paused and not broken*: a valid draft that you finish and then [activate](#activate-an-automation).
-   Node IDs inside `filter` and `actions` are optional. Tape creates them when you leave them out.
-   `description` and `trigger` don't accept `null` here, unlike in [update](#update-an-automation).
-   Tape checks create and update bodies against a *closed schema*. Any top-level property that isn't in the table below returns `400`. So does an unknown key inside a trigger's `config`.
-   Each action in `actions[]` needs both `type` and `config`. The `config` can be an empty `{}`. An action without a `config` key returns `400`.

> What happens to `app_id` in a trigger config?
> 
> Tape accepts a legacy `app_id` key in a trigger's `config`, checks that it's an integer (otherwise `400`) and drops it unread. The automation's app comes from the automation itself, so a wrong or unknown `app_id` has no effect. Leave it out in new integrations.

> How many automations can an app hold?
> 
> An app can hold at most 500 automations. When an app reaches this limit, Tape rejects further create requests with an error until you delete an automation.

**Requirements:** `automations:edit`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | yes | 1 to 5000 characters. |
| `description` | `string` | no | Up to 25000 characters. |
| `trigger` | `object` | no | A [trigger](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers) `{ type, config }`. |
| `filter` | `object` | no | A [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters). |
| `actions` | `array` | no | An ordered list of [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions). |

## Retrieve an automation

Use this endpoint to read one automation with its trigger, filter and actions.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

The response is `{ automation }` with its `trigger`, `filter` and `actions` inlined.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## List automations

Use these endpoints to list the automations in an app, in a workspace, or in every workspace you administer in your organization.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/app/{app_id}`

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/workspace/{workspace_id}`

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/org`

*Request*

```shell
curl "https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/app/87?limit=2" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 12,
  "automations": [ { "id": 4021, "name": "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead", "paused": false, "broken": false }  ],
  "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJI..."
}
```

Each entry is a full automation object. The example is shortened.

**General behavior**

-   The `org` variant takes the organization from your credential. It has no path scope. If you administer nothing, it returns an *empty page*, not `404`.
-   With a personal access token, the `org` variant lists only automations in apps of the token's [content access](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#content-selection). The `workspace` variant needs the whole workspace in the content access. Selected apps alone return `404` there.
-   Looking for one automation? Add `query` with part of its name.
-   Results are sorted *oldest first*, by ID.
-   `total` is a snapshot taken on the first page. `cursor` is `null` on the last page. See [Pagination](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/pagination).
-   The `cursor` is *bound to its scope*: this app, this workspace or your organization. A cursor sent to a different scope returns `400`, not an empty page. Send each cursor back only to the list call that produced it.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the workspaces you list. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cursor` | `string` | The `cursor` of the previous response. Leave it out for the first page. |
| `limit` | `integer` | Page size, `1` to `100`. Defaults to `50`. |
| `query` | `string` | Only automations whose name contains this text, ignoring case. An empty value returns `400`. Leave it out to list all. |

## Update an automation

Use this endpoint to change some fields of an automation and keep the rest.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{ "description": "Notifies the owner of new leads." }'
```

The response is `200` with the whole automation, wrapped as `{ "automation": { … } }`.

**General behavior**

-   This is a *partial update*. A field you leave out stays unchanged.
-   An explicit `null` clears `description`, `trigger` or `filter`. `name` can't be `null`.
-   `actions`, when present, *replaces the whole list*. Send `[]` to empty it.
-   Every update that changes the automation creates a new [revision](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/revisions).

> Why doesn't `broken` change when I save?
> 
> `broken` shows the last verdict Tape *stored*: create, update, `activate` and `validate` never write it, and a failed `activate` returns `409` with the object unchanged. Call [`validate`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) for a current verdict. [The automation object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/object#the-broken-flag) has the full `broken` model.

**Requirements:** `automations:edit`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Body parameters** (all optional)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | New name, 1 to 5000 characters. |
| `description` | `string` | `null` | Set, or `null` to clear. |
| `trigger` | `object` | `null` | Replace, or `null` to remove. |
| `filter` | `object` | `null` | Replace, or `null` to clear. |
| `actions` | `array` | Replace the whole list. |

## Replace the trigger

Use this endpoint to swap the trigger of an automation.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}/trigger`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/trigger \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{ "type": "record_updated", "config": {} }'
```

The response is `200` with the whole automation, wrapped as `{ "automation": { … } }`.

**General behavior**

-   The *whole body is the trigger*, `{ type, config }`.
-   It replaces any existing trigger and creates a revision.
-   To *remove* a trigger, use [update](#update-an-automation) with `trigger: null`.

**Requirements:** `automations:edit`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Activate an automation

Use this endpoint to set an automation live.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}/activate`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/activate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

The response is `200` with the whole automation, wrapped as `{ "automation": { … } }`.

**General behavior**

-   No request body.
-   Tape checks the definition again on every call. A broken definition returns `409`. Use `validate` to see the reasons.
-   Activating an automation that is already live succeeds and changes nothing, as long as the definition stays valid.

**Requirements:** `automations:edit`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Pause an automation

Use this endpoint to stop the trigger from firing an automation.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}/pause`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/pause \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

The response is `200` with the whole automation, wrapped as `{ "automation": { … } }`.

**General behavior**

-   No request body.
-   Pausing twice changes nothing. A broken definition never blocks a pause.

**Requirements:** `automations:edit`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Delete an automation

Use this endpoint to delete an automation.

`DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

**General behavior**

-   This is a *soft delete*, the same as in Tape. The automation drops out of every list and can't be retrieved, but the data stays.
-   The response is `200` with the final, soft-deleted automation as confirmation, not `204`.

**Requirements:** `automations:edit`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Rate limit credits

The three *list* endpoints cost `2x` base credits. Every other endpoint on this page costs `1x`. See [Request limits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits).

## Errors

-   A body with a property the schema doesn't know, an action without `config`, a path ID that isn't an integer, or a `cursor` sent to another scope returns `400`.
-   A credential that doesn't act on behalf of a user, for example an automation API key, returns `401`.
-   A token without `automations:read` or `automations:edit` returns `403`.
-   An automation, app or workspace that isn't available to you returns `404`. This includes automations in workspaces you don't administer and apps outside your personal access token's content access.
-   [Activating](#activate-an-automation) a broken automation returns `409`.

See [Errors & broken reasons](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors) for the Automation API and [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Automation

> The Tape Automation API — discover the catalog, then create, version, validate, and run automations (a trigger, an optional filter, and ordered actions) scoped to an app.

Use the Automation API to build, version, check and run automations in Tape through code.

Only want to start an automation that already exists in Tape? You build nothing: [find its ID and run it](#run-an-existing-automation).

An *automation* has a *trigger* that starts it, an optional *filter* that decides whether it goes on, and ordered *actions* that do the work. Each automation belongs to one [app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app).

With this API you can:

-   Discover what an automation can be built from.
-   Create, update and version automations.
-   Validate an automation.
-   Run or simulate an automation on a record.

This API manages the *definitions*. Each time an automation fires, Tape creates an [automation run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation-run), which you read through its own endpoints.

Writing JavaScript inside an automation? See [Automations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/introduction#execution-environment) for script filters, **Perform a calculation** and **Execute a script**.

## Working with automations

| Page | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| [Quickstart](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/quickstart) | The whole lifecycle end to end: discover, create, configure, validate, activate, run, observe. |
| [Discovery](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) | The catalog of trigger, action and filter types, with their config schemas. |
| [Manage](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage) | Create, retrieve, list, update, replace the trigger, activate, pause and delete. |
| [Revisions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/revisions) | The version history of an automation. |
| [Run & simulate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) | Run and simulate on a record, and validate a definition. |
| [Advanced / sandbox](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/advanced) | The call automation and generate weblink endpoints behind those actions. |
| [Dynamic values](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | How values reference live record and run data. |
| Reference: [object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/object) · [triggers](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers) · [filters](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) · [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions) · [errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors) | The full object, the lists of types and the error codes. |

## Run an existing automation

Start an automation that someone already built in Tape. You need the **Admin** role in the app's workspace and a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) with the capabilities **Read automations** (`automations:read`) and **Run automations** (`automations:run`).

**1\. Find the automation ID.** List the automations you administer. `query` keeps those whose name contains the text, ignoring case.

*Request*

```shell
curl "https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/org?query=lead" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 1,
  "automations": [ { "id": 4021, "app_id": 87, "name": "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead", "paused": false, "broken": false } ],
  "cursor": null
}
```

Each entry is a full automation object. The example is shortened. Keep the `id`.

Have the automation open in Tape? Its ID is the number after `/edit-workflow/` in the address.

**2\. Run it on a record.** The record must be in the automation's app.

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/manual-run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{ "record_id": 5001 }'
```

*Response*

```json
{ "message": "Use the automation-run API to poll the run. Based on queueing and limitations, this may be delayed." }
```

The response is `202` with no run ID. The run has real side effects. [The run body depends on the trigger](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution#the-run-body-is-trigger-aware).

**3\. Check the run.** List the runs of the automation and find the one with your `triggered_on_record_id`.

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/automation/4021 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{ "limit": 5 }'
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 1,
  "automation_runs": [ { "id": "9001", "automation_id": 4021, "status": "completed", "type": "manual", "triggered_on_record_id": 5001 } ],
  "cursor": null
}
```

The example is shortened. `status` is `pending` or `running` while the run works, then `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`. [Retrieve the run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation-run#retrieve-an-automation-run) by its `id` to read the step logs.

> Does the automation have to be live?
> 
> No, a manual run also starts a paused automation. Only a broken one returns `409`. To test without side effects, [simulate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution#simulate-an-automation) it.

> Want another system to start the automation without a token?
> 
> Give the automation a **Webhook received** trigger and send a `POST` to its webhook URL. [Retrieve the automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#retrieve-an-automation) to read it from `trigger.config.webhook_url`. See [Connect Google Forms to Tape](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18449044-save-form-responses-with-a-webhook).

## The anatomy of an automation

| Part | Cardinality | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Trigger** | 0 or 1 | The event that starts the automation: a record is created, a date arrives, a schedule fires, a webhook comes in, and so on. See [Triggers](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers). |
| **Filter** | 0 or 1 | A recursive `and`/`or` tree of conditions the triggering record must match. Omitted or `null` means the automation runs every time. See [Filters](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters). |
| **Actions** | 0 or more | An ordered list of steps: send an email, create a record, branch, loop, and so on. See [The action object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#the-action-object). |

The discovery endpoints serve the live *catalog* of trigger types, action types and filter operators, with the exact `config` each one accepts. Build against it instead of hard-coding the list: new types show up there without an API change.

> Coming from Podio?
> 
> A Podio flow or a Globiflow flow becomes an automation. Field references use the `field_id`, not the `external_id`. See [Move your flows](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/coming-from-podio#move-your-flows) for the trigger and action of each flow step.

## Authentication and permissions

> Which credential and capability do I need?
> 
> Every endpoint on this resource needs a credential that acts on behalf of a user: a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens), an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview) or a [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key). A token also needs the matching capability from the table below. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

| Capability | Endpoints |
| --- | --- |
| `automations:read` | Discovery, retrieve, list, revisions, validate |
| `automations:edit` | Create, update, replace the trigger, activate, pause, delete |
| `automations:run` | Run, simulate, and the two [Advanced / sandbox](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/advanced) endpoints |

For the endpoints on Manage, Revisions and Run & simulate, you need the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. That workspace must be in your own organization. A personal access token also needs the app in its [content access](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#content-selection).

> Can I use an automation API key?
> 
> Only on the [discovery endpoints](#discovery-is-the-exception) and the two Advanced / sandbox endpoints (call automation and generate weblink). Everywhere else it returns `401`, because an [automation API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication) authenticates an automation, not a person. The error message names only the user API key (`Automations can only be retrieved with a user API key.`), but a personal access token or an OAuth access token works too.

#### Discovery is the exception

The three discovery endpoints (`meta/trigger`, `meta/action`, `meta/filter`) return a *static catalog* that is the same for everyone. They have no workspace scope. A token still needs `automations:read`.

#### Unavailable automations return `404`

Tape IDs are unique across all organizations. Every automation you can't use returns the same `404`, so the API never reveals which IDs exist. That covers an automation that doesn't exist, was deleted, is an unsaved draft, is in a workspace you don't administer, or is outside your personal access token's content access.

## The automation object

[The automation object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/object) lists every property with an example. [Triggers](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers), [Filters](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) and [Actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#the-action-object) describe each part.

Config values can pull in live record data through [dynamic values](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values).

The object page also explains the `broken` flag. [Errors & broken reasons](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors) lists every code in `broken_reason`.

## Status and lifecycle

An automation has no single `status` field. Its state is the pair of booleans `paused` and `broken`:

| `paused` | `broken` | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `false` | `false` | **Live.** The automation runs when its trigger fires. |
| `true` | `false` | **Paused.** A valid automation that its trigger doesn't fire. You can still run or simulate it manually. |
| any | `true` | **Broken.** The definition can't run, so it doesn't. |

-   A new automation starts *paused* and not broken: a valid draft that you set up and then activate.
-   **Activate** checks the definition again and refuses a broken one with `409`. **Pause** succeeds every time.
-   Every change creates a new, unchangeable [revision](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/revisions).

## Identifiers and timestamps

Most IDs on this resource are plain JSON *integers*: `id`, `app_id`, `workspace_id`, and the `automation_id` in a path. Two are *strings*:

-   A revision ID is a 64-bit value, returned as a string so any language can handle it safely.
-   Action `id`s are opaque. Treat them as handles, not numbers.

All timestamps use the Tape API datetime format `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, with no `T` separator, no `Z` suffix and no milliseconds. A plain timestamp such as `created_at` is in your timezone, and its `_utc` twin holds the same instant in UTC. See [Date & timezone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone).

## Rate limit credits

| Endpoints | Cost |
| --- | --- |
| The list endpoints (app, workspace, organization) | `2x` base credits |
| Everything else: discovery, retrieve, create, update, lifecycle, revisions, validate, run, simulate | `1x` base credits |

These [request credits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits) are separate from the automation *action credits* that a real run uses and reports as `num_consumed_actions`. Runtime limits, such as the cap on actions per run, the cap of 1000 records per collection and the shared email quota, are on [Limits and throttling](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/limitations).

## Errors

Errors use the standard envelope: `status_code`, `endpoint`, `error_code` and `error_message`. On this resource:

-   A malformed body, a path ID that isn't an integer, or a run body that doesn't match the trigger returns `400`.
-   A credential that doesn't act on behalf of a user, where the endpoint needs one, returns `401`.
-   A token without the capability the endpoint needs returns `403`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   An automation, app, workspace, revision or record that isn't available to you returns `404`. See [Unavailable automations return `404`](#unavailable-automations-return-404).
-   Activating, running or simulating a broken automation returns `409`.

See [Errors & broken reasons](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors) for the Automation API and [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

## Next steps

# Automation API quickstart

> Build a Tape automation end to end with copy-paste API calls — discover, create, configure, validate, activate, run, and observe.

Use this quickstart to build your first automation through the API, from the catalog to a finished run.

You go through the full lifecycle: *discover → create → configure → validate → activate → run → observe*. The example builds an automation that sends an email when a new high-priority lead comes in.

Only want to start an automation that already exists? Skip this guide and see [Run an existing automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/overview#run-an-existing-automation).

**Requirements**

-   A [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) with the capabilities **Read automations**, **Edit automations** and **Run automations** (`automations:read`, `automations:edit` and `automations:run`). Store it in the variable `TAPE_TOKEN`. A [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key) or an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview) works too.
-   The **Admin** role in the app's workspace. The token's [content access](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#content-selection) must include the app.

## Step 1: Discover the vocabulary

Read which triggers, actions and filter operators exist. Don't hard-code them.

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/meta/trigger \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

Do the same for [`/meta/action` and `/meta/filter?field_type=number`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery). Trigger and action entries have a `config_schema` to build against. A `/meta/filter` entry is an operator, `{ operator, label, description?, value_arity }`, without one.

## Step 2: Create the automation

Create the automation in an app. A new automation starts *paused* and not broken: a draft that you finish and then activate.

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/app/87 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "name": "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead",
    "trigger": { "type": "record_created", "config": {} }
  }'
```

Replace `87` with the ID of your app. [Retrieve all available apps](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-all-available-apps) lists the app IDs.

The response is the [automation object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/object), wrapped as `{ "automation": … }`. Keep its `id` for the next steps.

## Step 3: Configure the filter and actions

Add a [filter](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) and [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions) with a partial [update](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage). Fields you leave out stay unchanged.

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "filter": {
      "operator": "and",
      "rows": [
        {
          "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 512, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
          "operator": "is_any_of",
          "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [9001] }
        }
      ]
    },
    "actions": [
      { "type": "send_email", "config": { "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"], "subject": ["A new high-priority lead was created"] } }
    ]
  }'
```

Replace `4021` with the `id` from step 2, `512` with a [category field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/category) of your app and `9001` with the ID of one of its options. [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app) returns the `field_id` and, in `config.settings.options`, the option IDs. To send the email for every new record, leave out `filter`.

Node IDs are optional: Tape creates them when you leave them out. The field reference in `subject` is a [dynamic value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) that pulls in live record data.

## Step 4: Validate

Check the definition before it goes live. Create and update don't store a new verdict, so `broken` can lag behind your edit.

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/validate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

`{ "valid": true, "errors": [] }` means it's ready. Otherwise each entry names the fault. See [Errors & broken reasons](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors).

## Step 5: Activate

Set the automation live. Tape checks the definition again and refuses a broken one with `409`.

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/activate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

From now on, every new record that matches the filter fires the automation. [Pause](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#pause-an-automation) it when you finish testing.

## Step 6: Run and observe

Run the automation manually on a record, then poll for the result. A manual run has real side effects. It runs *asynchronously*: the response is `202` with a message and *no run ID*.

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/manual-run \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{ "record_id": 5001 }'
```

Replace `5001` with the ID of a record in the automation's app that matches the filter. A record that doesn't match creates no run. [Retrieve records for an app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-records-for-an-app) lists the record IDs. Then list the automation's runs and find the one with your `triggered_on_record_id`:

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation-run/automation/4021 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{ "limit": 5 }'
```

Its `status` ends as `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`. See [List runs for an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation-run#list-runs-for-an-automation) for the response, and [Run & simulate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) for the run body per trigger and the polling model.

A `failed` run names the cause in `failure_reason` and `error_message`. [Retrieve the run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation-run#retrieve-an-automation-run) by its `id` to read the step logs.

> Want to test without sending the email?
> 
> Send the same request to `/v1/automation/4021/simulate` instead of `/manual-run`. Tape creates a run with `type: "simulation"` and no side effects. Its filter step reads `skipped`. The email step reads `success`, and its log message says that Tape skipped the email because of the simulation. See [Simulate an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution#simulate-an-automation).
