# Actions

> The 35 Tape automation action types, grouped by family, each with its label and where to read its config schema.

Use actions to define *what* an automation does.

An automation's actions are an ordered list of steps: leaf steps (`group: "action"`) and *control-flow* actions (`group: "control_flow"`) that nest more actions.

## The action object

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Opaque node ID. Optional on input, Tape creates one when you leave it out. Present on every read. |
| `type` | `string` | The action type. See [Action types](#action-types). |
| `group` | `string` | `action` or `control_flow`. Follows from `type` and is read-only. You can leave it out on input. |
| `custom_name` | `string` | Optional label. Absent when not set. |
| `deactivate` | `boolean` | Whether the step is skipped. Absent when not set. |
| `continue_on_error` | `boolean` | Whether the run goes on when this step fails. Absent when not set. |
| `config` | `object` | The step's settings, keyed as the action's `config_schema` describes. Required on every action you write through the API. An empty `{}` is valid for a step you haven't set up yet, unless the type's `config_schema` requires members, for example `code` for `custom_code` or `exit_type` for `exit`. Such a config and a missing `config` key return `400`. [Dynamic values](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) inside use the reference model. |
| *(control-flow `config`)* |  | For `conditional` and `for_loop`, `config` holds the branch and loop structure. See [Control-flow actions](#control-flow-actions). |

### Write and read a config

`config` keys come from the action's `config_schema` on [`meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery), but a written `config` doesn't read back byte for byte.

-   **Tape fills in defaults for missing members on read.** A missing `match_condition` or `attach_files_match_condition` reads back as an empty filter group or `null`, missing required arrays (`ref_collection_defs`, `field_assignments`, `call_arguments`, `http_call_headers`, `sorts`) as `[]`. The exception is `field_assignments` of `record_create`: left out, it stays out on read. An unchanged `GET` → `PUT` still works, but don't compare write and read.
-   **`field_assignments` is a typed union per field type.** It's the payload of every action that changes records (`record_create`, `current_record_update`, `referenced_records_update`, `collected_records_update`) and is told apart by `field_type`. The `meta/action` schema describes its array items only loosely, so copy the filled assignments from [`record_create`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/record-create) or [`current_record_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-update). An empty `[]` is accepted in every case and changes no field value.
-   **A paired `_enabled` flag controls `limit`.** In `collect_app_records` and `collect_app_view_records`, `limit` only takes effect when `limit_enabled` is `true`, so send both. Either way, a collect stops at the server maximum of 1000 records and cuts off the rest without an error when the automation runs. See [Limits and throttling](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/limitations). The `_enabled` flags for `triggering_app_ids` and `custom_variable_defs` belong to the *trigger* config, not the action config.
-   **A condition inside `config`**, for example the `match_condition` of a collect or filter action, uses the *same public [filter tree](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters)* as the `condition` of a `conditional`: lower-case `operator: "and" | "or"` with `rows`.
-   **Passing `config_schema` checks only the structure.** A config that passes the schema is *saved*. Rules that depend on meaning show up later as [broken-reason codes](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors) when you [validate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) or activate. Examples: the `app_id` of `referenced_records_update` must be an app that the trigger app relates to, and a sort key must be scoped to the collection.
-   **All config enum values are lower-case.** Send them exactly as `meta/action` lists them, for example `http_call_type: "post"`, `exit_type: "success"`, `ref_collection_defs[].direction: "incoming"`, `match_type: "all"`.

Stricter config shapes per type may follow. Read the keys from `meta/action`, and don't hard-code internal encodings.

## Action types

There are 35 action types: 33 leaf actions (`group: "action"`) and 2 control-flow actions (`group: "control_flow"`).

-   Each type's `config` keys come from its `config_schema` on [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery).
-   The labels and descriptions below follow that endpoint. The automation editor can name an action differently. Each action page gives its editor name.
-   The families only help you read the list. An action's real grouping is its `group` field.

### Code & variables

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`custom_code`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/custom-code) | **Run code**: runs custom code in the automation sandbox. |
| [`custom_variable`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/custom-variable) | **Set variable**: computes and stores a custom variable for later actions. |

### Current record

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`record_create`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/record-create) | **Create record**: creates a record in a database app. |
| [`current_record_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-update) | **Update record**: updates the current record. |
| [`current_record_delete`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-delete) | **Delete record**: deletes the current record. |
| [`current_record_restore`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-restore) | **Restore record**: restores the current (soft-deleted) record. |
| [`current_record_get_previous_revision`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-get-previous-revision) | **Get previous revision**: loads the previous revision of the current record. |
| [`current_record_comment_create`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-comment-create) | **Add comment**: adds a comment to the current record. |
| [`current_record_comment_or_reply_reply_create`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-comment-or-reply-reply-create) | **Add reply**: adds a reply to the current comment or reply. |
| [`current_record_comment_or_reply_delete`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-comment-or-reply-delete) | **Delete comment or reply**: deletes the current comment or reply. |

### Record collections

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records) | **Collect app records**: collects records from a database app, optionally filtered. |
| [`collect_app_view_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-view-records) | **Collect app view records**: collects records from a view of a database app. |
| [`collect_referenced_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-referenced-records) | **Collect referenced records**: collects records referenced by the current record. |
| [`collected_records_collect_referenced_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collected-records-collect-referenced-records) | **Collect referenced records (from collection)**: collects records referenced by a starting record collection. |
| [`filter_record_collection`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/filter-record-collection) | **Filter collection**: filters a record collection. |
| [`sort_record_collection`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/sort-record-collection) | **Sort collection**: sorts a record collection. |
| [`clear_record_collection`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/clear-record-collection) | **Clear collection**: empties a record collection. |
| [`collected_records_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collected-records-update) | **Update collected records**: updates every record in a collection. |
| [`referenced_records_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/referenced-records-update) | **Update referenced records**: updates records referenced by the current record. |
| [`collected_records_comment_create`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collected-records-comment-create) | **Comment on collected records**: adds a comment to every record in a collection. |
| [`rollup_iterable_values`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/rollup-iterable-values) | **Roll up values**: aggregates the values of an iterable (count, sum, average, …). |

Most of these actions work in pairs: one creates a collection, a later one uses it.

-   A `collect_*` action creates a `record_collection`.
-   A later action uses it: `filter_record_collection`, `sort_record_collection`, `clear_record_collection`, the `collected_records_*` family, or the `iterable` of a `for_loop`.
-   The action that creates the collection must come *first* in the automation.
-   The later action references the collection with an object, `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": … }`. Tape resolves it to the *nearest earlier action* that creates such a collection. It never names that action's `id`.
-   An action that uses a collection without a matching earlier action fails validation.

### Automation calls & weblinks

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`current_record_call_automation`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-call-automation) | **Call automation**: calls another automation with the current record. |
| [`collected_records_call_automation`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collected-records-call-automation) | **Call automation for collected records**: calls another automation for every record in a collection. |
| [`current_record_generate_automation_weblink`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-generate-automation-weblink) | **Generate weblink**: generates a weblink that calls an automation with the current record. |
| [`display_webpage`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/display-webpage) | **Display webpage**: displays a webpage in a weblink flow. |
| [`redirect_user`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/redirect-user) | **Redirect user**: redirects the user to a URL in a weblink flow. |

The call and weblink actions reference a target automation by ID. The target must *exist*, be in the *right database app* and have the matching trigger. Otherwise the definition fails validation.

-   `current_record_call_automation` needs a target with `automation_called` in the same database app as the trigger.
-   `collected_records_call_automation` needs a target with `automation_called` in the database app of its `record_collection`. Without `record_collection`, validation reports `action_invalid` and `action_automation_invalid`.
-   `current_record_generate_automation_weblink` needs a target with `weblink_clicked` in the same database app as the trigger. The action itself runs with any trigger that has a record. See [Trigger context](#trigger-context).

A *paused* target is a valid reference, but a call to it creates no run. See [Call an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/advanced#call-an-automation).

### Email & documents

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`send_email`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/send-email) | **Send email**: sends an email. |
| [`collected_records_send_email`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collected-records-send-email) | **Send email for collected records**: sends an email for every record in a collection. |
| [`create_pdf`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/create-pdf) | **Create PDF**: renders an HTML template to a PDF file. |

### HTTP requests

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`http_call`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/http-call) | **HTTP request**: makes an outbound HTTP request. |
| [`authenticated_http_call`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/authenticated-http-call) | **Authenticated HTTP request**: makes an outbound HTTP request signed by an authentication provider. |

-   Outbound requests have [SSRF protection](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18448976-automation-ip-addresses). Tape refuses hosts that resolve to private or internal addresses.
-   `authenticated_http_call` also needs an `authentication_provider_id`. The public API has *no endpoint to create or list connections*. An organization admin sets them up in Tape. You can *define* the action through the API, but without a valid provider ID, Tape skips it when the automation runs.

### Flow control

| Action | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| [`delay`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/delay) | **Delay**: pauses the automation for a fixed duration. |
| [`exit`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/exit) | **Exit**: ends the automation run with success or failure. |
| [`for_loop`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/for-loop) | **For loop**: runs nested actions for each item of an iterable. `group: "control_flow"`. |
| [`conditional`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/conditional) | **Condition**: runs nested actions only when a condition holds. `group: "control_flow"`. |

### Trigger context

Some actions are only valid with a matching trigger. A wrong pairing fails validation with `action_invalid`, unless the row says otherwise.

| Action(s) | Requires trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `display_webpage` | `weblink_clicked` |
| `redirect_user` | `weblink_clicked`. Validation doesn't check this pairing. The editor offers the action only there. |
| `current_record_comment_or_reply_reply_create`, `current_record_comment_or_reply_delete` | `record_comment_or_reply_created` |
| `current_record_*` (update, delete, restore, get\_previous\_revision, comment\_create, call\_automation, generate\_automation\_weblink), `collect_referenced_records` | Any trigger *with a record* (not `periodic` or `webhook_received` without a record) |
| `referenced_records_update` | Any trigger *with a record*. Validation doesn't check the trigger, only `app_id`: without it `action_app_missing`, without a relation to the trigger's database app `action_app_invalid`. Without a current record, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. |

Triggers with a record are `record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted`, `record_comment_or_reply_created`, `date_field_arrived`, `automation_called` and `weblink_clicked`.

## Control-flow actions

`conditional` and `for_loop` keep their whole structure *inside `config`*, like every other action. There are no top-level control-flow fields.

-   Each branch or condition is switched on by *presence*. A member you leave out is off.
-   A nested body is an array of actions in `action_rows`.

**`conditional`**: `config` keys

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | The branch condition. `null` or left out means true in every case. |
| `action_rows` | array of [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions) | The if/then branch. |
| `else_action_rows` | array of [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions) | The else branch. Leave it out to switch it off. |

**`for_loop`**: `config` keys

| Key | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `iterable` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | The collection to loop over. The public name is `iterable`; the internal name is `iterable_variable_def`. |
| `action_rows` | array of [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions) | The loop body. |
| `break_condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | Stops the loop when it matches. Leave it out to switch it off. |
| `continue_condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | Skips to the next item when it matches. Leave it out to switch it off. |

See [`conditional`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/conditional) and [`for_loop`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/for-loop) for full config examples.

## Coming from Podio

Find the Tape action for each step of a Podio flow or a Globiflow flow.

| Podio flow or Globiflow step | Tape action |
| --- | --- |
| Create item | [`record_create`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/record-create) |
| `item.update`, update item | [`current_record_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-update), [`referenced_records_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/referenced-records-update), [`collected_records_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collected-records-update) |
| `comment.create`, comment | [`current_record_comment_create`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-comment-create) |
| Send email | [`send_email`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/send-email) |
| Wait | [`delay`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/delay), 15, 30, 45 or 60 seconds |
| Call flow | [`current_record_call_automation`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-call-automation) |
| Webhook call, `octoblu.trigger` | [`http_call`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/http-call) |
| Generate PDF | [`create_pdf`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/create-pdf) |
| Search items, loop | [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records), [`for_loop`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/for-loop) |
| `task.create`, `status.create` | No action. Use a checklist field instead of tasks. |

# authenticated_http_call

> Config reference for the Tape automation authenticated_http_call action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to send an HTTP request through an OAuth 2.0 connection and keep the response for later actions.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Send an API request** in the [HTTP requests](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#http-requests) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

When a deal is won, this action sends the deal to a sales system through a connection and saves the response:

```json
{
  "type": "authenticated_http_call",
  "config": {
    "http_call_type": "post",
    "http_call_url": ["https://crm.acme.com/api/v2/deals"],
    "http_call_headers": [
      { "key": "Content-Type", "value": ["application/json"] }
    ],
    "http_call_body": ["{\"deal\": \"", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }, "\", \"stage\": \"won\"}"],
    "http_call_follow_redirects": false,
    "authentication_provider_id": 44,
    "custom_variable_defs": [
      { "custom_type": "any", "label": "API response" }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `http_call_type` | enum | **Required.** HTTP method: `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` or `delete`. | `"post"` |
| `http_call_url` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** Request URL. | `["https://crm.acme.com/api/v2/deals"]` |
| `authentication_provider_id` | integer | ID of the connection that signs the request. Optional in the schema, but without it Tape skips the action when the automation runs. | `44` |
| `http_call_body` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Request body. Empty when left out. | `["{\"stage\": \"won\"}"]` |
| `http_call_headers` | array of headers | Request headers. Each entry is `{ "key", "value" }`, both required, with an optional `id`. Empty when left out. | `[]` |
| `http_call_follow_redirects` | boolean | Follows `3xx` redirects. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `custom_variable_defs` | array of variable declarations | Variables this action declares. Empty when left out. | `[{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "API response" }]` |

The headers and `custom_variable_defs` work the same way as in [`http_call`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/http-call#headers).

## Connections

In the editor, the connection is the **Connection** field of the action. It's an OAuth 2.0 connection that an organization admin sets up in Tape.

-   The public API has *no endpoint to create or list connections*.
-   To find `authentication_provider_id`, select the connection in this action in the automation editor, then [retrieve the automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#retrieve-an-automation).
-   You can define the action through the API without a valid ID. Tape saves it, and validation doesn't report it. When the automation runs, Tape skips the action without a per-action log.

## Use the response in a later action

Tape stores the response body in the first variable of `custom_variable_defs`. A later action reads it with a `custom` reference that has the same `custom_type` and `label`:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "API response" }
```

Without a declared variable, Tape sends the request and keeps no response. The editor declares one variable called **API response**.

## General behavior

-   `http_call_type` and `http_call_url` are required. Neither has a default.
-   Every other key except `authentication_provider_id` has a default: an empty body, no headers, no redirects and no declared variables.
-   With an empty `http_call_url`, Tape skips the action when the automation runs.
-   Outbound requests have [SSRF protection](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18448976-automation-ip-addresses). Tape refuses hosts that resolve to private or internal addresses.
-   Each header needs `key` and `value`. Send `""` or `[]` for a blank value.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An organization admin has set up the connection in Tape.

# clear_record_collection

> Config reference for the Tape automation clear_record_collection action, with its config key and an example.

Use this action to empty a record collection from an earlier action.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Clear collected records** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger but needs an earlier action that creates the record collection.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

An earlier action collected job candidates from database app `100`. This action empties that collection:

```json
{
  "type": "clear_record_collection",
  "config": {
    "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 100 }
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_collection` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The collection to empty, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_invalid`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 100 }` |

## General behavior

-   `record_collection` is the only key. It has no default.
-   Without `record_collection`, Tape saves the action, and validation reports `action_invalid`.
-   A `record_collection` without a matching earlier action fails validation with `action_variable_missing`.
-   Reference a collection from a collect action, not a single field value.
-   Later actions that reference the same collection get an empty list.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in `record_collection`, for example [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records).

# collect_app_records

> Config reference for the Tape automation collect_app_records action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to collect records from a database app into a record collection that later actions can use.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Search for records** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action collects up to 100 listings whose **Address** field isn't empty:

```json
{
  "type": "collect_app_records",
  "config": {
    "app_id": 4821,
    "match_condition": {
      "operator": "and",
      "rows": [
        {
          "subject": {
            "kind": "variable",
            "source": "field",
            "field_id": 55012,
            "field_type": "single_text",
            "previous": false,
            "collection": false,
            "triggering": false
          },
          "operator": "is_not_empty"
        }
      ]
    },
    "limit": 100,
    "limit_enabled": true
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | integer | ID of the database app to collect records from. Without it, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. | `4821` |
| `match_condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | Filters the records to collect. Left out, Tape collects every record of the database app. A filter that matches everything reads back as `null`. | `null` |
| `limit` | integer | Maximum number of records to collect. Takes effect only when `limit_enabled` is `true`. Default `1`. | `100` |
| `limit_enabled` | boolean | Whether Tape applies `limit`. Default `false`. | `true` |

To find `app_id` and the field IDs for `match_condition`, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

## Use the collection in later actions

This action creates a `record_collection` for the database app in `app_id`. A later action references it with this object:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 4821 }
```

-   Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same `app_id`.
-   Use it in `filter_record_collection`, `sort_record_collection`, `clear_record_collection`, the `collected_records_*` actions and the `iterable` of a `for_loop`.
-   See [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) for the pattern.

## General behavior

-   Every key is optional when you save. Tape fills in the defaults.
-   Every collect stops at 1000 records when the automation runs, with or without `limit_enabled`.
-   Tape stores a `limit` above 1000 and reads it back unchanged. Neither the write nor `validate` warns. See [Limits and throttling](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/limitations).
-   Without `app_id`, the action saves and passes validation. When the automation runs, Tape skips it.
-   An `app_id` of a deleted app fails validation with `action_app_missing`. An `app_id` that never existed makes `validate` and activate return `404`. See [Errors & broken reasons](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors).

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

## Next steps

# collect_app_view_records

> Config reference for the Tape automation collect_app_view_records action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to collect the records of a view into a record collection that later actions can use.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Get records of a view** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action collects up to 100 records from an **Open deals** view:

```json
{
  "type": "collect_app_view_records",
  "config": {
    "app_id": 4201,
    "app_view_id": 9317,
    "limit": 100,
    "limit_enabled": true
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | integer | ID of the database app the view belongs to. Without it, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. | `4201` |
| `app_view_id` | integer | **Required.** ID of the view to collect records from. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_view_missing`. | `9317` |
| `limit` | integer | Maximum number of records to collect. Takes effect only when `limit_enabled` is `true`. Default `1`, like a new action in the editor. | `100` |
| `limit_enabled` | boolean | Whether Tape applies `limit`. Default `false`. | `true` |

To find `app_id`, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids). To find `app_view_id`, see [Retrieve views for an app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-views-for-an-app). It returns the ID of each public view as `view_id`.

## Use the collection in later actions

This action creates a `record_collection` for the database app in `app_id`. A later action references it with this object:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 4201 }
```

-   Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same `app_id`.
-   Use it in `filter_record_collection`, `sort_record_collection`, `clear_record_collection`, the `collected_records_*` actions and the `iterable` of a `for_loop`.
-   See [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) for the pattern.

## General behavior

-   Tape collects the records that the view returns, with the view's own filters.
-   Validation checks `app_view_id` for presence only. A view ID that doesn't exist passes validation and fails when the automation runs.
-   Without `app_id`, the action saves and passes validation. When the automation runs, Tape skips it.
-   An `app_id` of a deleted app fails validation with `action_app_missing`. An `app_id` that never existed makes `validate` and activate return `404`.
-   Without `limit` and `limit_enabled`, Tape fills in the defaults.
-   Every collect stops at 1000 records when the automation runs, with or without `limit_enabled`.
-   Tape stores a `limit` above 1000, or one with `limit_enabled: false`, and reads it back unchanged. Neither the write nor `validate` warns. See [Limits and throttling](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/limitations).

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The view in `app_view_id` must exist in the database app in `app_id`.

# collect_referenced_records

> Config reference for the Tape automation collect_referenced_records action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to collect the records that the current record relates to, by following its relation fields.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Get related records for the current record** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it needs a trigger with a record: `record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted`, `record_comment_or_reply_created`, `date_field_arrived`, `automation_called` or `weblink_clicked`. The current record is the record that the automation runs on.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

Starting from a project, this action collects the open tasks that the project's **Tasks** relation field points to:

```json
{
  "type": "collect_referenced_records",
  "config": {
    "ref_collection_defs": [
      {
        "direction": "outgoing",
        "match_type": "filtered",
        "app_id": 1204,
        "via_field_ids": [88123],
        "match_condition": {
          "operator": "and",
          "rows": [
            {
              "subject": {
                "kind": "variable",
                "source": "field",
                "field_id": 88140,
                "field_type": "single_category",
                "previous": false,
                "collection": false,
                "triggering": false
              },
              "operator": "is_any_of",
              "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [3] }
            }
          ]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ref_collection_defs` | array of [reference steps](#reference-steps) | The steps that Tape follows from the current record. Empty when left out, and then the action collects nothing. | `[{ "direction": "outgoing", "match_type": "all", "app_id": 1204 }]` |

To find `app_id` and the relation field IDs for `via_field_ids`, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids). To find the option IDs for `ids`, see [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app). It returns them in `config.settings.options` of the field.

### Reference steps

Each entry in `ref_collection_defs` is one step along the relations:

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `direction` | enum | **Required.** Which relations to follow. See [Directions](#directions). | `"outgoing"` |
| `match_type` | enum | **Required.** `all` keeps every related record. `filtered` keeps only the records that match `match_condition`. | `"filtered"` |
| `app_id` | integer | **Required.** ID of the related database app to collect from. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_app_missing`. | `1204` |
| `via_field_ids` | array of integers | The relation fields to follow. Left out, Tape follows every relation field to that database app. | `[88123]` |
| `match_condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | Filters the related records in the `filtered` mode. Ignored with `match_type: "all"`. An empty AND group when left out, read back as `null`. | `null` |
| `id` | string | Stable ID of the step. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. | `"step-1"` |

### Directions

`direction` takes one of these lower-case tokens:

-   `outgoing`: records that this record points to through its own relation fields. In the editor, **Outgoing via**.
-   `incoming`: records that point to this record through their relation fields. In the editor, **Incoming via**.
-   `both`: records in either direction. In the editor, **Both directions**.

### Several steps in a row

With more than one step, Tape follows them as a chain.

-   The first step starts from the current record.
-   Each later step starts from the records that the step before it found.
-   Each step fills a record collection for its own `app_id`.
-   A step's `app_id` must be a database app that the previous database app relates to. Otherwise validation reports `action_app_invalid`.

## Use the collection in later actions

Each step creates a `record_collection` for its `app_id`. A later action references the tasks from the example with this object:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 1204 }
```

-   Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same `app_id`.
-   Use it in `filter_record_collection`, `sort_record_collection`, `clear_record_collection`, the `collected_records_*` actions and the `iterable` of a `for_loop`.
-   See [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) for the pattern.

## General behavior

-   `ref_collection_defs` is optional when you save.
-   `direction` and `match_type` have no default. Send both on every step, as lower-case tokens.
-   Neither the save nor [`validate`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) reports a step without `direction` or `match_type`. The step then reads back without both keys.
-   Without a trigger that has a record, validation reports the [broken reason](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#broken-reason-codes) `action_invalid`. `periodic` and `webhook_received` have no record.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The automation needs a trigger with a record.
-   The database app of each step must relate to the database app before it.

## Next steps

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters)[

# collected_records_call_automation

> Config reference for the Tape automation collected_records_call_automation action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to call another automation once for every record in a collection.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Trigger another automation on collected records** in the [Automation calls & weblinks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#automation-calls--weblinks) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger but needs an earlier action that creates the record collection.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

An earlier action collects the contracts that renew next quarter. This action calls the renewal reminder automation for each of them:

```json
{
  "type": "collected_records_call_automation",
  "config": {
    "automation_id": 4022,
    "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 2087 },
    "call_arguments": [
      {
        "variable_def": { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Renewal quarter" },
        "assignment_type": "set",
        "value": ["Q1 2027"]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `automation_id` | integer | **Required.** ID of the automation to call for each record. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_automation_missing`. | `4022` |
| `record_collection` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The collection whose records Tape calls the automation for, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_invalid` and `action_automation_invalid`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 2087 }` |
| `call_arguments` | array of call arguments | Values for the inputs that the called automation declares. Empty when left out. | `[]` |

To find `automation_id`, see [List automations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#list-automations). It returns the ID of each automation as `id`.

Each `call_arguments` entry has the same shape as in [`current_record_call_automation`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-call-automation#call-arguments):

-   `variable_def` (*required*): the input to fill, as `{ "custom_type", "label" }`.
-   `assignment_type`: `set` uses `value` (a template value), `set_code` uses `code` (a code value). Default `set`.
-   `id`: stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read.

## General behavior

-   No key is required by the schema. Tape saves the action without `automation_id`, `record_collection` or `call_arguments`.
-   Tape calls the target automation *once per record* in the collection.
-   Without `record_collection`, validation reports `action_invalid`. It also reports `action_automation_invalid`, because Tape then has no database app to check the target against.
-   A `record_collection` without a matching earlier action fails validation with `action_variable_missing`. Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same `app_id`.
-   The target automation must exist. Otherwise validation reports `action_automation_missing`.
-   The target must live in the database app of the collected records and use the `automation_called` trigger. Otherwise validation reports `action_automation_invalid`.
-   A *paused* target is a valid reference.
-   Each `call_arguments` label must match a custom variable of the target's trigger, with `custom_variable_defs_enabled` set to `true`. Otherwise validation reports `action_call_argument_invalid`.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in `record_collection`, for example [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records).
-   The target automation uses the `automation_called` trigger and lives in the database app of the collected records.

## Next steps

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-call-automation)[

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers)[

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values)[

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/action-examples)[

# collected_records_collect_referenced_records

> Config reference for the Tape automation collected_records_collect_referenced_records action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to collect the records that the records of an earlier collection relate to.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Get related records** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger but needs an earlier action that creates the record collection it starts from.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

An earlier action collected solar installations from database app `87`. This action collects the customers that those installations point to:

```json
{
  "type": "collected_records_collect_referenced_records",
  "config": {
    "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 87 },
    "ref_collection_defs": [
      {
        "direction": "outgoing",
        "match_type": "all",
        "app_id": 91,
        "via_field_ids": [55012]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_collection` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The collection to start from, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_invalid`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 87 }` |
| `ref_collection_defs` | array of reference steps | The steps that Tape follows from the records in the collection. Empty when left out, and then the action collects nothing. | `[{ "direction": "outgoing", "match_type": "all", "app_id": 91 }]` |

Each step has the same keys as in [`collect_referenced_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-referenced-records#reference-steps):

-   `direction` (*required*): `outgoing`, `incoming` or `both`.
-   `match_type` (*required*): `all` keeps every related record, `filtered` keeps only the records that match `match_condition`.
-   `app_id`: the related database app. Validation reports `action_app_missing` without it.
-   `via_field_ids`: the relation fields to follow.
-   `match_condition`: a [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) for the `filtered` mode. An empty AND group when left out, read back as `null`.
-   `id`: stable ID of the step. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read.

With more than one step, Tape follows them as a chain. Each step starts from the records that the step before it found.

To find `app_id` and the relation field IDs for `via_field_ids`, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

## Use the collection in later actions

Each step creates a `record_collection` for its `app_id`. A later action references the customers from the example with this object:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 91 }
```

-   Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same `app_id`.
-   Use it in `filter_record_collection`, `sort_record_collection`, `clear_record_collection`, the `collected_records_*` actions and the `iterable` of a `for_loop`.
-   See [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) for the pattern.

## General behavior

-   This action uses one collection and creates another. It starts from `record_collection` and fills a record collection for the `app_id` of each step.
-   `record_collection` has no default. Without it, Tape saves the action, and validation reports `action_invalid`.
-   A `record_collection` without a matching earlier action fails validation with `action_variable_missing`.
-   `direction` and `match_type` have no default. Send both on every step, as lower-case tokens.
-   Neither the save nor [`validate`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) reports a step without `direction` or `match_type`. The step then reads back without both keys.
-   Each step's `app_id` must relate to the database app before it. Otherwise validation reports `action_app_invalid`.
-   For each step, the run log shows how many records Tape collected.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in `record_collection`, for example [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records).

# collected_records_comment_create

> Config reference for the Tape automation collected_records_comment_create action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to add a comment to every record in a collection that an earlier action built.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Add a comment to all collected records** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger but needs an earlier action that creates the record collection.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action asks every collected applicant to pick an interview slot:

```json
{
  "type": "collected_records_comment_create",
  "config": {
    "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 123 },
    "comment_content": ["Interview slots for next week are open. Pick one by Friday."],
    "silent": true
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `comment_content` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The comment text. | `["Contract signed."]` |
| `record_collection` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The collection to comment on, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_invalid`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 123 }` |
| `author_id` | integer | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | User Tape attributes the comment to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. | `812` |
| `trigger_webhooks` | boolean | Whether the comment fires outbound webhooks. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `trigger_other_flows` | boolean | Whether the comment starts other automations. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `silent` | boolean | Whether Tape sends no notifications for the comment. Default `false`. | `true` |

`author_id`, `trigger_webhooks`, `trigger_other_flows` and `silent` are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are **Author**, **Trigger webhooks**, **Trigger automations** and **Silent**. To find a user ID for `author_id`, see [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).

## General behavior

-   `comment_content` is the only key the schema requires. Without `record_collection`, Tape saves the action, and validation reports `action_invalid`.
-   A `record_collection` without a matching earlier action fails validation with `action_variable_missing`. Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same `app_id`.
-   Tape adds the comment to each record in the collection. A field or meta reference with `collection: true` in `comment_content` reads that record's value.
-   With an empty `comment_content`, Tape skips the action when the automation runs.
-   If the references in `comment_content` resolve to empty text when the automation runs, the action fails, and so does the run.
-   Mentions in `comment_content` can only point to members of the workspace that the collection's database app belongs to.
-   Without `author_id`, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason `action_user_missing`.
-   Tape returns `silent` on every read. It's `false` when you left it out.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in `record_collection`, for example [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records).

# collected_records_send_email

> Config reference for the Tape automation collected_records_send_email action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to send one email for each record in a collection that an earlier action built.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Send an email to all collected records** in the [Email & documents](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#email--documents) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger but needs an earlier action that creates the record collection.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action reminds the buyer of every collected viewing, using the email field of each record:

```json
{
  "type": "collected_records_send_email",
  "config": {
    "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 640 },
    "to_address": [{ "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 6120, "field_type": "multi_email", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false }],
    "subject": ["Your viewing tomorrow"],
    "message_body": ["<p>See you at the property tomorrow. Reply to this email to reschedule.</p>"],
    "reply_address": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "smtp_account_id": 812
  }
}
```

## Config

The config matches [`send_email`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/send-email), plus `record_collection` and `fields_expanded`.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_collection` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The collection whose records get one email each, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_invalid`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 640 }` |
| `to_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Recipient address or addresses. Empty when left out. Without it, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. | `["romeo@acme.com"]` |
| `subject` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Subject line. Empty when left out. | `["Your viewing tomorrow"]` |
| `reply_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Reply-to address. Empty when left out. | `["juliet@acme.com"]` |
| `cc_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | CC address or addresses. Empty when left out. | `["romeo@acme.com"]` |
| `bcc_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | BCC address or addresses. Empty when left out. | `["archive@acme.com"]` |
| `from_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Sender address. Empty when left out. | `["sales@acme.com"]` |
| `from_name` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Sender display name. Empty when left out. | `["Acme Realty"]` |
| `message_body` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | HTML body. Empty when left out. | `["<p>Hello</p>"]` |
| `smtp_account_id` | integer | ID of the SMTP account to send from. Left out, Tape uses the organization's *default* SMTP account. See [Sender address](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/email#sender-address). Same ID as `smtp_settings_id` of the [email endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/email#sending-an-email). | `812` |
| `attach_files_variable_defs` | array of [references](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | File variables Tape can attach: attachment or image fields, file custom variables such as the PDF from [`create_pdf`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/create-pdf), or the files of the trigger. Empty when left out. | `[]` |
| `attach_files_match_type` | enum | Which of those files Tape attaches. Default `all`. See [Attachment modes](#attachment-modes). | `"all"` |
| `attach_files_match_condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | Limits the attached files in the `filtered` and `most_recent_filtered` modes. An empty AND group when left out or `null`. | `null` |
| `fields_expanded` | boolean | Editor only: whether the address fields show expanded in the automation editor. Tape keeps it on read and write. Left out when not set. | `false` |

To find `smtp_account_id`, select the account in this action in the automation editor, then [retrieve the automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#retrieve-an-automation). The API has no endpoint that lists SMTP accounts.

### Attachment modes

`attach_files_match_type` takes one of these lower-case tokens:

-   `all`: attaches every candidate file. Ignores the condition.
-   `most_recent`: attaches the most recent file. Ignores the condition.
-   `filtered`: attaches the files that match `attach_files_match_condition`.
-   `most_recent_filtered`: attaches the most recent file that matches `attach_files_match_condition`.

## General behavior

-   Tape sends one email for each record in the collection. A field or meta reference with `collection: true` reads that record's value, like the email field in the example.
-   Unlike `send_email`, the schema marks no key as required. Without `record_collection`, Tape saves the action, and validation reports `action_invalid`.
-   A `record_collection` without a matching earlier action fails validation with `action_variable_missing`.
-   Without `to_address`, Tape skips the action when the automation runs. Set `to_address` and `subject` for a useful email.
-   Every other address, name and body defaults to empty.
-   Every email an automation sends counts against the organization's shared 24-hour send quota.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in `record_collection`, for example [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records).

# collected_records_update

> Config reference for the Tape automation collected_records_update action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to update every record in a collection that an earlier action built.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Update all collected records** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger but needs an earlier action that creates the record collection.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action marks every collected task as ready for review:

```json
{
  "type": "collected_records_update",
  "config": {
    "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 5 },
    "field_assignments": [
      {
        "field_type": "single_text",
        "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4021, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
        "assignment_type": "set",
        "field_value": ["Ready for review"]
      }
    ],
    "silent": true
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_collection` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The collection to update, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_invalid`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 5 }` |
| `field_assignments` | array of field assignments | The values to set on each collected record, one entry per field. Empty when left out. See [Field assignments](#field-assignments). | `[]` |
| `author_id` | integer | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | User Tape attributes the change to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. | `812` |
| `trigger_webhooks` | boolean | Whether the change fires outbound webhooks. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `trigger_other_flows` | boolean | Whether the change starts other automations. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `silent` | boolean | Whether Tape sends no notifications for the change. Default `false`. | `true` |

To find the field IDs, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

`author_id`, `trigger_webhooks`, `trigger_other_flows` and `silent` are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are **Author**, **Trigger webhooks**, **Trigger automations** and **Silent**. To find a user ID for `author_id`, see [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).

### Field assignments

Each entry in `field_assignments` sets one field on every collected record.

-   `field_type` tells the 20 field-type shapes apart, for example `single_text` or `number`.
-   `variable_def` is a [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) to the target field.
-   `assignment_type` picks how Tape produces the value. `set` uses `field_value`, `set_code` uses `code`.

[`meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) describes the populated shape only loosely. Copy the shapes from [`current_record_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-update#field-assignments) and check the live `config_schema` before you send filled assignments.

## General behavior

-   No key is required by the schema. Without `record_collection`, Tape saves the action, and validation reports `action_invalid`.
-   A `record_collection` without a matching earlier action fails validation with `action_variable_missing`. Tape resolves the reference to the nearest earlier action that creates a collection for the same `app_id`.
-   Left out or `[]`, `field_assignments` changes no field value. The action still logs a `success` step for each collected record.
-   On an empty collection, the action changes nothing and logs one `success` step with the message `No records were found in the collection.`
-   Without `author_id`, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason `action_user_missing`.
-   Tape returns `silent` on every read. It's `false` when you left it out.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in `record_collection`, for example [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records).

# conditional

> Config reference for the Tape automation conditional action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to run nested actions only when a condition holds, with an optional else branch.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Conditional actions** in the [Flow control](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#flow-control) family. Its `group` is `control_flow`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

When a deal is worth more than 50,000, this action asks the sales director for approval. Otherwise, it tells the account owner that the deal is ready to close:

```json
{
  "type": "conditional",
  "config": {
    "condition": {
      "operator": "and",
      "rows": [
        {
          "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 601, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
          "operator": "greater_than",
          "value": { "type": "number", "number": ["50000"] }
        }
      ]
    },
    "action_rows": [
      {
        "type": "send_email",
        "config": {
          "to_address": ["romeo@acme.com"],
          "subject": ["Approval needed: deal over 50,000"]
        }
      }
    ],
    "else_action_rows": [
      {
        "type": "send_email",
        "config": {
          "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"],
          "subject": ["Deal ready to close"]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | The if condition. `null` or left out counts as true. | `{ "operator": "and", "rows": [ … ] }` |
| `action_rows` | array of nested [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions) | The then branch. Runs when the condition holds. Empty when left out. | `[{ "type": "send_email", "config": { … } }]` |
| `else_action_rows` | array of nested [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions) | The else branch. Runs when the condition fails. Leave it out to switch the else branch off. | `[{ "type": "exit", "config": { "exit_type": "success" } }]` |

To find the field IDs, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

## General behavior

-   No key is required.
-   The condition and both branches live in `config`, like every other action. Each branch is a nested list of actions.
-   A missing, `null` or empty `condition` counts as true. The then branch runs on every run. It reads back as `condition: null`.
-   Leave `else_action_rows` out to switch the else branch off. Send it, even as `[]`, to switch it on. There are no `*_enabled` flags.
-   `action_rows` and `else_action_rows` hold full action objects. `GET /v1/automation/meta/action` lists the types you can nest.
-   When the API rejects the input of a nested action, the error names its path, for example `config/else_action_rows/0`.
-   `condition` uses the same filter tree as the collect actions. [`GET /v1/automation/meta/filter`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) lists the operators for each field type.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

## Next steps

[

exit

end the run inside a branch.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/exit)[

for\_loop

check the condition once per collected record.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/for-loop)[

Filters

the filter group used by `condition`.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters)[

Dynamic values

field references for the condition's subject.

Action examples

configs to copy for the common actions.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions)
