# create_pdf

> Config reference for the Tape automation create_pdf action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to render an HTML template to a PDF file that later actions can use.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Create a PDF** in the [Email & documents](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#email--documents) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action renders an invoice for the current record:

```json
{
  "type": "create_pdf",
  "config": {
    "filename": ["invoice-", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }, ".pdf"],
    "page_size": "a4",
    "page_orientation": "portrait",
    "page_margins": "normal",
    "pdf_body": ["<h1>Invoice</h1><p>Thank you for your order.</p>"],
    "custom_variable_def": { "custom_type": "single_file", "label": "Invoice PDF" }
  }
}
```

## Config

Every key is optional. Tape fills in the same defaults as the editor, so a short config still gives a complete action.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `filename` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Name of the generated file. Empty when left out. | `["invoice.pdf"]` |
| `custom_variable_def` | object | The output variable that holds the generated PDF file. Default `{ "custom_type": "single_file", "label": "PDF" }`. | `{ "custom_type": "single_file", "label": "Invoice PDF" }` |
| `pdf_body` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | HTML template for the PDF content. Empty when left out. | `["<h1>Invoice</h1>"]` |
| `page_size` | enum | Page size. Default `a4`. See [Page sizes](#page-sizes). | `"a4"` |
| `page_custom_width` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Custom page width. Used only when `page_size` is `custom_size`. Empty when left out. | `["210"]` |
| `page_custom_height` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Custom page height. Used only when `page_size` is `custom_size`. Empty when left out. | `["297"]` |
| `page_orientation` | enum | Page orientation: `portrait` or `landscape`. Default `portrait`. | `"portrait"` |
| `page_margins` | enum | Page margin preset. Default `normal`. See [Page margins](#page-margins). | `"normal"` |
| `page_custom_margin_top` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Custom top margin. Used only when `page_margins` is `custom_margins`. Empty when left out. | `["20"]` |
| `page_custom_margin_right` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Custom right margin. Used only when `page_margins` is `custom_margins`. Empty when left out. | `["15"]` |
| `page_custom_margin_bottom` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Custom bottom margin. Used only when `page_margins` is `custom_margins`. Empty when left out. | `["20"]` |
| `page_custom_margin_left` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Custom left margin. Used only when `page_margins` is `custom_margins`. Empty when left out. | `["15"]` |
| `pdf_header_custom_margin_top` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Custom top margin of the header. Used only when `page_margins` is `custom_margins`. Empty when left out. | `["10"]` |
| `pdf_footer_custom_margin_bottom` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Custom bottom margin of the footer. Used only when `page_margins` is `custom_margins`. Empty when left out. | `["10"]` |
| `page_numbers_enabled` | boolean | Whether Tape adds page numbers. Default `false`. | `true` |
| `page_number_style` | enum | Numbering style of the page numbers. Default `decimal`. See [Page number styles](#page-number-styles). | `"decimal"` |
| `page_number_start` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | The number of the first page. Empty when left out. | `["1"]` |
| `header_and_footer_enabled` | boolean | Whether Tape adds the header and footer. Default `false`. | `true` |
| `pdf_header` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | HTML template for the header on the first page. Empty when left out. | `["<p>Acme Inc.</p>"]` |
| `pdf_header_following_pages_enabled` | boolean | Whether the following pages get their own header. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `pdf_header_following_pages` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | HTML template for the header on the following pages. Empty when left out. | `["<p>Invoice, continued</p>"]` |
| `pdf_footer` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | HTML template for the footer on the first page. Empty when left out. | `["<p>Thank you for your business.</p>"]` |
| `pdf_footer_following_pages_enabled` | boolean | Whether the following pages get their own footer. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `pdf_footer_following_pages` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | HTML template for the footer on the following pages. Empty when left out. | `["<p>Acme Inc.</p>"]` |
| `options_expanded` | boolean | Editor only: whether the advanced options section shows expanded. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `pdf_header_expanded` | boolean | Editor only: whether the header section shows expanded. Default `true`. | `true` |
| `pdf_footer_expanded` | boolean | Editor only: whether the footer section shows expanded. Default `true`. | `true` |
| `pdf_body_expanded` | boolean | Editor only: whether the body section shows expanded. Default `true`. Stays `true` while `header_and_footer_enabled` is `false`. | `true` |

### Page sizes

`page_size` takes one of these lower-case tokens:

-   `letter`
-   `tabloid`
-   `legal`
-   `a3`
-   `a4`
-   `a5`
-   `envelope_10`
-   `custom_size`: uses `page_custom_width` and `page_custom_height`.

### Page margins

`page_margins` takes one of these lower-case tokens:

-   `normal`
-   `narrow`
-   `moderate`
-   `wide`
-   `custom_margins`: uses the four `page_custom_margin_*` values and the header and footer margins.

### Page number styles

`page_number_style` takes one of these lower-case tokens:

-   `decimal`: 1, 2, 3
-   `decimal_leading_zero`: 01, 02, 03
-   `lower_latin`: a, b, c
-   `upper_latin`: A, B, C
-   `lower_roman`: i, ii, iii
-   `upper_roman`: I, II, III

### Editor-only flags

The four `*_expanded` keys only control which sections the automation editor shows expanded. They don't change the PDF.

-   `meta/action` lists them in the `config_schema`.
-   Tape keeps them on read and write, so a read-modify-write preserves them.
-   While `header_and_footer_enabled` is `false`, Tape sets `pdf_body_expanded` to `true`. In that state the editor has no control to open a closed body section.

## Use the file in a later action

The action stores the file in the variable from `custom_variable_def`. A later action reads it with a `custom` reference that has the same `custom_type` and `label`. This `send_email` entry attaches the invoice:

```json
{
  "type": "send_email",
  "config": {
    "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "subject": ["Your invoice"],
    "attach_files_variable_defs": [
      { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "single_file", "label": "Invoice PDF" }
    ]
  }
}
```

## General behavior

-   The defaults are the ones in the [Config](#config) table. Without `custom_variable_def`, the output variable has the label `PDF`.
-   Tape ignores the custom sizes and margins unless `page_size` is `custom_size` or `page_margins` is `custom_margins`.
-   Code values for sizes, margins and `page_number_start` must resolve to a number.
-   Tape reads custom sizes and margins in millimeters, so `["210"]` by `["297"]` is A4.
-   The action writes no reliable success entry to the run log. Don't use the log to confirm that the PDF was rendered.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

# current_record_call_automation

> Config reference for the Tape automation current_record_call_automation action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to call another automation and pass it the record that this automation runs on.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Trigger another automation on the current record** in the [Automation calls & weblinks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#automation-calls--weblinks) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it needs a trigger with a record: `record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted`, `record_comment_or_reply_created`, `date_field_arrived`, `automation_called` or `weblink_clicked`.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

When a listing is marked as sold, this action calls the automation that notifies the buyer's agent and passes a closing note:

```json
{
  "type": "current_record_call_automation",
  "config": {
    "automation_id": 4021,
    "call_arguments": [
      {
        "variable_def": { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Closing note" },
        "assignment_type": "set",
        "value": ["Sold at asking price. Listing ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `automation_id` | integer | **Required.** ID of the automation to call. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_automation_missing`. | `4021` |
| `call_arguments` | array of [call arguments](#call-arguments) | Values for the inputs that the called automation declares. Empty when left out. | `[]` |

To find `automation_id`, see [List automations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#list-automations). It returns the ID of each automation as `id`.

### Call arguments

Each entry in `call_arguments` binds one input of the called automation:

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variable_def` | object | **Required.** The input to fill, as `{ "custom_type", "label" }`. The `label` must match a custom variable that the called automation's trigger declares. | `{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Closing note" }` |
| `assignment_type` | enum | Where the value comes from: `set` uses `value`, `set_code` uses `code`. Default `set`. | `"set"` |
| `value` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | The value for `set`. Empty when left out. | `["Sold"]` |
| `code` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | The expression for `set_code`. Empty when left out. | `["1 + 1"]` |
| `id` | string | Stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. | `"a1b2c3"` |

`custom_type` takes one of `any`, `single_file`, `multi_file`, `single_link`, `html_table_rows`.

The called automation declares the input in its trigger:

```json
{ "type": "automation_called", "config": { "custom_variable_defs_enabled": true, "custom_variable_defs": [{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Closing note" }] } }
```

## General behavior

-   No key is required by the schema. Tape saves the action without `automation_id` or `call_arguments`.
-   The target automation must exist. Otherwise validation reports `action_automation_missing`.
-   The target must live in the same database app as this automation's trigger and use the `automation_called` trigger. Otherwise validation reports `action_automation_invalid`.
-   A *paused* target is a valid reference.
-   Each `call_arguments` label must match a custom variable of the target's trigger, with `custom_variable_defs_enabled` set to `true`. Otherwise validation reports `action_call_argument_invalid`.
-   Without a trigger that has a record, validation reports the [broken reason](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#broken-reason-codes) `action_invalid`. `periodic` and `webhook_received` have no record.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The automation needs a trigger with a record.
-   The target automation uses the `automation_called` trigger and lives in the same database app.

# current_record_comment_create

> Config reference for the Tape automation current_record_comment_create action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to add a comment to the record that an automation runs on.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Add a comment to the current record** in the [Current record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#current-record) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it needs a trigger with a record: `record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted`, `record_comment_or_reply_created`, `date_field_arrived`, `automation_called` or `weblink_clicked`.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

When an invoice record comes in, this action leaves a note for the finance team:

```json
{
  "type": "current_record_comment_create",
  "config": {
    "comment_content": ["Invoice ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }, " is ready for approval."],
    "silent": true
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `comment_content` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** Text of the comment. A plain string works too. Tape turns it into an array. | `["Invoice approved."]` |
| `author_id` | integer | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | User Tape attributes the comment to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. | `812` |
| `trigger_webhooks` | boolean | Whether the comment fires outbound webhooks. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `trigger_other_flows` | boolean | Whether the comment starts other automations. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `silent` | boolean | Whether Tape sends no notifications for the comment. Default `false`. | `true` |

`author_id`, `trigger_webhooks`, `trigger_other_flows` and `silent` are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are **Author**, **Trigger webhooks**, **Trigger automations** and **Silent**. To find a user ID for `author_id`, see [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).

## General behavior

-   `comment_content` is the only required key. It has no default.
-   With an empty `comment_content`, Tape skips the action when the automation runs.
-   If the references in `comment_content` resolve to empty text when the automation runs, the action fails, and so does the run.
-   Mentions in `comment_content` can only point to members of the workspace that the trigger's database app belongs to.
-   Without a trigger that has a record, validation reports the [broken reason](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#broken-reason-codes) `action_invalid`. `periodic` and `webhook_received` have no record.
-   Without `author_id`, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason `action_user_missing`.
-   Tape returns `silent` on every read. It's `false` when you left it out.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The automation needs a trigger with a record.

# current_record_delete

# current_record_generate_automation_weblink

> Config reference for the Tape automation current_record_generate_automation_weblink action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to create a weblink that runs another automation on the current record when someone opens it.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Create a web link for the current record** in the [Automation calls & weblinks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#automation-calls--weblinks) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it needs a trigger with a record: `record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted`, `record_comment_or_reply_created`, `date_field_arrived`, `automation_called` or `weblink_clicked`. The current record is the record that this automation runs on.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

When a new hire is added, this action creates a weblink that lets them confirm their start date. The link runs the confirmation automation and expires after a week:

```json
{
  "type": "current_record_generate_automation_weblink",
  "config": {
    "automation_id": 4023,
    "call_arguments": [
      {
        "variable_def": { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Confirmed via" },
        "assignment_type": "set",
        "value": ["Onboarding email"]
      }
    ],
    "custom_variable_def": { "custom_type": "single_link", "label": "Weblink" },
    "weblink_expiration": "one_week"
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `automation_id` | integer | **Required.** ID of the automation that the weblink runs. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_automation_missing`. | `4023` |
| `call_arguments` | array of call arguments | Values for the inputs that the target automation declares. Empty when left out. | `[]` |
| `custom_variable_def` | object | The variable that holds the generated weblink, as `{ "custom_type", "label" }`. Both keys are required in the object. Default `{ "custom_type": "single_link", "label": "Weblink" }`. | `{ "custom_type": "single_link", "label": "Weblink" }` |
| `weblink_expiration` | enum | When the weblink stops working. Default `never`. See [Expiration values](#expiration-values). | `"one_week"` |

To find `automation_id`, see [List automations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#list-automations). It returns the ID of each automation as `id`.

Each `call_arguments` entry has the same shape as in [`current_record_call_automation`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-call-automation#call-arguments):

-   `variable_def` (*required*): the input to fill, as `{ "custom_type", "label" }`.
-   `assignment_type`: `set` uses `value` (a template value), `set_code` uses `code` (a code value). Default `set`.
-   `id`: stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read.

`custom_variable_def.custom_type` takes one of `any`, `single_file`, `multi_file`, `single_link`, `html_table_rows`. The weblink is a link, so use `single_link`.

### Expiration values

`weblink_expiration` takes one of these lower-case tokens. The editor name is in brackets.

-   `never` (**Never**): the weblink keeps working.
-   `on_click` (**On click**): the weblink stops working after the first click.
-   `one_day` (**In a day**): the weblink stops working after one day.
-   `one_week` (**In a week**): the weblink stops working after one week.
-   `one_month` (**In a month**): the weblink stops working after one month.
-   `one_year` (**In a year**): the weblink stops working after one year.

> Copying from the generate-weblink endpoint?
> 
> [`POST /v1/automation/weblink/generate`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/advanced#generate-a-weblink) is a different surface. Its parameter is `expiration_type`, its tokens are upper-case (`NEVER`, `ONE_DAY`, `ONE_WEEK`, `ONE_MONTH`, `ONE_YEAR`), and it has no `on_click` (the endpoint uses `expire_after_first_click` for that). In this action's `config`, use `weblink_expiration` with lower-case tokens.

## Use the weblink in a later action

The action stores the weblink in the variable from `custom_variable_def`. A later action reads it with a `custom` reference that has the same `custom_type` and `label`. This `send_email` entry puts the link into the email body:

```json
{
  "type": "send_email",
  "config": {
    "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "subject": ["Please confirm your start date"],
    "message_body": [
      "<p>Welcome to Acme. Confirm your start date here: ",
      { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "single_link", "label": "Weblink" },
      "</p>"
    ]
  }
}
```

## General behavior

-   No key is required by the schema. Left out, `call_arguments` is empty, `custom_variable_def` is the `Weblink` variable and `weblink_expiration` is `never`.
-   The target automation must exist. Otherwise validation reports `action_automation_missing`.
-   The target must live in the same database app as this automation's trigger and use the `weblink_clicked` trigger. Otherwise validation reports `action_automation_invalid`.
-   Each `call_arguments` label must match a custom variable of the target's trigger, with `custom_variable_defs_enabled` set to `true`. Otherwise validation reports `action_call_argument_invalid`.
-   Without a trigger that has a record, validation reports the [broken reason](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#broken-reason-codes) `action_invalid`. `periodic` and `webhook_received` have no record.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The automation needs a trigger with a record.
-   The target automation uses the `weblink_clicked` trigger and lives in the same database app.

# current_record_get_previous_revision

> Config reference for the Tape automation current_record_get_previous_revision action, with its config and an example.

Use this action to load the previous revision of the record that an automation runs on.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Get previous values of the current record** in the [Current record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#current-record) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it needs a trigger with a record: `record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted`, `record_comment_or_reply_created`, `date_field_arrived`, `automation_called` or `weblink_clicked`.

## Example

Put this action before an action that compares a deal's old and new amount:

```json
{
  "type": "current_record_get_previous_revision",
  "config": {}
}
```

## Config

This action takes no config. Send an empty object: `"config": {}`.

## Use the previous values in a later action

Later actions read a value of the previous revision with a field [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) that has `"previous": true`. This reference reads the old deal amount:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 601, "field_type": "number", "previous": true, "collection": false, "triggering": false }
```

To find the field IDs, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

## General behavior

-   The schema has no properties and refuses any extra key. Leaving out the `config` key returns `400`.
-   The action loads the revision before the current one.
-   Without a trigger that has a record, validation reports the [broken reason](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#broken-reason-codes) `action_invalid`. `periodic` and `webhook_received` have no record.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The automation needs a trigger with a record.

# current_record_restore

> Config reference for the Tape automation current_record_restore action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to restore the deleted record that an automation runs on.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Restore the current record** in the [Current record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#current-record) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it needs a trigger with a record: `record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted`, `record_comment_or_reply_created`, `date_field_arrived`, `automation_called` or `weblink_clicked`.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

Under the `record_deleted` trigger, this action restores an employee record in an HR database app and attributes the restore to the user who last changed it:

```json
{
  "type": "current_record_restore",
  "config": {
    "author_id": { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "last_modified_by", "app_id": 87 },
    "silent": true
  }
}
```

## Config

The action has no keys of its own. It takes only the keys that every record-changing action shares.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `author_id` | integer | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | User Tape attributes the restore to: a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "created_by", "app_id": 87 }` |
| `trigger_webhooks` | boolean | Whether the restore fires outbound webhooks. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `trigger_other_flows` | boolean | Whether the restore starts other automations. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `silent` | boolean | Whether Tape sends no notifications for the restore. Default `false`. | `true` |

In the action menu of the automation editor, these keys are **Author**, **Trigger webhooks**, **Trigger automations** and **Silent**.

## General behavior

-   No key is required. `"config": {}` restores the current record with the defaults.
-   The action restores the record the run works on. It's useful when that record is deleted: under the `record_deleted` trigger, or after [`current_record_delete`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-delete) earlier in the same run.
-   Without a trigger that has a record, validation reports the [broken reason](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#broken-reason-codes) `action_invalid`. `periodic` and `webhook_received` have no record.
-   Without `author_id`, the automation itself is the author. Use a reference in `author_id`: with a literal user ID, `validate` reports `action_user_missing`, even for an existing user, and activation fails.
-   Tape returns `silent` on every read. It's `false` when you left it out.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The automation needs a trigger with a record.

# current_record_update

> Config reference for the Tape automation current_record_update action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to change field values of the record that an automation runs on.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Update the current record** in the [Current record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#current-record) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it needs a trigger with a record: `record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted`, `record_comment_or_reply_created`, `date_field_arrived`, `automation_called` or `weblink_clicked`.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

When a property listing changes, this action stamps a review note and sets the category option **In review**:

```json
{
  "type": "current_record_update",
  "config": {
    "field_assignments": [
      {
        "field_type": "single_text",
        "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4021, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
        "assignment_type": "set",
        "field_value": ["Listing changed, review the asking price"]
      },
      {
        "field_type": "single_category",
        "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4022, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
        "assignment_type": "set",
        "field_category_option_id": 2
      }
    ],
    "silent": true
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field_assignments` | array of [field assignments](#field-assignments) | Values Tape writes into the current record, one entry per field. Empty when left out. | `[]` |
| `author_id` | integer | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | User Tape attributes the change to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "last_modified_by", "app_id": 87 }` |
| `trigger_webhooks` | boolean | Whether the change fires outbound webhooks. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `trigger_other_flows` | boolean | Whether the change starts other automations. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `silent` | boolean | Whether Tape sends no notifications for the change. Default `false`. | `true` |

To find the field IDs, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids). To find the option ID for `field_category_option_id`, see [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app). It returns the options in `config.settings.options` of the field.

`author_id`, `trigger_webhooks`, `trigger_other_flows` and `silent` are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are **Author**, **Trigger webhooks**, **Trigger automations** and **Silent**. To find a user ID for `author_id`, see [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).

### Field assignments

Each entry of `field_assignments` sets one field of the current record. There are 20 assignment shapes, one per field type. They share these members:

-   `field_type` (*required*): the type of the target field, for example `single_text` or `single_category`. It selects the shape of the entry.
-   `variable_def` (*required*): a field [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) to the target field, with `source: "field"`, `field_id` and `field_type`.
-   `assignment_type`: how Tape produces the value. The modes depend on the field type. A `single_text` entry takes `set`, `unset` or `set_code`.
-   A value member that fits the mode: `field_value` for `set` on a text field, `field_category_option_id` for `set` on a category field, `code` for `set_code`. `unset` carries no value. `code` holds a JavaScript expression, for example `[<reference>, ".price"]`. For a text field, the expression must return text, for example `["String(", <reference>, ".price)"]`. A number fails the action when the automation runs. `field_value` is a [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) and can hold references, for example to a `custom` variable.
-   `id`: stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read.

[`meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) describes the populated shape only loosely. Copy the shapes from the example above and check the live `config_schema` before you send filled assignments.

## General behavior

-   No key is required by the schema. Left out or `[]`, `field_assignments` changes no field value. The action still logs a `success` step and updates the record's `last_modified_on` and `last_modified_by`.
-   The action changes the record the run works on. To change other records, use `referenced_records_update` or `collected_records_update`.
-   Without a trigger that has a record, validation reports the [broken reason](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#broken-reason-codes) `action_invalid`. `periodic` and `webhook_received` have no record.
-   Tape refuses an entry with `400` when its mode needs a value that the entry doesn't send. For example, `set` without `field_value` on a text field.
-   Without `author_id`, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason `action_user_missing`.
-   Tape returns `silent` on every read. It's `false` when you left it out.
-   Keep `trigger_other_flows` at `false` to avoid a loop when the automation triggers on record updates.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The automation needs a trigger with a record.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collected-records-update)[

# custom_code

> Config reference for the Tape automation custom_code action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to run your own JavaScript in an automation.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Execute a script** in the [Code & variables](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#code--variables) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action reads the deal value of a sales record and stores a 3 % commission in the variable `Commission`:

```json
{
  "type": "custom_code",
  "config": {
    "code": [
      "const dealValue = Number(",
      { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 601, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
      ");\n",
      { "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "Commission" },
      " = Math.round(dealValue * 0.03);"
    ],
    "custom_variable_defs": [
      { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Commission" }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The JavaScript the action runs. String literals mixed with variable references. A plain string works too. | `["const total = 1 + 1;"]` |
| `custom_variable_defs` | array of [variable declarations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Custom variables this action declares. Its own code and later actions can use them. Empty when left out. | `[{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Commission" }]` |

### Variable types

Each entry of `custom_variable_defs` needs a `label` and a `custom_type`. `custom_type` takes one of these lower-case tokens:

-   `any`
-   `single_file`
-   `multi_file`
-   `single_link`
-   `html_table_rows`

## Use the variable in a later action

Assign the result to a declared variable, as in the example. A later action reads it with a `custom` reference that has the same `custom_type` and `label`:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "Commission" }
```

## General behavior

-   `code` is the only required key.
-   `code` is a code value. It holds string literals and variable references only. Tape doesn't resolve template values in it.
-   Tape runs `code` as a block of statements inside the automation's script. It isn't a single expression like the `assignment_code` of [`custom_variable`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/custom-variable).
-   The write path doesn't check the syntax. A broken script saves and passes `validate`. The error shows up only in the run log.
-   `custom_variable_defs` defaults to `[]`. On read, Tape leaves it out when the action declares no variables.
-   A `custom` reference resolves only when this action or an earlier one declares a variable with the same `custom_type` and `label`. Otherwise validation reports `action_variable_missing`. See [Errors & broken reasons](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors).

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

# custom_variable

> Config reference for the Tape automation custom_variable action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to compute a value and store it in a variable for later actions.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Perform a calculation** in the [Code & variables](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#code--variables) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action estimates the yearly yield of a solar system from its size in kWp and stores the result in the variable `Annual yield (kWh)`:

```json
{
  "type": "custom_variable",
  "config": {
    "assignment_code": [
      "Math.round(Number(",
      { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 702, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
      ") * 950)"
    ],
    "custom_variable_defs": [
      { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Annual yield (kWh)" }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `assignment_code` | [code value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** One JavaScript expression. Tape stores its value in the declared variable. A plain string works too. | `["1 + 1"]` |
| `custom_variable_defs` | array of [variable declarations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | The variable that receives the value. Each entry is `{ "custom_type", "label" }`, and both keys are required. Empty when left out. | `[{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Total" }]` |

### Variable types

`custom_type` takes one of these lower-case tokens:

-   `any`
-   `single_file`
-   `multi_file`
-   `single_link`
-   `html_table_rows`

> Why does my action save but do nothing?
> 
> With an empty or missing `custom_variable_defs`, this action still validates and saves. When the automation runs, Tape skips it without a per-action log, as it does with an empty `assignment_code`. Declare one variable so the action has a target.

## Use the variable in a later action

Tape stores the value in the first variable of `custom_variable_defs`. A later action reads it with a `custom` reference that has the same `custom_type` and `label`:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "Annual yield (kWh)" }
```

## General behavior

-   `assignment_code` is the only required key. It has no default. `custom_variable_defs` defaults to `[]`.
-   Tape evaluates `assignment_code` as one expression. Write `1 + 1`, not `return 1 + 1;`. A top-level `return` fails when the automation runs, with `Illegal return statement`.
-   To store an object literal, wrap it in parentheses: `["({ total: ", …, " })"]`. Without them, JavaScript reads the braces as a block.
-   Declare one variable per action.
-   The action's own `assignment_code` can't reference the variable.
-   The write path doesn't check the syntax. A broken expression saves and passes `validate`. The error shows up only in the run log.
-   For a block of statements instead of one expression, use [`custom_code`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/custom-code).

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/custom-code)[

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/for-loop)[

# delay

> Config reference for the Tape automation delay action, with its config key, allowed values and an example.

Use this action to pause an automation run for a fixed time before the next action.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Delay execution** in the [Flow control](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#flow-control) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action waits 30 seconds, for example to give a teammate time to finish editing a task before the next action reads it:

```json
{
  "type": "delay",
  "config": {
    "delay_ms": 30000
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `delay_ms` | enum (integer) | **Required.** How long the run pauses, in milliseconds. See [Delay values](#delay-values). | `30000` |

### Delay values

`delay_ms` takes one of these numbers:

-   `15000`: 15 seconds.
-   `30000`: 30 seconds.
-   `45000`: 45 seconds.
-   `60000`: 60 seconds.

## General behavior

-   `delay_ms` is the only key, and it's required. It has no default.
-   Tape accepts only `15000`, `30000`, `45000` and `60000`. It rejects any other value.
-   The run pauses for the given time, then goes on with the next action.
-   For a longer wait, use the `date_field_arrived` or `periodic` [trigger](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers).
-   With a trigger that has a record, Tape reloads the current record after the pause. Later actions see its latest field values.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

# display_webpage

> Config reference for the Tape automation display_webpage action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to show a webpage to the person who opened a weblink.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Display a message on a web page** in the [Automation calls & weblinks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#automation-calls--weblinks) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it needs the `weblink_clicked` trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

A customer opens the weblink to confirm the installation date of their solar system. The page thanks them and shows the installation number:

```json
{
  "type": "display_webpage",
  "config": {
    "join_type": "replace_previous",
    "fullscreen": false,
    "remove_branding": true,
    "webpage_body": [
      "<h1>Thanks, your installation is confirmed</h1><p>Installation ",
      { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 },
      "</p>"
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `join_type` | enum | How this page joins a page that an earlier action displayed. Default `add_below`. See [Join types](#join-types). | `"add_below"` |
| `fullscreen` | boolean | Shows the page in fullscreen. Kept only when you set it. | `false` |
| `remove_branding` | boolean | Removes the Tape branding from the page. Kept only when you set it. | `true` |
| `webpage_body` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | HTML body of the page. Empty when left out. | `["<h1>Thanks</h1>"]` |

In the editor, `fullscreen` is **Fullscreen** and `remove_branding` is **Remove Tape info**.

### Join types

`join_type` takes one of these lower-case tokens. The editor name is in brackets.

-   `add_below` (**Add below**): adds this page below the page shown before.
-   `add_above` (**Add above**): adds this page above the page shown before.
-   `replace_previous` (**New page**): replaces the page shown before.

Tape rejects any other value with `400`.

## General behavior

-   No key is required. Tape saves the action with an empty config.
-   Without `join_type`, Tape uses `add_below`, the same value the editor sets.
-   Without `webpage_body`, the page is empty.
-   `fullscreen` and `remove_branding` come back on read only when you set them.
-   Without the `weblink_clicked` trigger, validation reports the [broken reason](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#broken-reason-codes) `action_invalid`.
-   References in `webpage_body` that don't resolve show up as broken reasons when you validate.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The automation needs the `weblink_clicked` trigger.

# exit

> Config reference for the Tape automation exit action, with its config key, allowed values and an example.

Use this action to end an automation run as a success or a failure.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **End run** in the [Flow control](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#flow-control) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

Inside the else branch of a [`conditional`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/conditional), this action stops the run as failed when a job application has no CV attached:

```json
{
  "type": "exit",
  "config": {
    "exit_type": "failure"
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exit_type` | enum | **Required.** How the run ends: `success` or `failure`. | `"success"` |

## General behavior

-   `exit_type` is the only key, and it's required. It has no default, because a successful end and a failed end mean different things.
-   Tape stops the run at this action. Later actions don't run.
-   `success` ends the run with status `completed`.
-   `failure` ends the run with status `failed` and `failure_reason: "exit_on_purpose"`. The [run object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation-run#the-run-object) tells this deliberate stop apart from an action error, which has a different `failure_reason`.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

# filter_record_collection

> Config reference for the Tape automation filter_record_collection action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to narrow a record collection from an earlier action down to the records that match a condition.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Filter collected records** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger but needs an earlier action that creates the record collection.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

An earlier action collected invoices from database app `42`. This action keeps only the invoices whose **Payment status** is **Overdue**:

```json
{
  "type": "filter_record_collection",
  "config": {
    "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 42 },
    "match_condition": {
      "operator": "and",
      "rows": [
        {
          "subject": {
            "kind": "variable",
            "source": "field",
            "field_id": 512,
            "field_type": "single_category",
            "previous": false,
            "collection": true,
            "triggering": false
          },
          "operator": "is_any_of",
          "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [9001] }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_collection` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The collection to filter, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_invalid`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 42 }` |
| `match_condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | The condition the records must match. An empty AND group when left out or `null`. | `{ "operator": "and", "rows": [] }` |

To find the field IDs for `match_condition`, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids). To find the option IDs for `ids`, see [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app). It returns them in `config.settings.options` of the field.

## Build the condition

-   Each `subject` is a field of the collection's database app, scoped to the collection: `"collection": true`.
-   A subject outside the collection's database app fails validation with `filter_variable_missing`.
-   [`GET /v1/automation/meta/filter`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) returns the operators for each field type.
-   See [Filters](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) for the group shape and the value union.

## General behavior

-   `record_collection` has no default. Without it, Tape saves the action, and validation reports `action_invalid`.
-   A `record_collection` without a matching earlier action fails validation with `action_variable_missing`.
-   Without `match_condition`, the filter keeps every record. An empty condition reads back as `null`.
-   Later actions that reference the same collection get the filtered records.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in `record_collection`, for example [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records).

## Next steps

[

put the filtered records in order.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/sort-record-collection)[

Filters

the filter group used by `match_condition`.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters)[

Dynamic values

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values)[

Action examples

a collect action followed by an update of the collection.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/action-examples)[

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions)

# for_loop

> Config reference for the Tape automation for_loop action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to run a set of nested actions once for each item of a collection.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Loop actions** in the [Flow control](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#flow-control) family. Its `group` is `control_flow`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

An earlier `collect_app_records` action collected the open invoices of database app `12345`. The loop skips invoices with the category option **Paid** (`9001`) and emails a payment reminder for each other one:

```json
{
  "type": "for_loop",
  "config": {
    "iterable": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 12345 },
    "continue_condition": {
      "operator": "and",
      "rows": [
        {
          "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 512, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false },
          "operator": "is_any_of",
          "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [9001] }
        }
      ]
    },
    "action_rows": [
      {
        "type": "send_email",
        "config": {
          "to_address": [
            { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 514, "field_type": "multi_email", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false }
          ],
          "subject": [
            "Payment reminder for invoice ",
            { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "collection": true, "app_id": 12345 }
          ],
          "message_body": ["<p>This invoice is overdue.</p>"]
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `iterable` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | What the loop goes through: a `record_collection` from an earlier `collect_*` action, a multi-value field or a custom variable. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 12345 }` |
| `action_rows` | array of nested [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions) | The loop body. Tape runs it once per item. Empty when left out. | `[{ "type": "send_email", "config": { … } }]` |
| `break_condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | Stops the loop when it matches. Off when left out. | `{ "operator": "and", "rows": [ … ] }` |
| `continue_condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | Skips to the next item when it matches. Off when left out. | `{ "operator": "and", "rows": [ … ] }` |

To find the field IDs, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids). To find the option IDs for `ids`, see [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app). It returns them in `config.settings.options` of the field.

## What happens for each item

1.  Tape loads the item. Inside the loop, references with `collection: true` to fields and metadata of the collection's database app point to this item. For a custom variable, a `custom` reference to that variable points to this item. To read one property of it, use a code value such as `[<reference>, ".price"]`. This works in field assignments and template values. The `assignment_code` of a `custom_variable` inside the loop body doesn't see the item yet and reads `undefined`.
2.  Tape checks `continue_condition`. When it matches, Tape skips the body and moves to the next item.
3.  Tape runs the actions in `action_rows`.
4.  Tape checks `break_condition`. When it matches, the loop stops.

An item that matches `break_condition` still runs the body once. Then the loop stops.

## General behavior

-   No key is required. An empty `config` is valid, but the loop does nothing.
-   The whole loop lives in `config`, like every other action.
-   Send the collection as `iterable`. The internal name `iterable_variable_def` isn't part of the API.
-   Leave `break_condition` or `continue_condition` out to switch it off. There are no `*_enabled` flags. A condition sent as `null` or as an empty group has no effect and reads back as `null`.
-   Without `iterable`, Tape skips the loop when the automation runs.
-   [`validate`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) checks that `iterable` resolves. A reference with no matching earlier action, for example a `collect_*` action placed after the loop, reports `action_variable_missing`.
-   `validate` doesn't check that the value can be looped over. A single-value field, or an action output that isn't a `record_collection`, passes `validate` and fails when the automation runs. Use only a `record_collection`, a multi-value field or a custom variable.
-   An `iterable` that's empty or `null` when the automation runs gives zero iterations, without an error.
-   A custom variable that holds an array gives one iteration per entry. Any other value gives one iteration with the whole value.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   When `iterable` references a collection or custom variable, an earlier action must create it, for example `collect_app_records`, `custom_variable` or `http_call`.

## Next steps

[

create the record collection to loop over.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records)[

Dynamic values

references such as `iterable`.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values)[

Filters

the filter group used by `break_condition` and `continue_condition`.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters)[

Action examples

configs to copy for the common actions.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/action-examples)[

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions)

# http_call

> Config reference for the Tape automation http_call action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to send an HTTP request from an automation and keep the response for later actions.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Send a HTTP request** in the [HTTP requests](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#http-requests) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

When an invoice in database app `87` is approved, this action posts the invoice number to the accounting system and saves the response:

```json
{
  "type": "http_call",
  "config": {
    "http_call_type": "post",
    "http_call_url": ["https://accounting.acme.com/api/invoices"],
    "http_call_headers": [
      { "key": "Content-Type", "value": ["application/json"] }
    ],
    "http_call_body": ["{\"invoice\": \"", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }, "\", \"status\": \"approved\"}"],
    "http_call_follow_redirects": false,
    "custom_variable_defs": [
      { "custom_type": "any", "label": "HTTP response" }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `http_call_type` | enum | **Required.** HTTP method: `get`, `post`, `put`, `patch` or `delete`. | `"post"` |
| `http_call_url` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** Request URL. | `["https://accounting.acme.com/api/invoices"]` |
| `http_call_body` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Request body. Empty when left out. | `["{\"status\": \"approved\"}"]` |
| `http_call_headers` | array of [headers](#headers) | Request headers. Empty when left out. | `[]` |
| `http_call_follow_redirects` | boolean | Follows `3xx` redirects. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `custom_variable_defs` | array of variable declarations | Variables this action declares. Empty when left out. | `[{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "HTTP response" }]` |

`custom_variable_defs[].custom_type` takes one of `any`, `single_file`, `multi_file`, `single_link`, `html_table_rows`. Each declaration also needs a `label`.

### Headers

Each entry in `http_call_headers` is one request header:

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | string | **Required.** Header name. | `"Content-Type"` |
| `value` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** Header value. Send `""` or `[]` for a blank value. | `["application/json"]` |
| `id` | string | Stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. | `"h1"` |

## Use the response in a later action

Tape stores the response body in the first variable of `custom_variable_defs`. A later action reads it with a `custom` reference that has the same `custom_type` and `label`:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "HTTP response" }
```

Without a declared variable, Tape sends the request and keeps no response. The editor declares one variable called **HTTP response**.

A response with `Content-Type: application/json` arrives as parsed JSON. Any other response arrives as a string.

-   To loop over a JSON array in the response, pass the reference as `iterable` of a [`for_loop`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/for-loop). When the array sits inside an object, first pick it out with a [`custom_variable`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/custom-variable), for example `[<reference>, ".items"]`, and loop over that variable.
-   To branch on the response, give a [`conditional`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/conditional) a [filter](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) row with `code`, for example `{ "code": [<reference>, " != null"] }`. A `custom` reference as `subject` returns `400`.

## General behavior

-   `http_call_type` and `http_call_url` are required. Neither has a default.
-   Every other key has a default: an empty body, no headers, no redirects and no declared variables.
-   `http_call_url`, `http_call_body` and each header `value` are template values. References in them resolve when the automation runs.
-   With an empty `http_call_url`, Tape skips the action when the automation runs.
-   Outbound requests have [SSRF protection](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18448976-automation-ip-addresses). Tape refuses hosts that resolve to private or internal addresses.
-   With `http_call_follow_redirects` set to `false`, Tape doesn't follow `3xx` responses.
-   Tape keeps only the response body, not the status code. A `4xx` or `5xx` response doesn't fail the action. A network error does.
-   Tape sends `http_call_body` as text and adds no `Content-Type`. Set the header yourself, as in the example.
-   A `custom` reference resolves only when its `custom_type` and `label` match a declaration in `custom_variable_defs`.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The target server accepts requests from Tape's IP addresses.

# record_create

> Config reference for the Tape automation record_create action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to create a record in a database app from an automation.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Create a record** in the [Current record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#current-record) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

When a deal is won in a CRM, this action creates a kick-off task in the **Tasks** database app:

```json
{
  "type": "record_create",
  "config": {
    "app_id": 4021,
    "field_assignments": [
      {
        "field_type": "single_text",
        "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 51207, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
        "assignment_type": "set",
        "field_value": ["Kick-off call for deal ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }]
      },
      {
        "field_type": "single_category",
        "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 51208, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
        "assignment_type": "set",
        "field_category_option_id": 3
      }
    ],
    "author_id": { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "created_by", "app_id": 87 },
    "trigger_other_flows": false
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | integer | ID of the database app Tape creates the record in. | `4021` |
| `field_assignments` | array of [field assignments](#field-assignments) | Values Tape writes into the new record, one entry per field. Left out or `[]`, Tape creates an empty record. | `[]` |
| `author_id` | integer | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | User Tape attributes the new record to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. | `812` |
| `trigger_webhooks` | boolean | Whether the new record fires outbound webhooks. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `trigger_other_flows` | boolean | Whether the new record starts other automations. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `silent` | boolean | Whether Tape sends no notifications for the new record. Default `false`. | `true` |

To find `app_id` and the field IDs, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids). To find the option ID for `field_category_option_id`, see [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app). It returns the options in `config.settings.options` of the field.

`author_id`, `trigger_webhooks`, `trigger_other_flows` and `silent` are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are **Author**, **Trigger webhooks**, **Trigger automations** and **Silent**. To find a user ID for `author_id`, see [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).

### Field assignments

Each entry of `field_assignments` sets one field of the new record. There are 20 assignment shapes, one per field type. They share these members:

-   `field_type` (*required*): the type of the target field, for example `single_text` or `single_category`. It selects the shape of the entry.
-   `variable_def` (*required*): a field [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) to the target field, with `source: "field"`, `field_id` and `field_type`.
-   `assignment_type`: how Tape produces the value. The modes depend on the field type. A `single_text` entry takes `set`, `unset` or `set_code`.
-   A value member that fits the mode: `field_value` for `set` on a text field, `field_category_option_id` for `set` on a category field, `code` for `set_code`. `unset` carries no value.
-   `id`: stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read.

[`meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) describes the populated shape only loosely. Copy the shapes from the example above and check the live `config_schema` before you send filled assignments.

## Use the new record in a later action

A later action reads the new record with a `created_record` reference. With `"property": "id"`, it returns the record ID:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "created_record", "app_id": 4021, "property": "id" }
```

## General behavior

-   No key is required by the schema. Send `app_id` anyway. Without it, the action saves but creates no record.
-   An `app_id` of a deleted app gives the [broken reason](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors#broken-reason-codes) `action_app_missing`. An `app_id` that never existed makes `validate` and activate return `404`.
-   Tape refuses an entry with `400` when its mode needs a value that the entry doesn't send. For example, `set` without `field_value` on a text field.
-   Without `author_id`, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason `action_user_missing`.
-   Tape returns `silent` on every read. It's `false` when you left it out.
-   Keep `trigger_other_flows` at `false` to avoid a loop when the automation triggers on the same database app.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The target database app must exist in your organization.
