# redirect_user

> Config reference for the Tape automation redirect_user action, with its config key and an example.

Use this action to send the person who opened a weblink to another URL.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Redirect users to another web page** in the [Automation calls & weblinks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#automation-calls--weblinks) family. Its `group` is `action`, and the editor offers it only with the `weblink_clicked` trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

A manager opens the weblink to approve a task. This action sends the manager to a confirmation page with the task number:

```json
{
  "type": "redirect_user",
  "config": {
    "redirect_url": ["https://acme.com/approvals/done?task=", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `redirect_url` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The URL to send the person to. | `["https://acme.com/approvals/done"]` |

## General behavior

-   `redirect_url` is the only key, and it's required. It has no default.
-   `redirect_url` is a template value. References in it resolve when the automation runs.
-   The redirect happens when the person opens the weblink and the automation reaches this action.
-   Validation doesn't check the trigger for this action. A wrong trigger doesn't show up as a broken reason, so pick `weblink_clicked` yourself.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The automation needs the `weblink_clicked` trigger.

# referenced_records_update

> Config reference for the Tape automation referenced_records_update action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to update the records that relate to the record an automation runs on.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Update all related records** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it needs a trigger with a record in a database app, because Tape looks up the related records from that record.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

When a solar project changes, this action updates every related installation:

```json
{
  "type": "referenced_records_update",
  "config": {
    "app_id": 1044,
    "field_assignments": [
      {
        "field_type": "single_text",
        "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4021, "field_type": "single_text", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
        "assignment_type": "set",
        "field_value": ["Permit approved"]
      }
    ],
    "silent": true
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | integer | **Required.** ID of the database app that holds the related records. It must relate to the trigger's database app, in either direction. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_app_missing`. | `1044` |
| `field_assignments` | array of field assignments | The values to set on each related record, one entry per field. Empty when left out. See [Field assignments](#field-assignments). | `[]` |
| `author_id` | integer | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | User Tape attributes the change to: a user ID, or a reference to the creator, the last modifier or a user field. Left out, the automation itself is the author. | `812` |
| `trigger_webhooks` | boolean | Whether the change fires outbound webhooks. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `trigger_other_flows` | boolean | Whether the change starts other automations. Default `false`. | `false` |
| `silent` | boolean | Whether Tape sends no notifications for the change. Default `false`. | `true` |

To find `app_id` and the field IDs, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

`author_id`, `trigger_webhooks`, `trigger_other_flows` and `silent` are shared by every action that changes records. In the action menu of the automation editor, they are **Author**, **Trigger webhooks**, **Trigger automations** and **Silent**. To find a user ID for `author_id`, see [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).

### Field assignments

Each entry in `field_assignments` sets one field on every related record.

-   `field_type` tells the 20 field-type shapes apart, for example `single_text` or `number`.
-   `variable_def` is a [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) to the target field.
-   `assignment_type` picks how Tape produces the value. `set` uses `field_value`, `set_code` uses `code`. The unused value stays empty.

[`meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) describes the populated shape only loosely. Copy the shapes from [`current_record_update`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/current-record-update#field-assignments) and check the live `config_schema` before you send filled assignments.

## General behavior

-   No key is required by the schema. Validation needs `app_id`.
-   Tape updates the records in `app_id` that relate to the current record, in both directions.
-   An `app_id` that doesn't relate to the trigger's database app fails validation with `action_app_invalid`.
-   Validation doesn't check the trigger for this action. With a trigger that has no record, such as `periodic`, Tape skips the action when the automation runs.
-   Left out or `[]`, `field_assignments` changes no field value. The action still logs a `success` step for each related record.
-   If the current record has no related records in `app_id`, the action does nothing and writes *no step* to the run log.
-   Later actions can use the updated records as a record collection of `app_id`.
-   Without `author_id`, the automation itself is the author. A user ID that Tape can't find gives the broken reason `action_user_missing`.
-   Tape returns `silent` on every read. It's `false` when you left it out.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   The trigger must run on a record of a database app. The database app in `app_id` must relate to it.

# rollup_iterable_values

> Config reference for the Tape automation rollup_iterable_values action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to aggregate a field across collected records into one value, for example a sum, a count or an average.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Rollup collected values** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger but needs an earlier action that creates the record collection.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action adds up the amounts of all collected open invoices:

```json
{
  "type": "rollup_iterable_values",
  "config": {
    "rollup_type": "sum",
    "rollup_variable_def": {
      "kind": "variable",
      "source": "field",
      "field_id": 123,
      "field_type": "number",
      "collection": true,
      "previous": false,
      "triggering": false
    },
    "custom_variable_def": { "custom_type": "any", "label": "Open invoice total" }
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `rollup_type` | enum | **Required.** The aggregation to run. See [Rollup types](#rollup-types). | `"sum"` |
| `rollup_variable_def` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The field whose values Tape aggregates, as a field reference with `collection: true`. An earlier collect action must put it in scope. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_variable_missing`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 123, "field_type": "number", "collection": true, "previous": false, "triggering": false }` |
| `custom_variable_def` | object | The output variable that holds the result. Default `{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Rollup" }`. | `{ "custom_type": "any", "label": "Open invoice total" }` |

To find the field ID for `rollup_variable_def`, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

### Rollup types

`rollup_type` takes one of these lower-case tokens:

-   `count_all`: counts all values.
-   `count_empty`: counts the empty values.
-   `count_not_empty`: counts the values that aren't empty.
-   `percent_empty`: share of empty values, in percent.
-   `percent_not_empty`: share of values that aren't empty, in percent.
-   `sum`: adds up the values.
-   `average`: the mean of the values.
-   `median`: the median of the values.
-   `min`: the smallest value.
-   `max`: the largest value.

## Use the result in a later action

The action stores the result in the variable from `custom_variable_def`. A later action reads it with a `custom` reference that has the same `custom_type` and `label`:

```json
{ "kind": "variable", "source": "custom", "custom_type": "any", "label": "Open invoice total" }
```

## General behavior

-   `rollup_type` is the only key the schema requires. It has no default.
-   Validation also needs `rollup_variable_def`. Without it, validation reports `action_variable_missing`.
-   Leave `custom_variable_def` out to get the default label `Rollup`.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An earlier action in the automation must collect the records whose field you roll up.

# send_email

> Config reference for the Tape automation send_email action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to send an email from an automation.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Send an email** in the [Email & documents](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#email--documents) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

This action tells [juliet@acme.com](mailto:juliet@acme.com) about a new lead and puts the record ID in the subject:

```json
{
  "type": "send_email",
  "config": {
    "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "subject": ["New record: ", { "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "app_record_id", "app_id": 87 }],
    "message_body": ["<p>A new lead came in.</p>"],
    "smtp_account_id": 812
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `to_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** Recipient address or addresses. | `["juliet@acme.com"]` |
| `subject` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** Subject line. | `["New lead"]` |
| `reply_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Reply-to address. Empty when left out. | `["sales@acme.com"]` |
| `cc_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | CC address or addresses. Empty when left out. | `["romeo@acme.com"]` |
| `bcc_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | BCC address or addresses. Empty when left out. | `["archive@acme.com"]` |
| `from_address` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Sender address. Empty when left out. | `["sales@acme.com"]` |
| `from_name` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Sender display name. Empty when left out. | `["Acme Sales"]` |
| `message_body` | [template value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | HTML body. Empty when left out. | `["<p>Hello</p>"]` |
| `smtp_account_id` | integer | ID of the SMTP account to send from. Left out, Tape uses the organization's *default* SMTP account. See [Sender address](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/email#sender-address). Same ID as `smtp_settings_id` of the [email endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/email#sending-an-email). | `812` |
| `attach_files_variable_defs` | array of [references](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | File variables Tape can attach: attachment or image fields, file custom variables such as the PDF from [`create_pdf`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/create-pdf), or the files of the trigger. Empty when left out. | `[]` |
| `attach_files_match_type` | enum | Which of those files Tape attaches. Default `all`. See [Attachment modes](#attachment-modes). | `"all"` |
| `attach_files_match_condition` | [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) | `null` | Limits the attached files in the `filtered` and `most_recent_filtered` modes. An empty AND group when left out. | `null` |

To find `smtp_account_id`, select the account in this action in the automation editor, then [retrieve the automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#retrieve-an-automation). The API has no endpoint that lists SMTP accounts. Without the automation API, see [Sender address](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/email#sender-address) for a way through the editor.

### Attachment modes

`attach_files_match_type` takes one of these lower-case tokens:

-   `all`: attaches every candidate file. Ignores the condition.
-   `most_recent`: attaches the most recent file. Ignores the condition.
-   `filtered`: attaches the files that match `attach_files_match_condition`.
-   `most_recent_filtered`: attaches the most recent file that matches `attach_files_match_condition`.

## General behavior

-   `to_address` and `subject` are the only required keys. Every other address, name and body defaults to empty.
-   Without `message_body`, Tape sends the email with an empty body.
-   Every email an automation sends counts against the organization's shared 24-hour send quota.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.

# sort_record_collection

> Config reference for the Tape automation sort_record_collection action, with its config keys, defaults and an example.

Use this action to put the records of a record collection from an earlier action in order.

> Tip
> 
> Read the live `config` shape of each action type from [`GET /v1/automation/meta/action`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) before you build on it.

In the automation editor, this action is **Sort collected records** in the [Record collections](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#record-collections) family. Its `group` is `action`, and it works with every trigger but needs an earlier action that creates the record collection.

Send it in the `actions` array of [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation) or [Update an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation). An update replaces the whole array, so include the other actions.

## Example

An earlier action collected deals from database app `42`. This action sorts them by **Amount**, highest first, and then by **Close date**:

```json
{
  "type": "sort_record_collection",
  "config": {
    "record_collection": { "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 42 },
    "sorts": [
      {
        "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4055, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false },
        "direction": "desc"
      },
      {
        "variable_def": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4061, "field_type": "single_date", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false },
        "direction": "asc"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

## Config

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_collection` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The collection to sort, created by an earlier action. The schema lets you save without it, but validation then reports `action_invalid`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "action", "action_type": "record_collection", "app_id": 42 }` |
| `sorts` | array of [sort entries](#sort-entries) | The sort order, applied in the order given. Empty when left out. | `[{ "variable_def": { … }, "direction": "asc" }]` |

To find the field IDs for `sorts`, see [App and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

### Sort entries

Each entry in `sorts` is an object:

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variable_def` | [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | **Required.** The field or record metadata to sort by. It must belong to the collection's database app, with `"collection": true`. | `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 4055, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": true, "triggering": false }` |
| `direction` | enum | **Required.** `asc` for ascending, `desc` for descending. | `"desc"` |
| `id` | string | Stable ID of the entry. Tape creates one when you leave it out and returns it on read. | `"sort-1"` |

To sort by record metadata, use a `meta` reference with `"collection": true`: record ID (`app_record_id`), created on (`created_at`), created by (`created_by`), last modified on (`last_modified_at`) or last modified by (`last_modified_by`). For example: `{ "kind": "variable", "source": "meta", "meta_type": "created_at", "app_id": 42, "collection": true }`.

## General behavior

-   `record_collection` has no default. Without it, Tape saves the action, and validation reports `action_invalid`.
-   A `record_collection` without a matching earlier action fails validation with `action_variable_missing`.
-   Without `sorts`, Tape stores an empty list, and the action doesn't change the order.
-   `variable_def` and `direction` are required in every sort entry. A missing one returns `400`.
-   A sort key outside the collection's database app fails validation with `action_variable_missing`.
-   A `meta` sort key without `"collection": true`, or with `record_id`, fails validation with `action_variable_missing`.
-   Tape applies the entries in order. Each later entry breaks ties of the entries before it.
-   Tape sorts the collection in place. Later actions that reference it get the new order.

## Requirements

-   To add or change this action through the API, your token needs the `automations:edit` capability. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).
-   You must administer the workspace that the automation's database app belongs to.
-   An earlier action in the automation must create the collection in `record_collection`, for example [`collect_app_records`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/collect-app-records).

## Next steps

for\_loop

go through the sorted records one by one.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/for-loop)[

# Errors & broken reasons

> HTTP status codes and the broken-reason codes returned across the Tape Automation API.

Use these codes to handle Automation API errors and to find out why an automation is broken.

## HTTP errors

The Automation endpoints use the standard Tape [error](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) envelope. On this resource:

| Status | When |
| --- | --- |
| `400` | A malformed body, a path ID that isn't an integer, or a run body that doesn't match the automation's trigger. The two [Advanced / sandbox](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/advanced) endpoints also return `400` for a missing automation or record. |
| `401` | The request carries no credential, or the credential doesn't act on behalf of a user where the endpoint needs one, for example an automation API key. |
| `403` | A personal access token or OAuth access token lacks the capability the endpoint needs. The response carries `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_scope"`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities). |
| `404` | The automation, app, workspace, revision or *record* isn't available to you. See [The 404 collapse](#the-404-collapse). Manual run and simulate also return `404` when the target record is missing or you can't view it. |
| `409` | A conflict with the automation's state: activating, running or simulating a broken automation. |

### What returns `400` in a definition body

Besides a malformed envelope, the input schema of a definition rejects the following when you write it:

-   An action *without a `config` key*, or with a `config` that lacks a member its `config_schema` requires. An empty `config: {}` passes only for types without required members, for example `current_record_update` or `collect_app_records`. `custom_code` without `code` returns `400`.
-   A *malformed dynamic-value reference*: an unknown `source` on a `kind: "variable"` reference, an unknown `value_type` on a `kind: "value"` reference, or a `field` reference without `field_type`.
-   An *unknown enum value*, for example an invalid `assignment_type` inside a `field_assignments` or `call_arguments` entry, or any config enum value that isn't one of the listed lower-case values.
-   A `filter` or `actions` tree nested *deeper than the maximum block depth*.
-   A *malformed `filter` comparison*, in the top-level `filter` or in a condition inside an action:
    -   a value tagged for a channel the field doesn't have,
    -   an empty comparison value,
    -   a value-arity mismatch: a value on an operator with arity `none` such as `is_empty`, or a missing value on an operator that needs one.
-   An explicitly *empty top-level `filter` group* (`rows: []`). Send `filter: null` to run without a filter.
-   A *malformed `value` union in a filter condition*:
    -   a payload key that belongs to a different channel than its `type` tag (each `type` branch accepts only its own keys),
    -   a relative `date` value with an `operator` or `unit` outside the listed values,
    -   a scalar `amount` (it must be a code-value array),
    -   an unknown member.

Problems of meaning don't return `400` on write. Examples: a member that only validation requires, a referenced ID that doesn't exist, or an operator outside a field's channel. They show up as [broken-reason codes](#broken-reason-codes) when you `validate` or activate, and some only when the automation runs. One exception: an action `app_id` that never existed (not a deleted app) makes `validate` and activate return `404`.

### The 404 collapse

Tape IDs are unique across all organizations, so existence and access *collapse into a single `404`*. An automation that is missing, soft-deleted, in another organization (*not `403`*), in a workspace you don't administer or outside your personal access token's [content access](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#content-selection) returns the *same `404`*. The API never reveals which IDs exist.

## The broken state

An automation's `broken_reason` is `{ errors: [...] }` or `null`. It's also `null` when `broken` is `true` because Tape marked the automation broken during a run. [`GET /v1/automation/{id}/validate`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) returns `{ valid, errors }` with the same entry shape, computed fresh.

Each error entry:

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `code` | `string` | Machine-readable reason. See [Broken-reason codes](#broken-reason-codes). |
| `message` | `string` | English description. Not translated. |
| `deactivated` | `boolean` | `true` when the fault is inside a deactivated block, which doesn't break the automation. `false` on filter and action entries in an active block. Absent on trigger entries. Treat a missing value as `false`: test `!entry.deactivated`, not `=== false`. |
| `block_id` / `action_id` | `string` | `null` | The node at fault. `action_id` is `null` for a top-level fault, for example a filter or field assignment reason. |
| `app_id` / `field_id` / `view_id` / `automation_id` / `user_id` / `record_id` / `option_id` | `integer` | The referenced entity at fault, depending on `code`. |
| `match_type` | `string` | Present for `filter_match_type_invalid`: the invalid filter match type. |
| `assignment_type` | `string` | Present for `field_assignment_type_invalid`: the invalid field assignment type. |
| `call_argument` | `string` | Present for `action_call_argument_invalid`: the ID of the invalid call argument. |

> Why can `broken` lag behind the current definition?
> 
> `broken` shows the last verdict Tape *stored*: create, update, `activate` and `validate` never write it, and a failed `activate` returns `409` with the object unchanged. Call `validate` for a current verdict. [The automation object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/object#the-broken-flag) has the full `broken` model.

## Broken-reason codes

The codes use public names, never internal ones. **Where** shows where the fault sits. **Description** is the English `message` that Tape returns with the code.

| Code | Where | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `trigger_variable_missing` | Trigger | The trigger references a variable that no longer exists. |
| `trigger_app_missing` | Trigger | The trigger references an app that no longer exists. |
| `trigger_date_field_not_date` | Trigger | The date-arrived trigger references a calculation field that does not produce a date. |
| `trigger_periodic_week_days_empty` | Trigger | The weekly periodic trigger has no weekdays selected. |
| `trigger_periodic_month_days_empty` | Trigger | The monthly periodic trigger has no days selected. |
| `trigger_updated_fields_empty` | Trigger | The record-updated trigger has an empty list of watched fields. |
| `filter_match_type_invalid` | Filter | A filter condition uses an operator that is not valid in this context. |
| `filter_variable_missing` | Filter | A filter condition references a variable that no longer exists. |
| `filter_value_missing` | Filter | *Reserved.* A filter condition references a value that no longer exists. No validation path returns it, see the note below. |
| `filter_value_variable_missing` | Filter | A filter condition's value references a variable that no longer exists. |
| `filter_value_value_missing` | Filter | A filter condition's value references a value that no longer exists. |
| `filter_user_missing` | Filter | A filter condition references a user that no longer exists. |
| `filter_app_missing` | Filter | A filter condition references an app that no longer exists. |
| `filter_record_missing` | Filter | A filter condition references a record that no longer exists. |
| `filter_option_missing` | Filter | A filter condition references a select option that no longer exists. |
| `field_assignment_type_invalid` | Field assignment | A field assignment has an invalid type. |
| `field_assignment_end_date_disabled` | Field assignment | A field assignment sets an end date on a field that has end dates disabled. |
| `field_assignment_variable_missing` | Field assignment | A field assignment references a field that no longer exists. |
| `field_assignment_value_missing` | Field assignment | A field assignment references a value that no longer exists. |
| `field_assignment_value_variable_missing` | Field assignment | A field assignment's value references a variable that no longer exists. |
| `field_assignment_value_variable_invalid` | Field assignment | A field assignment's value references a variable that is not valid here. |
| `field_assignment_value_value_missing` | Field assignment | A field assignment's value references a value that no longer exists. |
| `field_assignment_user_missing` | Field assignment | A field assignment references a user that no longer exists. |
| `field_assignment_app_missing` | Field assignment | A field assignment references an app that no longer exists. |
| `field_assignment_record_missing` | Field assignment | A field assignment references a record that no longer exists. |
| `field_assignment_option_missing` | Field assignment | A field assignment references a select option that no longer exists. |
| `checklist_property_value_variable_missing` | Checklist property | A checklist property assignment references a variable that no longer exists. |
| `checklist_property_value_value_missing` | Checklist property | A checklist property assignment references a value that no longer exists. |
| `checklist_property_user_missing` | Checklist property | A checklist property assignment references a user that no longer exists. |
| `action_invalid` | Action | An action is invalid. |
| `action_variable_missing` | Action | An action references a variable that no longer exists. |
| `action_value_missing` | Action | An action references a value that no longer exists. |
| `action_user_missing` | Action | An action references a user that no longer exists. |
| `action_app_missing` | Action | An action references an app that no longer exists. |
| `action_app_invalid` | Action | An action references an app that is not valid here. |
| `action_view_missing` | Action | An action references an app view that no longer exists. |
| `action_automation_missing` | Action | An action calls an automation that no longer exists. |
| `action_automation_invalid` | Action | An action calls an automation that is not callable here. |
| `action_call_argument_invalid` | Action | An action passes a call argument that the target automation does not accept. |

> What about `filter_value_missing`?
> 
> `filter_value_missing` is still part of the published `AutomationBrokenReasonCode` type, but no validation path returns it. Treat it as *reserved*: your code can keep handling it, but don't expect it.
> 
> `validate` checks only meaning, and create and [update](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage) already reject a malformed value with `400`. A value that references a deleted field or variable returns `filter_value_variable_missing`. A value that resolves to empty isn't a `validate` fault: it [matches every record when the automation runs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/troubleshooting/filter-values).

# Filters

> The Tape automation filter model — the recursive and/or condition tree, the operators, and the tagged value union.

Use a filter to decide *whether* an automation runs.

A filter is a recursive `and`/`or` tree of conditions that the triggering record must match.

## The tree: groups and conditions

*Filter — "Priority is High AND Amount ≥ 1000"*

```json
{
  "operator": "and",
  "rows": [
    {
      "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 512, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
      "operator": "is_any_of",
      "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [9001] }
    },
    {
      "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 513, "field_type": "number", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
      "operator": "greater_or_equal_than",
      "value": { "type": "number", "number": ["1000"] }
    }
  ]
}
```

A *group* combines its `rows`, nested groups or conditions, with `and` (match all) or `or` (match any). The *root* group has no `id`.

| Property | Type | On | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | Nested nodes | Opaque node ID. Optional on input, Tape creates one when you leave it out. Present on every read. |
| `operator` | `string` | Group | `and` or `or`. |
| `rows` | `array` | Group | Nested groups and conditions. |
| `subject` | `object` | Condition | A [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) to the value being tested: a field, record metadata, a trigger output or an action's file collection. See [v1 limitations](#v1-limitations). |
| `operator` | `string` | Condition | One of the [operators](#operators) below. |
| `value` | `object` | Condition | The tagged comparison value, see [The value union](#the-value-union). Absent for operators without a value. |
| `code` | `array` | Condition | A raw code condition, a [code dynamic value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values). A *script condition* has `code` *instead of* `subject`, `operator` and `value`. |

**General behavior**

-   An automation without a filter has `filter: null` and runs every time.
-   To run without a filter, send `filter: null` explicitly. An explicitly *empty* top-level group (`rows: []`) returns `400`. It narrows nothing and would fire on every record.
-   An empty group is still allowed *inside* an action, for example a `conditional` `condition` that is true every time, or a `match_condition` that keeps everything. The trigger filter already limits which records the automation runs on.

> Where else is this tree used?
> 
> The same public tree (`operator: "and" | "or"`, `rows`) appears everywhere conditions do:
> 
> -   an automation's `filter`,
> -   a control-flow action's `condition`, `break_condition` and `continue_condition`,
> -   a condition inside an action's `config`, for example the `match_condition` of `collect_app_records` or `filter_record_collection`.
> 
> All of them use the same lower-case `operator` and `rows`. See [Actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions).

## Operators

Each operator has a `value_arity`: `none` (no value, for example `is_empty`), `single` or `multiple`. The valid operators differ per field type. [`GET /v1/automation/meta/filter?field_type=…`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) returns the exact set.

| Operator | Arity |  | Operator | Arity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `is` | single |  | `has_any_of` | multiple |
| `is_not` | single |  | `has_all_of` | multiple |
| `contains` | single |  | `has_none_of` | multiple |
| `does_not_contain` | single |  | `is_exactly` | multiple |
| `starts_with` | single |  | `is_any_of` | multiple |
| `ends_with` | single |  | `is_none_of` | multiple |
| `greater_than` | single |  | `has_changed_to_any_of` | multiple |
| `greater_or_equal_than` | single |  | `is_empty` | none |
| `less_than` | single |  | `is_not_empty` | none |
| `less_or_equal_than` | single |  | `is_completed` | none |
| `is_before` | single |  | `is_incomplete` | none |
| `is_after` | single |  | `has_changed` | none |
| `glob_pattern` | single |  |  |  |
| `has_changed_to` | single |  |  |  |

### File name patterns

`glob_pattern` (label **Matches pattern**) checks whether file names match a glob pattern, for example `"*.pdf"`.

-   It works only on subjects that carry files: `single_attachment`, `multi_attachment`, `multi_image`, an action's file collection, webhook payload files and comment attachments.
-   Tape rejects it in `collect_app_records`, `collect_referenced_records`, `collected_records_collect_referenced_records` and in the `search_condition` of a relation field assignment.

### Change tracking

`has_changed`, `has_changed_to` and `has_changed_to_any_of` compare a field with the previous revision of the record.

-   They're valid only under a `record_updated` trigger, or after a `current_record_get_previous_revision` action on the same app. Otherwise `validate` reports the automation as invalid.
-   `has_changed` (label **Has changed**) takes no value.
-   `has_changed_to` (label **Has changed to**) works on subjects with a single choice: status, single category, single user, single relation, last modified by, and on a checklist.
-   `has_changed_to_any_of` (label **Has changed to any of**) works on subjects with multiple choices: multi category, multi user, multi relation.

## The value union

The condition `value` is tagged by `type`, so you can read it without knowing the rules for each field:

| `type` | Payload | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `text`: a [template dynamic value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Text or template comparison. |
| `number` | `number`: a [code dynamic value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | Number comparison as a code expression. |
| `ids` | `ids`: array of `number` or [reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) | A set of option, status, relation or user IDs. |
| `date` | `date`: `{ base?, operator, unit, amount }` | Relative date. `operator` is `"plus"` or `"minus"`, `unit` is `"hour"`, `"day"`, `"week"` or `"month"`. See [Relative dates](#relative-dates). |
| `boolean` | `boolean` | Boolean comparison. Comes from a webhook payload property subject. Sends back without change. |
| `entity_type` | `entity_type`: `string` | Comparison of the comment or reply entity type. Sends back without change. |

[Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app) returns the option IDs for `ids` in `config.settings.options` of each field.

### Relative dates

-   `base` is *optional*. Without it, Tape uses the `current_date` global. Tape stores it on write, so it reads back and sends back unchanged. Set a `base` reference to count from something other than today.
-   `operator` and `unit` only accept the listed values. Anything else returns `400`. Leave them out to keep the defaults `plus` and `day`.
-   `amount` is a code dynamic value: an *array of strings* (for example `["1"]`) or a plain *string* (`"1"`, returned as `["1"]`). A plain *number* (`1`) returns `400`. A read returns the array form, so a retrieved definition sends back unchanged.

### Match the value type to the field

Tape reads a value by its tag, but *writes* it by field. On create and update, Tape picks the value channel from the *type of the subject field*:

-   number and unique ID → `number`
-   date fields → `date`
-   category, status, relation and user → `ids`
-   text → `text`

On create and update:

-   A value whose `type` doesn't match the field's channel returns `400`. The check goes through *all levels* of nested groups. The response names the condition (by its `id`, or by its JSON path, for example `filter.rows[1].rows[0]`) and the tag it expected.
-   An *empty* comparison value returns `400` the same way. So does an *arity* mismatch: a value on an operator with arity `none` such as `is_empty`, or a missing value on an operator that needs one.
-   Existing rows aren't checked again. Definitions saved before this check, or in the automation editor in Tape, can still hold an empty comparison.
-   An *operator* outside the field type's channel is *not* rejected if it's otherwise well-formed, for example a text operator on a number field with a number value. It passes `validate` and never matches when the automation runs.

`meta/filter` returns only operators, not the accepted tag. Match the tag to the field yourself, and use only the operators it returns for the field's type.

> Why does my filter match every record?
> 
> A value built from a *reference* (a field, a variable or the output of an earlier action) passes the write check, but it can resolve to *empty* for a record. An empty value matches everything, so under the default `and` group the filter matches *every* record. [Guard such references](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/troubleshooting/filter-values). A [simulation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) skips the filter, a manual run applies it.

## v1 limitations

-   **A subject needs a condition it can be tested with.** On create and update, a condition's `subject` can be a *field* reference, most *record metadata* references (`app_record_id`, `created_at`, `last_modified_at`, `created_by`, `last_modified_by`), a *trigger output* reference (for example `webhook_payload_property`) or the *file collection* of an earlier action. All of these are writable and send back unchanged. Tokens that only carry a value and can't be tested (`meta_type` `record_id`, `record_url`, `revision`, `all_comments`, the raw `webhook_payload`) and `global` or `custom` references return `400` on write.
-   **Collection-change conditions are read-only.** **Has been added** and **Has been deleted** on an attachment, image or checklist field, and **Changed item contains** on a checklist field, have no public operator. They read as an `{ id, subject }` without an operator and *can't be sent back* unchanged. Other change-tracking conditions use the public operators `has_changed`, `has_changed_to` and `has_changed_to_any_of` and send back without problems.

A `GET` followed by an unchanged `PUT` fails only for an automation with such a collection-change condition, so remove these conditions first. All other subjects send back unchanged, including the `boolean` and `entity_type` value kinds.

# The automation object

> The Tape automation object — its fields, the paused/broken status model, and identifiers.

The automation object describes one automation: its trigger, filter and actions, its state and its timestamps.

Retrieve, create, update, the lifecycle endpoints and delete return it wrapped as `{ "automation": … }`. The [list endpoints](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage) return it in `automations[]`.

*Response*

```json
{
  "automation": {
    "id": 4021,
    "app_id": 87,
    "workspace_id": 12,
    "name": "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead",
    "description": "Notifies the record owner whenever a lead is created.",
    "paused": false,
    "broken": false,
    "broken_reason": null,
    "trigger": { "type": "record_created", "config": {} },
    "filter": {
      "operator": "and",
      "rows": [
        {
          "id": "6a1f…",
          "subject": { "kind": "variable", "source": "field", "field_id": 512, "field_type": "single_category", "previous": false, "collection": false, "triggering": false },
          "operator": "is_any_of",
          "value": { "type": "ids", "ids": [9001] }
        }
      ]
    },
    "actions": [
      { "id": "3f9a2c", "type": "send_email", "group": "action", "config": { "to_address": ["juliet@acme.com"], "subject": ["A new lead was created"] } }
    ],
    "created_at": "2024-05-14 11:12:31",
    "created_at_utc": "2024-05-14 09:12:31",
    "updated_at": "2024-05-20 18:03:08",
    "updated_at_utc": "2024-05-20 16:03:08"
  }
}
```

The example comes from a user whose timezone is two hours ahead of UTC.

## Automation object properties

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `integer` | ID of the automation. | `4021` |
| `app_id` | `integer` | The app the automation belongs to. Only database apps can have automations. | `87` |
| `workspace_id` | `integer` | The workspace the app belongs to. | `12` |
| `name` | `string` | Name of the automation. | `"Email the owner on a new high-priority lead"` |
| `description` | `string` | Optional. Absent when the automation has none. | `"Notifies the record owner whenever a lead is created."` |
| `paused` | `boolean` | Whether the automation is paused. See [Status and lifecycle](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/overview#status-and-lifecycle). | `false` |
| `broken` | `boolean` | Whether the definition can't run. Shows the last verdict Tape *stored*, not your current edit. See [The `broken` flag](#the-broken-flag). | `false` |
| `broken_reason` | `object` | `null` | `{ errors: [...] }` when Tape recorded reasons, otherwise `null`. Can be `null` even when `broken` is `true`, see [The `broken` flag](#the-broken-flag). The entries have the same shape as in [validate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors). | `null` |
| `trigger` | `object` | `null` | The single [trigger](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers) `{ type, config }`, or `null`. | `{ "type": "record_created", "config": {} }` |
| `filter` | `object` | `null` | The root [filter group](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters), or `null` when there is no filter. | See the example above. |
| `actions` | `array` | The ordered list of [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions). `[]` when there are none. | See the example above. |
| `created_at` | `string` | Creation time, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, in your timezone. | `"2024-05-14 11:12:31"` |
| `created_at_utc` | `string` | Same instant as `created_at`, in UTC. | `"2024-05-14 09:12:31"` |
| `updated_at` | `string` | Last-modified time, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, in your timezone. | `"2024-05-20 18:03:08"` |
| `updated_at_utc` | `string` | Same instant as `updated_at`, in UTC. | `"2024-05-20 16:03:08"` |

The object has *no `status` field*. The state is the pair `paused` and `broken`. It also has *no owner or author field* in this release.

## The `broken` flag

`broken` shows the last verdict Tape *stored*. Create, update, `activate` and `validate` never write it, and a failed `activate` returns `409` with the object unchanged. So a newly saved definition that can't run still reads `broken: false`, and `broken_reason` can differ from what [`validate`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) returns.

Tape *does* set `broken: true` when a run finds that a valid automation stopped working, for example because:

-   its filter can't be built anymore,
-   a field it watches is deleted,
-   a connection it uses is removed.

Until such a run, the object still reads `broken: false`: `activate` refuses with `409`, but a manual run or a simulation is accepted and fails. Once `broken` is `true`:

-   the trigger doesn't fire the automation,
-   a manual run or a simulation returns `409`,
-   `broken_reason` can be `null`.

Call [`validate`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) for a current verdict.

## Identifiers

`id`, `app_id` and `workspace_id` are plain JSON *integers*. A [revision](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/revisions) ID is a 64-bit value, sent as a string.

Node IDs inside `filter` and `actions` are opaque *strings*: treat them as handles, not numbers. Tape keeps an ID you send and creates a UUID when you leave it out.

# Triggers

> The nine Tape automation trigger types and how to configure them.

Use one of the nine trigger types to decide *when* an automation runs.

A trigger is a flat object `{ type, config }`, and an automation has zero or one. [`GET /v1/automation/meta/trigger`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/discovery) returns the full, current catalog with the `config_schema` of each type. Build against it instead of hard-coding.

## Trigger types

`Label` is the name that `meta/trigger` returns. **Name in Tape** is the name in the automation editor.

| `type` | Label | Name in Tape | Fires when … |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_created` | Record created | **Record created** | A record is created in the app. |
| `record_updated` | Record updated | **Record updated** | A record is updated, optionally only when specific fields change. |
| `record_deleted` | Record deleted | **Record deleted** | A record is deleted. |
| `record_comment_or_reply_created` | Comment or reply created | **Comment added** | A comment or reply is added to a record. |
| `date_field_arrived` | Date arrived | **Date arrives** | A date from a field is reached, optionally with an offset. |
| `automation_called` | Automation called | **Automation calls** | Another automation calls this one. |
| `periodic` | Periodic | **On schedule** | A recurring schedule is due. |
| `webhook_received` | Webhook received | **Webhook received** | An inbound webhook comes in. |
| `weblink_clicked` | Weblink clicked | **Web link clicked** | Someone opens a generated weblink. |

![Trigger picker in the automation editor with the list of all nine triggers](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/trigger-picker-2de368882811db1d37c91f422fb565c4.png)

## Config

This trigger fires only when the field with ID `512` changes:

*Trigger*

```json
{ "type": "record_updated", "config": { "trigger_on_changes_field_ids": [512] } }
```

Each type has its own `config` shape, described by its `config_schema`. Values can be [dynamic](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/dynamic-values) where the type allows it.

> Which field changes fire `record_updated`?
> 
> `trigger_on_changes_field_ids` has three states:
> 
> -   `null` or left out: fires on a change to *any* field.
> -   A list with field IDs: fires only on changes to those fields.
> -   An *empty `[]`: never fires*. `validate` reports `trigger_updated_fields_empty`.

`app_id` is *not* a config field. Tape takes the app from the automation itself and ignores a legacy `config.app_id`. See [Create an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#create-an-automation).

> Why does Tape reject a config field it returned?
> 
> Some config fields are *set by Tape and read-only*, for example the `webhook_url` of a `webhook_received` trigger. They appear when you read a config, and Tape *rejects them on write*. The `config_schema` marks them with `"readOnly": true` (standard JSON Schema), so remove them before you send a config.

> What are the `_enabled` flags for?
> 
> Some config values only take effect when a boolean next to them, `<field>_enabled`, is `true`. The `automation_called` and `weblink_clicked` triggers pair `triggering_app_ids` with `triggering_app_ids_enabled`, and `custom_variable_defs` with `custom_variable_defs_enabled`.
> 
> A minimal `{}` config is accepted, because all members are optional. Send the paired `_enabled` flag whenever you set its value.

## Set or remove a trigger

-   To set or replace a trigger, use [`PUT /v1/automation/{automation_id}/trigger`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage), where the whole body is the trigger. Or include `trigger` when you [create or update](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage) an automation.
-   To remove a trigger, send `trigger: null` in an update.

# Revisions

> Every automation edit appends an immutable revision — list and retrieve the version history, and roll a definition back.

Use these endpoints to read the version history of an automation and to roll its definition back.

Every change to an automation adds a *revision*: a frozen, unchangeable snapshot of its definition. There is no pointer to an "active version". To [roll back](#roll-back-to-a-revision), retrieve a revision and send its definition back with [`PUT`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#update-an-automation).

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> Both endpoints need **Read automations** (`automations:read`) and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. They work with a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens), an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview) or a [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key). Each request costs `1x` base credits.

## List revisions

Use this endpoint to list the full history of an automation.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}/revision`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/revision \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "revisions": [
    {
      "id": "90071992547409929",
      "automation_id": 4021,
      "created_at": "2024-05-20 18:03:08",
      "created_at_utc": "2024-05-20 16:03:08",
      "name": "Email the owner on a new high-priority lead",
      "paused": false,
      "broken": false,
      "trigger": { "type": "record_created", "config": {} },
      "filter": null,
      "actions": []
    }
  ]
}
```

**General behavior**

-   Revisions are sorted *newest first*.
-   The list has *no pagination*: no `cursor` and no `total`.
-   Simulation snapshots aren't included.

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Retrieve a revision

Use this endpoint to read one revision of an automation.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/{automation_id}/revision/{revision_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/automation/4021/revision/90071992547409929 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

The response is `{ revision }`.

**General behavior**

-   The revision must belong to this automation.
-   The endpoint never reveals which revision IDs exist. See [Errors](#errors).

**Requirements:** `automations:read`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Roll back to a revision

A revision is a *read* snapshot. Its envelope is wider than the [update](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage) body accepts, so a `PUT` of the whole revision fails with `400`.

The first revision in the list is the current state. Pausing and activating add revisions too. Pick the revision whose `filter` and `actions` you want back.

Send back only its definition members: `name`, `trigger`, `filter` and `actions`. The `PUT` needs `automations:edit`. Then [validate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution#validate-an-automation) the automation: an older definition can point to fields that no longer exist.

-   The envelope keys `id`, `automation_id`, `created_at`, `created_at_utc`, `paused` and `broken` aren't writable. The update body rejects unknown keys.
-   A `filter` or action condition with a *collection-change condition* (**Has been added**, **Has been deleted** or **Changed item contains**) has no writable form. Remove it first. See [Filters](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters#v1-limitations).
-   Conditions with `has_changed`, `has_changed_to` and `has_changed_to_any_of` are writable. So are conditions on fields, record metadata, trigger outputs and action outputs.
-   The server-assigned `webhook_url` of a `webhook_received` trigger is on the live automation object, but not in a revision. It never causes a `400` on rollback.

> Why doesn't a rollback restore the description?
> 
> A revision has *no `description`*. `description` keeps its current value, so reset it separately if you need to revert it too.

## The revision object

A revision is a snapshot of the automation's *definition* at one edit.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `string` | The revision ID, a 64-bit value returned as a string. | `"90071992547409929"` |
| `automation_id` | `integer` | The automation this revision belongs to. | `4021` |
| `created_at` | `string` | When the revision was created, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, in your timezone. | `"2024-05-20 18:03:08"` |
| `created_at_utc` | `string` | Same instant as `created_at`, in UTC. | `"2024-05-20 16:03:08"` |
| `name` | `string` | The name at this revision. | `"Email the owner on a new high-priority lead"` |
| `paused` / `broken` | `boolean` | The state at this revision. | `false` |
| `trigger` | `object` | `null` | The [trigger](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers) at this revision. | `{ "type": "record_created", "config": {} }` |
| `filter` | `object` | `null` | The [filter](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters) at this revision. | `null` |
| `actions` | `array` | The [actions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions) at this revision. | `[]` |

A revision has fewer fields than the [automation object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/object). It has no `description`, `broken_reason`, `updated_at`, `app_id` or `workspace_id`.

## Errors

-   An automation ID that isn't an integer returns `400`.
-   A credential that doesn't act on behalf of a user, for example an automation API key, returns `401`.
-   A token without `automations:read` returns `403`.
-   An automation or revision that isn't available to you returns `404`. A `revision_id` that is unknown, malformed or belongs to another automation returns the same `404`.

See [Errors & broken reasons](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/errors) for the Automation API and [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Email

> Use this endpoint to send emails from Tape to people outside Tape.

Use this endpoint to send emails from Tape to people outside Tape.

## Send an email

Use this endpoint to send an email to one or more recipients.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/email/send`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/email/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "to": "riley@acme.com",
    "subject": "Your viewing on Friday",
    "html": "<p>Your viewing of 12 Harbor Street is confirmed for Friday at 10 am.</p>",
    "reply_to": "juliet@acme.com"
}'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "to": "riley@acme.com",
  "subject": "Your viewing on Friday",
  "html": "<p>Your viewing of 12 Harbor Street is confirmed for Friday at 10 am.</p>",
  "reply_to": "juliet@acme.com"
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "status": "SUCCESSFULLY_SCHEDULED"
}
```

Send the recipients in `to`, the subject in `subject` and the formatted body in `html`.

The example sends an email to `riley@acme.com`. When Riley replies, the reply goes to `juliet@acme.com`.

> Did the email reach the recipient?
> 
> Tape hands the email to the mail server during the request. `SUCCESSFULLY_SCHEDULED` means the mail server accepted it, not that it reached the recipient. The API can't check delivery.

**General behavior**

-   Content access doesn't limit this endpoint. A token limited to one workspace can still send email.
-   If the mail server rejects a recipient, Tape tries that recipient again a few times within the same request.
-   Tape limits how many emails an organization sends per day through Tape's own servers. To send more, use your own SMTP server. See [Sender address](#sender-address).

**Requirements:** `email:send`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Errors**

-   A request without a valid recipient in `to`, `cc` or `bcc` returns `400` with `email_send_failure`. The message reads `[EmailSendFailureException] Sending Email failed with reason: Error: No recipients defined`.
-   A mail server that can't be reached, or still rejects the email at the last attempt, returns `400` with `email_send_failure`.
-   An email over your organization's daily limit for Tape's own servers returns `400` with `email_send_failure`.
-   Attachments over the maximum total size return `400` with `validation`. See [Limits](#limits).
-   A file in `attachment_ids` you don't have access to returns `403`.

**Optional body parameters**

-   `cc`, `bcc` and `reply_to`: one email address or a list of them.
-   `from_name`: the sender name your recipients see.
-   `attachment_ids`: a list of file IDs to attach. See [Attachments](#attachments).
-   `from_address` and `smtp_settings_id`: send from your own address. See [Sender address](#sender-address).

### Attachments

`attachment_ids` accepts these file IDs:

-   files in attachment or image fields of records. See [Attachment field value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/attachment).
-   files you uploaded with the [File resource](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/file).
-   files attached to record comments or replies.

You need access to every file you attach.

### Sender address

Without your own email server, Tape sends from `noreply@automations.tapeapp.com`. If you set `reply_to`, Tape sends from `reply@automations.tapeapp.com`. Set `from_name` to show your own sender name.

To send from your own address, add an SMTP account in the **Send an email** action of an automation:

1.  Open an automation and add the action **Send an email**.
2.  Select **Show more**, open the **Account** menu and select **Add account**.
3.  On the **SMTP** tab, enter the user name, password, server address and port, then select **Save account**.
4.  To make the account the default of your organization, open the **Account** menu, select the three dots next to the account and select **Set as default**.

Tape then sends through your organization's default SMTP account. To pick another one, set `smtp_settings_id`.

The API has no endpoint that lists SMTP accounts, and the **Account** menu doesn't show the ID. To find it in the automation editor:

1.  In a **Send an email** action, select the account in the **Account** menu.
2.  In the action menu, select **Duplicate**.
3.  In the action menu of the copy, select **Turn into** → **Execute script**. The script shows the ID in `smtp_settings_id`.
4.  Remove the copy.

The [automation API](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/manage#retrieve-an-automation) returns the same ID as `smtp_account_id` of the action.

Set the sender address in `from_address`. Without it, Tape uses the user name of the SMTP server.

Your SMTP server must be allowed to send emails for this address. Otherwise, delivery fails.

The example sends an email from `juliet@acme.com` to two recipients, with two people in copy. It attaches the file with ID `42`, a file in an attachment field of a record.

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/email/send \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "from_address": "juliet@acme.com",
    "from_name": "Juliet from Acme",
    "to": ["riley@acme.com", "sam@acme.com"],
    "subject": "Offer for 12 Harbor Street",
    "html": "<p>The signed offer is attached.</p>",
    "cc": ["will@acme.com", "nora@acme.com"],
    "attachment_ids": [42]
}'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "from_address": "juliet@acme.com",
  "from_name": "Juliet from Acme",
  "to": ["riley@acme.com", "sam@acme.com"],
  "subject": "Offer for 12 Harbor Street",
  "html": "<p>The signed offer is attached.</p>",
  "cc": ["will@acme.com", "nora@acme.com"],
  "attachment_ids": [42]
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "status": "SUCCESSFULLY_SCHEDULED"
}
```

## Limits

Tape enforces these limits for each email:

| Variable | Limit |
| --- | --- |
| Maximum total attachment size | 20 MB |

## Rate limit credits

Sending an email costs the [base request cost](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits) of 10 credits, whatever the number of recipients in `to`, `cc` and `bcc`.

One email to several recipients uses fewer credits than separate emails to each of them. Recipients in `to` and `cc` see each other. Put recipients in `bcc` if they shouldn't, and check that your choice fits your privacy policy.

# Attachment field value

> Use an attachment field value to read and write the files of a record.

Use an attachment field value to read and write the files of a record.

Each value of an [attachment field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/attachment) is one file. A `single_attachment` field holds at most one file. A `multi_attachment` field holds several files.

Attachment fields accept any file type. For a field that holds only images, see [Image field value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/image).

*Attachment field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "letter_of_recommendation",
  "label": "Letter of recommendation",
  "type": "file",
  "field_type": "single_attachment",
  "values": [
    {
      "value": {
        "file_id": 100,
        "name": "letter-of-recommendation.pdf",
        "size": 123000,
        "mimetype": "application/pdf",
        "download_url": "https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/tape-attachments/9d43730ffad8d249e3ac313193cd83?Expires=1772442000&Signature=VzrbvlfI35hp4iU7jMa%2BK%2FnutPU%3D",
        "view_url": "https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/tape-attachments/9d43730ffad8d249e3ac313193cd83?Expires=1772442000&Signature=Hk2c8vQx1pLm9sTnW4yR%2FaB7dEo%3D",
        "link": "https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/tape-attachments/9d43730ffad8d249e3ac313193cd83?Expires=1772442000&Signature=VzrbvlfI35hp4iU7jMa%2BK%2FnutPU%3D",
        "created_by": null,
        "created_on": "2026-03-02 09:15:00",
        "created_on_utc": "2026-03-02 08:15:00",
        "last_modified_on": "2026-03-02 09:15:00",
        "last_modified_on_utc": "2026-03-02 08:15:00"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"file"` for both attachment field types. | `"file"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_attachment"` or `"multi_attachment"`. | `"single_attachment"` |
| `values[].value.file_id` | `number` | ID of the file in this field. | `100` |
| `values[].value.name` | `string` | File name. | `"letter-of-recommendation.pdf"` |
| `values[].value.size` | `number` | File size in bytes. | `123000` |
| `values[].value.mimetype` | `string` | Media type of the file. | `"application/pdf"` |
| `values[].value.download_url` | `string` | Signed URL that downloads the file. |  |
| `values[].value.view_url` | `string` | Signed URL that opens the file in the browser. |  |
| `values[].value.link` | `string` | Same as `download_url`, for older integrations. Use `download_url` instead. |  |
| `values[].value.created_by` | `null` | Not filled. The value is `null`. | `null` |
| `values[].value.created_on` | `string` | When the file was added, in your timezone. | `"2026-03-02 09:15:00"` |
| `values[].value.created_on_utc` | `string` | When the file was added, in UTC. | `"2026-03-02 08:15:00"` |
| `values[].value.last_modified_on` | `string` | When the file last changed, in your timezone. | `"2026-03-02 09:15:00"` |
| `values[].value.last_modified_on_utc` | `string` | When the file last changed, in UTC. | `"2026-03-02 08:15:00"` |

The signed URLs expire after some hours. Retrieve the record again to get new ones.

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out. They also shorten each file to `file_id`, `name`, `size` and `mimetype`.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to attach files to a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "name": "Zoe Maxwell",
      "letter_of_recommendation": "temporary-file-1",
      "hr_documents": ["temporary-file-2", "temporary-file-3"]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "name": "Zoe Maxwell",
    "letter_of_recommendation": "temporary-file-1",
    "hr_documents": ["temporary-file-2", "temporary-file-3"]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Zoe Maxwell",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Zoe Maxwell" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "letter_of_recommendation",
      "label": "Letter of recommendation",
      "type": "file",
      "field_type": "single_attachment",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 100,
            "name": "letter-of-recommendation.pdf",
            "size": 123000,
            "mimetype": "application/pdf"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 3,
      "external_id": "hr_documents",
      "label": "HR documents",
      "type": "file",
      "field_type": "multi_attachment",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 101,
            "name": "employment-contract.pdf",
            "size": 150000,
            "mimetype": "application/pdf"
          }
        },
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 102,
            "name": "tax-form.pdf",
            "size": 160000,
            "mimetype": "application/pdf"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

First, [upload the files](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/file#upload-a-file). Each upload returns a temporary file ID like `temporary-file-1`. Then send these IDs in the field values.

The example creates the applicant "Zoe Maxwell". It sets the "Letter of recommendation" field (ID `2`, type `single_attachment`, slug `letter_of_recommendation`) and the "HR documents" field (ID `3`, type `multi_attachment`, slug `hr_documents`).

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   A field value accepts these file IDs:
    -   Temporary file IDs from your own uploads, like `"temporary-file-1"`.
    -   File IDs of comment and reply attachments, like `"comment-file-12"` or `"reply-file-7"`. See [Record comment](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record-comment).
    -   The `file_id` of a file in another attachment or image field, as a number. Tape copies the file, and the copy gets a new `file_id`.
-   Tape also accepts objects like `{ "file_id": "temporary-file-1" }` or `{ "value": "temporary-file-1" }`, and arrays of these.
-   Send one file to a `single_attachment` field. If you send an array, Tape uses its first file.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A temporary file ID that you didn't upload yourself returns `403`.
-   A string that isn't a valid file ID returns `400`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 100,
            "name": "letter-of-recommendation.pdf",
            "size": 123000,
            "mimetype": "application/pdf"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 3,
      "external_id": "hr_documents",
      "label": "HR documents",
      "type": "file",
      "field_type": "multi_attachment",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 101,

          }
        },

## Record update

Use the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to change the files of a record.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "letter_of_recommendation": "temporary-file-4",
      "hr_documents": ["temporary-file-5", 102]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "letter_of_recommendation": "temporary-file-4",
    "hr_documents": ["temporary-file-5", 102]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Zoe Maxwell",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Zoe Maxwell" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "letter_of_recommendation",
      "label": "Letter of recommendation",
      "type": "file",
      "field_type": "single_attachment",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 103,
            "name": "letter-of-recommendation-signed.pdf",
            "size": 125000,
            "mimetype": "application/pdf"
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 3,
      "external_id": "hr_documents",
      "label": "HR documents",
      "type": "file",
      "field_type": "multi_attachment",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 102,
            "name": "tax-form.pdf",
            "size": 160000,
            "mimetype": "application/pdf"
          }
        },
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 104,
            "name": "employment-contract-signed.pdf",
            "size": 152000,
            "mimetype": "application/pdf"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example replaces the letter of recommendation of the applicant with ID `1` with a new upload. In "HR documents", it adds a new upload and keeps the file with ID `102`. The file with ID `101` isn't in the request, so Tape removes it from the field.

**General behavior**

-   The files in the request replace the old files. To keep a file, send its `file_id` again.
-   In a `multi_attachment` field, a file that's already in the field keeps its `file_id`.
-   Tape lists the files in the order they were added, not in the order of the request. A kept file comes before a new one.
-   To clear the field, send `null` or an empty array `[]`.
-   You can't clear a required field. The request returns `400`.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "hr_documents": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation). An update also returns this error:

-   A numeric `file_id` that isn't a positive whole number, like `1.5`, returns `400` with `validation` and the message `… Expected a valid existing attachment ID …`. A number in a string, like `"100"`, returns the same error.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.
