# Calculation field value

> Use a calculation field value to read the computed value of a record.

Use a calculation field value to read the computed value of a record.

Tape computes the value of a [calculation field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/calculation) from its script. The value is text, a number or a date, depending on the `return_type` of the field. Text can be plain text or rich text with Markdown or HTML.

*Calculation field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 4,
  "external_id": "vacation_days_left",
  "label": "Vacation Days Left",
  "type": "calculation",
  "field_type": "calculation",
  "values": [
    {
      "value": 12,
      "value_string": "12",
      "decimal": 12,
      "start": null,
      "start_utc": null,
      "start_date": null,
      "start_date_utc": null,
      "start_time": null,
      "start_time_utc": null
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"calculation"`. | `"calculation"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"calculation"`. | `"calculation"` |
| `values[].value` | `string` or `number` | The computed value. A string for text, a number for numbers, the date as text for dates. | `12` |
| `values[].value_string` | `string` | The value as text. For numbers, with the decimal places and the unit of the field. | `"12"` |
| `values[].decimal` | `number` or `null` | Number results only. The number. `null` otherwise. | `12` |
| `values[].start` | `string` or `null` | Date results only. Date and time in your [timezone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone). `null` otherwise. | `"2026-12-01 09:00:00"` |
| `values[].start_date` | `string` or `null` | Date results only. The date in your timezone. `null` otherwise. | `"2026-12-01"` |
| `values[].start_time` | `string` or `null` | Date results only. The time in your timezone. `null` for a date without time and for other results. | `"09:00:00"` |
| `values[].start_utc`, `values[].start_date_utc`, `values[].start_time_utc` | `string` or `null` | Date results only. The same values in UTC. `null` otherwise. | `"2026-12-01 08:00:00"` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Record retrieval

Use the [retrieve record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-a-record) to read the calculation values of a record.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Juliet Adams",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 4,
      "external_id": "vacation_days_left",
      "label": "Vacation Days Left",
      "type": "calculation",
      "field_type": "calculation",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": 12,
          "value_string": "12",
          "decimal": 12,
          "start": null,
          "start_utc": null,
          "start_date": null,
          "start_date_utc": null,
          "start_time": null,
          "start_time_utc": null
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 5,
      "external_id": "next_review",
      "label": "Next Review",
      "type": "calculation",
      "field_type": "calculation",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": "2026-12-01 09:00",
          "value_string": "2026-12-01 09:00",
          "decimal": null,
          "start": "2026-12-01 09:00:00",
          "start_utc": "2026-12-01 08:00:00",
          "start_date": "2026-12-01",
          "start_date_utc": "2026-12-01",
          "start_time": "09:00:00",
          "start_time_utc": "08:00:00"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 6,
      "external_id": "profile_link",
      "label": "Profile Link",
      "type": "calculation",
      "field_type": "calculation",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": "<a href='https://acme.com/team/juliet' target='_blank'>Team profile</a>",
          "value_string": "<a href='https://acme.com/team/juliet' target='_blank'>Team profile</a>",
          "decimal": null,
          "start": null,
          "start_utc": null,
          "start_date": null,
          "start_date_utc": null,
          "start_time": null,
          "start_time_utc": null
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example reads an employee record with three calculation fields: "Vacation Days Left" returns a number, "Next Review" a date and "Profile Link" HTML.

**General behavior**

-   Tape computes calculation values. It ignores them in create and update requests and returns no error. See [Read-only field values](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/overview#field-type).
-   A calculation that never had a result isn't in `fields`. One whose result became empty, for example after you clear a value it uses, stays in `fields` with an empty `values` array.
-   A number result of 0 also comes back with an empty `values` array.
-   Tape computes the result after the write. The response to a create or update can still show the previous result, so read the record again for the new one.
-   For a date result, `value` holds the date and the time without seconds.

**Requirements:** `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Reading calculation values has no field-specific errors. See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Category field value

> Use a category field value to read and set the selected options of a record.

Use a category field value to read and set the selected options of a record.

The value of a [category field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/category) is a list of selected options. Each element of `values` holds one option with its `id`, `text` and `color`. A `single_category` field holds at most one option, a `multi_category` field any number.

*Category field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "products",
  "label": "Products",
  "type": "category",
  "field_type": "multi_category",
  "values": [
    { "value": { "id": 5, "text": "Solar panels", "color": "DEA700" } },
    { "value": { "id": 6, "text": "Battery storage", "color": "00866A" } }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"category"` for both category field types. | `"category"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_category"` or `"multi_category"`. | `"multi_category"` |
| `values[].value.id` | `number` | ID of the selected option. | `5` |
| `values[].value.text` | `string` | Label of the selected option. | `"Solar panels"` |
| `values[].value.color` | `string` | Color of the option as a hex value without `#`. | `"DEA700"` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to select options on a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "pipeline_stage": "Contacted",
      "products": [5, 6]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "pipeline_stage": "Contacted",
    "products": [5, 6]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Contacted",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "pipeline_stage",
      "label": "Pipeline Stage",
      "type": "category",
      "field_type": "single_category",
      "values": [
        { "value": { "id": 2, "text": "Contacted", "color": "0077DE" } }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "products",
      "label": "Products",
      "type": "category",
      "field_type": "multi_category",
      "values": [
        { "value": { "id": 5, "text": "Solar panels", "color": "DEA700" } },
        { "value": { "id": 6, "text": "Battery storage", "color": "00866A" } }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example creates a lead with the "Pipeline Stage" field (ID `1`, type `single_category`, slug `pipeline_stage`) and the "Products" field (ID `2`, type `multi_category`, slug `products`). It selects "Contacted" by its label and two products by their option IDs.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Select an option by its ID or by its label. Tape compares labels case-insensitively and ignores spaces at the start and the end.
-   Find the option IDs in `config.settings.options` of the field, for example with [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app).
-   Send one option or an array of options. Tape also accepts `{ "id": 5 }`, `{ "value": 5 }` and the option objects of a record response.
-   A number selects the option with that ID. If no option has that ID, Tape compares the number with the labels.
-   A `single_category` field keeps the first option that matches.
-   If two options share a label, select the option by its ID.
-   Tape skips a label that matches no option. To get a `400` instead, add the query parameter `reject_unresolvable_option_values=true`.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A label that two options share returns `400`.
-   A number that matches neither an option ID nor a label of the field returns `400`.
-   A value that matches no option returns `400` if you add `reject_unresolvable_option_values=true`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

## Record update

Use the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to change the selected options of a record.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "pipeline_stage": 3,
      "products": ["Battery storage"]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "pipeline_stage": 3,
    "products": ["Battery storage"]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Won",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "pipeline_stage",
      "label": "Pipeline Stage",
      "type": "category",
      "field_type": "single_category",
      "values": [
        { "value": { "id": 3, "text": "Won", "color": "00866A" } }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "products",
      "label": "Products",
      "type": "category",
      "field_type": "multi_category",
      "values": [
        { "value": { "id": 6, "text": "Battery storage", "color": "00866A" } }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example moves the lead with ID `1` to "Won" (option ID `3`) and keeps only "Battery storage" in the "Products" field.

**General behavior**

-   The options you send replace the selected options.
-   To clear the field, send `null`, an empty string `""` or an empty array `[]`.
-   You can't clear a required field. The request returns `400`.
-   A value in which no option matches clears the field. To get a `400` instead, add the query parameter `reject_unresolvable_option_values=true`.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "products": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation).

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Checklist field value

> Use a checklist field value to read and write the tasks of a record.

Use a checklist field value to read and write the tasks of a record.

The value of a [checklist field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/checklist) is a list of tasks. Each element of `values` is one task with its title, description, due date, assignee, priority and completion state.

*Checklist field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "onboarding_tasks",
  "label": "Onboarding Tasks",
  "type": "checklist",
  "field_type": "checklist",
  "values": [
    {
      "id": 300,
      "title": "Order laptop",
      "description": "14-inch, with docking station.",
      "due_at": "2026-03-02 00:00:00",
      "due_at_date": "2026-03-02",
      "due_at_time": null,
      "due_at_utc": "2026-03-02 00:00:00",
      "due_at_date_utc": "2026-03-02",
      "due_at_time_utc": null,
      "assignee_user_id": 600,
      "assignee_user": {
        "user_id": 600,
        "type": "user",
        "name": "Will Dawson",
        "org_id": 1,
        "mail": ["will@acme.com"]
      },
      "priority": "high",
      "completed": false,
      "completed_at": null,
      "completed_at_utc": null
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"checklist"`. | `"checklist"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"checklist"`. | `"checklist"` |
| `values[].id` | `number` | ID of the task. Send it with the title in an update to keep the task. | `300` |
| `values[].title` | `string` | Title of the task. | `"Order laptop"` |
| `values[].description` | `string` | Description of the task. | `"14-inch, with docking station."` |
| `values[].due_at` | `string` or `null` | Due date in your timezone, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`. | `"2026-03-02 00:00:00"` |
| `values[].due_at_date` | `string` or `null` | Date part of `due_at`. | `"2026-03-02"` |
| `values[].due_at_time` | `string` or `null` | Time part of `due_at`. `null` for a whole calendar day. | `null` |
| `values[].due_at_utc`, `due_at_date_utc`, `due_at_time_utc` | `string` or `null` | The due date in UTC, in the same three parts. | `"2026-03-02 00:00:00"` |
| `values[].assignee_user_id` | `number` or `null` | User ID of the assignee. | `600` |
| `values[].assignee_user` | `object` or `null` | The assignee with `user_id`, `type`, `name`, `org_id` and `mail`. |  |
| `values[].priority` | `string` or `null` | `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"` or `"urgent"`. | `"high"` |
| `values[].completed` | `boolean` | Whether the task is done. | `false` |
| `values[].completed_at` | `string` or `null` | When the task was completed, in your timezone. | `null` |
| `values[].completed_at_utc` | `string` or `null` | When the task was completed, in UTC. | `null` |

Due dates follow the rules of date field values: a whole calendar day has `due_at_time: null`. See [Date & timezone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone#calendar-days).

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to add tasks to a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "name": "Ava Chen",
      "onboarding_tasks": [
        {
          "title": "Order laptop",
          "description": "14-inch, with docking station.",
          "due_at": "2026-03-02",
          "assignee_user_id": 600,
          "priority": "high"
        },
        {
          "title": "Set up email account",
          "due_at": "2026-03-02 15:00",
          "assignee_user_id": 601
        },
        "Book welcome lunch"
      ]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "name": "Ava Chen",
    "onboarding_tasks": [
      {
        "title": "Order laptop",
        "description": "14-inch, with docking station.",
        "due_at": "2026-03-02",
        "assignee_user_id": 600,
        "priority": "high"
      },
      {
        "title": "Set up email account",
        "due_at": "2026-03-02 15:00",
        "assignee_user_id": 601
      },
      "Book welcome lunch"
    ]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Ava Chen",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Ava Chen" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "onboarding_tasks",
      "label": "Onboarding Tasks",
      "type": "checklist",
      "field_type": "checklist",
      "values": [
        {
          "id": 300,
          "title": "Order laptop",
          "description": "14-inch, with docking station.",
          "due_at": "2026-03-02 00:00:00",
          "due_at_date": "2026-03-02",
          "due_at_time": null,
          "due_at_utc": "2026-03-02 00:00:00",
          "due_at_date_utc": "2026-03-02",
          "due_at_time_utc": null,
          "assignee_user_id": 600,
          "assignee_user": {
            "user_id": 600,
            "type": "user",
            "name": "Will Dawson",
            "org_id": 1,
            "mail": ["will@acme.com"]
          },
          "priority": "high",
          "completed": false,
          "completed_at": null,
          "completed_at_utc": null
        },
        {
          "id": 301,
          "title": "Set up email account",
          "description": "",
          "due_at": "2026-03-02 16:00:00",
          "due_at_date": "2026-03-02",
          "due_at_time": "16:00:00",
          "due_at_utc": "2026-03-02 15:00:00",
          "due_at_date_utc": "2026-03-02",
          "due_at_time_utc": "15:00:00",
          "assignee_user_id": 601,
          "assignee_user": {
            "user_id": 601,
            "type": "user",
            "name": "Juliet Adams",
            "org_id": 1,
            "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"]
          },
          "priority": null,
          "completed": false,
          "completed_at": null,
          "completed_at_utc": null
        },
        {
          "id": 302,
          "title": "Book welcome lunch",
          "description": "",
          "due_at": null,
          "due_at_date": null,
          "due_at_time": null,
          "due_at_utc": null,
          "due_at_date_utc": null,
          "due_at_time_utc": null,
          "assignee_user_id": null,
          "assignee_user": null,
          "priority": null,
          "completed": false,
          "completed_at": null,
          "completed_at_utc": null
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example creates the new hire "Ava Chen" with three tasks in the "Onboarding Tasks" field (ID `2`, type `checklist`, slug `onboarding_tasks`). The first task is due on a whole day, the second at 15:00 UTC, the third is a plain title. The responses on this page belong to a user in the `Europe/Berlin` timezone (UTC+1 in March).

The app also has a "Name" text field (ID `1`, slug `name`), which the [Checklist field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/checklist#app-creation) example leaves out. Use the field IDs and slugs of your app.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Send an array of tasks. A task is an object or a plain string, which becomes the title.
-   Set the assignee with `assignee_user_id`, the user ID of a user of your organization. Tape also accepts `assignee`.
-   Set `priority` to `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"` or `"urgent"`. Tape reads it case-insensitively.
-   Send `due_at` as `YYYY-MM-DD` for a whole day or with a time for a point in time.
-   Tape reads a time without an offset as UTC. To send your local time instead, add the query parameter `apply_user_timezone_on_date_inputs=true`. Tape never shifts `due_at_utc`.
-   Send `"completed": true` to create a task that's done.
-   Tape removes spaces at the start and the end of titles and descriptions.
-   A required checklist field needs at least one task on a new record. An empty array `[]` counts as missing.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A `priority` other than `"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"` or `"urgent"` returns `400` with `validation`.
-   A `due_at` that isn't a date or a date with a time returns `400` with `validation`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

## Record retrieval

The example marks "Order laptop" (ID `300`) as done and gives "Set up email account" (ID `301`) to Will Dawson with urgent priority. It removes "Book welcome lunch" and adds a new task "Add to payroll".

**General behavior**

-   The tasks you send replace the whole list. Send every task you want to keep.
-   A task with `id` updates that task. A task without `id` becomes a new task.
-   Send the properties you want to keep for each task, like `due_at` or `assignee_user_id`.
-   To write back a due date from a response, send `due_at_utc`. Tape reads it as UTC.
-   To clear the field, send `null` or an empty array `[]`. This also works for a required checklist field.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "onboarding_tasks": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A task without a title returns `400`. Every task in an update needs a title, so a typo can't replace your list with empty tasks.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Date field value

> Use a date field value to read and write the dates and date ranges of a record.

Use a date field value to read and write the dates and date ranges of a record.

The value of a [date field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/date) is one object in `values`. It holds the start date in six properties: three in the timezone of the user who makes the request, three in UTC. A `range_date` value can add the same six properties for the end date.

For the formats and the timezone rules, see [Date & timezone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone).

*Date field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 1,
  "external_id": "site_visit",
  "label": "Site Visit",
  "type": "date",
  "field_type": "single_date",
  "values": [
    {
      "start": "2026-03-10 09:30:00",
      "start_date": "2026-03-10",
      "start_time": "09:30:00",
      "start_utc": "2026-03-10 08:30:00",
      "start_date_utc": "2026-03-10",
      "start_time_utc": "08:30:00"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"date"` for both date field types. | `"date"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_date"` or `"range_date"`. | `"single_date"` |
| `values[].start` | `string` | Start as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` in your timezone. | `"2026-03-10 09:30:00"` |
| `values[].start_date` | `string` | Date part of `start`. | `"2026-03-10"` |
| `values[].start_time` | `string` or `null` | Time part of `start`. `null` for a whole calendar day. | `"09:30:00"` |
| `values[].start_utc` | `string` | Start in UTC. | `"2026-03-10 08:30:00"` |
| `values[].start_date_utc` | `string` | Date part of `start_utc`. | `"2026-03-10"` |
| `values[].start_time_utc` | `string` or `null` | Time part of `start_utc`. `null` for a whole calendar day. | `"08:30:00"` |
| `values[].end`, `end_date`, `end_time`, `end_utc`, `end_date_utc`, `end_time_utc` | `string` or `null` | `range_date` only, if the value has an end date. Same format as the start properties. | `"2026-04-17 00:00:00"` |

A whole calendar day has `start_time: null`, and its local and UTC properties are equal. Tape doesn't convert a calendar day between timezones. See [Calendar days](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone#calendar-days).

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to set dates on a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "site_visit": "2026-03-10 08:30",
      "installation_window": "2026-03-23 - 2026-03-27"
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "site_visit": "2026-03-10 08:30",
    "installation_window": "2026-03-23 - 2026-03-27"
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Tuesday, 10. March 2026",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "site_visit",
      "label": "Site Visit",
      "type": "date",
      "field_type": "single_date",
      "values": [
        {
          "start": "2026-03-10 09:30:00",
          "start_date": "2026-03-10",
          "start_time": "09:30:00",
          "start_utc": "2026-03-10 08:30:00",
          "start_date_utc": "2026-03-10",
          "start_time_utc": "08:30:00"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "installation_window",
      "label": "Installation Window",
      "type": "date",
      "field_type": "range_date",
      "values": [
        {
          "start": "2026-03-23 00:00:00",
          "start_date": "2026-03-23",
          "start_time": null,
          "start_utc": "2026-03-23 00:00:00",
          "start_date_utc": "2026-03-23",
          "start_time_utc": null,
          "end": "2026-03-27 00:00:00",
          "end_date": "2026-03-27",
          "end_time": null,
          "end_utc": "2026-03-27 00:00:00",
          "end_date_utc": "2026-03-27",
          "end_time_utc": null
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example creates an installation with two fields. "Site Visit" (ID `1`, type `single_date`, slug `site_visit`) has time enabled. "Installation Window" (ID `2`, type `range_date`, slug `installation_window`) has time disabled.

The responses on this page belong to a user in the `Europe/Berlin` timezone (UTC+1 until daylight saving time starts on March 29, 2026).

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Send `YYYY-MM-DD` for a whole calendar day and `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` for a point in time.
-   For a `range_date` value, send `"<start> - <end>"` or an object with `start` and `end`. Tape also reads `start_date` and `end_date`, `start_utc` and `end_utc`, and an array with one value.
-   For a `single_date` value, don't send only `start_date` and `start_time`. Tape then saves no value and returns no error. Use `start` or `start_utc` for a date with time.
-   Tape reads a point in time without an offset as UTC. Here, `08:30` UTC reads back as `09:30` in Berlin.
-   To send a time in another timezone, add its offset, like `2026-03-10 09:30:00+01:00`.
-   To send your local time without an offset, add the query parameter `apply_user_timezone_on_date_inputs=true`. Tape never shifts `start_utc`, `end_utc` or a value with its own offset.
-   The `time` setting of the field decides what Tape stores. With `"disabled"`, Tape keeps only the date. With `"required"`, a bare date becomes midnight UTC. With `"enabled"`, Tape stores what you send.
-   You can write a value from a record response back unchanged. Its `_utc` properties take precedence.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A value without an end date returns `400` if the `range_date` field has `"end": "required"`.
-   A start after the end returns `400`.
-   An end date without a start date returns `400`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "site_visit",
      "label": "Site Visit",
      "type": "date",
      "field_type": "single_date",
      "values": [
        {
          "start": "2026-03-10 09:30:00",
          "start_date": "2026-03-10",
          "start_time": "09:30:00",
          "start_utc": "2026-03-10 08:30:00",

        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "installation_window",
      "label": "Installation Window",
      "type": "date",
      "field_type": "range_date",
      "values": [

          "start": "2026-03-23 00:00:00",

        }

**General behavior**

-   Tape returns the unsuffixed properties in the timezone setting of the user who owns the token. The `_utc` properties are the same for every user.

**Requirements:** `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Record update

Use the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to change the dates of a record.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT "https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1?apply_user_timezone_on_date_inputs=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "site_visit": "2026-03-12 14:00",
      "installation_window": { "start": "2026-03-30", "end": "2026-04-03" }
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "site_visit": "2026-03-12 14:00",
    "installation_window": { "start": "2026-03-30", "end": "2026-04-03" }
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Thursday, 12. March 2026",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "site_visit",
      "label": "Site Visit",
      "type": "date",
      "field_type": "single_date",
      "values": [
        {
          "start": "2026-03-12 14:00:00",
          "start_date": "2026-03-12",
          "start_time": "14:00:00",
          "start_utc": "2026-03-12 13:00:00",
          "start_date_utc": "2026-03-12",
          "start_time_utc": "13:00:00"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "installation_window",
      "label": "Installation Window",
      "type": "date",
      "field_type": "range_date",
      "values": [
        {
          "start": "2026-03-30 00:00:00",
          "start_date": "2026-03-30",
          "start_time": null,
          "start_utc": "2026-03-30 00:00:00",
          "start_date_utc": "2026-03-30",
          "start_time_utc": null,
          "end": "2026-04-03 00:00:00",
          "end_date": "2026-04-03",
          "end_time": null,
          "end_utc": "2026-04-03 00:00:00",
          "end_date_utc": "2026-04-03",
          "end_time_utc": null
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example moves the site visit of the record with ID `1` to 14:00 Berlin time and the installation to the following week. It adds `apply_user_timezone_on_date_inputs=true`, so Tape reads `14:00` in the user's timezone. The range uses the object form.

**General behavior**

-   The new date replaces the old date.
-   To clear the field, send `null`.
-   You can't clear a required field. The request returns `400`.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "installation_window": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation).

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Email field value

> Use an email field value to read and write the email addresses of a record.

Use an email field value to read and write the email addresses of a record.

The value of an [email field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/email) is a list of email addresses in `values`. Each email address has an `id`, the address in `value` and a type label in `type`.

*Email field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "email",
  "label": "Email",
  "type": "email",
  "field_type": "multi_email",
  "values": [
    {
      "id": 100,
      "value": "juliet@acme.com",
      "type": "work",
      "created_at": "2026-11-11 10:15:00",
      "created_at_utc": "2026-11-11 09:15:00",
      "last_modified_at": "2026-11-11 10:15:00",
      "last_modified_at_utc": "2026-11-11 09:15:00",
      "created_by_user_id": 1,
      "created_by_workflow_def_id": null,
      "created_by_share_session_id": null,
      "last_modified_by_user_id": 1,
      "last_modified_by_workflow_def_id": null,
      "last_modified_by_share_session_id": null
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"email"` for an email field. | `"email"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"multi_email"`. | `"multi_email"` |
| `values[].id` | `number` | ID of the email address. Send it with the email address in an update to keep the ID. | `100` |
| `values[].value` | `string` | The email address. | `"juliet@acme.com"` |
| `values[].type` | `string` | Type label: `"work"`, `"home"`, `"other"` or the text of a custom label of the field. | `"work"` |
| `values[].created_at`, `values[].last_modified_at` | `string` | When the email address was added and last changed, in your timezone. | `"2026-11-11 10:15:00"` |
| `values[].created_at_utc`, `values[].last_modified_at_utc` | `string` | The same times in UTC. | `"2026-11-11 09:15:00"` |
| `values[].created_by_user_id`, `values[].last_modified_by_user_id` | `number` or `null` | ID of the user who added or last changed the email address. | `1` |
| `values[].created_by_workflow_def_id`, `values[].last_modified_by_workflow_def_id` | `number` or `null` | ID of the automation that added or last changed the email address. | `null` |
| `values[].created_by_share_session_id`, `values[].last_modified_by_share_session_id` | `string` or `null` | Session ID (UUID) of an anonymous visitor who added or changed the email address through a shared link. | `null` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out. They also leave out the times and author IDs of each email address.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to set email addresses on a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "name": "Juliet Adams",
      "email": [
        { "type": "work", "email": "juliet@acme.com" },
        { "type": "home", "email": "juliet.adams@acme.com" }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "name": "Juliet Adams",
    "email": [
      { "type": "work", "email": "juliet@acme.com" },
      { "type": "home", "email": "juliet.adams@acme.com" }
    ]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Juliet Adams",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Juliet Adams" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "email",
      "label": "Email",
      "type": "email",
      "field_type": "multi_email",
      "values": [
        { "id": 100, "value": "juliet@acme.com", "type": "work" },
        { "id": 101, "value": "juliet.adams@acme.com", "type": "home" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example sets two email addresses in the "Email" field (ID `2`, type `multi_email`, slug `email`) of a new contact.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Send an array of email addresses. Each one is an object `{ "email": "...", "type": "..." }` or a string. `value` works in place of `email`.
-   Tape reads `type` case-insensitively. Without `type`, or with a `type` Tape doesn't know, the email address gets the label `work`.
-   A `type` that matches the text of a custom label of the field (not case-sensitive) gets that label.
-   If the field's `label_setting` is `"none"`, Tape ignores `type`.
-   Tape removes spaces at the start and the end of each email address and skips empty ones.
-   Tape doesn't check the format of an email address.
-   A required email field needs at least one email address on a new record. An empty array `[]` counts as missing.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A `type` that matches more than one custom label of the field returns `400`. Use a unique label.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

## Record retrieval

Use the [retrieve record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-a-record) to read the email addresses of a record.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Juliet Adams",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Juliet Adams" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "email",
      "label": "Email",
      "type": "email",
      "field_type": "multi_email",
      "values": [
        { "id": 100, "value": "juliet@acme.com", "type": "work" },
        { "id": 101, "value": "juliet.adams@acme.com", "type": "home" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**General behavior**

-   An email address without a label shows `"type": "work"`. This includes all email addresses of a field with `"label_setting": "none"`.

**Requirements:** `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Record update

Use the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to change the email addresses of a record.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "email": [
        { "id": 100, "type": "work", "email": "juliet.adams@acme.com" },
        { "type": "other", "email": "sales@acme.com" }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "email": [
      { "id": 100, "type": "work", "email": "juliet.adams@acme.com" },
      { "type": "other", "email": "sales@acme.com" }
    ]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Juliet Adams",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Juliet Adams" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "email",
      "label": "Email",
      "type": "email",
      "field_type": "multi_email",
      "values": [
        { "id": 100, "value": "juliet.adams@acme.com", "type": "work" },
        { "id": 102, "value": "sales@acme.com", "type": "other" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example changes the work email address with ID `100`, removes the home email address and adds a new one with the label `other`.

**General behavior**

-   The new list replaces the old list. Tape removes email addresses that aren't in the request.
-   An email address sent with its `id` keeps that ID. Tape removes an entry with only `id`. An email address without `id` becomes a new one.
-   To clear the field, send `null` or an empty array `[]`. This also works for a required email field.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "email": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation). An update also returns these errors:

-   An email address that isn't a string, like `{ "email": 5 }`, returns `400` with `validation` and the message `Invalid input for email field with ID …`.
-   An entry that's `null`, or an object without `email`, `value`, `type` or `id`, returns the same error.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Image field value

> Use an image field value to read and write the images of a record.

Use an image field value to read and write the images of a record.

Each value of an [image field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/image) is one image. The `multi_image` field holds one or more images. Image fields work like [attachment fields](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/attachment), but accept only images.

*Image field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 3,
  "external_id": "photos",
  "label": "Photos",
  "type": "file",
  "field_type": "multi_image",
  "values": [
    {
      "value": {
        "file_id": 100,
        "name": "living-room.jpg",
        "size": 412000,
        "mimetype": "image/jpeg",
        "download_url": "https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/tape-attachments/4be1c09a7d2f8e63b5a0f1d29c7e48?Expires=1772442000&Signature=VzrbvlfI35hp4iU7jMa%2BK%2FnutPU%3D",
        "view_url": "https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/tape-attachments/4be1c09a7d2f8e63b5a0f1d29c7e48?Expires=1772442000&Signature=Hk2c8vQx1pLm9sTnW4yR%2FaB7dEo%3D",
        "link": "https://s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com/tape-attachments/4be1c09a7d2f8e63b5a0f1d29c7e48?Expires=1772442000&Signature=VzrbvlfI35hp4iU7jMa%2BK%2FnutPU%3D",
        "thumbnail": "5501",
        "created_by": null,
        "created_on": "2026-03-02 09:15:00",
        "created_on_utc": "2026-03-02 08:15:00",
        "last_modified_on": "2026-03-02 09:15:00",
        "last_modified_on_utc": "2026-03-02 08:15:00"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"file"` for the image field. | `"file"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"multi_image"`. | `"multi_image"` |
| `values[].value.file_id` | `number` | ID of the image in this field. | `100` |
| `values[].value.name` | `string` | File name. | `"living-room.jpg"` |
| `values[].value.size` | `number` | File size in bytes. | `412000` |
| `values[].value.mimetype` | `string` | Media type of the image. | `"image/jpeg"` |
| `values[].value.download_url` | `string` | Signed URL that downloads the image. |  |
| `values[].value.view_url` | `string` | Signed URL that opens the image in the browser. |  |
| `values[].value.link` | `string` | Same as `download_url`, for older integrations. Use `download_url` instead. |  |
| `values[].value.thumbnail` | `string` | ID of the image's thumbnail. Appears only if Tape created a thumbnail. | `"5501"` |
| `values[].value.created_by` | `null` | Not filled. The value is `null`. | `null` |
| `values[].value.created_on` | `string` | When the image was added, in your timezone. | `"2026-03-02 09:15:00"` |
| `values[].value.created_on_utc` | `string` | When the image was added, in UTC. | `"2026-03-02 08:15:00"` |
| `values[].value.last_modified_on` | `string` | When the image last changed, in your timezone. | `"2026-03-02 09:15:00"` |
| `values[].value.last_modified_on_utc` | `string` | When the image last changed, in UTC. | `"2026-03-02 08:15:00"` |

The signed URLs expire after some hours. Retrieve the record again to get new ones.

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out. They also shorten each image to `file_id`, `name`, `size` and `mimetype`.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to add images to a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "name": "12 Harbor View, Unit 4",
      "photos": ["temporary-file-1", "temporary-file-2"]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "name": "12 Harbor View, Unit 4",
    "photos": ["temporary-file-1", "temporary-file-2"]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "12 Harbor View, Unit 4",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "12 Harbor View, Unit 4" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 3,
      "external_id": "photos",
      "label": "Photos",
      "type": "file",
      "field_type": "multi_image",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 100,
            "name": "living-room.jpg",
            "size": 412000,
            "mimetype": "image/jpeg"
          }
        },
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 101,
            "name": "kitchen.jpg",
            "size": 388000,
            "mimetype": "image/jpeg"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

First, [upload the images](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/file#upload-a-file). Each upload returns a temporary file ID like `temporary-file-1`. Then send these IDs in the field value.

The example creates the property "12 Harbor View, Unit 4" and sets the "Photos" field (ID `3`, type `multi_image`, slug `photos`).

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   A field value accepts these file IDs:
    -   Temporary file IDs from your own uploads, like `"temporary-file-1"`.
    -   File IDs of comment and reply attachments, like `"comment-file-12"` or `"reply-file-7"`. See [Record comment](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record-comment).
    -   The `file_id` of a file in another image or attachment field, as a number. Tape copies the file, and the copy gets a new `file_id`.
-   Tape also accepts objects like `{ "file_id": "temporary-file-1" }` or `{ "value": "temporary-file-1" }`, and arrays of these.
-   Tape accepts images of type `jpeg`, `jpg`, `png`, `gif`, `tiff`, `bmp` and `webp`. It also accepts the media type `image/svg`, but not `image/svg+xml`, the usual type of SVG files.
-   Tape skips files from attachment fields that aren't images.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   An uploaded file or a comment or reply attachment that isn't an image returns `400`.
-   A temporary file ID that you didn't upload yourself returns `403`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

## Record update

Use the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to change the images of a record.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "photos": ["temporary-file-3", 101]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "photos": ["temporary-file-3", 101]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "12 Harbor View, Unit 4",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "12 Harbor View, Unit 4" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 3,
      "external_id": "photos",
      "label": "Photos",
      "type": "file",
      "field_type": "multi_image",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 101,
            "name": "kitchen.jpg",
            "size": 388000,
            "mimetype": "image/jpeg"
          }
        },
        {
          "value": {
            "file_id": 102,
            "name": "terrace.jpg",
            "size": 455000,
            "mimetype": "image/jpeg"
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example adds a new upload to the "Photos" field of the property with ID `1` and keeps the image with ID `101`. The image with ID `100` isn't in the request, so Tape removes it from the field.

**General behavior**

-   The images in the request replace the old images. To keep an image, send its `file_id` again. An image that's already in the field keeps its `file_id`.
-   Tape lists the images in the order they were added, not in the order of the request. A kept image comes before a new one.
-   To clear the field, send `null` or an empty array `[]`.
-   You can't clear a required field. The request returns `400`.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "photos": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation). An update also returns this error:

-   A numeric `file_id` that isn't a positive whole number, like `1.5`, returns `400` with `validation` and the message `… Expected a valid existing image ID …`. A number in a string, like `"100"`, returns the same error.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Link field value

> Use a link field value to read and write the links of a record.

Use a link field value to read and write the links of a record.

The value of a [link field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/link) is a list of links in `values`. Each link has an `embed_id`, the `url`, a preview with `title` and `description`, and a type label in `link_type`.

*Link field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "website",
  "label": "Website",
  "type": "embed",
  "field_type": "multi_link",
  "values": [
    {
      "embed_id": 100,
      "url": "https://acme.com",
      "original_url": "https://acme.com",
      "title": "Acme Inc.",
      "description": "Solar panels and storage for homes and businesses.",
      "type": "link",
      "link_type": "homepage",
      "created_at": "2026-11-11 10:15:00",
      "created_at_utc": "2026-11-11 09:15:00",
      "last_modified_at": "2026-11-11 10:15:00",
      "last_modified_at_utc": "2026-11-11 09:15:00",
      "created_by_user_id": 1,
      "created_by_workflow_def_id": null,
      "created_by_share_session_id": null,
      "last_modified_by_user_id": 1,
      "last_modified_by_workflow_def_id": null,
      "last_modified_by_share_session_id": null
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"embed"` for a link field. | `"embed"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"multi_link"`. | `"multi_link"` |
| `values[].embed_id` | `number` | ID of the link. Send it in an update to keep the link. | `100` |
| `values[].url` | `string` | The web address. | `"https://acme.com"` |
| `values[].original_url` | `string` | The same web address as `url`. | `"https://acme.com"` |
| `values[].title` | `string` | Title of the web page. Empty until Tape has created the preview. | `"Acme Inc."` |
| `values[].description` | `string` | Description of the web page. Empty until Tape has created the preview. | `"Solar panels and storage for homes and businesses."` |
| `values[].type` | `string` | `"link"` for every link. | `"link"` |
| `values[].link_type` | `string` or `null` | Type label: `"homepage"`, `"work"`, `"home"`, `"linkedin"`, `"x"`, `"instagram"`, `"facebook"`, `"youtube"`, `"tiktok"`, `"threads"`, `"reddit"`, `"bluesky"`, `"other"` or the text of a custom label of the field. `null` for a link without a label. | `"homepage"` |
| `values[].created_at`, `values[].last_modified_at` | `string` | When the link was added and last changed, in your timezone. | `"2026-11-11 10:15:00"` |
| `values[].created_at_utc`, `values[].last_modified_at_utc` | `string` | The same times in UTC. | `"2026-11-11 09:15:00"` |
| `values[].created_by_user_id`, `values[].last_modified_by_user_id` | `number` or `null` | ID of the user who added or last changed the link. | `1` |
| `values[].created_by_workflow_def_id`, `values[].last_modified_by_workflow_def_id` | `number` or `null` | ID of the automation that added or last changed the link. | `null` |
| `values[].created_by_share_session_id`, `values[].last_modified_by_share_session_id` | `string` or `null` | Session ID (UUID) of an anonymous visitor who added or changed the link through a shared link. | `null` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out. They also leave out the times and author IDs of each link.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to set links on a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "name": "Acme Inc.",
      "website": [
        { "url": "https://acme.com", "type": "homepage" },
        { "url": "https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme", "type": "linkedin" }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "name": "Acme Inc.",
    "website": [
      { "url": "https://acme.com", "type": "homepage" },
      { "url": "https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme", "type": "linkedin" }
    ]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Acme Inc.",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Acme Inc." }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "website",
      "label": "Website",
      "type": "embed",
      "field_type": "multi_link",
      "values": [
        {
          "embed_id": 100,
          "url": "https://acme.com",
          "original_url": "https://acme.com",
          "title": "",
          "description": "",
          "type": "link",
          "link_type": "homepage"
        },
        {
          "embed_id": 101,
          "url": "https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme",
          "original_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/company/acme",
          "title": "",
          "description": "",
          "type": "link",
          "link_type": "linkedin"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example sets the homepage and the LinkedIn profile in the "Website" field (ID `2`, type `multi_link`, slug `website`) of a new company.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Send an array of links. Each one is an object `{ "url": "...", "type": "..." }` or a URL string.
-   `type` is optional. Without it, or with a `type` Tape doesn't know, the link has no label (`"link_type": null`).
-   A `type` that matches the text of a custom label of the field (not case-sensitive) gets that label.
-   If the field's `label_setting` is `"none"`, Tape ignores `type`.
-   A URL without a scheme gets `https://`, for example `acme.com` becomes `https://acme.com`.
-   Tape creates the link previews in the background. Right after the request, `title` and `description` are empty. [Retrieve the record](#record-retrieval) later to read them.
-   A required link field needs at least one link on a new record. An empty array `[]` counts as missing.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A link that isn't a valid URL returns `400`. This includes a URL made of digits only, such as `"1"`.
-   A `type` that matches more than one custom label of the field returns `400`. Use a unique label.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

Use the [retrieve record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-a-record) to read the links of a record.

## Record update

Use the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to change the links of a record.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "website": [
        { "embed_id": 100, "type": "homepage" },
        { "url": "https://x.com/acme", "type": "x" }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "website": [
      { "embed_id": 100, "type": "homepage" },
      { "url": "https://x.com/acme", "type": "x" }
    ]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Acme Inc.",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Acme Inc." }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "website",
      "label": "Website",
      "type": "embed",
      "field_type": "multi_link",
      "values": [
        {
          "embed_id": 100,
          "url": "https://acme.com",
          "original_url": "https://acme.com",
          "title": "Acme Inc.",
          "description": "Solar panels and storage for homes and businesses.",
          "type": "link",
          "link_type": "homepage"
        },
        {
          "embed_id": 102,
          "url": "https://x.com/acme",
          "original_url": "https://x.com/acme",
          "title": "",
          "description": "",
          "type": "link",
          "link_type": "x"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example keeps the homepage with `embed_id` `100`, removes the LinkedIn profile and adds a profile on X.

**General behavior**

-   The new list replaces the old list. Tape removes links that aren't in the request.
-   To keep a link with its preview, send its `embed_id`. Tape ignores `url`, `title` and `description` next to an `embed_id` the field holds.
-   An `embed_id` the field doesn't hold returns `400`. If you send a `url` next to it, Tape adds a new link from that `url` instead.
-   Send the `type` of a kept link again. A link you send without `type` loses its label.
-   Each URL adds a new link with a new `embed_id`, even if the record already has the same URL. Tape creates its preview in the background.
-   You can't change the URL of a link. Remove the link and add a new one.
-   To clear the field, send `null` or an empty array `[]`. This also works for a required link field.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "website": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation). An update also returns this error:

-   More links than Tape allows in one link field return `400` with `validation` and the message `Maximal number of link entries is …`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Location field value

> Use a location field value to read and write the address of a record.

Use a location field value to read and write the address of a record.

The value of a [location field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/location) is one address. `values` holds one object with the full address in `value`, its parts and its coordinates.

*Location field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "address",
  "label": "Address",
  "type": "location",
  "field_type": "single_location",
  "values": [
    {
      "city": "San Francisco",
      "country": "United States",
      "map_in_sync": false,
      "original_formatted_address": "221 Elm St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA",
      "postal_code": "94107",
      "state": "California",
      "street_address": "221 Elm St",
      "name": "221 Elm St",
      "value": "221 Elm St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA",
      "latitude": 37.7694,
      "longitude": -122.4012,
      "lat": 37.7694,
      "lng": -122.4012
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"location"` for a location field. | `"location"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_location"`. | `"single_location"` |
| `values[].value` | `string` | The full address. If a user picked the address in Tape, it's `original_formatted_address`. Otherwise Tape joins the street, the postal code and city, the state and the country with commas. | `"221 Elm St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA"` |
| `values[].street_address` | `string` | Street and house number. | `"221 Elm St"` |
| `values[].postal_code` | `string` | Postal code. | `"94107"` |
| `values[].city` | `string` | City. | `"San Francisco"` |
| `values[].state` | `string` | State or region. | `"California"` |
| `values[].country` | `string` | Country. | `"United States"` |
| `values[].latitude`, `values[].longitude` | `number` | Coordinates of the address. | `37.7694` |
| `values[].lat`, `values[].lng` | `number` | The same coordinates under their older names. | `37.7694` |
| `values[].original_formatted_address` (read-only) | `string` | The address as Google Maps formatted it when a user picked it in Tape. | `"221 Elm St, San Francisco, CA 94107, USA"` |
| `values[].name` (read-only) | `string` | Name of the place, such as a business or a landmark, when a user picked it in Tape. | `"221 Elm St"` |
| `values[].map_in_sync` (read-only) | `boolean` | Despite its name, `true` means the address was typed or changed by hand and doesn't come from a place picked on the map. Through the API, the value doesn't tell you whether the map matches: a record created through the API gets `true`, an update through the API sets `false`. | `true` |

A part without a value isn't in the response.

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to set the address of a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "name": "Elm Street Townhouse",
      "address": {
        "street_address": "221 Elm Street",
        "postal_code": "94107",
        "city": "San Francisco",
        "state": "California",
        "country": "United States",
        "latitude": 37.7694,
        "longitude": -122.4012
      }
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "name": "Elm Street Townhouse",
    "address": {
      "street_address": "221 Elm Street",
      "postal_code": "94107",
      "city": "San Francisco",
      "state": "California",
      "country": "United States",
      "latitude": 37.7694,
      "longitude": -122.4012
    }
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Elm Street Townhouse",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Elm Street Townhouse" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "address",
      "label": "Address",
      "type": "location",
      "field_type": "single_location",
      "values": [
        {
          "city": "San Francisco",
          "country": "United States",
          "map_in_sync": true,
          "postal_code": "94107",
          "state": "California",
          "street_address": "221 Elm Street",
          "value": "221 Elm Street, 94107 San Francisco, California, United States",
          "latitude": 37.7694,
          "longitude": -122.4012,
          "lat": 37.7694,
          "lng": -122.4012
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example sets the "Address" field (ID `2`, type `single_location`, slug `address`) of a new property, with coordinates for the map.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Send the address as an object with `street_address`, `postal_code`, `city`, `state` and `country`. Each part is optional.
-   `value` is another name for `street_address`. Tape uses it only without `street_address`. A plain string also sets `street_address`, so send a full address as separate parts.
-   Tape doesn't look up coordinates for an address. Send `latitude` and `longitude` to place the address on the map. `lat` and `lng` work too.
-   An address with coordinates only is valid. Tape shows the coordinates as its `value`.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   An object with none of the properties `value`, `street_address`, `postal_code`, `city`, `state`, `country`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `lat` and `lng` returns `400`.
-   A part of the address that isn't a string returns `400`.
-   A `latitude` that isn't a number between -90 and 90, or a `longitude` that isn't a number between -180 and 180, returns `400`.
-   A part of the address that's too long returns `400`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

## Record update

Use the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to change the address of a record.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "address": {
        "street_address": "225 Elm Street",
        "postal_code": "94107",
        "city": "San Francisco",
        "state": "California",
        "country": "United States",
        "latitude": 37.7695,
        "longitude": -122.4010
      }
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "address": {
      "street_address": "225 Elm Street",
      "postal_code": "94107",
      "city": "San Francisco",
      "state": "California",
      "country": "United States",
      "latitude": 37.7695,
      "longitude": -122.4010
    }
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Elm Street Townhouse",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Elm Street Townhouse" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "address",
      "label": "Address",
      "type": "location",
      "field_type": "single_location",
      "values": [
        {
          "city": "San Francisco",
          "country": "United States",
          "map_in_sync": false,
          "postal_code": "94107",
          "state": "California",
          "street_address": "225 Elm Street",
          "value": "225 Elm Street, 94107 San Francisco, California, United States",
          "latitude": 37.7695,
          "longitude": -122.401,
          "lat": 37.7695,
          "lng": -122.401
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example corrects the house number of the property with ID `1`. It sends the whole address again.

**General behavior**

-   The new address replaces the whole old address. Tape removes the parts you leave out, including the coordinates.
-   An update also removes `original_formatted_address` and `name`.
-   To clear the field, send `null`.
-   You can't clear a required field. The request returns `400`.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "address": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation).

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Number field value

> Use a number field value to read and write the number of a record.

Use a number field value to read and write the number of a record.

The value of a [number field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/number) is a `number`, like `1`, `1.0` or `1.5`. A `number` field holds at most one value.

*Number field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "closing_amount",
  "label": "Closing Amount",
  "type": "number",
  "field_type": "number",
  "values": [{ "value": 85000, "formatted": "85,000.00€" }]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"number"`. | `"number"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"number"`. | `"number"` |
| `values[].value` | `number` | The number. | `85000` |
| `values[].formatted` | `string` | The number with the decimal places and the unit from the field settings. | `"85,000.00€"` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to set number values on a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "deal_name": "Solar roof for Acme Inc.",
      "closing_amount": 85000
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "deal_name": "Solar roof for Acme Inc.",
    "closing_amount": 85000
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Solar roof for Acme Inc.",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "deal_name",
      "label": "Deal Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Solar roof for Acme Inc." }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "closing_amount",
      "label": "Closing Amount",
      "type": "number",
      "field_type": "number",
      "values": [{ "value": 85000, "formatted": "85,000.00€" }]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example creates a deal with the "Deal Name" field (ID `1`, type `single_text`, slug `deal_name`) and the "Closing Amount" field (ID `2`, type `number`, slug `closing_amount`). The "Closing Amount" field has two decimal places and the unit "€" after the value.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Send the number as a number or as a string, for example `85000` or `"85000.50"`. Tape also accepts `{ "value": 85000 }` or an array with one of these.
-   Tape removes spaces at the start and the end of a string.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A value that isn't a number returns `400` with `validation` and the message `Invalid input for number field with ID …`.
-   A number outside the allowed range returns `400` with `validation`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.
