# Field value

> Use field values to read and write the data of a record.

Use field values to read and write the data of a record.

A record of a database app has static properties like `record_id`, `title` or `created_on`, and a value for the fields of its app. A field is the definition in the app: its name, type and settings, see [Field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview). A field value is what one record holds for that field.

A "Contacts" app could have the fields "First Name" (**Single line text**), "Last Name" (**Single line text**) and "Phone" (**Phone**). To create a contact, send a value for each of these fields.

Looking for the format of one field type? See [Formats by field type](#formats-by-field-type).

The record endpoints return field values in the `fields` array of a record. A field without a value isn't in the array, except a [calculation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/calculation) whose result became empty. Each entry is a field value object:

*Field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "notes",
  "label": "Notes",
  "type": "text",
  "field_type": "multi_text",
  "values": [
    {
      "value": "<p>Called about the <b>solar roof</b> offer.</p>",
      "unformatted_value": "Called about the solar roof offer."
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field_id` | `number` | ID of the field. | `2` |
| `external_id` | `string` | Slug of the field. Use it or the field ID as the key when you write the value. | `"notes"` |
| `label` | `string` | Name of the field in Tape. | `"Notes"` |
| `type` | `string` | Kind of data the value holds. See [Field type](#field-type). | `"text"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | Exact type of the field. | `"multi_text"` |
| `config` | `object` | Configuration of the field, as in the [field object](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#common-properties). |  |
| `values` | `array` | The values. The structure of one value depends on the field type. See the page of each field type. | `[{ "value": "..." }]` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Field type

Each field value has a `type` and a `field_type`. The `type` is the kind of data returned, like `text`, `category` or `phone`. The `field_type` is the exact type of the field, like `single_text` or `multi_phone`.

The [field type table](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#field-type) lists all values. The `field_type` says whether a field holds one value or several values.

A `single_category` field value never has more than one option. Switching a field from `single_category` to `multi_category` converts the field and all its values.

**Read-only field values**

Tape computes the values of `calculation`, `unique_id`, `created_on`, `created_by`, `last_modified_on` and `last_modified_by` fields. You can't write them.

-   `calculation` and `unique_id` values appear in the `fields` of a record. Tape ignores them in create and update requests.
-   `created_on`, `created_by`, `last_modified_on` and `last_modified_by` values don't appear in `fields`. Read them from the record properties of the same name.

A `unique_id` value holds the number of the record within its app and the formatted ID:

*Unique ID field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 7,
  "external_id": "deal_id",
  "label": "Deal ID",
  "type": "unique_id",
  "field_type": "unique_id",
  "values": [{ "value": 12, "formatted": "DEAL-0012" }]
}
```

`value` is the number of the record within its app, the same number as the record's `app_record_id`. `formatted` adds the prefix, the suffix and the leading zeros from the [field settings](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/unique-id).

## Write field values

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) and the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to write field values.

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "first_name": "Juliet",
    "2": "<p>Called about the <b>solar roof</b> offer.</p>"
  }
}
```

**General behavior**

-   Send the values in the `fields` object. Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key.
-   Find the app ID, field IDs and slugs in the app's **Developer** window, see [Find the app ID and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids), or in the `fields` of [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app).
-   Each field type accepts its own input formats. See [Formats by field type](#formats-by-field-type).
-   When you create a record, send a value for every required field (`"required": true` in the field's `config`). A missing value returns `400`.
-   In an update, fields that aren't in the request keep their values.
-   To clear a value, send `null`. Some field types also accept an empty value.
-   Clearing a required field returns `400` for these field types: `multi_text`, `single_category`, `multi_category`, `single_date`, `range_date`, `single_user`, `multi_user`, `single_attachment`, `multi_attachment`, `multi_image`, `single_location` and `status`. You can't clear a status value at all.
-   Tape doesn't stop you from clearing a required field of the types `single_text`, `number`, `single_relation`, `multi_relation`, `checklist`, `multi_email`, `multi_link` and `multi_phone` in an update. Send a value instead. A new record still needs a value for them.
-   A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit` to write field values, `records:read` to read them. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. The token from the [Quickstart](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/getting-started) only reads records.

## Formats by field type

Each row shows one accepted input. The page of each field type has all input formats, a full request with its response, and the errors. Its examples read your token from `$TAPE_TOKEN` and use example IDs like `1`. Replace them with your own.

Know the field only by its name in Tape, like **Member** or **Files**? Find its `field_type` in the [field type table](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#field-type).

| Field value | `field_type` | To set, send | To clear, send |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Text](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/text) | `single_text`, `multi_text` | `"Clara Weber"` | `null` or `""` |
| [Number](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/number) | `number` | `85000` | `null` or `""` |
| [Category](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/category) | `single_category`, `multi_category` | `"Contacted"` or `[5, 6]` | `null`, `""` or `[]` |
| [Status](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/status) | `status` | `1` or `"Done"` | Not possible |
| [Date](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/date) | `single_date`, `range_date` | `"2026-03-10 08:30"` (UTC) or `"2026-03-23 - 2026-03-27"` | `null` |
| [User](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/user) | `single_user`, `multi_user` | `1` or `[4, "sierra@acme.com"]` | `null`. For a `multi_user` field, `[]` also works |
| [Relation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/relation) | `single_relation`, `multi_relation` | `100` or `[110, 111]` | `null` or `[]` |
| [Attachment](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/attachment) | `single_attachment`, `multi_attachment` | `"temporary-file-1"` from [Upload a file](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/file#upload-a-file) | `null` or `[]` |
| [Image](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/image) | `multi_image` | `["temporary-file-1"]` | `null` or `[]` |
| [Checklist](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/checklist) | `checklist` | `["Book welcome lunch"]` | `null` or `[]` |
| [Link](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/link) | `multi_link` | `[{ "url": "https://acme.com", "type": "homepage" }]` | `null` or `[]` |
| [Location](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/location) | `single_location` | `{ "street_address": "221 Elm Street", "city": "San Francisco" }` | `null` |
| [Email](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/email) | `multi_email` | `[{ "email": "juliet@acme.com", "type": "work" }]` | `null` or `[]` |
| [Phone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/phone) | `multi_phone` | `[{ "phone": "+1 202 555 0143", "type": "mobile" }]` | `null` or `[]` |
| [Calculation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/calculation) | `calculation` | Read-only | Read-only |
| [Unique ID](#field-type) | `unique_id` | Read-only | Read-only |

> Coming from Podio?
> 
> Field values keep the shape of Podio item fields: a `fields` object keyed by field ID or slug when you write, a `values` array per field when you read. Find the Tape field type of each Podio field type in [Podio field types](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#podio-field-types), and its input format in the table above.

# Phone field value

> Use a phone field value to read and write the phone numbers of a record.

Use a phone field value to read and write the phone numbers of a record.

The value of a [phone field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/phone) is a list of phone numbers in `values`. Each phone number has an `id`, the number in `value` and a type label in `type`.

*Phone field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 3,
  "external_id": "phone",
  "label": "Phone",
  "type": "phone",
  "field_type": "multi_phone",
  "values": [
    {
      "id": 100,
      "value": "+1 202 555 0143",
      "type": "mobile",
      "created_at": "2026-11-11 10:15:00",
      "created_at_utc": "2026-11-11 09:15:00",
      "last_modified_at": "2026-11-11 10:15:00",
      "last_modified_at_utc": "2026-11-11 09:15:00",
      "created_by_user_id": 1,
      "created_by_workflow_def_id": null,
      "created_by_share_session_id": null,
      "last_modified_by_user_id": 1,
      "last_modified_by_workflow_def_id": null,
      "last_modified_by_share_session_id": null
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"phone"` for a phone field. | `"phone"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"multi_phone"`. | `"multi_phone"` |
| `values[].id` | `number` | ID of the phone number. Send it with the phone number in an update to keep the ID. | `100` |
| `values[].value` | `string` | The phone number as it was entered. | `"+1 202 555 0143"` |
| `values[].type` | `string` | Type label: `"mobile"`, `"work"`, `"home"`, `"main"`, `"work_fax"`, `"home_fax"`, `"pager"`, `"other"` or the text of a custom label of the field. | `"mobile"` |
| `values[].created_at`, `values[].last_modified_at` | `string` | When the phone number was added and last changed, in your timezone. | `"2026-11-11 10:15:00"` |
| `values[].created_at_utc`, `values[].last_modified_at_utc` | `string` | The same times in UTC. | `"2026-11-11 09:15:00"` |
| `values[].created_by_user_id`, `values[].last_modified_by_user_id` | `number` or `null` | ID of the user who added or last changed the phone number. | `1` |
| `values[].created_by_workflow_def_id`, `values[].last_modified_by_workflow_def_id` | `number` or `null` | ID of the automation that added or last changed the phone number. | `null` |
| `values[].created_by_share_session_id`, `values[].last_modified_by_share_session_id` | `string` or `null` | Session ID (UUID) of an anonymous visitor who added or changed the phone number through a shared link. | `null` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out. They also leave out the times and author IDs of each phone number.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to set phone numbers on a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "name": "Juliet Adams",
      "phone": [
        { "type": "mobile", "phone": "+1 202 555 0143" },
        { "type": "work", "phone": "+1 202 555 0178" }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "name": "Juliet Adams",
    "phone": [
      { "type": "mobile", "phone": "+1 202 555 0143" },
      { "type": "work", "phone": "+1 202 555 0178" }
    ]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Juliet Adams",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Juliet Adams" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 3,
      "external_id": "phone",
      "label": "Phone",
      "type": "phone",
      "field_type": "multi_phone",
      "values": [
        { "id": 100, "value": "+1 202 555 0143", "type": "mobile" },
        { "id": 101, "value": "+1 202 555 0178", "type": "work" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example sets two phone numbers in the "Phone" field (ID `3`, type `multi_phone`, slug `phone`) of a new lead.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Send an array of phone numbers. Each one is an object `{ "phone": "...", "type": "..." }` or a string. `value` works in place of `phone`.
-   Send `type` in lowercase. Without `type`, or with a `type` Tape doesn't know, the phone number gets the label `work`.
-   The API accepts all eight built-in labels, even if the field's `label_setting` offers fewer.
-   A `type` that matches the text of a custom label of the field (not case-sensitive) gets that label.
-   If the field's `label_setting` is `"none"`, Tape ignores `type`.
-   Tape stores the phone number as you send it. It removes spaces at the start and the end and skips empty phone numbers.
-   A required phone field needs at least one phone number on a new record. An empty array `[]` counts as missing.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A `type` that matches more than one custom label of the field returns `400`. Use a unique label.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

## Record retrieval

Use the [retrieve record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-a-record) to read the phone numbers of a record.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Juliet Adams",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Juliet Adams" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 3,
      "external_id": "phone",
      "label": "Phone",
      "type": "phone",
      "field_type": "multi_phone",
      "values": [
        { "id": 100, "value": "+1 202 555 0143", "type": "mobile" },
        { "id": 101, "value": "+1 202 555 0178", "type": "work" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**General behavior**

-   A phone number without a label shows `"type": "work"`. This includes all phone numbers of a field with `"label_setting": "none"`.

**Requirements:** `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Record update

Use the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to change the phone numbers of a record.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "phone": [
        { "id": 100, "type": "mobile", "phone": "+1 202 555 0199" },
        { "type": "main", "phone": "+1 202 555 0100" }
      ]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "phone": [
      { "id": 100, "type": "mobile", "phone": "+1 202 555 0199" },
      { "type": "main", "phone": "+1 202 555 0100" }
    ]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Juliet Adams",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "name",
      "label": "Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Juliet Adams" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 3,
      "external_id": "phone",
      "label": "Phone",
      "type": "phone",
      "field_type": "multi_phone",
      "values": [
        { "id": 100, "value": "+1 202 555 0199", "type": "mobile" },
        { "id": 102, "value": "+1 202 555 0100", "type": "main" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example changes the mobile number with ID `100`, removes the work number and adds a main number.

**General behavior**

-   The new list replaces the old list. Tape removes phone numbers that aren't in the request.
-   A phone number sent with its `id` keeps that ID. Tape removes an entry with only `id`. A phone number without `id` becomes a new one.
-   To clear the field, send `null` or an empty array `[]`. This also works for a required phone field.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "phone": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation). An update also returns these errors:

-   A phone number that isn't a string, like `{ "phone": 5 }`, returns `400` with `validation` and the message `Invalid input for Phone field with ID …`.
-   An entry that's `null`, or an object without `phone`, `value`, `type` or `id`, returns the same error.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Relation field value

> Use a relation field value to read and write the related records of a record.

Use a relation field value to read and write the related records of a record.

Each value of a [relation field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/relation) is a short preview of one related record. A `single_relation` field holds at most one record. A `multi_relation` field holds several records.

*Relation field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 1,
  "external_id": "belongs_to_epic",
  "label": "Belongs to Epic",
  "type": "app",
  "field_type": "single_relation",
  "values": [
    {
      "value": {
        "record_id": 100,
        "app_id": 2,
        "title": "Tenant portal relaunch",
        "created_on": "2026-03-02 09:15:00",
        "created_on_utc": "2026-03-02 08:15:00",
        "app": {
          "app_id": 2,
          "icon": "event_available",
          "name": "Epics",
          "slug": "epics",
          "external_id": "epics",
          "record_name": "Epic",
          "item_name": "Epic",
          "workspace_id": 1,
          "config": {
            "name": "Epics",
            "icon": "event_available",
            "record_name": "Epic",
            "workspace_id": 1
          }
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"app"` for both relation field types. | `"app"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_relation"` or `"multi_relation"`. | `"single_relation"` |
| `values[].value.record_id` | `number` | ID of the related record. | `100` |
| `values[].value.app_id` | `number` | ID of the app of the related record. | `2` |
| `values[].value.title` | `string` | Title of the related record. | `"Tenant portal relaunch"` |
| `values[].value.created_on` | `string` | When the related record was created, in your timezone. | `"2026-03-02 09:15:00"` |
| `values[].value.created_on_utc` | `string` | When the related record was created, in UTC. | `"2026-03-02 08:15:00"` |
| `values[].value.app` | `object` | A short preview of the app of the related record, like in `referenced_apps` of the relation field. |  |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out. They also shorten each `app` preview to `app_id`, `name` and `record_name`.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to set related records on a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "title": "Fix login timeout on the tenant portal",
      "belongs_to_epic": 100,
      "sprints": [110, 111]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "title": "Fix login timeout on the tenant portal",
    "belongs_to_epic": 100,
    "sprints": [110, 111]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Fix login timeout on the tenant portal",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 3,
      "external_id": "title",
      "label": "Title",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Fix login timeout on the tenant portal" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "belongs_to_epic",
      "label": "Belongs to Epic",
      "type": "app",
      "field_type": "single_relation",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "record_id": 100,
            "app_id": 2,
            "title": "Tenant portal relaunch",
            "created_on": "2026-03-02 09:15:00",
            "created_on_utc": "2026-03-02 08:15:00",
            "app": { "app_id": 2, "name": "Epics", "record_name": "Epic" }
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "sprints",
      "label": "Sprints",
      "type": "app",
      "field_type": "multi_relation",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "record_id": 110,
            "app_id": 3,
            "title": "Sprint 14",
            "created_on": "2026-03-02 09:20:00",
            "created_on_utc": "2026-03-02 08:20:00",
            "app": { "app_id": 3, "name": "Sprints", "record_name": "Sprint" }
          }
        },
        {
          "value": {
            "record_id": 111,
            "app_id": 3,
            "title": "Sprint 15",
            "created_on": "2026-03-04 14:05:00",
            "created_on_utc": "2026-03-04 13:05:00",
            "app": { "app_id": 3, "name": "Sprints", "record_name": "Sprint" }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example creates the issue "Fix login timeout on the tenant portal" in the issues app from [Relation field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/relation). It sets the "Belongs to Epic" field (ID `1`, type `single_relation`, slug `belongs_to_epic`) and the "Sprints" field (ID `2`, type `multi_relation`, slug `sprints`). The "Sprints" field links to the "Sprints" app with ID `3`.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Send record IDs as numbers or numeric strings. Tape also accepts objects like `{ "record_id": 100 }` or `{ "value": 100 }`, and arrays of these.
-   Tape links a record only if it exists, isn't deleted, isn't a template or a draft, and belongs to an app that the field links to (`referenced_apps`).
-   Tape drops related records that don't meet these conditions and saves the rest.
-   Send one record ID to a `single_relation` field. If you send several, Tape keeps one record it can link and drops the others.
-   The filters of a `view_id` in the field settings limit the records you can select in Tape. The API doesn't apply them.
-   To search for records you can add to the field, use [Find relatable records](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#find-relatable-records-for-a-relation-field).

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A related record Tape can't link returns `400` if you add the query parameter `reject_unreferencable_relation_targets=true`. Tape then writes no values.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

```json
            "app_id": 2,
            "title": "Mobile check-in",
            "created_on": "2026-02-11 16:40:00",
            "created_on_utc": "2026-02-11 15:40:00",
            "app": { "app_id": 2, "name": "Epics", "record_name": "Epic" }
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "sprints",
      "label": "Sprints",
      "type": "app",
      "field_type": "multi_relation",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "record_id": 111,
            "app_id": 3,
            "title": "Sprint 15",
            "created_on": "2026-03-04 14:05:00",
            "created_on_utc": "2026-03-04 13:05:00",
            "app": { "app_id": 3, "name": "Sprints", "record_name": "Sprint" }
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example moves the issue with ID `1` to the epic with ID `101` and keeps only the sprint with ID `111`.

**General behavior**

-   The new records replace the old ones. To add a record to a `multi_relation` field, send the existing record IDs together with the new one.
-   To clear the field, send `null` or an empty array `[]`.
-   Tape doesn't stop you from clearing a required relation field through the API. Send a value instead.
-   Tape drops related records it can't link, like on record creation. See [Update a record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record).
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "sprints": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation).

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Status field value

> Use a status field value to read and set the status of a record.

Use a status field value to read and set the status of a record.

The value of a [status field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/status) is one option with its `id`, `text`, `color` and `means_completed`. `means_completed` tells you whether the record is done.

*Status field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 1,
  "external_id": "status",
  "label": "Status",
  "type": "category",
  "field_type": "status",
  "values": [
    {
      "value": {
        "id": 1,
        "text": "Open",
        "color": "0077DE",
        "means_completed": false
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"category"`. A status field value has the same `type` as a category field value. | `"category"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"status"`. | `"status"` |
| `values[].value.id` | `number` | ID of the selected option. | `1` |
| `values[].value.text` | `string` | Label of the selected option. | `"Open"` |
| `values[].value.color` | `string` | Color of the option as a hex value without `#`. | `"0077DE"` |
| `values[].value.means_completed` | `boolean` | Whether the option marks the record as done. | `false` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to set the status of a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "title": "Send signed lease to the tenant",
      "status": 1
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "title": "Send signed lease to the tenant",
    "status": 1
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Send signed lease to the tenant",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "title",
      "label": "Title",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Send signed lease to the tenant" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "status",
      "label": "Status",
      "type": "category",
      "field_type": "status",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "id": 1,
            "text": "Open",
            "color": "0077DE",
            "means_completed": false
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example creates the task "Send signed lease to the tenant" in the tasks app from [Status field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/status). It sets the "Status" field (ID `1`, type `status`, slug `status`) to the option with ID `1`, "Open".

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Select an option by its ID or by its label. Tape compares labels case-insensitively and ignores spaces at the start and the end.
-   Find the option IDs in `config.settings.options` of the field, for example with [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app).
-   Tape also accepts `{ "id": 1 }`, `{ "value": 1 }` and the option object of a record response.
-   If you send several options, Tape keeps the first option that matches.
-   If two options share a label, select the option by its ID.
-   Every status field is required. Send a status value with every new record.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A new record without a status value returns `400`.
-   A value that matches no option returns `400`, with or without the query parameter `reject_unresolvable_option_values=true`.
-   A label that two options share returns `400`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

```json
    },
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "status",
      "label": "Status",
      "type": "category",
      "field_type": "status",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "id": 1,

            "means_completed": false
          }
        }

  ]
}
```

**Requirements:** `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Record update

**General behavior**

# Text field value

> Use a text field value to read and write the text of a record.

Use a text field value to read and write the text of a record.

The value of a [text field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/text) is a `string`. For a `single_text` field, it's plain text. For a `multi_text` field, it's rich text (HTML), unless the field's `config.settings.format` sets another text format.

*Text field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "notes",
  "label": "Notes",
  "type": "text",
  "field_type": "multi_text",
  "values": [
    {
      "value": "<p>Registered <b>10</b> months ago.</p>",
      "unformatted_value": "Registered 10 months ago."
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"text"` for both text field types. | `"text"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_text"` or `"multi_text"`. | `"multi_text"` |
| `values[].value` | `string` | The text. Plain text for `single_text`, rich text (HTML) for `multi_text`. | `"<p>Registered <b>10</b> months ago.</p>"` |
| `values[].unformatted_value` | `string` | `multi_text` only. The text without HTML tags. | `"Registered 10 months ago."` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to set text values on a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "first_name": "Clara Weber",
      "notes": "<p>Registered <b>10</b> months ago.</p>"
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "first_name": "Clara Weber",
    "notes": "<p>Registered <b>10</b> months ago.</p>"
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Clara Weber",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "first_name",
      "label": "First Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Clara Weber" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "notes",
      "label": "Notes",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "multi_text",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": "<p>Registered <b>10</b> months ago.</p>",
          "unformatted_value": "Registered 10 months ago."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example sets the "First Name" field (ID `1`, type `single_text`, slug `first_name`) and the "Notes" field (ID `2`, type `multi_text`, slug `notes`).

Use the field IDs and slugs of your app. A renamed field keeps its first slug, see the [Text field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/text#app-update) example.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Send the text as a string. Tape also accepts `{ "value": "..." }` or an array with one of these.
-   Tape removes spaces at the start and the end of the text.
-   A `single_text` value holds up to 500 characters, a `multi_text` value up to 150000 characters.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A value that isn't text returns `400` with `validation` and the message `Invalid input for text field with ID …`.
-   Text above the length limit returns `400` with `validation`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# User field value

> Use a user field value to read and write the users of a record.

Use a user field value to read and write the users of a record.

Each value of a [user field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/user) is a short preview of one user of your organization. A `single_user` field holds at most one user. A `multi_user` field holds several users.

*User field value object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 1,
  "external_id": "responsible_for_note_taking",
  "label": "Responsible for Note taking",
  "type": "contact",
  "field_type": "single_user",
  "values": [
    {
      "value": {
        "user_id": 1,
        "name": "Juliet Adams",
        "email": "juliet@acme.com",
        "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
        "phone": "+1 555 0100",
        "org_id": 1,
        "type": "user",
        "image": null
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"contact"` for both user field types. | `"contact"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_user"` or `"multi_user"`. | `"single_user"` |
| `values[].value.user_id` | `number` | ID of the user. | `1` |
| `values[].value.name` | `string` | Name of the user. | `"Juliet Adams"` |
| `values[].value.email` | `string` | Email address of the user. | `"juliet@acme.com"` |
| `values[].value.mail` | `string[]` | The email address as an array, for older integrations. Use `email` instead. | `["juliet@acme.com"]` |
| `values[].value.phone` | `string` or `null` | Phone number of the user, or `null` if the user has none. | `"+1 555 0100"` |
| `values[].value.org_id` | `number` | ID of the user's organization. | `1` |
| `values[].value.type` | `string` | `"user"`. | `"user"` |
| `values[].value.image` | `null` | Not filled. The value is `null`. | `null` |

Each field in a record response also contains the field's `config`. The examples on this page leave it out.

## Record creation

Use the [create record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) to assign users to a new record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/{app_id}`

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/1 \

    "fields": {
      "title": "Quarterly pipeline review",
      "responsible_for_note_taking": 1,
      "participants": [4, "sierra@acme.com"]
    }
  }'
```

```json
{
```

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Quarterly pipeline review",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 4,
      "external_id": "title",
      "label": "Title",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Quarterly pipeline review" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "responsible_for_note_taking",
      "label": "Responsible for Note taking",
      "type": "contact",
      "field_type": "single_user",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "user_id": 1,
            "name": "Juliet Adams",
            "email": "juliet@acme.com",
            "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
            "phone": "+1 555 0100",
            "org_id": 1,
            "type": "user",
            "image": null
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "participants",
      "label": "Participants",
      "type": "contact",
      "field_type": "multi_user",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "user_id": 4,
            "name": "Dan Jacob",
            "email": "dan@acme.com",
            "mail": ["dan@acme.com"],
            "phone": null,
            "org_id": 1,
            "type": "user",
            "image": null
          }
        },
        {
          "value": {
            "user_id": 5,
            "name": "Sierra Johns",
            "email": "sierra@acme.com",
            "mail": ["sierra@acme.com"],
            "phone": null,
            "org_id": 1,
            "type": "user",
            "image": null
          }
        }
      ]

```

The example creates the meeting "Quarterly pipeline review" in the meetings app from [User field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/user). It sets the "Responsible for Note taking" field (ID `1`, type `single_user`, slug `responsible_for_note_taking`) and the "Participants" field (ID `2`, type `multi_user`, slug `participants`). The second participant is set by email address.

**General behavior**

-   Use the field ID or the field's slug (returned as `external_id` in records) as the key in `fields`.
-   Identify a user by user ID, email address or name. Tape compares email addresses and names case-insensitively and looks only at users of your organization. Tape also accepts objects like `{ "user_id": 1 }` or `{ "value": 1 }`, and arrays of these.
-   Find user IDs with [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).
-   Send one user to a `single_user` field. If you send an array, Tape uses its first user.
-   Tape drops a user ID that belongs to no user.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   An email address or name that matches no user of your organization returns `400` with the message `Could not resolve a user for "<value>".`

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

## Record retrieval

## Record update

Use the [update record endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record) to change the users assigned to a record.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": {
      "responsible_for_note_taking": 2,
      "participants": [5]
    }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "responsible_for_note_taking": 2,
    "participants": [5]
  }
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "title": "Quarterly pipeline review",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 4,
      "external_id": "title",
      "label": "Title",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [{ "value": "Quarterly pipeline review" }]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "responsible_for_note_taking",
      "label": "Responsible for Note taking",
      "type": "contact",
      "field_type": "single_user",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "user_id": 2,
            "name": "Delaney Beatty",
            "email": "delaney@acme.com",
            "mail": ["delaney@acme.com"],
            "phone": null,
            "org_id": 1,
            "type": "user",
            "image": null
          }
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "field_id": 2,
      "external_id": "participants",
      "label": "Participants",
      "type": "contact",
      "field_type": "multi_user",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": {
            "user_id": 5,
            "name": "Sierra Johns",
            "email": "sierra@acme.com",
            "mail": ["sierra@acme.com"],
            "phone": null,
            "org_id": 1,
            "type": "user",
            "image": null
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

The example hands note taking for the meeting with ID `1` to the user with ID `2` and keeps only Sierra Johns as participant.

**General behavior**

-   The new users replace the old ones. To add a user to a `multi_user` field, send the existing users together with the new one.
-   To clear the field, send `null`. For a `multi_user` field, an empty array `[]` also works.
-   You can't clear a required field. The request returns `400`.
-   Fields that aren't in the request keep their values.

*Request: clear the field*

```json
{
  "fields": {
    "participants": null
  }
}
```

A cleared field isn't in the `fields` of the response.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Same errors as under [Record creation](#record-creation).

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Attachment field

> Use an attachment field to store files like PDFs, spreadsheets or images in a record.

Use an attachment field to store files like PDFs, spreadsheets or images in a record.

Tape has two attachment field types. Both are the **Files** field in Tape:

-   `single_attachment` holds one file.
-   `multi_attachment` holds several files.

An attachment field has the [common field properties](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#common-properties) and read-only `settings`. To read and write the files of a record, see [Attachment field value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/attachment).

*Attachment field object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "receipts",
  "slug": "receipts",
  "label": "Receipts",
  "type": "file",
  "field_type": "multi_attachment",
  "config": {
    "label": "Receipts",
    "slug": "receipts",
    "external_id": "receipts",
    "description": "Receipts that belong to the invoice.",
    "show_description": true,
    "required": false,
    "always_hidden": false,
    "hidden_if_empty": false,
    "primary": false,
    "settings": {
      "multiple": true
    }
  }
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"file"` for both attachment field types. | `"file"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_attachment"` or `"multi_attachment"`. | `"multi_attachment"` |
| `config.settings.multiple` (read-only) | `boolean` | `false` for `single_attachment`, `true` for `multi_attachment`. | `true` |

You can't set `settings` through the API. The field type decides whether the field holds one or several files.

# Calculation field

> Use a calculation field to compute a value from other fields of a record or from related records.

Use a calculation field to compute a value from other fields of a record or from related records.

Tape has one calculation field type: `calculation` is the **Calculation** field. It has a JavaScript `script` that Tape runs for every new record and whenever one of the referenced values changes.

The script returns text, a number or a date. The [Calculation field documentation](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18449157-calculation-syntax-examples) shows how to write scripts.

Through the API, you write the same script as in Tape. The difference is how the script references fields. See [Writing scripts for calculation fields via the API](#writing-scripts-for-calculation-fields-via-the-api).

A calculation field has the [common field properties](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#common-properties) and the `settings` below. A calculation field can't be required. Tape ignores `required: true`. To read the computed values of a record, see [Calculation field value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/calculation).

*Calculation field object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 3,
  "external_id": "price_per_square_meter",
  "slug": "price_per_square_meter",
  "label": "Price per Square Meter",
  "type": "calculation",
  "field_type": "calculation",
  "config": {
    "label": "Price per Square Meter",
    "slug": "price_per_square_meter",
    "external_id": "price_per_square_meter",
    "description": "Asking price divided by living area.",
    "show_description": true,
    "required": false,
    "always_hidden": false,
    "hidden_if_empty": false,
    "primary": false,
    "settings": {
      "decimals": 2,
      "return_type": "number",
      "script": "@[Price](field_1) / @[Living Area](field_2)",
      "script_last_modified_at": null,
      "script_last_modified_at_utc": null,
      "script_last_modified_by_user_id": null,
      "script_created_at": "2026-11-11 10:30:00",
      "script_created_at_utc": "2026-11-11 09:30:00",
      "script_created_by_user_id": 1,
      "unit_location": "suffix",
      "calendar": false,
      "unit": "€/m²",
      "time": "enabled",
      "trigger_webhooks": false,
      "trigger_automations": false
    }
  }
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"calculation"`. | `"calculation"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"calculation"`. | `"calculation"` |
| `config.settings.script` | `string` | The JavaScript code Tape runs to compute the value. It references fields with tokens, see [Writing scripts](#writing-scripts-for-calculation-fields-via-the-api). | `"@[Price](field_1) / @[Living Area](field_2)"` |
| `config.settings.return_type` | `string` | What the script returns: `"text"`, `"number"` or `"date"`. Tape works it out from the script when you create or update the field. | `"number"` |
| `config.settings.decimals` | `number` | Number results only. Number of decimal places. | `2` |
| `config.settings.unit` | `string` | Number results only. Unit shown with the value. | `"€/m²"` |
| `config.settings.unit_location` | `string` | Number results only. Where Tape shows the unit: `"prefix"` or `"suffix"`. Responses can show `"prefix_and_suffix"` for fields set up in Tape. `unit` then holds only the prefix. The API can't set a prefix and a suffix together. | `"suffix"` |
| `config.settings.calendar` | `boolean` | Date results only. Whether Tape shows the records in the calendar sidebar and includes them in the iCal export. | `false` |
| `config.settings.time` | `string` | Date results only. Whether the date has a time: `"disabled"`, `"enabled"` or `"required"`. | `"enabled"` |
| `config.settings.trigger_webhooks` | `boolean` | Whether a change of the computed value triggers webhooks. A field you create through the API starts with `false`. | `false` |
| `config.settings.trigger_automations` | `boolean` | Whether a change of the computed value triggers automations. A field you create through the API starts with `false`. | `false` |
| `config.settings.script_created_at` (read-only) | `string` | When the script was created, in your timezone. `null` for fields that are older than this property. | `"2026-11-11 10:30:00"` |
| `config.settings.script_created_by_user_id` (read-only) | `number` | ID of the user who created the script. `null` for older fields or deleted users. | `1` |
| `config.settings.script_last_modified_at` (read-only) | `string` | When a user last changed the script, in your timezone. `null` if nobody changed it yet. | `null` |
| `config.settings.script_last_modified_by_user_id` (read-only) | `number` | ID of the user who last changed the script. `null` if nobody changed it yet or the user was deleted. | `null` |

`script_created_at` and `script_last_modified_at` also come as `script_created_at_utc` and `script_last_modified_at_utc` in UTC.

## Writing scripts for calculation fields via the API

The API reads and writes the script in its stored form. In the stored form, every reference to a field is a token:

```text
@[Display name](variable_name)
```

The variable name in parentheses holds the field IDs and says which field Tape reads. The display name in square brackets only labels the token.

In Tape, the calculation editor shows these tokens as JavaScript names, for example `Price` or `Tasks.Title.all`. Tape converts between both forms when the editor opens and saves the script.

### Referencing fields of the same app as the calculation field

To reference a field of the same app, use its field ID. Find it in the [Developer view of the app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

```text
@[Field name](field_<field ID>)
```

The example references a `number` field "Price" with ID `1`:

```text
@[Price](field_1)
```

The calculation editor shows this as `Price`. Spaces in field names become underscores, so "Living Area" shows as `Living_Area`.

-   For a **Date** field with an end date, add `_start_date` or `_end_date`, for example `@[Sprint](field_5_end_date)`. The calculation editor shows `Sprint.start` and `Sprint.end`.
-   To reference the ID of the record, use `@[Record ID](meta_recordId)`. The calculation editor shows `Record_ID`.
-   Relation fields can't be referenced with `field_`. Use the tokens below to read the related records.

### Referencing fields of related records

If the app has a relation field (`single_relation` or `multi_relation`), the script can read fields of the related records. These tokens carry two IDs: first the field on the related records, then the relation field.

The examples use a projects app with the calculation field. Its relation field "Tasks" (ID `654`) links each project to task records. The tasks app has a field "Title" (ID `123`) and a field "Hours" (ID `321`).

#### Referencing a single field of all related records

To get the values of one field of all related records, use:

```text
@[All of Field name](out_<field ID>_<relation field ID>)
```

The example gets the titles of all tasks of the project:

```text
@[All of Title](out_123_654)
```

The token becomes an array with the values. Records without a value are left out. The calculation editor shows this as `Tasks.Title.all`.

A script that ends with the array itself stores no value. Turn it into text or a number first, for example with `.join(", ")` or `.length`.

#### Referencing a single field of all related records with nulls

To keep the records without a value, use:

```text
@[All of Field name with nulls](outn_<field ID>_<relation field ID>)
```

The example gets the titles of all tasks, with `null` for tasks without a title:

```text
@[All of Title with nulls](outn_123_654)
```

The token becomes an array with one entry per related record. The calculation editor shows this as `Tasks.Title.allWithNull`.

#### Referencing a single field of all relating records

Relating records are records of another database app whose relation field points to this record. For these tokens, the relation field ID is the ID of the relation field in the other app.

In the example, the tasks app has a relation field "Project" (ID `655`) that links each task to a project. In the projects app, the script gets the titles of all tasks that link to the project:

```text
@[All of Title](in_123_655)
```

The token becomes an array with the values. Records without a value are left out. The calculation editor names the namespace after the other app and shows this as `Tasks.Title.all`.

#### Referencing a single field of all relating records with nulls

To keep the relating records without a value, use `inn_`:

```text
@[All of Title with nulls](inn_123_655)
```

The token becomes an array with one entry per relating record, with `null` for records without a value. The calculation editor shows this as `Tasks.Title.allWithNull`.

#### Referencing a number field of all related records (incoming or outgoing)

For `number` fields, a token can return the sum, the average, the minimum or the maximum of all values instead of an array. Add the aggregation after `out_` or `in_`:

| Aggregation | Outgoing relation | Incoming relation | Calculation editor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Sum | `@[Sum of Hours](out_sum_321_654)` | `@[Sum of Hours](in_sum_321_655)` | `Tasks.Hours.sum` |
| Average | `@[Average of Hours](out_avg_321_654)` | `@[Average of Hours](in_avg_321_655)` | `Tasks.Hours.avg` |
| Minimum | `@[Minimum of Hours](out_min_321_654)` | `@[Minimum of Hours](in_min_321_655)` | `Tasks.Hours.min` |
| Maximum | `@[Maximum of Hours](out_max_321_654)` | `@[Maximum of Hours](in_max_321_655)` | `Tasks.Hours.max` |

Date fields support the minimum and the maximum. Tokens with nulls (`outn_`, `inn_`) don't take an aggregation. An aggregation on another field type, for example `out_sum_` on a text field, returns `500` with `unknown`.

The example script returns the hours of all tasks of the project as text:

```text
@[Sum of Hours](out_sum_321_654) + " hours"
```

## App creation

You can't create calculation fields together with a new app. Create the app first. Then add the calculation fields with an [app update](#app-update).

**Errors**

-   A request to the [create app endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#create-an-app) with a `calculation` field returns `400` with a message that starts with `Cannot create Calculation Field upon App creation.`

## App update

Use the [update app endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#update-an-app) to create new calculation fields in an app or to change existing ones.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/{appId}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell

curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": [
      {
        "field_type": "calculation",
        "config": {
          "label": "Price per Square Meter",
          "description": "Asking price divided by living area.",
          "settings": {
            "script": "@[Price](field_1) / @[Living Area](field_2)",
            "decimals": 2,
            "unit": "€/m²",
            "unit_location": "suffix"
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

```json
          "script": "@[Price](field_1) / @[Living Area](field_2)",
          "script_last_modified_at": null,

          "script_last_modified_by_user_id": null,
```

The example adds a calculation field to a listings app with ID `1`. The app has two `number` fields: "Price" (ID `1`) and "Living Area" (ID `2`). The new field "Price per Square Meter" divides the price by the living area.

Find the app ID and the field IDs in the [Developer view of the app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

**General behavior**

-   Tape runs the script with sample values to work out `return_type`. Here, the script returns a number.
-   Tape computes the values of the existing records in the background.
-   A new calculation field doesn't trigger webhooks or automations. Set `trigger_webhooks` or `trigger_automations` to `true` to change that. In a field update, leaving them out keeps their values.
-   An empty script or a script that fails to run doesn't fail the request. Tape saves the field and marks it as invalid.
-   A new calculation field doesn't show its `description` as help text yet (`show_description` is `false`). To show it, send the `description` again in a field update.
-   A field with `field_id` updates that field. In a field update, a `script` you leave out stays as it is.
-   Send `always_hidden`, `hidden_if_empty` and `description` with every field you update. Tape sets left-out switches to `false` and hides the help text without `description`. See [Create and update fields](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#create-and-update-fields).
-   Fields that aren't in the request stay unchanged.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and **Full access** to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   Every field you update needs `config.label`, even if the label stays the same. Without it, Tape rejects the request with `400` and `input_validation`. The message reads, for example, `Invalid input: data/fields/0/config must have required property 'label'`.
-   A `return_type` that doesn't match the result of the script returns `400` with the message `inferred result type from script execution does not match provided return type`.
-   A script that references fields that don't exist, or calculation fields that reference each other in a loop, returns `400`.

# Category field

> Use a category field to let a record pick from a fixed list of options, like a pipeline stage or a product.

Use a category field to let a record pick from a fixed list of options, like a pipeline stage or a product.

Tape has two category field types:

-   `single_category` is the **Single select** field. A record holds at most one option.
-   `multi_category` is the **Multiple select** field. A record holds any number of options.

A category field has the [common field properties](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#common-properties) and `settings` with its options and layout. To read and set the selected options of a record, see [Category field value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/category).

*Category field object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 1,
  "external_id": "pipeline_stage",
  "slug": "pipeline_stage",
  "label": "Pipeline Stage",
  "type": "category",
  "field_type": "single_category",
  "config": {
    "label": "Pipeline Stage",
    "slug": "pipeline_stage",
    "external_id": "pipeline_stage",
    "description": "The current stage of the lead in the sales pipeline.",
    "show_description": true,
    "required": true,
    "always_hidden": false,
    "hidden_if_empty": false,
    "primary": true,
    "settings": {
      "multiple": false,
      "layout": "dropdown",
      "options": [
        { "id": 1, "text": "New", "color": "6E7174" },
        { "id": 2, "text": "Contacted", "color": "0077DE" },
        { "id": 3, "text": "Won", "color": "00866A" },
        { "id": 4, "text": "Lost", "color": "FE001A" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"category"` for both category field types. | `"category"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_category"` or `"multi_category"`. | `"single_category"` |
| `config.settings.multiple` (read-only) | `boolean` | `false` for `single_category`, `true` for `multi_category`. | `false` |
| `config.settings.layout` | `string` | Older layout setting: `"dropdown"` (default), `"list"` or `"inline"`. Tape stores and returns the value, but it doesn't change how the options look. Set that in the record layout of the app. | `"dropdown"` |
| `config.settings.options` | `array` | The options of the field, in their order. |  |
| `config.settings.options[].id` | `number` | ID of the option. Use it to change the option or to select it in a record. | `2` |
| `config.settings.options[].text` | `string` | Label of the option. Required for every option you send. | `"Contacted"` |
| `config.settings.options[].color` | `string` | Color of the option. Responses return a hex value without `#`. See [Option colors](#option-colors). | `"0077DE"` |
| `config.settings.options_to_delete` (write-only) | `array` | App update only. The IDs of the options to delete. | `[{ "id": 4 }]` |

### Option colors

Send a color by name or as its hex value without `#`. Tape reads names case-insensitively.

An unknown color gives the option the `default` color (`CDCCC9`), without an error. This includes a hex value with `#`.

| Name | Hex value |
| --- | --- |
| `default` | `CDCCC9` |
| `gray` | `6E7174` |
| `brown` | `8B2E00` |
| `orange` | `F45D00` |
| `yellow` | `DEA700` |
| `green` | `00866A` |
| `blue` | `0077DE` |
| `purple` | `6724DD` |
| `pink` | `DC0080` |
| `red` | `FE001A` |

Find the workspace ID with [Retrieve workspaces](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/workspace#retrieve-workspaces).

**General behavior**

-   Tape keeps the order of `options` from the request.
-   Without `layout`, a new field uses `"dropdown"`.
-   Without `color`, a new option is gray (`6E7174`). Here, that's "Heat pump".
-   Without `primary`, Tape makes the first field of the request the primary field. Here, that's "Pipeline Stage".
-   A new category field doesn't show its `description` as help text (`show_description` is `false`).

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and a workspace role that may edit apps in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   An option without `text` returns `400`.
-   A `layout` other than `"dropdown"`, `"list"` or `"inline"` returns `400`.

## App update

Use the [update app endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#update-an-app) to create new category fields in an app or to change existing ones.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/{appId}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell

curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": [
      {
        "field_id": 1,
        "config": {
          "label": "Pipeline Stage",
          "required": true,
          "settings": {
            "layout": "list",
            "options": [
              { "id": 1, "text": "New", "color": "gray" },
              { "id": 2, "text": "Contacted", "color": "blue" },
              { "text": "Negotiating", "color": "yellow" },
              { "id": 3, "text": "Won", "color": "green" },
              { "id": 4, "text": "Lost", "color": "orange" }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "config": {
        "label": "Pipeline Stage",

        "settings": {
```

The example changes the "Pipeline Stage" field (ID `1`) of the leads app. It adds the option "Negotiating" between "Contacted" and "Won", changes the color of "Lost" to orange and sets `layout` to `"list"`. The "Products" field isn't in the request, so it stays unchanged.

Find the app ID and the field IDs in the [Developer view of the app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids). Find the option IDs in `config.settings.options` of the field, for example with [Retrieve a single app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app).

**General behavior**

-   A field with `field_id` updates that field. A field without `field_id` creates a new field and needs a `field_type`.
-   An option with `id` changes that option. To rename it, send its `id` with the new `text`. An option without `id` creates a new option.
-   Options you leave out of `options` stay unchanged. To set a new order, send all existing options in that order.
-   An option you send without the other options moves to the end of the list, also when you only rename it. To keep the order, send all options in the order you want.
-   To delete options, list their IDs in `settings.options_to_delete`, for example `"options_to_delete": [{ "id": 4 }]`. Tape also accepts plain IDs: `[4]`. An option that is also in `options` stays.
-   Without `layout`, the field keeps its layout.
-   Send `required`, `always_hidden` and `hidden_if_empty` with every field you update. Tape sets left-out switches to `false`. `show_description` stays as it is, with or without `description`. See [Create and update fields](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#create-and-update-fields).
-   Fields that aren't in the request stay unchanged.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and **Full access** to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   Every field you update needs `config.label`, even if the label stays the same. Without it, Tape rejects the request with `400` and `input_validation`. The message reads, for example, `Invalid input: data/fields/0/config must have required property 'label'`.
-   An option without `text` returns `400`.
-   An option ID in `options` or `options_to_delete` that doesn't belong to the field returns `400`.
-   A `layout` other than `"dropdown"`, `"list"` or `"inline"` returns `400`.

# Checklist field

> Use a checklist field to keep a list of tasks in a record, each with its own assignee, due date and priority.

Use a checklist field to keep a list of tasks in a record, each with its own assignee, due date and priority.

Tape has one checklist field type: `checklist` is the **Task list** field.

A checklist field has the [common field properties](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#common-properties) and one setting, `show_in_focus`. To read and write the tasks of a record, see [Checklist field value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/checklist).

*Checklist field object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 1,
  "external_id": "onboarding_tasks",
  "slug": "onboarding_tasks",
  "label": "Onboarding Tasks",
  "type": "checklist",
  "field_type": "checklist",
  "config": {
    "label": "Onboarding Tasks",
    "slug": "onboarding_tasks",
    "external_id": "onboarding_tasks",
    "description": "Everything to prepare before the first day.",
    "show_description": true,
    "required": false,
    "always_hidden": false,
    "hidden_if_empty": false,
    "primary": true,
    "settings": {
      "show_in_focus": true
    }
  }
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"checklist"`. | `"checklist"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"checklist"`. | `"checklist"` |
| `config.settings.show_in_focus` | `boolean` | Shows the tasks of this field in the **Focus** of their assignees. Default: `true`. | `true` |

## App creation

Use the [create app endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#create-an-app) to create a checklist field together with a new app.

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/ \
```

The example creates an onboarding app for new hires in the workspace with ID `1`. The app gets a `checklist` field "Onboarding Tasks". The example leaves out other fields of an onboarding app, like "Name" or "Start Date".

**General behavior**

-   Without `show_in_focus`, a new field shows its tasks in **Focus**.
-   Without `primary`, Tape makes the first field of the request the primary field. Here, that's "Onboarding Tasks".
-   A new checklist field doesn't show its `description` as help text yet (`show_description` is `false`). To show it, send the `description` again in a field update.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and a workspace role that may edit apps in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.


```json
{
  "app_id": 1,
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "slug": "onboarding",

        "label": "Onboarding Tasks",

        "show_description": true,
```

The example sets `show_in_focus` of the "Onboarding Tasks" field (ID `1`) to `false`. The tasks of this field no longer appear in the **Focus** of their assignees.

Find the app ID and the field IDs in the [Developer view of the app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

**General behavior**

-   A field with `field_id` updates that field. A field without `field_id` creates a new field and needs a `field_type`.
-   Without `show_in_focus`, the setting stays as it is.

See [Create and update fields](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#create-and-update-fields).
-   Fields that aren't in the request stay unchanged.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and **Full access** to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   Every field you update needs `config.label`, even if the label stays the same. Without it, Tape rejects the request with `400` and `input_validation`. The message reads, for example, `Invalid input: data/fields/0/config must have required property 'label'`.

# Date field

> Use a date field to store a date, a date with a time, or a date range in a record.

Use a date field to store a date, a date with a time, or a date range in a record.

Tape has two date field types. Both are the **Date** field in Tape:

-   `single_date` holds one date.
-   `range_date` holds a start date and an optional end date.

A date field has the [common field properties](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#common-properties) and `settings` that decide whether a value has a time, an end date and a place in the calendar. To read and write the dates of a record, see [Date field value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/date).

*Date field object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "installation_window",
  "slug": "installation_window",
  "label": "Installation Window",
  "type": "date",
  "field_type": "range_date",
  "config": {
    "label": "Installation Window",
    "slug": "installation_window",
    "external_id": "installation_window",
    "description": "The days the crew installs the panels.",
    "show_description": true,
    "required": false,
    "always_hidden": false,
    "hidden_if_empty": false,
    "primary": false,
    "settings": {
      "calendar": true,
      "time": "disabled",
      "end": "required",
      "is_due_date_of_status_field": false
    }
  }
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"date"` for both date field types. | `"date"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"single_date"` or `"range_date"`. | `"range_date"` |
| `config.settings.calendar` | `boolean` | Shows the field in the Tape calendar and in iCal exports. Default: `false`. | `true` |
| `config.settings.time` | `string` | Whether a value has a time: `"disabled"`, `"enabled"` (default) or `"required"`. | `"disabled"` |
| `config.settings.end` | `string` | `range_date` only. Whether a value needs an end date: `"enabled"` (default) or `"required"`. | `"required"` |
| `config.settings.is_due_date_of_status_field` | `boolean` | Uses this field as the due date of the app's [status field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/status), for example in **Focus**. Default: `false`. | `false` |

In Tape, `time` is the **Time** setting of the field: `"disabled"` is **Hidden**, `"enabled"` is **Shown**, `"required"` is **Required**. `end` is the **End date** setting.

The API has no value to hide the end date. An end date hidden in Tape reads as `"enabled"`. For a date without an end, use a `single_date` field.

![Settings of a Date field with the Time options and the End date setting](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/date-field-settings-403970c8eb2c44e792972dd4f965720d.png)

## App creation

**General behavior**

**Errors**

# Email field

> Use an email field to store one or more email addresses in a record.

Use an email field to store one or more email addresses in a record.

Tape has one email field type: `multi_email` is the **Email** field. It holds one or more email addresses, each with a type label such as `work` or `home`.

An email field has the [common field properties](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#common-properties) and its own `settings`. To read and write the email addresses of a record, see [Email field value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/email).

*Email field object*

```json
{
  "field_id": 2,
  "external_id": "email",
  "slug": "email",
  "label": "Email",
  "type": "email",
  "field_type": "multi_email",
  "config": {
    "label": "Email",
    "slug": "email",
    "external_id": "email",
    "description": "The email addresses of the contact.",
    "show_description": true,
    "required": false,
    "always_hidden": false,
    "hidden_if_empty": false,
    "primary": false,
    "settings": {
      "only_allow_single_entry": false,
      "label_setting": "default"
    }
  }
}
```

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | `"email"` for an email field. | `"email"` |
| `field_type` | `string` | `"multi_email"`. | `"multi_email"` |
| `config.settings.only_allow_single_entry` | `boolean` | If `true`, users can add only one email address in Tape. The API still accepts more than one. Default: `false`. | `false` |
| `config.settings.label_setting` (read-only) | `string` | Which type labels the field offers: `"default"` (`home`, `work`, `other`), `"custom_only"` (only the field's own labels) or `"none"`. With `"none"`, Tape ignores a `type` you send with a field value. | `"default"` |

You can't set `label_setting` through the API. Choose the labels of an email field in Tape.

## App creation

Use the [create app endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#create-an-app) to create email fields together with a new app.

The example creates a contacts app in the workspace with ID `1`. The app gets a `single_text` field "Name" and a `multi_email` field "Email".

Find the workspace ID with [Retrieve workspaces](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/workspace#retrieve-workspaces).

**General behavior**

-   Without `settings`, `only_allow_single_entry` is `false`.
-   A new email field offers the built-in labels (`"label_setting": "default"`).
-   Without `primary`, Tape makes the first field of the request the primary field. Here, that's "Name".
-   A new email field doesn't show its `description` as help text yet (`show_description` is `false`). To show it, send the `description` again in a field update.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and a workspace role that may edit apps in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## App update

Use the [update app endpoint](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#update-an-app) to create new email fields in an app or to change existing ones.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/{appId}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell

curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "fields": [
      {
        "field_id": 2,
        "config": {
          "label": "Email",
          "description": "The email address of the contact.",
          "required": false,
          "settings": {
            "only_allow_single_entry": true
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "fields": [
    {
```
