# Record comment

> Use these endpoints to create, read and delete the comments and replies on a record.

Use these endpoints to create, read and delete the comments and replies on a record.

Comments and replies appear in the activity of a record, next to its field changes.

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> Endpoints that read comments and replies need `records.comments:read`. Endpoints that create or delete them need `records.comments:edit`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

## The comment object

Every comment endpoint returns comments in this format. The example comment has one attached file:

*Comment*

```json
{
  "comment_id": 1000,
  "value": "The contract is attached.",
  "ref": { "type": "record", "id": 1 },
  "files": [
    {
      "file_id": "comment-file-5001",
      "name": "contract.pdf",
      "mimetype": "application/pdf",
      "size": 48213,
      "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00",
      "created_on_utc": "2022-03-01 11:00:00"
    }
  ],
  "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00",
  "created_on_utc": "2022-03-01 11:00:00",
  "created_by": {
    "user_id": 600,
    "type": "user",
    "org_id": 1,
    "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "name": "Juliet Adams"
  },
  "user": {
    "user_id": 600,
    "type": "user",
    "org_id": 1,
    "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "name": "Juliet Adams"
  }
}
```

The example comes from a user whose timezone is one hour ahead of UTC.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `comment_id` | number | The comment ID. | `1000` |
| `value` | string | Text of the comment, as plain text. Line breaks are `\n`. Mentions use the same syntax as in [Create a record comment](#create-a-record-comment). | `"The contract is attached."` |
| `ref` | object | What the comment belongs to. `type` is `record`, `id` is the record ID. | `{ "type": "record", "id": 1 }` |
| `files` | array | Files attached to the comment. Empty when there are none. See [Comment files](#comment-files). | `[]` |
| `created_on` | string | When the comment was written, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` in your timezone. See [Date & timezone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone). | `"2022-03-01 12:00:00"` |
| `created_on_utc` | string | The same moment as `created_on`, in UTC. | `"2022-03-01 11:00:00"` |
| `created_by` | object | null | The user who wrote the comment, or `null` if no user is the author. | `{ "user_id": 600, "type": "user", … }` |
| `user` | object | null | Same as `created_by`. | `{ "user_id": 600, "type": "user", … }` |

The author object has `user_id`, `type` (`"user"`), `org_id`, `mail` (a list with the email address of the user) and `name`.

### Comment files

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file_id` | string | ID of the file, with the prefix `comment-file-`. Use it in `attachment_ids` of the [Email resource](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/email#attachments). | `"comment-file-5001"` |
| `name` | string | File name. | `"contract.pdf"` |
| `mimetype` | string | MIME type of the file. | `"application/pdf"` |
| `size` | number | File size in bytes. | `48213` |
| `created_on` | string | When the file was uploaded, in your timezone. | `"2022-03-01 12:00:00"` |
| `created_on_utc` | string | The same moment as `created_on`, in UTC. | `"2022-03-01 11:00:00"` |

## Create a record comment

Use this endpoint to add a comment to a record.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/comment/record/{record_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/comment/record/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "value": "This is a comment on record with ID 1."
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "value": "This is a comment on record with ID 1."
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "comment_id": 1000,
  "value": "This is a comment on record with ID 1.",
  "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00",
  "ref": { "type": "record", "id": 1 },
  "files": [],
  "created_by": {
    "user_id": 600,
    "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "name": "Juliet Adams",
    "org_id": 1,
    "type": "user"
  },
  "user": {
    "user_id": 600,
    "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "name": "Juliet Adams",
    "org_id": 1,
    "type": "user"
  }
}
```

Send the text of the comment in `value`. The example adds a plain text comment to the record with ID `1`.

**General behavior**

-   `value` supports plain text with a few formatting options:
    -   Force a line break with `\n`.
    -   Mention a user with the ID and name of the user, for example `@[Juliet Adams](user:123)` for the user with ID `123`. To find a user ID, see [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).
-   To attach files, send their temporary file IDs in `file_ids`, like for the attachment field type. See [File](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/file).

**Requirements:** `records.comments:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `silent` | `boolean` | Don't send notifications for this change (default: `false`). |
| `hook` | `boolean` | Run webhooks for this change (default: `true`). |
| `workflow` | `boolean` | Trigger automations for this change (default: `true`). |

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | Required. Text of the comment. |
| `file_ids` | `Array` | Temporary file IDs of the files to attach. |

## Retrieve a comment

Use this endpoint to read one comment by its ID.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/comment/{comment_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/comment/1000 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "comment_id": 1000,
  "value": "This is a comment on record with ID 1.",
  "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00",
  "ref": { "type": "record", "id": 1 },
  "files": [],
  "created_by": {
    "user_id": 600,
    "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "name": "Juliet Adams",
    "org_id": 1,
    "type": "user"
  },
  "user": {
    "user_id": 600,
    "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
    "name": "Juliet Adams",
    "org_id": 1,
    "type": "user"
  }
}
```

`ref` points to the record the comment belongs to.

**Requirements:** `records.comments:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Reply to a comment

Use this endpoint to reply to a comment or to another reply.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/reply/comment-or-reply/{comment_or_reply_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/reply/comment-or-reply/1000 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "value": "Thanks, I will check it today."
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "value": "Thanks, I will check it today."
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "reply_id": 2000,
  "ref": { "type": "record", "id": 1 },
  "parent": { "type": "comment", "id": 1000 },
  "created_on": "2022-03-01 14:00:00",
  "created_on_utc": "2022-03-01 13:00:00",
  "last_edit_on": null,
  "last_edit_on_utc": null,
  "files": [],
  "value": "Thanks, I will check it today.",
  "user": {
    "mail": ["will@acme.com"],
    "user_id": 601,
    "org_id": 1,
    "name": "Will Dawson",
    "type": "user"
  },
  "created_by": {
    "mail": ["will@acme.com"],
    "user_id": 601,
    "org_id": 1,
    "name": "Will Dawson",
    "type": "user"
  }
}
```

To find a `comment_id` or `reply_id`, see [Retrieve comments for a record](#retrieve-comments-for-a-record) and [Retrieve replies for a record](#retrieve-replies-for-a-record).

Send the text of the reply in `value`. The example replies to the comment with ID `1000`.

`ref` points to the record. `parent` points to the activity the reply answers, here the comment with ID `1000`.

**General behavior**

-   `value` supports the same formatting as a comment: line breaks with `\n` and user mentions.
-   To attach files, send their temporary file IDs in `file_ids`.
-   Replies have one level. A reply to a reply goes to the same parent as the reply you answer.
-   `created_by` and `user` are `null` if Tape can't show the author, for example when an automation wrote the reply.
-   Unlike a comment, a reply runs webhooks and automations only if you set `hook` and `workflow` to `true`.

**Requirements:** `records.comments:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `silent` | `boolean` | Don't send notifications for this change (default: `false`). |
| `hook` | `boolean` | Run webhooks for this change (default: `false`). |
| `workflow` | `boolean` | Trigger automations for this change (default: `false`). |

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `string` | Required. Text of the reply. |
| `file_ids` | `Array` | Temporary file IDs of the files to attach. |

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 3,
  "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJibGFiRGVmSWQiOjgsInZhbHVlcyI6WzE1OV0sImV4cCI6MTY1MDYxODc3OH0.iY5TnLSBDGCnFXbStcrLPTmP6MATnS_JKywbvC4tx3g",
  "replies": [
    {
      "reply_id": 2000,
      "ref": { "type": "record", "id": 1 },
      "parent": { "type": "comment", "id": 1000 },
      "created_on": "2022-03-01 14:00:00",
      "created_on_utc": "2022-03-01 13:00:00",
      "last_edit_on": null,
      "last_edit_on_utc": null,
      "files": [],
      "value": "Thanks, I will check it today.",
      "user": {
        "mail": ["will@acme.com"],
        "user_id": 601,
        "org_id": 1,
        "name": "Will Dawson",
        "type": "user"
      },
      "created_by": {
        "mail": ["will@acme.com"],
        "user_id": 601,
        "org_id": 1,
        "name": "Will Dawson",
        "type": "user"
      }
    },
    {
      "reply_id": 2001,
      "ref": { "type": "record", "id": 1 },
      "parent": { "type": "comment", "id": 1000 },
      "created_on": "2022-03-01 15:00:00",
      "created_on_utc": "2022-03-01 14:00:00",
      "last_edit_on": null,
      "last_edit_on_utc": null,
      "files": [],
      "value": "Great, thank you.",
      "user": {
        "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
        "user_id": 600,
        "org_id": 1,
        "name": "Juliet Adams",
        "type": "user"
      },
      "created_by": {
        "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
        "user_id": 600,
        "org_id": 1,
        "name": "Juliet Adams",
        "type": "user"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The results are paginated. Pass `cursor` from the response to get the next page.

**General behavior**

-   The response contains every reply on the record. A reply can answer a comment, a field change or the creation of the record. `parent.type` tells you which: `comment`, `revision`, `created`, `deleted`, `restored` or `invitation`.
-   Replies come grouped by the activity they answer, oldest activity first and oldest reply first. Replies with the same `parent.id` belong to the same thread.
-   `total` is the number of all replies on the record. Only the first page contains it. Pages you get with a `cursor` return `null`.
-   `cursor` is `null` on the last page.
-   Use a `cursor` only with this endpoint and the same record. Any other cursor returns an error.

**Requirements:** `records.comments:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description | Min | Max |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `integer` | Number of replies to return (default: `50`). | 1 | 100 |
| `cursor` | `string` | Cursor of the next page. | \- | \- |

## Delete a comment or reply

Use this endpoint to delete a comment or a reply by its ID.

`DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/comment-or-reply/{comment_or_reply_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/comment-or-reply/2000 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{}
```

**General behavior**

-   Send the ID of a comment (`comment_id`) or of a reply (`reply_id`).
-   You can delete only your own comments and replies.

**Requirements:** `records.comments:edit`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `silent` | `boolean` | Don't send notifications for this change (default: `false`). |

## Errors

-   A record you can't view or comment on returns `400` with `record_no_permission`.
-   Deleting a comment or reply that isn't your own returns `401`. So does a request without a credential.
-   A token without `records.comments:read` or `records.comments:edit` returns `403`.
-   A comment or reply that doesn't exist returns `404`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

# Record follow

> Use this endpoint to stop notifications about the records of a database app for everyone who follows them.

Use this endpoint to stop notifications about the records of a database app for everyone who follows them.

Users who follow a record get notified about its updates.

In the Podio API, a follow is a subscription.

## Unfollow all records in a database app

Use this endpoint to remove every follower from every record of a database app.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/unfollow-all/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/app/unfollow-all/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{}'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total_unfollowed_count": 6
}
```

The example unfollows all records of the database app with ID `1`. To find your app ID, see [Find the app ID and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

**General behavior**

-   The request unfollows all users of your organization, not only you.
-   The request blocks until Tape has removed all follows. On large databases, this takes a while.
-   If nobody follows a record of the database, `total_unfollowed_count` is `0`.

**Requirements:** `records:edit`, and **Full access** to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Errors**

-   A request without **Full access** to the app returns `400` with `app_no_permission`.
-   A request without a credential returns `401`.
-   A token without `records:edit` returns `403`.
-   A token whose content access doesn't include the app returns `404`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

**Response fields**

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `total_unfollowed_count` | `integer` | Number of follows that were removed. |

# Record sharing & permissions

> Use this endpoint to share records with individual users and to change or remove their access.

Use this endpoint to share records with individual users and to change or remove their access.

In the Podio API, a record permission is a grant.

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> This endpoint needs `records:share`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

## Batch update multiple records' permissions

Use this endpoint to add, change and remove the permissions of users on up to 50 records in one request.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/permission/batch`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/permission/batch \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "inputs": [
      {
        "record_id": 1,
        "add_permissions": [
          {
            "user_id": 100,
            "permission_level": 5
          }
        ],
        "remove_permissions": [101]
      },
      {
        "record_id": 2,
        "add_permissions": [
          {
            "user_id": 100,
            "permission_level": 5
          },
          {
            "email": "juliet@acme.com",
            "permission_level": 4
          }
        ],
        "remove_permissions": [101]
      }
    ]
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "record_id": 1,
      "add_permissions": [
        {
          "user_id": 100,
          "permission_level": 5
        }
      ],
      "remove_permissions": [101]
    },
    {
      "record_id": 2,
      "add_permissions": [
        {
          "user_id": 100,
          "permission_level": 5
        },
        {
          "email": "juliet@acme.com",
          "permission_level": 4
        }
      ],
      "remove_permissions": [101]
    }
  ]
}
```

*Response*

```json
{}
```

Send one object per record in the `inputs` array. Each object has a `record_id` and up to three lists: `add_permissions`, `update_permissions` and `remove_permissions`.

The example changes the permissions of records `1` and `2`:

-   User `100` gets **Full access** to both records.
-   `juliet@acme.com` gets access to record `2` with the level **Can share**.
-   User `101` loses access to both records.

**General behavior**

-   One request changes at most 50 records. A longer `inputs` array returns an error. For more records, send several requests.
-   All records of one request must belong to the same database app.
-   A personal access token with limited content access shares only records in apps its content access includes. If one record lies outside, the whole request returns `404`.

**Requirements:** `records:share`, and **Can share** or **Full access** on each record. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A permission level that isn't a number from `0` to `5`, or records from more than one database app, return `400` with `validation`.
-   An `email` in `update_permissions` that belongs to no user in your organization returns `500` with `unknown` and the message `User with email … not found`.
-   A request without a credential returns `401`.
-   A token without `records:share` returns `403`.
-   A record outside the content access of a personal access token returns `404`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

### Add permissions

Each entry in `add_permissions` has a `user_id` or an `email`, and a `permission_level`. If no user in your organization has the `email`, Tape creates a new user and sends an invitation to join Tape. To find a user ID, see [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).

### Update permissions

Each entry in `update_permissions` has a `user_id` or an `email`, and a `permission_level`. Tape changes the existing permission of that user. The `email` must belong to a user in your organization.

Unlike `add_permissions`, `update_permissions` sends no invitation email. Use it to change a user's permission without notifying them.

### Remove permissions

Each entry in `remove_permissions` is a user ID or an email address. Tape removes the access you gave this user on the record. Access through a workspace membership or app permissions stays.

### Permission levels

Send `permission_level` as a number:

| Number | Level |
| --- | --- |
| `5` | Full access |
| `4` | Can share |
| `3` | Can edit |
| `2` | Can comment |
| `1` | Can view |
| `0` | No access |

A name such as `CAN_SHARE` or any other value returns `400` with `validation`. The message reads `expected a valid permission level (3, 4 or 5)`, but all six numbers work.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user)[

Capabilities

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities)[

# Record revision

> Use these endpoints to see what changed in a record, who changed it and when.

Use these endpoints to see what changed in a record, who changed it and when.

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> All revision endpoints need `records:read`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

## Revisions concept

Every record has a revision number, `current_revision.revision` in the record. It starts at `0` when the record is created and goes up by one with each change. Use this number as `revision_id` in the endpoints below.

A revision contains its author as `created_by`, its date and time as `created_on` and its revision number.

## Retrieve revisions for a record

Use this endpoint to list all revisions of a record.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}/revision`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1/revision \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 2,
  "revisions": [
    {
      "created_by": {
        "user_id": 600,
        "name": "Dan Jacob",
        "type": "user"
      },
      "created_on": "2022-03-16 14:25:00",
      "type": "creation",
      "revision": 0
    },
    {
      "created_by": {
        "user_id": 600,
        "name": "Dan Jacob",
        "type": "user"
      },
      "created_on": "2022-03-16 14:30:00",
      "type": "update",
      "revision": 1
    }
  ]
}
```

The example reads the revisions of record `1`. User `Dan Jacob` (ID `600`) created the record and updated it once.

The response has no pagination and no `cursor`.

> Looking for the changed values?
> 
> A revision holds only metadata, not the changed values. To see the changes, use [Retrieve revision delta](#retrieve-revision-delta).

**Requirements:** `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `include_deleted` | `boolean` | Also return the revisions of a deleted record that is still in a trash you can access (default: `false`). |

## Retrieve revision delta

Use this endpoint to see which field values changed in one revision.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}/revision/previous/{revision_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1/revision/previous/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "from_revision_id": 0,
  "to_revision_id": 1,
  "revision_deltas": [
    {
      "from": [],
      "external_id": "notes",
      "field_id": 2000,
      "label": "Notes",
      "to": [
        {
          "value": "Some important notes"
        }
      ],
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "config": {
        "description": null,
        "required": false,
        "label": "Notes"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

The example compares revision `1` of record `1` with the revision before it, revision `0`.

In the example, the single text field `notes` changed from no value to `Some important notes`.

**Key fields**

-   `revision_deltas`: one entry per changed field. One revision can change several fields when the same author changed them at the same time.
-   `from` and `to`: the values before and after the change. They have the same format as the `values` of a record field. See [Field values](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/overview).

**Requirements:** `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

### Revision lookback limit

You can read deltas only for the *last 50 revisions* of a record. An older revision returns a `400` error (see [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors)):

*Response*

```json
{
  "status_code": 400,
  "endpoint": "/v1/record/1/revision/previous/123",
  "error_code": "validation",
  "error_message": "Revision ID 123 is too old. You can maximally go back 50 revisions"
}
```

## Retrieve the last revision

Use this endpoint to read a record as it was before its most recent change.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}/revision/last`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1/revision/last \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "app_record_id": 1,
  "app_id": 1,
  "created_on": "2022-03-16 14:25:00",
  "created_on_utc": "2022-03-16 13:25:00",
  "last_modified_on": "2022-03-16 14:25:00",
  "last_modified_on_utc": "2022-03-16 13:25:00",
  "created_by": {
    "user_id": 600,
    "name": "Dan Jacob",
    "type": "user"
  },
  "last_modified_by": {
    "user_id": 600,
    "name": "Dan Jacob",
    "type": "user"
  },
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 2000,
      "external_id": "notes",
      "label": "Notes",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": []
    }
  ]
}
```

The response has the same `fields` format as a record.

**Requirements:** `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

## Retrieve a record at a revision

Use this endpoint to read a record as it was at a given revision.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/{record_id}/revision/at/{revision_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/1/revision/at/0 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

The response has the same format as [Retrieve the last revision](#retrieve-the-last-revision).

**General behavior**

-   `revision_id` `0` returns the record as it was created.
-   The [revision lookback limit](#revision-lookback-limit) applies here too.

**Requirements:** `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token, a user API key or an automation API key.

**Errors**

A `revision_id` higher than the latest revision of the record returns `400`.

# Search

> Search across every app and record you have access to, with optional filtering, sorting and cursor-based pagination.

Use these endpoints to find apps and records by text across your whole organization.

One search covers every workspace and every app you have access to. It returns two kinds of result, *apps* and *records*, mixed in one list and ranked by relevance.

Use search when you know *what* you're looking for but not *where* it is. Already know the database app? [`POST /v1/record/filter/app/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-filtered-records-for-an-app) filters on specific fields, returns full field values and gives you a `total`.

Both endpoints share one URL, `/v1/search`:

-   [`GET`](#search) takes the search as query parameters. Use it in most cases.
-   [`POST`](#search-with-a-filter) takes the same search as a JSON body. Only the body can carry a *filter* that narrows the search to workspaces, apps, authors or time windows.

Whichever you start with, [page through the results](#pagination) with `GET`.

Results are *previews*. An app result has no fields, and a record result has no field values. For the full object, use [`GET /v1/record/{record_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-a-record) or [`GET /v1/app/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app).

## Authentication and permissions

Both endpoints need a credential that belongs to a user: a [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key), a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) or an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#oauth-access-token). An automation API key returns a `400`:

*Response*

```json
{
  "status_code": 400,
  "endpoint": "/v1/search",
  "error_code": "validation",
  "error_message": "Invalid API key for accessing endpoint '/v1/search' (this endpoint can only be accessed with a user API key)"
}
```

Every search uses the permissions of the user behind the credential, and an automation API key has no user. Organization guests get a `401`.

Tape filters results by permission on every request, for records *and* apps. Two credentials of two users can return different results, and a different number of results, for the same query. Search never shows anything you can't open in Tape.

> Missing app or record results?
> 
> A [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) or an OAuth access token can search with *either* the `apps:read` or the `records:read` [capability](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities). You don't need both.
> 
> -   A token with only one of them gets a `200` with only the result type it may see. With `records:read` alone, you get record results and no app results, even if `types` asks for both.
> -   A token with neither gets a `403`.
> -   A personal access token restricted to selected workspaces and apps gets a `200` with only the results inside its [content access](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#content-selection).
> 
> A user API key has neither restriction. It gets both result types across everything its owner can see.

### Rate limit credits

The [base request cost](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits) is 10 credits. A search costs 50 credits (5× base) with either endpoint. On the standard budget of 2,000 credits per minute, that's about 40 searches per minute.

| Endpoint | Credits |
| --- | --- |
| [`GET /v1/search`](#search) | 50 (5× base) |
| [`POST /v1/search`](#search-with-a-filter) | 50 (5× base) |

Every page costs another 50 credits. Prefer a large `limit` over many small pages.

## The search result object

Every response has the same two keys:

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `results` | `array` | The matches, in the requested order. Empty when nothing matched. | `[{ "type": "app", "app": { … } }]` |
| `cursor` | `string` | `null` | Send it back to get the next page. `null` means this was the last page. | `"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."` |

There is *no `total`*, because counting matches would double the cost of every search. Page until `cursor` is `null`.

Each entry in `results` has exactly two keys: `type`, and a payload named after it. Check `type` to know which payload you have.

| `type` | Payload key | Payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"app"` | `app` | An app preview, including the name of the workspace it lives in. |
| `"record"` | `record` | A record preview, without its field values. |

Apps and records come in *one* `results` array, mixed by relevance, not in separate lists. To get only one kind, narrow the search with `types`: [`?types=record`](#search) on `GET`, or [`filter.types`](#search-with-a-filter) on `POST`.

### App results

The `app` payload is the same as an entry from [`GET /v1/app`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-all-available-apps), including `workspace_name`.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `app_id` | `integer` | The app ID. | `4821` |
| `workspace_id` | `integer` | The workspace the app lives in. | `913` |
| `workspace_name` | `string` | The workspace's name. Empty string if the workspace is being deleted. | `"Sales"` |
| `slug` | `string` | The app's URL slug. | `"customer-onboarding"` |
| `external_id` | `string` | *Deprecated.* Identical to `slug`. | `"customer-onboarding"` |
| `name` | `string` | The app's name. | `"Customer Onboarding"` |
| `record_name` | `string` | Singular noun for one of the app's records, for example `Project`. | `"Onboarding"` |
| `item_name` | `string` | *Deprecated.* Identical to `record_name`. | `"Onboarding"` |
| `type` | `string` | One of `database`, `dashboard`, `form`. Legacy apps without a type report `database`. | `"database"` |
| `description` | `string` | Optional. Missing when the app has no description. | `"Every new customer, start to finish"` |
| `position` | `number` | The app's position within its workspace. Fractional: Tape reorders apps by inserting between neighbors, so expect values like `107.125125118059`. | `3` |
| `config` | `object` | Legacy-compatible copy of `name`, `item_name` and `description`. | `{ "name": "Customer Onboarding", … }` |

### Record results

The `record` payload is the same as a record preview from [`GET /v1/record/field/{field_id}/find`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#find-relatable-records-for-a-relation-field).

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `record_id` | `integer` | The global record ID. Use it to fetch the record. | `170471696` |
| `app_record_id` | `integer` | The record's running number within its database app. | `42` |
| `record_url` | `string` | Link to the record in Tape. | `"https://tapeapp.com/acme/record/170471696"` |
| `app_id` | `integer` | The database app the record belongs to. | `4821` |
| `app` | `object` | Preview of the database app, including its `workspace`. | `{ "app_id": 4821, "name": "Customer Onboarding", … }` |
| `title` | `string` | The record's computed title. May be missing. | `"Acme Corp onboarding"` |
| `created_on` | `string` | `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, in your timezone. | `"2026-08-03 09:14:22"` |
| `created_on_utc` | `string` | The same moment as `created_on`, in UTC. | `"2026-08-03 07:14:22"` |
| `deleted_on` | `string` | Only for a record in the trash. In your timezone. | `"2026-08-12 10:00:00"` |
| `deleted_on_utc` | `string` | The same moment as `deleted_on`, in UTC. | `"2026-08-12 08:00:00"` |
| `created_by` | `object` | `null` | The user or automation that created the record. | `{ "type": "user", "user_id": 5501, … }` |
| `current_revision` | `object` | `null` | The record's latest revision. | `{ "type": "update", "revision": 7, … }` |
| `initial_revision` | `object` | `null` | The record's first revision. | `{ "type": "creation", "revision": 0, … }` |

A record preview has no `fields`, `last_modified_on`, `last_modified_by` or `comment_count`. Fetch the record itself if you need them.

## Search

Use this endpoint to search all apps and records you can see.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/search`

*Request*

```shell
curl -G https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "text=onboarding" \
  --data-urlencode "limit=20"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "results": [
    {
      "type": "app",
      "app": {
        "app_id": 4821,
        "workspace_id": 913,
        "workspace_name": "Sales",
        "slug": "customer-onboarding",
        "external_id": "customer-onboarding",
        "name": "Customer Onboarding",
        "record_name": "Onboarding",
        "item_name": "Onboarding",
        "type": "database",
        "description": "Every new customer, start to finish",

          }

        "title": "Acme Corp onboarding",
        "created_on": "2026-08-03 09:14:22",
        "created_on_utc": "2026-08-03 07:14:22",
        "created_by": {
          "id": 5501,
          "user_id": 5501,
          "org_id": 77,
          "type": "user",
          "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],

          "type": "update",
          "revision": 7,

          "created_by": {
            "id": 5501,
            "user_id": 5501,
            "org_id": 77,
            "type": "user",
            "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
            "name": "Juliet Adams"
          }
        },
        "initial_revision": {
          "type": "creation",
          "revision": 0,
          "record_id": 170471696,
          "created_on": "2026-08-03 09:14:22",

            "user_id": 5501,

            "type": "user",
            "mail": ["juliet@acme.com"],
            "name": "Juliet Adams"
          }
        }
      }

  "cursor": "eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."

```

Send `text` to start a search, or `cursor` to continue one.

The example returns one app and one record that match "onboarding". To get the next page, send the `cursor` back ([Pagination](#pagination)).

**General behavior**

-   Send exactly one of `text` or `cursor`. Neither returns a `400`. Both is accepted, but the cursor wins and Tape ignores `text`.
-   `types` is comma-separated (`?types=app,record`). The repeated form `?types=app&types=record` doesn't work. An unknown member returns a `400`; Tape doesn't drop it.
-   Narrowing `types` to one kind doesn't enlarge the page. A page still holds at most `limit` results, but the other kind no longer takes slots in it.
-   URL-encode `text`. An unencoded `&` or `=` cuts your query short without an error.
-   Records shared with you individually, in apps you can't open, match only if you set `search_shared_content` to `true`.

**Requirements:** `apps:read` or `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

See [Errors](#errors).

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | Yes\* | The text to search for. Between 1 and 100 characters, and must contain a searchable term. |
| `cursor` | `string` | Yes\* | Cursor from a previous response, to get the next page. Send it on its own. |
| `limit` | `integer` | No | Results per page. Between `1` and `100`. Defaults to `50`. |
| `types` | `string` | No | Comma-separated kinds to return: `app`, `record`, or `app,record`. Leave it out to get both. |
| `sort_by` | `string` | No | One of `ranking_score`, `created_on`, `last_modified_on`. Defaults to `ranking_score`. |
| `sort_desc` | `boolean` | No | Order descending. Defaults to `true`. See [Sorting](#sorting). |
| `search_shared_content` | `boolean` | No | Also search records shared with you individually (through a grant on the record or a permission rule that matches you) in apps you can't open. Defaults to `false`. Records you can already reach through an app come back once. |

\* Exactly one of `text` or `cursor` is required.

## Search with a filter

Use this endpoint to search with a filter for workspaces, apps, authors or time windows.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/search`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/search?limit=20 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "text": "onboarding",
    "filter": {
      "types": ["record"],
      "workspace_ids": [913, 914],
      "last_modified_at_from": "2026-08-01 00:00:00"
    },
    "sort_by": "last_modified_on"
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "text": "onboarding",
  "filter": {
    "types": ["record"],
    "workspace_ids": [913, 914],
    "last_modified_at_from": "2026-08-01 00:00:00"
  },
  "sort_by": "last_modified_on"
}
```

This is the same URL and the same search as [`GET /v1/search`](#search), sent as a JSON body. The request creates nothing, so it returns `200`, not `201`.

The example finds records that mention "onboarding" in two workspaces and changed after a fixed moment.

The response has the same shape as for [`GET /v1/search`](#search).

**General behavior**

-   The filter only restricts *which* apps and records count. It doesn't change *how* text matches.
-   Filter members combine with `AND`. Each member is optional. A member you leave out means no restriction.
-   The four date bounds are *absolute and independent*. Send only a `_from` for "since", only a `_to` for "until", or both for a closed window.
-   A `_from` later than its `_to` returns a `400`, not an empty result. So does a date that doesn't exist, such as `2026-02-30`.
-   Tape rejects unknown keys. `workspaceIds` instead of `workspace_ids` returns a `400`, so the API never accepts a filter it doesn't apply.
-   `limit` is the only query parameter. There is no `cursor` here. Continue a filtered search with [`GET /v1/search?cursor=…`](#pagination), because the cursor carries the filter.
-   Set `search_shared_content` to `true` to also find records shared with you individually.

**Requirements:** `apps:read` or `records:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

See [Errors](#errors).

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `string` | Yes | The text to search for. Between 1 and 100 characters, and must contain a searchable term. |
| `filter` | `object` | No | Restrictions on which apps and records count. See below. |
| `sort_by` | `string` | No | One of `ranking_score`, `created_on`, `last_modified_on`. Defaults to `ranking_score`. |
| `sort_desc` | `boolean` | No | Order descending. Defaults to `true`. Must be a real JSON boolean, not a string. |
| `search_shared_content` | `boolean` | No | Also search records shared with you individually (through a grant on the record or a permission rule that matches you) in apps you can't open. Defaults to `false`. Records you can already reach through an app come back once. |

**`filter` object**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `types` | `string[]` | Kinds to return: `["app"]`, `["record"]` or both. Must not be empty or contain duplicates. Leave it out to get both. |
| `workspace_ids` | `integer[]` | Only results in one of these workspaces. At most 100 IDs. |
| `app_ids` | `integer[]` | Only records of one of these apps, and only these apps themselves. At most 100 IDs. |
| `created_by_user_ids` | `integer[]` | Only results created by one of these users. At most 100 IDs. |
| `created_at_from` | `string` | Only results created at or after this moment. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, in your timezone. |
| `created_at_to` | `string` | Only results created at or before this moment. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, in your timezone. |
| `last_modified_at_from` | `string` | Only results last changed at or after this moment. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, in your timezone. |
| `last_modified_at_to` | `string` | Only results last changed at or before this moment. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss`, in your timezone. |
| `created_at_from_utc` | `string` | Same as `created_at_from`, read as UTC. Wins if you send both. |
| `created_at_to_utc` | `string` | Same as `created_at_to`, read as UTC. Wins if you send both. |
| `last_modified_at_from_utc` | `string` | Same as `last_modified_at_from`, read as UTC. Wins if you send both. |
| `last_modified_at_to_utc` | `string` | Same as `last_modified_at_to`, read as UTC. Wins if you send both. |

To find these IDs, see [Retrieve workspaces](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/workspace#retrieve-workspaces), [Retrieve all available apps](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-all-available-apps) and [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).

The unsuffixed bounds use the timezone `created_on` is returned in, so you can send a value from a result straight back. See [Date & timezone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone).

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | `integer` | No | Results per page. Between `1` and `100`. Defaults to `50`. |

### Polling for changes

Use `last_modified_at_from` for an incremental sync. Send the time of your last successful poll to get only what changed since then.

*Request*

```json
{
  "text": "invoice",
  "filter": {
    "types": ["record"],
    "app_ids": [4821],
    "last_modified_at_from": "2026-08-11 14:30:00"
  },
  "sort_by": "last_modified_on",
  "sort_desc": false
}
```

> Which bound should a sync loop send?
> 
> Send `last_modified_at_from_utc`. A local time has no offset, so it's ambiguous when daylight saving time ends.

> Why do unchanged apps and records drop out?
> 
> An app or record nobody changed after creating it has no last-modified timestamp, so it drops out as soon as you set either bound. A sync built only on `last_modified_at_from` never sees new records nobody touched yet. Add a search with `created_at_from` over the same window, or start with a search without a filter.

## Pagination

Search uses *cursor pagination*, not `limit` and `offset`. To go through all results:

1.  Search with either endpoint. Read `results`.
2.  If `cursor` is `null`, you're done.
3.  Otherwise, call `GET /v1/search` with only that `cursor`, and read the next `results`.

*Request*

```shell
curl -G https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/search \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  --data-urlencode "cursor=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..."
```

A cursor is an opaque, signed token. It holds the whole search: text, filter, `search_shared_content`, sorting and page size. That means:

-   **Continue with `GET`,** also for a search you started with `POST`. `POST` takes no cursor, because a cursor leaves nothing for a body to add.
-   **Send the cursor alone.** Tape ignores `text`, `sort_by` or `sort_desc` sent with it. It also ignores `limit`: a continued search keeps the page size of the search that created the cursor, so all pages have the same size.
-   **Don't build, edit or store cursors.** They're signed and can expire. Hand them straight back to the API.

A page can have fewer entries than `limit` and still not be the last page. For example, Tape drops a record whose workspace is being deleted instead of failing the request. Trust `cursor`, not the length of `results`.

> Can a search stop before the last page?
> 
> No, there is no partial mode. Tape rejects a search it can't page with a `400` instead of returning a cut-off first page, so a page with `cursor: null` means you've seen everything. [What matches](#what-matches) lists the queries Tape rejects.

## Sorting

| `sort_by` | Orders by |
| --- | --- |
| `ranking_score` | Relevance, best match first. The default. |
| `created_on` | When the app or record was created. |
| `last_modified_on` | When the app or record was last changed. |

`sort_desc` defaults to `true`: best match first for `ranking_score`, newest first for the two timestamps. Send `false` to reverse the order. With `ranking_score`, that puts the *worst* matches first, which you rarely want.

Results with the same sort value are ordered by ID *descending*, whatever `sort_desc` says. This keeps paging stable.

The API doesn't return the ranking score. You see relevance only in the order of the array.

## What matches

Search runs over a text index for each app and each record, not over raw field values. So some behavior differs from a `contains` filter.

**Terms match as prefixes, and all terms must match.** Each word of the query matches from the start of an indexed word: `onboard` finds "onboarding", but `onboardings` doesn't. With several words, a result must match every word.

**Matching ignores case** and knows common stop words.

**More than titles is indexed.** For a record, the index covers text and multi-line text fields, calculations, email, phone, link, location, unique ID, number, category, status, date and relation values, *and its comments*. A record can match on a comment, even though the result shows no comment data. For an app, the index covers its name, description and blocks. The index cuts long values at 2,000 characters per field.

**`text` is required and must contain a searchable term**, with 1 to 100 characters. Text made only of punctuation or symbols, such as `"..."` or `"!!!"`, returns a `400`, not an empty result. To narrow by filter alone, search for a term you expect and add the filter.

> Does a short query return `400`?
> 
> Most organizations can search for any term of one character or more. In a few very large organizations, a query with fewer than four characters returns a `400` that names the minimum. It's an error, not an empty `200`, so you can tell "query too short" apart from "nothing matched".

Tape checks both rules only when a search *starts*. Continuing with a cursor doesn't check them again.

## Errors

Every input problem returns `400`. Common causes:

-   Neither `text` nor `cursor` on `GET /v1/search`.
-   `text` that is empty, longer than 100 characters, or has no searchable term.
-   `text` shorter than the minimum your organization enforces.
-   `limit` that isn't an integer, is above `100`, or is below `1`.
-   `sort_by` outside the three accepted values.
-   `sort_desc` that isn't boolean-like on `GET`, or not a real boolean on `POST`.
-   `types` with anything other than `app` or `record`, or an empty `types` list.
-   A date bound that is malformed, doesn't exist (`2026-02-30`), or a `_from` later than its `_to`.
-   A `POST` body that is missing `text`, isn't valid JSON, has an unknown key, or has an ID array with more than 100 entries.
-   An automation API key.

*Response*

```json
{
  "status_code": 400,
  "endpoint": "/v1/search",
  "error_code": "validation",
  "error_message": "A search must provide either the \"text\" or the \"cursor\" query parameter (none provided)"
}
```

For body schema errors on `POST /v1/search`, `error_code` is `input_validation`, and `error_message` names the path that failed.

Other errors:

-   A request without a credential, or from an organization guest, returns `401`.
-   A personal access token or OAuth access token with neither `apps:read` nor `records:read` returns `403`.
-   Too many searches return `429`. See [Rate limit credits](#rate-limit-credits).
-   A search never returns `404`. Anything you can't see is missing from `results`.

See [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) for all error codes.

## Known limitations

-   **Apps and records only.** Search doesn't return workspaces, users, files, comments, tasks, views or automations, even though comment text feeds the record index.
-   **No `total`.** Page until `cursor` is `null`.
-   **No relevance score and no highlights.** You can't tell *how* well a result matched, or *where*.
-   **No browsing without a search term.** Every request needs real text. A filter alone can't produce results.
-   **No relative date windows.** Date bounds are absolute timestamps you compute yourself.
-   **No search in a single field.** To match a specific field, use [`POST /v1/record/filter/app/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-filtered-records-for-an-app).
-   **Previews only.** Search results have no field values.

# User

> Use these endpoints to read the current user, list and search the users of your organization, and invite new users.

Use these endpoints to read the current user, list and search the users of your organization, and invite new users.

Use a `user_id` to set a [user field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/user) or to [add a workspace member](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/workspace#add-a-workspace-member).

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> Retrieving the current user needs no capability. Listing and searching organization users needs `organization:read`. Adding users and resending invitations needs `organization.members:manage`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

> Coming from the Podio API?
> 
> The Tape API has no contacts endpoints, because a user is a person in your organization. Keep external contacts as records in a database app.

## Retrieve the current user

Use this endpoint to check which user a credential belongs to and what it may do.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/user`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/user \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "user_id": 10000,
  "org_id": 1337,
  "org_name": "Acme Inc.",
  "name": "Juliet Adams",
  "status": "active",
  "role": "owner",
  "email": "juliet@acme.com",
  "phone": "555 123 456",
  "job_description": "Founder & CEO",
  "authentication": {
    "method": "personal_access_token",
    "scopes": ["apps:read", "records:read"],
    "content_access": {
      "scope": "selected",
      "workspace_ids": [42],
      "app_ids": []
    }
  }
}
```

The response contains the user, the name of their organization and the `authentication` block of the credential. The endpoint returns only the credential's own user. Use it to find your own `user_id`.

`phone` and `job_description` appear only when the user has set them.

The `authentication` block describes the credential of the request:

| `method` | `scopes` | `content_access` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `personal_access_token` | The token's capabilities | `scope` is `all`, or `selected` with the selected `workspace_ids` and `app_ids` |
| `oauth_access_token` | The scopes of the access token | `{"scope": "all", "workspace_ids": [], "app_ids": []}` |
| `user_key` | `null`. A user API key has no restrictions | `null` |

**Requirements:** none. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Retrieve organization users

Use this endpoint to list all users of your organization.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/org/user`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/org/user \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "user_id": 10000,
      "name": "Juliet Adams",
      "org_id": 1337,
      "status": "active",
      "email": "juliet@acme.com",
      "phone": "555 123 456",
      "role": "owner",
      "job_description": "Founder & CEO"
    },
    {
      "user_id": 10001,
      "name": "Zoe Maxwell",
      "org_id": 1337,
      "status": "active",
      "email": "zoe@acme.com",
      "phone": "555 123 457",
      "role": "member",
      "job_description": "Executive"
    }
  ],
  "total": 2
}
```

Tape takes the organization from your credential. The example lists the users of the organization with ID `1337`.

**General behavior**

-   The list includes deactivated users. Their `status` is `deactivated`.
-   `phone` and `job_description` appear only when the user has set them.

**Requirements:** `organization:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Guests of the organization can't list its users.

## Search organization users

Use this endpoint to find users of your organization by name.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/org/user/search?query={query}`

*Request*

```shell
curl "https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/org/user/search?query=zoe" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "users": [
    {
      "user_id": 10001,
      "name": "Zoe Maxwell",
      "org_id": 1337,
      "status": "active",
      "email": "zoe@acme.com",
      "phone": "555 123 457",
      "role": "member",
      "job_description": "Executive"
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
```

**General behavior**

-   Tape returns every user whose name or short name contains `query`. Upper and lower case don't matter.
-   Deactivated users aren't returned.
-   `total` is the number of users in this response, not the number of all matches.

**Requirements:** `organization:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key. Guests of the organization can't search its users.

**Errors**

A missing or empty `query`, or a `limit` out of range, returns `400`.

**Query parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `query` | `string` | Text to search for in names and short names. |
| `limit` | `integer` | Number of users to return. Optional. |

## Add user to organization

Use this endpoint to add a new user to your organization.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/org/user`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/org/user \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "name": "Roger Klein",
    "email": "roger@acme.com",
    "role": "admin",
    "skip_invitation": true
  }'
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "user_id": 10002,
  "name": "Roger Klein",
  "org_id": 1337,
  "status": "active",
  "email": "roger@acme.com",
  "role": "admin"
}
```

Tape sends the new user an invitation email. To skip it, set `skip_invitation` to `true` and send the invitation later with [Resend user invitation email](#resend-user-invitation-email).

> Which organization roles can I give?
> 
> Set `role` to `"owner"`, `"admin"`, `"member"` or `"guest"`. These are the organization roles [described in the Help Center](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/6453902-manage-members-admins-guests-groups). You can't give a role higher than your own, and adding admins and members is billable.

**Requirements:** `organization.members:manage`, and the **Owner** or **Admin** role in the organization. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Required. Name of the user. |
| `email` | `string` | Required. Email address of the user. |
| `role` | `string` | Required. One of `owner`, `admin`, `member` or `guest`. |
| `skip_invitation` | `boolean` | Don't send the invitation email (default: `false`). |

## Resend user invitation email

Use this endpoint to send the invitation email to an organization user again.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/org/user/{user_id}/resend-invitation`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/org/user/10002/resend-invitation \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{}
```

Use it to invite a user you created with `skip_invitation`. You can send it more than once.

**Requirements:** `organization.members:manage`, and the **Owner** or **Admin** role in the organization. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.
