# View

> Use these endpoints to read, create, update, promote and delete the views of an app.

Use these endpoints to read, create, update, promote and delete the views of an app.

A *view* is a saved way of looking at the records of a database app. Every view belongs to exactly one app and stores:

-   a *layout* (`table`, `list` or `board`) and its layout-specific *display configuration*, such as table row height, board grouping and card preview;
-   an ordered list of *filters*: which records the view shows;
-   a *sort*: one field and a direction, or none, which means the manual record order of the app;
-   per-*field* display settings: which fields are visible and how wide the columns are;
-   an optional *split by*: the field the view groups its records into sections by;
-   how it renders *progress bars* (`show_progress`).

Every app has exactly one *default view*, the one users land on when they open the app. Views you create through this API are *public*: everyone who can see the app can see them.

A common use is to read a view in one app and recreate it in another, for example when you migrate a workspace between organizations. See [Copy a view to another app](#copy-a-view-to-another-app).

This resource returns no records and no computed data, such as sections, counts per section or column totals. To read the records of a view, use [`GET /v1/record/view/{view_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-records-for-a-view).

To find a view ID, see [Retrieve views for an app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-views-for-an-app), which lists the public views of an app. In Tape, open the view: its ID is the number after `/views/` in the address.

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> Reading a view needs `apps:read`. Creating, updating, promoting and deleting a view need `apps:edit`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

> Changing `filters` or `fields` with `PUT`?
> 
> An update *replaces* the `filters` array and the `fields` map and never merges them. A key you leave out keeps its stored value. Read [Update a view](#update-a-view) before you write.

## Authentication and permissions

The five `/v1/view/...` endpoints need a credential that acts on behalf of a user: a [user API key](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#user-api-key), a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) or an [OAuth access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview). Send it as a bearer token. Permissions depend on that user.

An automation API key returns `401` with the message `App views can only be accessed with a user API key.` The message names only the user API key, but a personal access token or an OAuth access token works too.

The list endpoint on the app resource is the one exception. It also accepts an automation API key, subject to view access.

Tape checks permissions in two layers against the app the view belongs to:

-   **Reading** a view needs *view access* to the app.
-   **Creating, updating, deleting or promoting** a view needs *share access* to the app (**Can share** or **Full access**), one level above edit access. Edit access to records is not enough to change how everyone in the app sees them.

### Rate limit credits

The [base request cost](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits) is 10 credits. This resource charges:

| Endpoint | Credits |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/app/{app_id}/views` | 50 (5× base) |
| [`GET /v1/view/{view_id}`](#retrieve-a-single-view) | 20 (2× base) |
| [`POST /v1/view/app/{app_id}`](#create-a-view) | 50 (5× base) |
| [`PUT /v1/view/{view_id}`](#update-a-view) | 50 (5× base) |
| [`POST /v1/view/{view_id}/default`](#set-the-default-view) | 50 (5× base) |
| [`DELETE /v1/view/{view_id}`](#delete-a-view) | 50 (5× base) |

## The view object

The list endpoint returns a *preview* of each view. Every other endpoint returns the *detail* object, which adds the full definition, inside a `{ "view": … }` envelope.

### Preview

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | number | The view ID. | `88123` |
| `view_id` | number | Same as `id`. Present for consistency with the rest of the API. | `88123` |
| `name` | string | null | Name of the view. `null` for a view that was never named. | `"Open tickets"` |
| `app_id` | number | The app the view belongs to. | `4711` |
| `is_default` | boolean | Exactly one view per app is `true`. | `false` |
| `layout` | `"table"` | `"list"` | `"board"` | Layout of the view. See [Field settings](#field-settings). | `"table"` |
| `private` | boolean | `false` for every view this API can create. See [Limitations](#known-limitations). | `false` |

### Detail

Everything in the preview, plus:

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sort_by` | number | null | The `field_id` the view is sorted by. `null` means manual record order. | `55204` |
| `sort_desc` | boolean | `true` for descending. `false` when there is no sort. | `false` |
| `filters` | array | The filters of the view, flat and combined with AND. See [Filters](#filters). | `[{ "field_id": 55203, … }]` |
| `fields` | object | Display settings per field, keyed by `field_id`, for the current layout of the view. See [Field settings](#field-settings). | `{ "55207": { "hidden": true } }` |
| `split_by` | object | null | The split-by definition, or `null`. See [Split by](#split-by). | `null` |
| `show_progress` | `"none"` | `"view"` | `"split_by"` | `"all"` | How the view renders progress bars. See [Display configuration](#display-configuration). | `"none"` |
| `table` | object | null | Display settings of the table layout, or `null` unless `layout` is `table`. See [Display configuration](#display-configuration). | `{ "row_height": "medium", "wrap_cells": false }` |
| `board` | object | null | Board grouping, card preview and display settings, or `null` unless `layout` is `board`. See [Display configuration](#display-configuration). | `null` |

The `fields` object contains an entry for *every* field of the app. Fields without a stored setting appear with their effective default. This makes a `GET` → `PUT` round trip faithful: you can send a detail response back to [Update a view](#update-a-view) unchanged.

## Retrieve a single view

Use this endpoint to read a view with its full definition.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/{view_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/88123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "view": {
    "id": 88123,
    "view_id": 88123,
    "name": "Open tickets",
    "app_id": 4711,
    "is_default": false,
    "layout": "table",
    "private": false,
    "sort_by": 55204,
    "sort_desc": false,
    "filters": [
      {
        "field_id": 55203,
        "field_type": "status",
        "type": "status",
        "match_type": "any",
        "values": [{ "value": 9001 }, { "value": 9002 }]
      },
      {
        "field_id": 55201,
        "field_type": "single_text",
        "type": "text",
        "match_type": "contains",
        "values": [{ "value": "urgent" }]
      }
    ],
    "fields": {
      "55201": { "hidden": false, "width": 320 },
      "55203": { "hidden": false, "width": 160 },
      "55204": { "hidden": false },
      "55207": { "hidden": true }
    },
    "split_by": null,
    "show_progress": "none",
    "table": { "row_height": "medium", "wrap_cells": false },
    "board": null
  }
}
```

**General behavior**

-   `width` appears only for `table` views, and only for fields with a stored width.
-   `table` is present only for `table` views, and `board` only for `board` views. The other one is `null`.
-   Filter operands come back *normalized to IDs*. A status or category filter written with option names comes back as `{ "value": <option_id> }`. A relation filter comes back as `{ "value": <record_id> }`.

**Requirements:** `apps:read`, and view access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Create a view

Use this endpoint to add a view to an app.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/app/4711 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "name": "Open tickets",
    "layout": "table",
    "sort_by": 55204,
    "sort_desc": false,
    "filters": [
      {
        "field_id": 55203,
        "field_type": "status",
        "type": "status",
        "match_type": "any",
        "values": [{ "value": 9001 }, { "value": 9002 }]
      }
    ],
    "fields": {
      "55201": { "hidden": false, "width": 320 },
      "55203": { "hidden": false, "width": 160 },
      "55207": { "hidden": true }
    },
    "split_by": { "field_id": 55203, "sorting": "label_asc", "limit": 25 }
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "name": "Open tickets",
  "layout": "table",
  "sort_by": 55204,
  "sort_desc": false,
  "filters": [
    {
      "field_id": 55203,
      "field_type": "status",
      "type": "status",
      "match_type": "any",
      "values": [{ "value": 9001 }, { "value": 9002 }]
    }
  ],
  "fields": {
    "55201": { "hidden": false, "width": 320 },
    "55203": { "hidden": false, "width": 160 },
    "55207": { "hidden": true }
  },
  "split_by": { "field_id": 55203, "sorting": "label_asc", "limit": 25 }
}
```

Send `name` and `layout`. Everything else is optional. The new view is never the default view until you [promote it](#set-the-default-view).

The response is `201` with the `{ "view": … }` envelope and the full [detail object](#the-view-object).

**General behavior**

-   `null` is *not* accepted for any key on create. Only an update can clear a value, because on create there is nothing to clear.
-   An unknown or misspelled key returns `400`.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and share access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Yes | Max 200 characters; empty string allowed. |
| `layout` | `"table"` | `"list"` | `"board"` | Yes | No default, send one. |
| `filters` | array | No | Max 100 entries; see [Filters](#filters). |
| `sort_by` | number (`field_id`) | No | Must be a field of this app. |
| `sort_desc` | boolean | No | Defaults to `false`; ignored without `sort_by`. |
| `fields` | object keyed by `field_id` | No | `hidden` required per entry; see [Field settings](#field-settings). |
| `split_by` | object | No | See [Split by](#split-by). |
| `show_progress` | `"none"` | `"view"` | `"split_by"` | `"all"` | No | Defaults to `none`; see [Display configuration](#display-configuration). |
| `table` | object | No | `table` layout only; see [Display configuration](#display-configuration). |
| `board` | object | No | `board` layout only; see [Display configuration](#display-configuration). |

## Update a view

Use this endpoint to change a view.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/{view_id}`

*Request*

```json
{ "name": "Open tickets — EMEA" }
```

Every key is optional. Send only what you want to change.

**Rename only.** Everything else stays:

**Replace the filters and clear the sort:**

*Request*

```json
{
  "filters": [
    {
      "field_id": 55201,
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "type": "text",
      "match_type": "starts_with",
      "values": [{ "value": "EMEA" }]
    }
  ],
  "sort_by": null
}
```

**Switch the layout and give the list layout its own field settings:**

*Request*

```json
{
  "layout": "list",
  "fields": {
    "55201": { "hidden": false },
    "55203": { "hidden": false },
    "55207": { "hidden": true }
  }
}
```

The response is `200` with the `{ "view": … }` envelope after the update.

**This is a partial update:**

| In the body | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| key *omitted* | the stored value is *preserved* |
| key present with a *value* | the stored value is *replaced* |
| key present with `null` | the stored value is *cleared* (two exceptions below) |

**Collections are replaced in full, never merged.**

-   `filters`: an array replaces the entire filter list. There is no "add one filter" operation. To add a filter, [retrieve the view](#retrieve-a-single-view), add it to the array you got back, and send the whole array with `PUT`. `null` clears all filters.
-   `fields`: the map replaces the display settings of the effective layout of the view in full. Fields you leave out lose their stored settings and fall back to the default visibility of the layout. `null` clears them all.

**Two exceptions to "`null` clears":**

1.  **`name: null` preserves the name.** An unnamed view reads as `name: null`, so the update accepts `null` to keep a read body `PUT`\-able. There is no way to remove a name: `null` and `""` both mean "leave it alone".
2.  **`width` is ignored on layouts other than `table`.** It is tolerated, not rejected. A client that reads a `table` view, switches `layout` to `"list"` and sends the body back doesn't need to strip `width` from every entry.

**Read-only keys are accepted and ignored.** So that you can send a detail response back as is, the update body also tolerates `id`, `view_id`, `app_id`, `is_default`, `private` and `sort_property`. None of them has any effect.

> Sending `is_default: true` in a `PUT` body?
> 
> Tape ignores `is_default` in an update body without an error. Promotion is a separate endpoint ([`POST /v1/view/{view_id}/default`](#set-the-default-view)).

**General behavior**

-   **The effective layout.** If you change `layout` and send `fields` in the same request, the map goes to the *new* layout. The other layouts keep their settings. See [Field settings](#field-settings).
-   **Display config.** You can replace `show_progress` but never clear it. `table` and `board` each replace their config in full when sent. Leaving them out, *or sending `null`*, keeps the stored config, so a detail `GET` with `table: null` or `board: null` round-trips unchanged. See [Display configuration](#display-configuration).
-   **Settings the API doesn't expose stay intact:** column footer statistics, the *lane customization* of a board, and the settings of the layouts the view is not in. The one exception is split-by drill-down filters (see [Limitations](#known-limitations)).
-   **Sort direction.** `sort_desc` on its own flips the direction of the existing sort and keeps the sort field. `sort_by` without `sort_desc` resets the direction to ascending, because `sort_by` replaces the whole sort.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and share access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Set the default view

Use this endpoint to make a view the default view of its app.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/{view_id}/default`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/88123/default \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

The request takes *no body*.

The response is `200` with the `{ "view": … }` envelope and `is_default: true`. The previous default view of the app loses its default flag in the same operation, so the app keeps exactly one default view.

**General behavior**

-   You can't remove the default flag from a view. You can only promote a different one.
-   Promoting a view that is already the default changes nothing and returns `200`.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and share access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Delete a view

Use this endpoint to delete a view.

`DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/{view_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/view/88123 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{ "view_id": 88123 }
```

The view is soft-deleted, and every endpoint returns `404` for it afterwards. Records are never affected.

**Requirements:** `apps:edit`, and share access to the app. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

Deleting the current default view of an app returns `400` with the message `The default view of an app cannot be deleted. Set another view as the default first.` [Promote another view](#set-the-default-view) first, then delete it.

## Filters

The filters of a view are a *flat array*, combined with `AND`, with no `OR`, grouping or nesting. The array order is the filter order (there is no `position` key). A view holds *at most 100 filters*.

**A view filter is the same filter object as in `POST /v1/record/filter/app/{app_id}`**, with the same `match_type` values and operand keys. The [filter reference](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/filter) lists every field type and its match types.

Every filter entry has at least a `field_id`, a `field_type`, a `type` discriminator and a `match_type`:

```json
{
  "field_id": 55201,
  "field_type": "single_text",
  "type": "text",
  "match_type": "contains",
  "values": [{ "value": "urgent" }]
}
```

-   `field_id`, `field_type` and `match_type` are *required*. `type` is required in practice: leaving it out returns `400`.
-   `values` is the operand list. Its shape depends on the field type. Leave it out for `empty` and `not_empty`.
-   Only *field filters* are accepted. The metadata filters of the record endpoint (`created_at`, `last_modified_at`, `app_record_id`) are not part of the stored filters of a view.

Three facts apply to views only:

-   **References must resolve.** Tape *stores* view filters, so an operand that names something invalid returns `400` instead of matching nothing. This applies to a `single_relation` or `multi_relation` filter that names a record that doesn't exist (`Record(s) with ID … referenced by filters do not exist.`), and to a user filter (`single_user`, `multi_user`, `created_by`, `last_modified_by`, checklist `assignee`) that names a user outside your organization. Deactivated organization members are still valid operands.
    
-   **`include_active_user` ("@me")** resolves to the owner of the credential you authenticate with. A view saved with it changes per viewer, as in the app:
    
    ```json
    {
      "field_id": 55208,
      "field_type": "single_user",
      "type": "contact",
      "match_type": "equal",
      "include_active_user": true
    }
    ```
    
-   A relative date filter or a checklist filter uses the same operand keys as in the record filter reference:
    
    ```json
    {
      "field_id": 55204,
      "field_type": "single_date",
      "type": "date",
      "match_type": "within",
      "relative_date_range_type": "next_week"
    }
    ```
    

## Field settings

`fields` is a JSON object keyed by `field_id`. The key is a string, because JSON object keys are strings. Each value is `{ "hidden": boolean, "width"?: number }`.

**It applies to one layout at a time.** A view stores display settings separately for each layout. `fields` addresses the current layout, or the new one on a write that also changes `layout`. Switch from `table` to `list` and back, and the original column widths and visibility return.

**`hidden` is required on every entry you write**, though optional in the response. The default means *visible* on `table` and *hidden* on `list` and `board`, so an entry like `{ "55201": { "width": 200 } }` on a list view would silently hide that field. A `GET` → `PUT` round trip is safe, because the read returns `hidden` for every field.

**`width` matters only for `table`.** It is in pixels and must be between 100 and 1500. On `list` and `board`, it is never returned. On write, it is accepted and ignored there, not rejected.

Defaults for fields you don't configure, which is what a `GET` reports for them:

| Layout | A field with no stored setting is… |
| --- | --- |
| `table` | *visible* (`hidden: false`), every field |
| `list`, `board` | *visible* for the first field of the app (its title field), hidden for all others |

Every `field_id` you name must belong to the app of the view, otherwise the response is `400`. You can't set the field order: it follows the field order of the app.

## Split by

`split_by` defines how a view groups its records into sections. The API exposes only this definition, never the sections.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `field_id` | number | The field to split by. **Required.** Must belong to the app of the view. | `55203` |
| `period` | `day` | `weekday` | `week` | `month` | `year` | null | Bucket size. Only meaningful for date fields. | `"month"` |
| `sorting` | `label_asc` | `label_desc` | `value_asc` | `value_desc` | null | Section order. | `"label_asc"` |
| `limit` | number 1–100, or null | Maximum number of sections (capped at 100). | `25` |

You can split a view by a field of type `single_category`, `multi_category`, `status`, `single_user`, `multi_user`, `single_relation`, `multi_relation`, `single_date`, `range_date`, `created_on`, `last_modified_on` or `calculation`. Any other field type returns `400` (`Invalid split_by field: a field of type '…' cannot be split by`).

-   On update, `"split_by": null` *removes* the split-by. Leaving out the key preserves it.
-   Tape fills in `sorting` with `label_asc` for `single_category`, `multi_category` and `status` fields, so a `GET` can report a `sorting` you never sent.
-   A `GET` can also report a `period` you never sent, for example `month` for a split by a relation field.

## Display configuration

`show_progress` applies to every layout. `table` and `board` are layout-specific: a view in another layout reports them as `null`. Each config is *replaced in full* on write.

### `show_progress`

How the view renders progress bars:

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `none` | No progress bars (the default on create). |
| `view` | One progress bar for the whole view. |
| `split_by` | One progress bar per split-by section. |
| `all` | Both. |

### `table` (table views only)

Accepted on create and update *only* when the effective layout is `table`, otherwise the response is `400 'table' settings are only valid on a 'table' view.` When you send the object, both fields are required.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `row_height` | `"short"` | `"medium"` | `"tall"` | `"extra_tall"` | Row height. | `"medium"` |
| `wrap_cells` | boolean | Wrap cell content onto several lines instead of cutting it off. | `true` |

*table config*

```json
{ "row_height": "medium", "wrap_cells": true }
```

### `board` (board views only)

Accepted on create and update *only* when the effective layout is `board`, otherwise the response is `400 'board' settings are only valid on a 'board' view.` When you send the object, all seven fields are required.

| Property | Type | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `group_by_field_id` | number | null | The field the board groups into lanes by. Must be a `status` or `single_category` field of the app, or `null` for a board without groups. | `55203` |
| `card_preview_field_id` | number | null | The field shown as the preview image of each card. Must be a `single_attachment`, `multi_attachment` or `multi_image` field of the app, or `null` for no preview. | `55210` |
| `card_size` | `"small"` | `"medium"` | `"large"` | Card size. | `"medium"` |
| `large_text` | boolean | Show card text in the larger size. | `false` |
| `hide_empty_columns` | boolean | Hide lanes without records. | `true` |
| `color_columns` | boolean | Tint each lane with the color of its group-by option. | `true` |
| `fit_preview_image` | boolean | Scale the preview image to fill the card instead of fitting inside it. | `false` |

A `group_by_field_id` of the wrong type returns `400 Invalid board group_by field: a field of type '…' cannot group a board`. A `card_preview_field_id` of the wrong type returns `400 Invalid board card_preview field: a field of type '…' cannot be a card preview`.

*board config*

```json
{
  "group_by_field_id": 55203,
  "card_preview_field_id": 55210,
  "card_size": "medium",
  "large_text": false,
  "hide_empty_columns": true,
  "color_columns": true,
  "fit_preview_image": false
}
```

## Errors

All errors use the standard [error envelope](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors) of the API.

-   Anything you can't see returns `404`, with one message shape whatever the cause: the view ID doesn't exist, the view was deleted, the view is private to another user, you have no view access to the app, or (on create) the app ID doesn't exist or isn't visible to you. A `403` would confirm that an ID exists, so read `404` as "not found *or* not yours".
-   A write to a view or app you can see, but without *share access*, returns `403`.
-   A request without a credential, with an invalid one or with an automation API key returns `401`. See [Authentication and permissions](#authentication-and-permissions).
-   A used-up credit budget returns `429`. See [Rate limit credits](#rate-limit-credits).

A request body that isn't acceptable returns `400`. Common causes:

-   an unknown or misspelled key anywhere in the body (both request schemas are strict);
-   `name` longer than 200 characters, or (on create) a missing `name` or `layout`;
-   `layout` not one of `table`, `list` or `board`;
-   more than 100 `filters`, or a filter without `type` or with a `match_type` the field type doesn't support;
-   a `fields` key that is not a plain non-negative integer, a `fields` entry without `hidden`, or a `width` outside 100–1500;
-   `split_by` without `field_id`, a `limit` outside 1–100, or a split-by field whose type can't be split by;
-   an unknown `period`, `sorting`, `field_type`, `match_type`, `show_progress`, `row_height` or `card_size` value, or a `table` or `board` config without a required field;
-   a `field_id` (in `filters`, `sort_by`, `fields`, `split_by`, or a board `group_by_field_id` or `card_preview_field_id`) that belongs to a different app;
-   a `table` config on a view that is not a `table` view, or a `board` config on a view that is not a `board` view;
-   a board `group_by_field_id` that is not a `status` or `single_category` field, or a `card_preview_field_id` that is not a `single_attachment`, `multi_attachment` or `multi_image` field;
-   a relation filter that names a record that doesn't exist, or a user filter that names a user outside your organization;
-   `null` for any key on create;
-   the app already holds the maximum of 2000 views;
-   deleting the current *default* view of the app (`The default view of an app cannot be deleted.`).

## Known limitations

Each of these is a deliberate boundary of version 1:

1.  **The checklist sort mode is not exposed.** A view sorted by a checklist field also stores *which* part it sorts by (status, title, assignee or due date), and a `GET` → `PUT` resets that mode. The `sort_property` key is reserved for a future release and is accepted and ignored today. Don't round-trip views sorted by a checklist until it ships.
2.  **Public views only.** Every view this API creates is public. Your *own* private views are readable and writable by ID and report `"private": true`. Private views of other users return `404`, and no private view appears in the list endpoint.
3.  **No gallery layout.** `layout` is `table`, `list` or `board`. The legacy gallery layout has no public value, and you can't read a view that still uses it through this API.
4.  **Board lane customization and column statistics are preserved but not exposed.** Every update keeps the custom lane order of a board and the column footer statistics of a table, but you can't read or set them here. The other display options are in [Display configuration](#display-configuration).
5.  **Any update drops split-by drill-down filters.** When a user clicks into a section of a split view, the app writes temporary filters derived from the split-by. `GET` never reports them, and any `PUT` removes them. The app creates them again from the split-by, so nothing a user set up is lost.
6.  **No timestamps.** Views have no creation or modification metadata.
7.  **No order control.** The list endpoint returns views in no guaranteed order. No endpoint changes the order of the views of an app.

## Copy a view to another app

To recreate a view on another app, read it and then create it. Views reference apps, fields, options, users and records by ID. IDs don't carry over between organizations, so first map every source ID to its target ID.

1.  List the views of the source app: `GET /v1/app/{source_app_id}/views`.
2.  For each view, [retrieve the full definition](#retrieve-a-single-view): `GET /v1/view/{view_id}`.
3.  Rewrite the body for the target app:
    -   `sort_by` → the target field ID, or drop it;
    -   every `filters[].field_id` → the target field ID, *and every operand in `values`*: option IDs, user IDs and record IDs all need a new mapping;
    -   the keys of `fields` → target field IDs;
    -   `split_by.field_id` → the target field ID;
    -   `board.group_by_field_id` and `board.card_preview_field_id` → the target field IDs;
    -   drop `id`, `view_id`, `app_id`, `is_default` and `private`. A `PUT` tolerates them, but `POST` rejects them;
    -   drop every key whose value is `null`, for example `sort_by`, `split_by` or `board` of a table view. `POST` rejects `null` for any key;
    -   but if `name` is `null`, send a name or `""` instead, because `name` is required on create.
4.  [Create the view](#create-a-view) on the target app: `POST /v1/view/app/{target_app_id}` with `name`, `layout` and the rewritten fields, including `show_progress` and, for a `table` or `board` view, its `table` or `board` config.
5.  If the source view was the default view of its app (`is_default: true`), [promote the new view](#set-the-default-view). You can't set this in the create body.

You need *share access* to the target app, not only edit access. Each app allows at most 2000 views, which a repeated or retried bulk migration can reach.

These don't carry over. Set them up again by hand:

-   the default flag (use the promote endpoint);
-   private views (not visible in the source list);
-   the checklist sort mode;
-   column footer statistics and board lane customization;
-   views in the gallery layout (not readable);
-   the field *order* within a layout (taken from the field order of the target app).

# Webhook

> Use these endpoints to create, verify, list and delete webhooks for an app.

Use these endpoints to create, verify, list and delete webhooks for an app.

A webhook sends a POST request to your URL whenever something changes in a database app. The JSON payload carries IDs only, for example `record_id` and `revision_id`. Tape doesn't sign webhook requests, so read the record with your token to get its values.

Your URL must answer every request with a `2xx` status code within 5 seconds. See [Error handling](#error-handling).

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> All webhook endpoints need `webhooks:manage`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

> New to webhooks?
> 
> Follow [Working with webhooks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/working-with-webhooks) for a complete handler in Node.js.
> 
> Used webhooks with the Podio API? Verification works the same. Tape sends JSON instead of form parameters, and event types start with `record.` instead of `item.`. See [Coming from the Podio API](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/coming-from-podio#move-your-webhooks).

## Create a webhook

Use this endpoint to register a URL that receives events of one type from an app.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/app/{app_id}`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "type": "record.create",
    "url": "https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint"
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "type": "record.create",
  "url": "https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint"
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "hook_id": 1,
  "app_id": 1,
  "status": "inactive",
  "num_failed_executions": 0,
  "type": "record.create",
  "url": "https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint"
}
```

Send the URL and the event `type` you want to receive. To find the `app_id`, see [Find the app ID and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

**General behavior**

-   A new webhook starts with the status `inactive`.
-   Right after you create it, Tape sends the `hook.verify` request to your URL.
-   Tape sends `hook.verify` only to an `http` or `https` URL on port 80 or 443. Tape saves any other URL too, but the webhook stays `inactive`.
-   Send the code to [Validate hook verification](#validate-hook-verification), and the webhook becomes `active` and receives events.
-   Missed the code? [Request hook verification](#request-hook-verification) again.

**Requirements:** `webhooks:manage`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

A request without the **Admin** role in the app's workspace returns `400` with `workspace_invalid_permission`.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | `string` | Required. The event type, see [Webhook types](#webhook-types). |
| `url` | `string` | Required. The URL that receives the events. |

## Request hook verification

Use this endpoint to send a verification code to the URL of a webhook.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/{hook_id}/verify/request`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/1/verify/request \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "hook_id": 1,
  "status": "inactive",
  "num_failed_executions": 0,
  "type": "record.create",
  "url": "https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint"
}
```

Tape then sends a POST request to the webhook URL with `type` set to `hook.verify` and the verification code in `code`:

*Incoming request*

```json
{
  "hook_id": 1,
  "type": "hook.verify",
  "code": "f43d05e6"
}
```

To complete the verification, send this code to [Validate hook verification](#validate-hook-verification).

**General behavior**

-   Tape sends events only to verified URLs. This keeps others from sending Tape traffic to a URL they don't control.
-   Your handler can send the code back itself, so verification needs no manual step. See [Working with webhooks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/working-with-webhooks#step-1-write-the-handler).
-   To reactivate an `inactive` webhook, request the verification again.
-   Tape sends the request in the background, so the response still shows `inactive`. An `active` webhook gets no new request.

**Requirements:** `webhooks:manage`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Validate hook verification

Use this endpoint to activate a webhook with the code it received.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/{hook_id}/verify/validate`

**cURL**

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/1/verify/validate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "code": "f43d05e6"
  }'
```

**JSON**

*Request*

```json
{
  "code": "f43d05e6"
}
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "hook_id": 1,
  "status": "active",
  "num_failed_executions": 0,
  "type": "record.create",
  "url": "https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint"
}
```

With the right code, the webhook becomes `active` and its count of failed executions starts at `0` again.

**Requirements:** `webhooks:manage`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

A wrong code, or a webhook that is already active, returns `400` with `validation`.

## Retrieve app webhooks

Use this endpoint to list all webhooks of an app.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/app/{app_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "webhooks": [
    {
      "hook_id": 1,
      "app_id": 1,
      "status": "active",
      "num_failed_executions": 0,
      "type": "record.create",
      "url": "https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint"
    }
  ],
  "total": 1
}
```

**Requirements:** `webhooks:manage`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

A request without the **Admin** role in the app's workspace returns `400` with `workspace_invalid_permission`.

## Delete a webhook

`DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/{hook_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "hook_id": 1,
  "status": "inactive",
  "num_failed_executions": 0,
  "type": "record.create",
  "url": "https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint"
}
```

**Requirements:** `webhooks:manage`, and the **Admin** role in the app's workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Webhook types

Every webhook has one `type`. It decides which events Tape sends to the webhook. To receive several types, create one webhook per type with the same URL.

### Record created

The `record.create` type notifies you when someone creates a record in the database app of the webhook. Example of an incoming POST request:

**JSON**

*Incoming request*

```json

  "hook_id": 1,
  "record_id": 100,
  "revision_id": 0,
  "type": "record.create"
}
```

**HTTP**

*Incoming request*

```http
POST https://webhook.example.org/example-webhook-endpoint

Accept          application/json, text/plain, */*
Content-type    application/json;charset=utf-8
User-agent      Tape Webhook
Content-length  68
Host            webhook.example.org
Connection      close

{
  "hook_id": 1,
  "record_id": 100,
  "revision_id": 0,
  "type": "record.create"
}
```

## Avoid endless loops

A handler that changes a record in the same app starts a new event, which calls the handler again. Add the query parameter `hook=false` to every request your handler sends to change records, for example `PUT /v1/record/{record_id}?hook=false`. It works on [create, update, delete, restore](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record) and the batch endpoints.

Add `silent=true` to skip notifications, and `workflow=false` to skip automations.

## Error handling

Respond to every webhook request with a `2xx` status code within 5 seconds. Handle heavy processing after you respond.

-   Send an empty body or a short one, such as `OK`. A long body, such as an HTML page, counts as a failed request.
-   After 100 failed requests in a row, the webhook becomes `inactive`. Request the verification again to activate it.
-   Tape retries a request briefly after a timeout, a network error, a `429` or a `5xx` response. Other status codes fail at once.
-   Tape doesn't follow redirects. Use the final URL, including `https`.
-   The same event can arrive more than once. Use `record_id` and `revision_id` to skip events you already handled.
-   Tape sends webhooks only to ports 80 and 443. `https://www.example.org:8080/webhook` doesn't work. Use `https://www.example.org/webhook`.

## Rate limits

Tape sends webhook requests at a limited rate. When many events happen at the same time, requests can arrive with a short delay.

> Can these limits change?
> 
> Yes. Tape can adjust rate limits to balance demand and reliability, also with different limits per pricing plan.

## Next steps

-   [Working with webhooks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/working-with-webhooks): build, verify and test a handler end to end.
-   [Record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record): read the record that an event points to.
-   [Record comment](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record-comment): read the comment of a `comment.create` event.
-   [App](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app): read the app after an `app.update` event.
-   [Request limits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits): the limits of the API itself.
-   [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities): what `webhooks:manage` allows.
-   In the Help Center: [App webhooks](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18449250-app-webhooks)

# Workspace

> Use these endpoints to list, create, update and delete workspaces, and to manage their members.

Use these endpoints to list, create, update and delete workspaces, and to manage their members.

A *workspace* groups apps and their members within your organization. The Podio API calls it a space, and `workspace_id` replaces `space_id`.

To find a workspace ID, see [Retrieve workspaces](#retrieve-workspaces). The **Developer** info of any of its apps also shows it. See [Find the app ID and field IDs](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids).

> Which capability do I need?
> 
> Endpoints that read workspaces need `workspaces:read`. Creating, updating and deleting need `workspaces:edit`. Adding and removing members needs `workspaces.members:manage`. See [Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities).

## Retrieve workspaces

Use this endpoint to list all workspaces you can access in your organization.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/org`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/org \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "total": 2,
  "workspaces": [
    {
      "workspace_id": 1,
      "name": "Task management",
      "slug": "task-management",
      "type": "closed",
      "description": "Manage all tasks and projects inside this workspace.",
      "org_id": 1337
    },
    {
      "workspace_id": 2,
      "name": "Contact directory",
      "slug": "contact-directory",
      "type": "default",
      "description": "Keep track of our contacts here.",
      "org_id": 1337
    }
  ]
}
```

Tape takes the organization from your credential. The example lists the workspaces of the organization with ID `1337`.

**Requirements:** `workspaces:read`. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Retrieve a workspace

Use this endpoint to read one workspace by its ID.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/{workspace_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "name": "Task management",
  "slug": "task-management",
  "type": "closed",
  "description": "Manage all tasks and projects inside this workspace.",
  "org_id": 1337
}
```

**Requirements:** `workspaces:read`, and membership in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

-   A workspace you aren't a member of, for example one in another organization, returns `400` with `workspace_invalid_permission`.
-   A workspace ID that doesn't exist returns `404`.

## Create a workspace

Use this endpoint to create a new workspace.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "name": "Task management",
    "type": "closed",
    "description": "Manage all tasks and projects inside this workspace."
  }'
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "name": "Task management",
  "slug": "task-management",
  "type": "closed",
  "description": "Manage all tasks and projects inside this workspace.",
  "org_id": 1337
}
```

The response contains the new workspace:

> Which workspace types are there?
> 
> Set `type` to `"closed"`, `"open"`, `"default"` or `"private"`. These are the workspace types [described in the Help Center](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/8000930-intro-to-workspaces).

**General behavior**

-   An organization can hold at most 500 workspaces. When it reaches this limit, Tape rejects further create requests until you delete a workspace.
-   You can't change the type of a workspace later through the API. Choose the right `type` when you create it.
-   A personal access token with limited content access can't create workspaces. Use a token whose content access is **All**.

**Requirements:** `workspaces:edit`, and an organization role that may create workspaces. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Required. Name of the workspace. |
| `type` | `string` | Required. One of `closed`, `open`, `default` or `private`. |
| `description` | `string` | Description of the workspace. Optional. |
| `slug` | `string` | Slug of the workspace. Optional. |
| `icon` | `object` | Icon of the workspace. Optional, see [Icon](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/icon). |

## Update a workspace

Use this endpoint to change the name, description, slug or icon of a workspace.

`PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/{workspace_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X PUT https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "name": "Task management (NEW)",
    "description": "Manage all tasks and projects inside this NEW workspace."
  }'
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "name": "Task management (NEW)",
  "slug": "task-management",
  "type": "closed",
  "description": "Manage all tasks and projects inside this NEW workspace.",
  "org_id": 1337
}
```

The response contains the updated workspace:

**General behavior**

-   A new name doesn't change the slug. Send `slug` to change it.
-   Tape ignores `type` in an update. A workspace keeps the type it was created with.

**Requirements:** `workspaces:edit`, and the **Admin** role in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | New name of the workspace. Optional. |
| `description` | `string` | New description. Optional. |
| `slug` | `string` | New slug. Optional. |
| `icon` | `object` | New icon. Optional, see [Icon](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/icon). |

## Delete a workspace

Use this endpoint to delete a workspace with all its apps and records.

`DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/{workspace_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "name": "Task management (NEW)",
  "slug": "task-management",
  "type": "closed",
  "description": "Manage all tasks and projects inside this NEW workspace.",
  "org_id": 1337
}
```

The response contains the deleted workspace:

**Requirements:** `workspaces:edit`, and the **Admin** role in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Retrieve workspace members

Use this endpoint to list the members of a workspace and their roles.

`GET https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/{workspace_id}/member`

*Request*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/1/member \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "workspace_members": [
    {
      "workspace_id": 1,
      "user_id": 10000,
      "role": "admin"
    },
    {
      "workspace_id": 1,
      "user_id": 10001,
      "role": "member"
    }
  ]
}
```

`role` is `admin` or `member`. Older memberships can also return `guest`.

**Requirements:** `workspaces:read`, and membership in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

## Add a workspace member

Use this endpoint to add a user of your organization to a workspace, or to change their role.

`POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/{workspace_id}/member`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/1/member \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "user_id": 10002,
    "role": "admin"
  }'
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "workspace_id": 1,
  "user_id": 10002,
  "role": "admin"
}
```

If the user is already a member, Tape updates their role. To find the `user_id`, see [Retrieve organization users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-organization-users).

> Which workspace roles can I give?
> 
> Set `role` to `"admin"` or `"member"`. These are the workspace roles [described in the Help Center](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/8000930-intro-to-workspaces). Tape no longer accepts `"guest"` here.

**Requirements:** `workspaces.members:manage`, and the **Admin** role in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

**Errors**

A `user_id` outside your organization returns `404`.

**Body parameters**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `user_id` | `integer` | Required. ID of the user to add. |
| `role` | `string` | Required. `admin` or `member`. |

## Remove a workspace member

Use this endpoint to remove a member from a workspace.

`DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/{workspace_id}/member/{user_id}`

*Request*

```shell
curl -X DELETE https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/workspace/1/member/10002 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

*Response*

```json
{}
```

**General behavior**

-   The user stays in your organization.
-   Removing a user who isn't a member returns `200` and changes nothing.

**Requirements:** `workspaces.members:manage`, and the **Admin** role in the workspace. Works with a personal access token, an OAuth access token or a user API key.

# Versioning

> Find out which API version to use and when Tape releases a new one.

Find out which API version to use and when Tape releases a new one.

The current version is `v1`. It's part of every path, for example `/v1/record/{record_id}`.

> When does Tape release a new version?
> 
> Tape releases a new API version only for a *backwards-incompatible* change, for example a renamed property. Additions, such as new endpoints or new response properties, don't get a new version. Use them right away on `v1`.

# Date, time & timezones

> Read, format and set dates in automations, and avoid timezone surprises in your scripts.

Read, format and set dates in automations, and avoid timezone surprises in your scripts.

## Datetime format

Automations use the same date and time formats as the Tape API:

| Format | Shape | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Datetime | `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss` | `2023-02-01 15:00:00` |
| Date | `YYYY-MM-DD` | `2023-02-01` |
| Time | `HH:mm:ss` | `15:00:00` |

These strings have no `Z` suffix and no offset. The variable name tells you the timezone: a name that ends in `_utc` holds UTC, the same name without `_utc` holds the same moment in the timezone of the automation.

## Variables

Each date field gives you several variables, named after the record name of the app, then `field` and the field name. Example: an app named `Tasks` with the record name `Task` has a date field named `Date`, with time and without an end date:

| Variable | Description | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `task_field_date_start_time` | Time in the timezone of the automation. | `15:00:00` |
| `task_field_date_start_time_utc` | Same time in UTC. | `14:00:00` |
| `task_field_date_start_date` | Date in the timezone of the automation. | `2023-02-01` |
| `task_field_date_start_date_utc` | Same date in UTC. Can be a different day than the local date near midnight. | `2023-02-01` |
| `task_field_date_formatted` | Date and time as one display string in the timezone of the automation, without seconds. Leaves out the time for a whole day. | `2023-02-01 15:00` |

> What about whole-day values?
> 
> If the date field holds a whole day and no time, both `_start_time` variables are `null`. The local date and the `_utc` date are the same, because Tape doesn't convert a calendar day between timezones. See [Calendar days](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone#calendar-days).

Use the UTC values when you set or update field values, as [Timezones](#timezones) explains.

## Formatting dates

Use the built-in `date_fns` library to format dates. Call its `format` function:

```js
date_fns.format(new Date(task_field_date_start_date), 'y') // the year
```

Test your format strings in the [interactive date-fns playground](https://date-fns-interactive.netlify.app/).

## Timezones

Automations run in UTC, and Tape's built-in actions handle this for you. Example: an action that copies a date from one record to another keeps the date and time people see in Tape.

Take care when you set dates in code, for example in **Perform a calculation** or **Execute a script**. The script reads every date string as UTC.

Example: a user in Amsterdam (UTC+1 in winter) wants to set a date field to 15:00 local time:

```js
var_target_datetime = new Date('2023-02-01 15:00');
```

The script reads `2023-02-01 15:00` as 15:00 UTC. After the record update, the user sees 16:00 instead of 15:00.

Convert the local time to UTC first with `zonedTimeToUtc` from `date_fns_tz`, and pass the timezone of the user:

```js
var_target_datetime = date_fns_tz.zonedTimeToUtc(new Date('2023-02-01 15:00'), 'Europe/Amsterdam');
```

Now the record shows 1 February 2023, 15:00 in the user's timezone. To use the timezone of the automation instead, pass `current_workflow_timezone`.

An automation with this conversion looks like this:

![The automation editor with a Perform a calculation action that runs date_fns_tz.zonedTimeToUtc and an Update the current record action that sets the date](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/automations-date-timezone-flow-b475c289783cac2dfc706a9407402669.png)

## Next steps

-   [Date & timezone](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/date-timezone): formats, calendar days and UTC values.
-   [Libraries](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/libraries): all libraries you can use in scripts, with versions.
-   [Automations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/introduction): execution variables like `current_workflow_timezone`.
-   [Code editor](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18448952-execute-script-action): autocompletion for `date_fns` and `date_fns_tz`.
-   In the Help Center: [Dates and time zones in automations](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18448996-dates-and-time-zones-in-automations)

# Execution types

> Run an automation through its trigger, by hand, or as a simulation that changes no data in Tape. The execution type of a run decides if filters apply and if changes are real.

Run an automation through its trigger, by hand, or as a simulation that changes no data in Tape. The execution type of a run decides if filters apply and if changes are real.

| Execution type | Started by | Filters | Changes data |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Regular (triggered) | The trigger of the automation | Yes | Yes |
| Manual run | A person in the automation editor | Yes | Yes |
| Simulation | A person in the automation editor | No | No data in Tape, but requests to other services are real |

To start a manual run or a simulation from code, use [Run & simulate](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) in the Automation API.

## Regular / triggered

The trigger of the automation starts the run. Example: an automation uses the trigger **Record created**. Someone creates a record in the web app, the mobile app or through the API, and the automation starts.

Tape checks the filters first. A run appears only if the record matches the filters of the automation.

## Manual run

Start a run yourself in the automation editor:

1.  Open the menu in the automation editor and select **Manual run**.
2.  Under **Run on**, choose the records: selected records, a view, a number of the most recent records, or all records of the database app. With the trigger **Webhook received**, choose **Last payload** or **Custom payload** instead.
3.  Select **Start run**.

![The automation editor with Manual run open and the Run on options for selected records, a view, a number of records or all records](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/manual-run-9a2296cbe0e5590d9062bbb745fa264a.png)

Filters apply. Only records that match the filters create a run.

## Simulation run

Use a simulation to test an automation without changing data:

1.  Open the menu in the automation editor and select **Simulated run**.
2.  Choose the records under **Simulate on**.
3.  Select **Start simulation**.

![The automation editor with the Simulate on options and the Start simulation button](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/simulated-run-ee4675560c20e2b01e08dfa8e65624fb.png)

Filters don't apply in a simulation. Actions that change data in Tape only pretend to run: record updates, record creation, comments and other changes return test data. Requests to other services run for real: **Send HTTP request**, **Send API request** and `http` calls in scripts.

Your scripts can check `current_workflow_is_simulation`. Use it to skip calls to other services, so a simulation can't change data outside Tape.

```js
if (!current_workflow_is_simulation) {
  await http.post('https://hooks.acme.com/deals', {
    data: { automation_id: current_workflow_id },
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });
}
```

Tape sends `data` as JSON, but doesn't set the `Content-Type` header for you. Add it yourself when the receiving service expects `application/json`.

The `tape` client in **Execute a script** works the same way. In a simulation, calls that change data, like creating or updating a record, return test data.

## Next steps

-   [Automations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/introduction): execution variables and where scripts run.
-   [Filter values](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/troubleshooting/filter-values): check that a filter matches only the records you expect.
-   [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/troubleshooting/automations-troubleshooting-errors): read failed runs and throw your own errors.
-   [Limits and throttling](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/limitations): limits for each run.
-   In the Help Center: [Test automations](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18449073-test-automations)
-   In the Help Center: [Run an automation on existing records](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18449055-run-an-automation-on-existing-records)

# Automations

> Write your own JavaScript in automations to filter, calculate and call the Tape API or other services.

Write your own JavaScript in automations to filter, calculate and call the Tape API or other services.

![The automation editor with the trigger When a record is updated, a filter on the Automation field and the action Update the current record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/automation-editor-bc913d1aafd5d43eb31bf0fd6a31df55.png)

An automation belongs to one app: it starts on a trigger, checks optional filters, and runs a list of actions. You build it in the automation editor in Tape. These pages cover the JavaScript you write inside it.

> Want to create or run automations from your own code?
> 
> Use the [Automation API](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/overview). It creates, changes and runs automations over HTTP. An AI assistant does the same through the [Tape MCP server](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/overview).

> Coming from Podio?
> 
> Automations take the place of Podio flows and Globiflow. Rebuild each flow in the automation editor, or [move it with the Automation API](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/coming-from-podio#move-your-flows).

## Execution environment

All scripts in automations are JavaScript, as in the [calculation field](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18449157-calculation-syntax-examples). Where you write the script decides what it can do:

| Where | Code | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Script filter | Synchronous only | Decide if the automation continues |
| **Perform a calculation** action | Synchronous only | Store a value in a variable |
| **Execute a script** action | Synchronous and asynchronous | Call the Tape API or other services |

### Synchronous code

Use synchronous code in script filters and in the **Perform a calculation** action. The last expression is the result.

Each field of the record is a variable, named after the record name of the app, `field` and the field name, for example `task_field_amount`. In the examples, `some_number_field_value` stands for such a variable. The [code editor](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18448952-execute-script-action) lists the exact names.

In a script filter, the result must be `true` or `false`:

```js
some_number_field_value >= 1000
```

```js
(some_number_field_value % 2 === 0) && (some_number_field_value < 50)
```

In **Perform a calculation**, Tape stores the result in a variable:

```js
some_number_field_value * 1000
```

```js
some_number_field_value < 100 ? some_number_field_value : 100;
```

Promises and `async`/`await` don't work here. Need them? Use an **Execute a script** action instead.

> Need functions or more than one statement?
> 
> Wrap your code in an immediately invoked function expression (IIFE) and return the result.

```js
(function yourFunctionName() {
  let variable1 = 1337;

  function yourSubFunctionName1() {
    return false;
  }

  function yourSubFunctionName2() {
    return true;
  }

  // ... more code

  return yourSubFunctionName1() || yourSubFunctionName2();
})();
```

### Asynchronous code

Use the **Execute a script** action to run asynchronous code. Add it in the automation editor with **Add action**. We recommend [async/await](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/async_function) over plain promises.

**Execute a script** gives you more APIs, modules and functions. The code editor shows autocompletion and types for all of them.

#### Tape API client

Use the `tape` client to call the [Tape API](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/introduction). It covers everything the action blocks don't, and gives you more control.

```js
const { data, headers } = await tape.Record.get(1234);

console.log({ record: data });
```

`data` is the record itself, with `record_id`, `title` and `fields`. You don't need to handle authentication. Each run gets its own token, valid for that run.

> Setting your own key with `tape.setApiKey()`?
> 
> Your user API key or personal access token then applies to all following actions too, including action blocks, because they use the same client.

#### HTTP client

Use the `http` client to call other services, like the **Send a HTTP request** action does.

```js
const { data, headers } = await http.get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts');

console.log({ data });
console.log({ headers });
```

`http` also has `post`, `put`, `patch` and `delete`. Pass request headers in the `headers` option and a body in `data`. A JSON response arrives parsed in `data`, any other response as text.

An error status doesn't make the call fail. Check `statusCode` and [throw an error](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/troubleshooting/automations-troubleshooting-errors#throwing-custom-errors) to stop the run:

```js
const { data, statusCode } = await http.get('https://api.acme.com/v1/rates?base=EUR', {
  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer YOUR_RATES_SERVICE_KEY' },
});

if (statusCode !== 200) {
  throw new Error(`Rate service returned ${statusCode}`);
}

var_usd_rate = data.rates.USD;
```

Does the other service only accept known IP addresses? Allow the [IP addresses of automations](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18448976-automation-ip-addresses) in its firewall.

### Custom variables

These actions create variables you can use in all following actions:

-   **Perform a calculation**
-   **Execute a script**
-   **Send a HTTP request**

A variable exists only after the action that creates it. There is no block scope. A later action with the same variable name overwrites the value.

In **Execute a script**, assign the value to the variable of the action. Its name is `var_` plus its label in lower case, with other characters as `_`: the label `USD rate` becomes `var_usd_rate`. To save the value in a field, use the variable in a later **Update the current record** action.

## Silent actions

Turn on **Silent** for an action that changes data, and Tape sends no notifications for that change. Use it for large data migrations, so people's inboxes don't fill up.

## Triggering other automations and webhooks

Every action that changes data has two options:

-   **Trigger automations**: the change can start other automations.
-   **Trigger webhooks**: the change sends webhook events.

Set both for each action. Example: an action updates a record and **Trigger automations** is off. Automations with the trigger **Record updated** don't run for that change.

In **Execute a script**, the `tape` client has the same options. The code editor shows them in the types.

## Execution variables

Tape sets these variables for every run:

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `current_workflow_is_simulation` | `true` in a simulated run. Use it to skip changes to Tape or other systems. |
| `current_workflow_id` | ID of the automation. Send it to other systems for debugging. |
| `current_workflow_name` | Name of the automation. Send it to other systems for debugging. |
| `current_workflow_timezone` | Timezone of the automation. Set it in the automation editor. |
| `current_date_local`, `current_date_utc` | Date of the run, in the timezone of the automation or in UTC. `current_date_formatted` holds it as display text. |
| `current_datetime_local`, `current_datetime_utc` | Date and time of the run. `current_datetime_formatted` holds it as display text. |
| `current_time_local`, `current_time_utc` | Time of the run. `current_time_formatted` holds it as display text. |
| `webhook_payload_parsed`, `webhook_payload_raw` | With the trigger **Webhook received**: the request body as an object, or as raw text. |

There are more. Some depend on the [execution type](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/execution-types) of the run.

## Logging and debugging

Use `console.log` to log any variable. The output appears in the logs of the run, under **Runs** in the automation editor.

```js
console.log('initial field value was: ' + task_field_estimation_days_decimal_value)
console.log('result of calculation was: ' + var_calculation_result)
```

# Available libraries (automations)

> Use these Node.js libraries in the code of your automations without importing them.

Use these Node.js libraries in the code of your automations without importing them.

They work in script filters, **Perform a calculation** and **Execute a script**. Call each library by its alias. Example: format a date with date-fns.

```js
date_fns.format(new Date(current_datetime_local), 'yyyy-MM-dd')
```

| Library | Aliases | Version | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Lodash](https://lodash.com/) | `lodash`, `_` | 4.17.21 | Utility functions for arrays, objects and strings. |
| [Moment.js](https://momentjs.com/) | `moment` | 2.30.1 | Parse, validate, change and format dates and times. |
| [date-fns](https://date-fns.org/) | `date_fns` | 2.30.0 | Date utility functions. |
| [date-fns-tz](https://github.com/marnusw/date-fns-tz/tree/v2.0.1) | `date_fns_tz` | 2.0.1 | Timezone support for date-fns, based on the Intl API. |
| [uuid](https://github.com/uuidjs/uuid#readme) | `uuid` | 8.3.2 | Create RFC4122 UUIDs. |
| [cheerio](https://cheerio.js.org/) | `cheerio` | 1.0.0-rc.10 | Parse and read HTML on the server, with a jQuery-like API. |
| [striptags](https://github.com/ericnorris/striptags) | `striptags` | 3.2.0 | Remove HTML tags from a string, like PHP's strip\_tags. |
| [minimatch](https://github.com/isaacs/minimatch) | `minimatch` | 9.0.5 | Match strings against glob patterns. |
| [jsonata](https://github.com/jsonata-js/jsonata) | `jsonata` | 1.8.6 | Query and transform JSON, see the [JSONata documentation](https://jsonata.org/). |

> Missing a library?
> 
> [Submit an issue](https://github.com/tape-dev/developers.tapeapp.com/issues/new?body=Hey%20Tape%20Team%2C%0A%0AI%20would%20like%20to%20propose%20the%20following%20Node.js%20library%20to%20be%20included%20in%20the%20automations%3A%0A%0AName%3A%0AVersion%3A%0ANPM%20Link%3A%0AWhy%20it%20would%20be%20useful%20to%20me%3A%0A%0AThanks%21) on GitHub, and the Tape team looks into it.

# Limits and throttling

> Keep each automation run within the limits for time, actions and computing power. Tape also throttles organizations with very heavy use.

Keep each automation run within the limits for time, actions and computing power. Tape also throttles organizations with very heavy use.

## Limits for each run

| Limit | Value | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Run time | 3 minutes | The run fails with an error message |
| Actions in one run | 1000 | The run fails with an error message |
| Memory and CPU | Limited | The run fails with an error message |
| Parallel async operations | Limited | Run HTTP calls one after another instead of in parallel |
| Records in one collection action | 1000 | The collection stops at 1000 records, without an error |
| Emails | Shared 24-hour quota of your organization | Further emails are refused until the quota renews |

### Record collections stop at 1000 records

Actions that collect records, like `collect_app_records` and `collect_app_view_records`, return at most 1000 records.

Tape saves a higher `limit`, `limit_enabled: false` or a value of 0 or below unchanged. The cap applies only when the run executes. Neither saving nor validating the automation warns you.

This cap is separate from the limit of 1000 actions per run.

### Emails use a shared quota

The actions `send_email` and `collected_records_send_email` use the 24-hour email quota of your organization. Once the quota is used up, Tape refuses further emails until the 24-hour window moves on.

### Stay within the limits

-   Split large jobs into several automations.
-   Avoid heavy computations, for example on large numbers of records.
-   Run HTTP calls one after another.

## Throttling

Tape can throttle an organization that uses a very large number of actions in a short time. Throttling affects the whole organization and delays runs for a while.

Tape checks the load regularly and lifts throttling as soon as the load drops below the limit. Until then, waiting runs show the orange status **Throttled** under **Runs** in the automation editor and under **Automations** → **Runs**.

## Next steps

-   [Execution types](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/execution-types): simulate a run before it changes data.
-   [Errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/troubleshooting/automations-troubleshooting-errors): read failed runs and their error messages.
-   [Request limits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits): limits for the Tape API.
-   [Automations](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/introduction): where scripts run and what they can do.
-   In the Help Center: [Automation limits and throttling](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18449020-automation-limits-and-throttling)

# Automation errors

> Find out why an automation run failed, and stop a run on purpose with your own error.

Find out why an automation run failed, and stop a run on purpose with your own error.

Tape lists every failed run under **Runs** in the automation editor, whatever its execution type. Open a run to see its logs, the action that failed and the error message. After the fix, start a [manual run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/execution-types#manual-run) to try again.

## Common API errors

Actions that call the Tape API can fail with these errors. The error message says what went wrong.

| HTTP status code | Code | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 400 | `validation` or `input_validation` | Validation error. | A required value is missing, like a required field when a record is created or updated, or the text of a comment. |
| 400 | `record_no_permission` or `app_no_permission` | Permission error. | The automation has no permission for the step. Also happens when the **Author** of an action lacks the permission. |

The code is the `error_code` of the API response. See [Error codes](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/errors#error-codes) in the API reference for all codes.

Calls to other services with the `http` client don't fail on an error status. Check `statusCode` in your script, as the [HTTP client](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/introduction#http-client) example shows.

## Throw a custom error

Throw an error in **Perform a calculation** or **Execute a script** to stop the run with a failed status. Tape logs your error message.

```js
if (some_condition) {
  throw new Error('Oops, some_condition was true');
}
```

The run stops at this point, and the remaining actions don't run. Use it when an important step fails and continuing makes no sense.

# Filter values

> Keep filters from matching every record when their comparison value turns out empty.

Keep filters from matching every record when their comparison value turns out empty.

A filter, or a search condition inside an action, compares a field with a value. Tape builds that value when the automation runs, from fixed input and references: a field, a variable or the output of an earlier action. A filter that looks complete can still end up with an empty value for one record.

## An empty filter value matches every record

> Using a field, a variable or an earlier output as the value?
> 
> If it is empty for one record when the automation runs, the condition is `true` for every record. Under the default `and` group, the automation then runs its actions on every record in scope, without an error. Before a bulk action like "update all" or "delete all", this can change your whole dataset and use credits for every record.

> Getting `400` when you save a filter?
> 
> Create and update in the Automation API reject a comparison that is empty or of the wrong type, and name the condition:
> 
> -   a value whose `type` doesn't match the field, for example `text` on a number field
> -   an empty comparison value, for example `{ "type": "text", "text": [] }`
> -   the wrong number of values
> 
> The error explains the risk. To check for an empty field on purpose, use `is_empty` or `is_not_empty`.

### How a value ends up empty

-   **A referenced value is empty.** The field, variable or earlier output is empty for this record. It passes the save check, because the reference exists.
-   **The value channel doesn't match the field.** Tape catches this on save and returns `400`. Tape picks the channel from the field type: number and unique ID use `number`, date fields use `date`, category, status, relation and user use `ids`, text uses `text`. See [Match the value type to the field](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/filters#match-the-value-type-to-the-field) for the channel rules.
-   **The automation is older than the check.** Automations saved before this check, or in the automation editor, can hold an empty comparison. Create and update don't check existing automations again.

### How to avoid it

-   **Check the source first.** If the value comes from a reference that can be empty, put the filter or action inside a [`conditional`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions/conditional) that checks the source, or set a fallback value.
-   **Simulate before you activate.** A [simulation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution) runs the actions on real records without changing data in Tape, so a search condition inside an action that matches too much shows up early. Requests to other services still go out. A simulation skips the filter of the automation itself.
-   **To match every record on purpose, remove the condition**, or send `filter: null`. A filter without conditions runs for every record. An empty top-level group returns `400`.

## Why `validate` does not flag an empty value

`GET /v1/automation/{id}/validate` returns `valid: true` for a condition with an empty comparison value, because the definition is valid. `validate` checks meaning only: it doesn't run the save checks of create and update, and can't know that a reference becomes empty for some record.

`validate` catches missing references, which is a different problem:

-   `filter_variable_missing`: the subject of a condition points to a field that no longer exists.
-   `filter_value_variable_missing`: the value points to a deleted field or variable.

Neither code flags an empty comparison. The code `filter_value_missing` is reserved and no longer raised.
