# Coming from the Podio API

> Move your Podio API integration to Tape. Map items, spaces, and hooks to records, workspaces, and webhooks, and switch authentication.

Move an integration from the Podio API to the Tape API with the same concepts and familiar endpoints.

Tape and Podio share their building blocks: organizations, workspaces, apps, fields, views, and webhooks. Most scripts need new names, a new base URL, and a new token.

## Before you begin

You need a Tape organization with your apps in it. Moving a whole Podio organization? Use the free Zooli Migration Tool first, as described in [Migrate to Tape](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/16738165-migrate-to-tape-podio-asana-hubspot-salesforce-and-other-import-options), then point your code at Tape.

The migration gives your apps, fields, and records new IDs. Replace the old IDs and `external_id` values in your scripts. The [Developer view of each app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#find-app-and-field-ids) lists the new IDs and slugs.

Tape builds each field slug from the field name, with underscores instead of hyphens. A Podio `external_id` like `due-date` usually becomes `due_date`.

Send every request to `https://api.tapeapp.com`. The API sends and receives JSON.

## Map the concepts

| Podio API | Tape API | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| item | record |  |
| `item_id` | `record_id` |  |
| `app_item_id` | `app_record_id` | Find a record by it with a [metadata filter](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/filter#app-record-id-metadata). |
| `external_id` on an item | – | Records have no `external_id`. Store it in a text field and filter by it. |
| `external_id` on a field | `slug` on a field | Records still return it as `external_id`. See [Podio field types](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field/overview#podio-field-types). |
| item `fields` | record `fields` | Write values as an object keyed by field ID or slug. The value format depends on the field type. See [Field values](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/overview#formats-by-field-type). |
| space, `space_id` | workspace, `workspace_id` | See [Workspace](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/workspace). |
| organization | organization | A token works in one organization. See [Organization](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/organization). |
| contact | – | No Tape endpoint. Use [users](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user) for people in your organization and records for external contacts. |
| app, app field | app, field | Change fields with [Update an app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#update-an-app). |
| calculation field | calculation field | JavaScript with plain field names, like `First_name` instead of `@First name`. See the [syntax table](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18449157-calculation-syntax-examples). |
| view | view | See [View](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/view). |
| filter | filter | Send `filters` as an array of filter objects, each with a field ID (not a slug) and a `match_type`. Send `sort_by`, `sort_desc`, `limit` and `cursor` in the query string, not in the body. Date ranges and categories: see [Filter](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/filter). |
| hook | webhook | Same verification flow. See [Move your webhooks](#move-your-webhooks). |
| flow, Podio Workflow Automation (Globiflow) | automation | Build them in the [automation editor](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/introduction) or with the [Automation API](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/overview). See [Move your flows](#move-your-flows). |
| app authentication, OAuth | personal access token, OAuth | See [Switch authentication](#switch-authentication). |
| comment | record comment | See [Record comment](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record-comment). |
| file | file | Upload first, then attach the file ID to a record or comment. See [File](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/file). |
| revision | record revision | See [Record revision](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record-revision). |
| grant | record permissions | See [Record permissions](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record-permissions). |
| subscription | follow | See [Unfollow all records in a database app](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record-follow#unfollow-all-records-in-an-app). |
| task | – | No Tape endpoint. See [Good to know](#good-to-know). |
| rate limit | request limits | Credits per minute. See [Plan for request limits](#plan-for-request-limits). |
| `offset` | `cursor` | No `offset`. Pass the `cursor` of the previous page to get the next one. See [Pagination](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/pagination). |

## Find the matching endpoint

| Task | Podio API | Tape API |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create a record | `POST /item/app/{app_id}/` | [`POST /v1/record/app/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) |
| Retrieve a record | `GET /item/{item_id}` | [`GET /v1/record/{record_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-a-record) |

| Delete a record | `DELETE /item/{item_id}` | [`DELETE /v1/record/{record_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#delete-a-record) |
| Records of a database app | `GET /item/app/{app_id}/` | [`GET /v1/record/app/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-records-for-an-app) |
| Filter records | `POST /item/app/{app_id}/filter/` | [`POST /v1/record/filter/app/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-filtered-records-for-an-app) |
| Records of a view | `POST /item/app/{app_id}/filter/{view_id}/` | [`GET /v1/record/view/{view_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#retrieve-records-for-a-view) |
| Create many records | – | [`POST /v1/record/app/batch/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#batch-create-multiple-records) |

| Record revisions | `GET /item/{item_id}/revision/` | [`GET /v1/record/{record_id}/revision`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record-revision#retrieve-revisions-for-a-record) |
| Add a comment | `POST /comment/item/{item_id}/` | [`POST /v1/comment/record/{record_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record-comment#create-a-record-comment) |
| Upload a file | `POST /file/` | [`POST /v1/file/upload`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/file#upload-a-file) |
| Attach a file | `POST /file/{file_id}/attach` | Send the file ID in an [attachment field value](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/field-value/attachment#record-creation) |
| Retrieve an app | `GET /app/{app_id}` | [`GET /v1/app/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-a-single-app) |
| Apps of a workspace | `GET /app/space/{space_id}/` | [`GET /v1/app/workspace/{workspace_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/app#retrieve-apps-for-a-workspace) |
| Create a view | `POST /view/app/{app_id}/` | [`POST /v1/view/app/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/view#create-a-view) |
| Create a workspace | `POST /space/` | [`POST /v1/workspace`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/workspace#create-a-workspace) |
| Workspace members | `GET /space/{space_id}/member/` | [`GET /v1/workspace/{workspace_id}/member`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/workspace#retrieve-workspace-members) |
| Search | `POST /search/` | [`GET /v1/search`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/search#search) |
| Create a webhook | `POST /hook/{ref_type}/{ref_id}/` | [`POST /v1/hook/app/{app_id}`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/webhook#create-a-webhook) |
| Current user | `GET /user` | [`GET /v1/user`](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/user#retrieve-the-current-user) |

## Switch authentication

Replace the Podio header `Authorization: OAuth2 <token>` with a bearer token:

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/user \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

Choose the credential that matches your Podio flow:

| Podio flow | Use in Tape |
| --- | --- |
| Server-side flow, for your own scripts | [Personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens). It can also act on a user's behalf when that user creates it |
| Server-side flow, for a product other Tape users connect | [OAuth](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow) with PKCE and a [client registered by Tape](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/clients#a-client-registered-by-tape) |
| Client-side flow | [OAuth](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow) with PKCE and a public client registered by Tape, no client secret needed |
| Username and password flow | [Personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) |
| App authentication | [Personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) with its [content access](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#content-selection) limited to that app and only the [capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities) your script needs. Tape has no token per app. Records, comments and revisions show the token's user as the author, so create the token from a dedicated user for the integration. See [Attribution](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#attribution) |

## Move your webhooks

Webhooks verify the same way. Tape sends `type` `hook.verify` with a `code`, and your endpoint calls [Validate hook verification](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/webhook#validate-hook-verification).

What changes:

-   Tape sends `hook.verify` right after you create a webhook. Call [Request hook verification](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/webhook#request-hook-verification) only if your endpoint missed it.
-   Tape sends a JSON body, not form parameters.
-   Events start with `record.` instead of `item.`, for example `record.create`. Tape adds `record.restore`.
-   The payload carries `record_id` and `revision_id` instead of `item_id` and `item_revision_id`.
-   Webhooks apply to a whole app. To react to one field, use an automation with a filter.

A minimal handler in Node.js:

```javascript
app.post('/tape-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  const { type, hook_id, code, record_id } = req.body;
  res.sendStatus(200);
  if (type === 'hook.verify') {
    await fetch(`https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/${hook_id}/verify/validate`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.TAPE_TOKEN}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ code }),
    });
  }
  if (type === 'record.create') {
    // For example, create a follow-up task for a new lead.
  }
});
```

> How do you avoid endless loops?
> 
> Update a record from a webhook with `hook=false`, as in the Podio API, plus `workflow=false`, because `hook=false` doesn't stop automations. Add `silent=true` to skip notifications. See [Avoid endless loops](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/webhook#avoid-endless-loops).

## Move your flows

A Podio flow or a Globiflow flow becomes an automation in one app. Field references use the `field_id`, not the `external_id`. Find the action for each flow step in [Coming from Podio](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/actions#coming-from-podio).

| In Podio, the flow starts when … | Tape [trigger](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/reference/triggers) |
| --- | --- |
| An item is created, updated or deleted | `record_created`, `record_updated`, `record_deleted` |
| A comment is added | `record_comment_or_reply_created` |
| A date in a field arrives | `date_field_arrived` |
| A schedule is due | `periodic` |
| A hook or webhook comes in | `webhook_received` |
| Another flow calls it | `automation_called` |
| Someone starts it by hand or with a button | Any trigger with [manual-run](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/overview#run-an-existing-automation), or a weblink with `weblink_clicked` |

## Plan for request limits

Tape counts credits per minute instead of calls per hour. All credentials of a user share one budget, so more tokens don't add throughput.

Each response carries rate limit headers. After a `429`, wait the seconds in `Retry-After` before you retry. See [Request limits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits).

## Good to know

-   Tape has no client libraries for PHP or Ruby. Call the API over HTTPS from any language.
-   Tasks, status updates, and the activity stream have no Tape endpoints. Use a checklist field and record revisions instead.
-   Tape adds endpoints the Podio API doesn't have: [batch create and update](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#batch-create-multiple-records), [restore a record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#restore-a-record), the [Automation API](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/overview), and the [Tape MCP server](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/overview).

# Quickstart

> Retrieve a record from your Tape organization with a personal access token and a single API request.

Retrieve your first record with a personal access token and a single API request.

## Before you begin

You need a Tape account and one record you can view. No account yet? [Sign up for Tape](https://tapeapp.com/signup).

The API sends and receives JSON over HTTPS. Send every request to `https://api.tapeapp.com`.

Tape keeps data as *records* in *database apps*. Each record has *fields*, such as a name or a status. Apps live in *workspaces*, and workspaces in your *organization*.

> New to APIs?
> 
> Follow the [Tape API guide, first steps](https://community.tapeapp.com/t/tape-api-guide-first-steps/2522) in the Tape Community. It walks you through three requests in Postman, without writing code.

## Step 1: Create a personal access token

1.  Select your profile picture, then select **Preferences**.
2.  In the settings window, select **Developer** (under **Features**).
3.  Under **Personal access tokens (PATs)**, select **New token**.
4.  Name the token, for example "Quickstart".
5.  Under **Content access**, clear **All**, then select the workspace that holds your record.
6.  Under **Capabilities**, clear **All**, then select **Read records**. A capability is one thing the token may do.
7.  Select **Create token** and copy the token.

![New personal access token dialog named Quickstart with one workspace and the capability Read records](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/quickstart-token-4e0a5c336632297d7109d2f54b742360.png)

> Copy the token now
> 
> Tape shows the token only once. Store it like a password.

Save the token as an environment variable:

```shell
export TAPE_TOKEN="tape_pat_..."
```

> Lost your token?
> 
> Revoke it under **Developer** and create a new one.

## Step 2: Retrieve a record

Make a `GET` request to `/v1/record/{record_id}`. Send the token as a bearer token in the `Authorization` header.

Use the ID of a record you can view: open the record in Tape, select **•••**, then select **Developer** and copy the **Record ID**. In the examples, replace `123456` with your record ID.

**cURL**

*Retrieve a record*

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/123456 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

**JavaScript**

*Retrieve a record*

```javascript
const response = await fetch("https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/123456", {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.TAPE_TOKEN}` },
});

console.log(JSON.stringify(await response.json(), null, 2));
```

**Python**

*Retrieve a record*

```python
import json
import os
import requests

response = requests.get(
    "https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/123456",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['TAPE_TOKEN']}"},
)
print(json.dumps(response.json(), indent=2))
```

**PHP**

*Retrieve a record*

```php
<?php
$context = stream_context_create([
  'http' => [
    'method' => 'GET',
    'header' => 'Authorization: Bearer ' . getenv('TAPE_TOKEN'),
  ],
]);

$data = file_get_contents('https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/record/123456', false, $context);
echo json_encode(json_decode($data, true), JSON_PRETTY_PRINT);
```

The API returns the record as JSON. Your response has the ID, title and fields of your record. This example shows a contact record:

*Response*

```json
{
  "record_id": 1,
  "app_id": 1,
  "title": "Clara Weber",
  "created_on": "2022-03-01 12:00:00",
  "fields": [
    {
      "field_id": 1,
      "external_id": "full_name",
      "label": "Full Name",
      "type": "text",
      "field_type": "single_text",
      "values": [
        {
          "value": "Clara Weber"
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

**Key fields**

-   `record_id`: the ID of the record.
-   `app_id`: the ID of the record's database app. You need it to create records there.
-   `title`: the record title, as shown in Tape.
-   `fields`: the fields of the record, one entry per field.
-   `field_id` and `external_id`: the field's ID and its slug, a readable ID such as `full_name`. Use either to write values.
-   `values`: the field values. Their shape depends on the field type.

**Getting an error?**

**400 or 401 error**

Check that `TAPE_TOKEN` holds the whole token, prefix included. See [Authentication errors](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/authentication#authentication-errors).

**403 error**

Your token is missing the capability **Read records**. Create a new token that has it.

**404 error**

Check the record ID, then check that your token's content access includes the record's workspace.

## Build on your first request

Pick your next task. Each page has a complete request and response.

| Task | Page | Capabilities the token needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create a record | [Create a record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#create-a-record) | **Edit records**, plus **Read records** to read it back |
| Receive a webhook | [Working with webhooks](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/guide/api/working-with-webhooks) | **Manage webhooks** and **Read records** |
| Run an automation | [Run an automation](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/automation/execution#run-an-automation) | **Run automations**, plus **Read automations** to find its ID |
| Connect an AI client | [Connect to Tape MCP](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/connect) | None. You sign in with your Tape account |

You can't add capabilities to an existing token. Create a new token for the task. Webhooks and automation runs also need the **Admin** role in the app's workspace.

# Working with webhooks

> Receive record changes from Tape in your own backend. Build a webhook handler in Node.js, verify it, avoid endless loops, and test it locally.

Build a webhook handler that receives record changes from Tape, verify it, and test it on your own machine.

A webhook sends a POST request to your URL whenever something changes in a database app. The [Webhook](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/webhook) reference lists every endpoint and event type.

## Before you begin

You need:

-   A [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) with the capabilities **Manage webhooks** (`webhooks:manage`) and **Read records** (`records:read`). Add **Edit records** (`records:edit`) if your handler changes records.
-   The ID of the app you want to watch. Open one of its records in Tape, select **•••**, then select **Developer**, and copy the **App ID**. A record you read with the API also returns it as `app_id`.
-   The **Admin** role in the app's workspace.
-   Node.js 18 or later, and the Express package (`npm install express`).

Store the token in an environment variable:

```shell
export TAPE_TOKEN=tape_pat_0a1b2c3d...
```

## How a webhook becomes active

1.  You create a webhook with a URL and an event `type`. It starts as `inactive`.
2.  Tape sends `hook.verify` with a `code` to your URL right away.
3.  Your handler sends the code back to Tape. The webhook becomes `active`.
4.  From then on, Tape sends one POST request per event to your URL.

Every event carries IDs only, for example `record_id` and `revision_id`. Read the record with your token to get its values.

## Step 1: Write the handler

Create `server.js`:

*server.js*

```javascript
const express = require('express');

const TAPE_API = 'https://api.tapeapp.com';
const headers = {
  Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.TAPE_TOKEN}`,
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
};

const app = express();
app.use(express.json());

app.post('/tape-webhook', async (req, res) => {
  // Answer first. Tape waits 5 seconds at most.
  res.sendStatus(200);

  const { type, hook_id, code, record_id } = req.body;

  if (type === 'hook.verify') {
    await fetch(`${TAPE_API}/v1/hook/${hook_id}/verify/validate`, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers,
      body: JSON.stringify({ code }),
    });
    console.log(`Webhook ${hook_id} verified`);
    return;
  }

  if (type === 'record.update') {
    const record = await fetch(`${TAPE_API}/v1/record/${record_id}`, { headers }).then((r) => r.json());
    console.log(`Record ${record_id} updated: ${record.title}`);
  }
});

app.listen(3000, () => console.log('Listening on port 3000'));
```

Start it:

```shell
node server.js
```

**Key points**

-   `res.sendStatus(200)` comes first. Slow work after the response doesn't count against the time limit.
-   The handler validates the code itself, so verification needs no manual step.
-   Tape doesn't sign webhook requests, so the handler reads the record with your token. Don't trust the payload for anything but IDs.

## Step 2: Make the handler reachable

Tape sends webhooks only to ports 80 and 443. A server on `localhost:3000` isn't reachable from the internet.

To test on your machine, start a tunnel such as ngrok or Cloudflare Tunnel. It forwards a public HTTPS URL on port 443 to your local port:

```shell
ngrok http 3000
```

Copy the HTTPS URL it prints, for example `https://acme-test.ngrok.app`. Your webhook URL is that address plus `/tape-webhook`.

In production, run the handler behind HTTPS on port 443. Tape sends the same payload over HTTP, but HTTPS keeps it private.

## Step 3: Create the webhook

Keep the handler and the tunnel running. Make a POST request with the URL and the event type. Replace `1` in the path with your app ID:

```shell
curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data '{
    "type": "record.update",
    "url": "https://acme-test.ngrok.app/tape-webhook"
  }'
```

*Response*

```json
{
  "hook_id": 7,
  "app_id": 1,
  "status": "inactive",
  "num_failed_executions": 0,
  "type": "record.update",
  "url": "https://acme-test.ngrok.app/tape-webhook"
}
```

One webhook receives one event type. To receive created and updated records, create two webhooks with the same URL.

## Step 4: Verify the webhook

Your handler received `hook.verify` right after Step 3 and logs `Webhook 7 verified`. Check the status, again with your app ID in place of `1`:

```shell
curl https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/app/1 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
```

The webhook now shows `"status": "active"`.

> Still inactive?
> 
> Check that the tunnel runs, that the URL ends with `/tape-webhook`, and that your handler answers within 5 seconds. Then request the verification again with the `hook_id` from the response:
> 
> ```shell
> curl -X POST https://api.tapeapp.com/v1/hook/7/verify/request \
>   -H "Authorization: Bearer $TAPE_TOKEN"
> ```

## Step 5: Send a test event

Change any field of a record in that database app, in Tape or with [Update a record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/resource/record#update-a-record). Tape sends this body to your handler:

*Incoming request*

```json
{
  "hook_id": 7,
  "record_id": 100,
  "revision_id": 1,
  "type": "record.update"
}
```

Your handler logs the update:

```text
Record 100 updated: Andrea Lim
```

## Avoid endless loops

A handler that updates a record in the same app starts a new `record.update` event. That event calls the handler again, and the loop never ends.

Add `hook=false` to every request your handler sends to change records. In this example, `status` is the slug of a field in the app:

```javascript
await fetch(`${TAPE_API}/v1/record/${record_id}?hook=false&silent=true`, {
  method: 'PUT',
  headers,
  body: JSON.stringify({ fields: { status: 'Reviewed' } }),
});
```

-   `hook=false` runs no webhooks for this change. It works on create, update, delete, restore and the batch endpoints.
-   `silent=true` sends no notifications for this change.
-   `workflow=false` also skips automations, if one of them reacts to the same field.

## Handle failures

Respond to every webhook request with a `2xx` status code within 5 seconds:

-   After more than 50 failed requests in a row, the webhook becomes inactive. Request the verification again to activate it.
-   Tape retries a request briefly after a timeout, a network error, a `429` or a `5xx` response. Other status codes fail at once.
-   Tape doesn't follow redirects. Use the final URL, including `https`.
-   Send an empty body or a short one, such as `OK`. A long body, such as an HTML page, counts as a failed request.
-   The same event can arrive more than once. Use `record_id` and `revision_id` to skip events you already handled.

Tape sends at most 100 webhook requests per minute per app.

# Convert a PDF file to text

> Build an automation that extracts the text of an attached PDF file and saves it in the record's description.

Build an automation that extracts the text of an attached PDF file and saves it in the record's description.

The example uses a task with an attached PDF and an external conversion API.

## Build the automation

The automation has these steps:

1.  **When a record is created:** the automation starts when someone creates a task record.
2.  **Filter:** it continues only if the task's attachment field is not empty. In the screenshot, that field is **PDF output**, so the filter reads **PDF output** **Is not empty**.
3.  **Execute a script:** a script sends the attached file to a conversion API with the `http.upload` function.
4.  The script decodes the base64 response with `Buffer.from` and stores the result in the custom variable **PDF plaintext**.
5.  **Update the current record:** the automation writes the **PDF plaintext** variable to a text field of the task, such as its description. In the screenshot, that field is **Note**.

Steps 3 and 4 need two statements:

```ts
const { data } = await http.upload(
  'https://v2.convertapi.com/convert/pdf/to/txt?Secret=YOUR_SECRET_HERE',
  task_field_attachment_file_url
);

var_pdf_plaintext = Buffer.from(data.Files[0].FileData, 'base64');
```

Replace `YOUR_SECRET_HERE` with the secret of your ConvertAPI account. `http.upload` downloads the file from the URL in its second argument and posts it as the form field `file`. `var_pdf_plaintext` is the [custom variable](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/automations/introduction#custom-variables) of the action, named after its label.

The finished automation looks like this:

![The automation editor with the trigger When a record is created, the filter PDF output is not empty, an Execute a script action that saves its output in PDF plaintext, and Update the current record](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/convert-pdf-to-text-b3c1f972863016385baf6e9bdb5b6944.png)

The name of the file URL variable depends on your app and its attachment field. The code above uses `task_field_attachment_file_url`; the app and field in the screenshot give `hc_test_task_field_pdf_output_file_url`. The editor's [autocompletion](https://help.tapeapp.com/en/articles/18448952-execute-script-action) lists the variables of your app.

The same approach works for other file formats, such as Word documents or PowerPoint presentations. To process the extracted text further, add a conditional action, for example one that assigns a user based on a keyword: "When the PDF contains the word 'legal', assign Juliet."

## Test the automation

Create a task with a PDF attached. After the run, the text of the PDF is in the field you chose in step 5.

# Build an MCP client for Tape

> What an MCP client needs to connect to Tape — Streamable HTTP and OAuth 2.1 with PKCE — with links to the details.

Use this page to build an MCP client that connects to Tape, or to add Tape support to an existing client.

Tape follows the [MCP authorization specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/authorization). A client that implements it connects without anything specific to Tape.

## Requirements at a glance

| Requirement | What Tape uses |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint | `https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP: JSON-RPC 2.0 over `POST`. There is no SSE endpoint |
| Authorization | [OAuth 2.1](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview) authorization code flow with PKCE (`S256`), the only supported flow |
| Discovery | Protected resource metadata (RFC 9728), then authorization server metadata (RFC 8414) |
| Client registration | A [client ID metadata document](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/clients#client-id-metadata-document) or [dynamic client registration](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/clients#dynamic-client-registration) (RFC 7591) |
| Credential | A bearer access token on every request, renewed with a refresh token |

## How a client connects

1.  **Discover.** Without a token, Tape answers `initialize` and every tool call with `401` and points to its protected resource metadata. Only `tools/list`, `resources/*` and `ping` work without a token. The metadata names Tape's authorization server and the scopes the Tape MCP tools use.
2.  **Register** as a public client. See [Register a client yourself](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/clients#register-a-client-yourself).
3.  **Authorize** with PKCE and request the scopes from the protected resource metadata. The user signs in to Tape and approves. See [the authorization flow](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow).
4.  **Call tools** with the access token, and [refresh](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow#refreshing-an-access-token) it when it expires.
5.  **Step up** when a tool needs a scope the connection lacks. Tape answers `403` and names the scopes to request. See [Asking for more scopes](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow#asking-for-more-scopes).

[Capabilities](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities) describes each scope. The same access token also works at the [Developer API](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/introduction).

> Can't run OAuth in your client?
> 
> Send a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/connect-with-token) as the bearer token instead.

## Next steps

[

OAuth overview

the endpoints, supported flows and token formats.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/overview)[

Register a client

set up metadata documents, dynamic registration and redirect URIs.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/clients)[

Authorization flow

every request, refreshing, step-up and errors.

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/oauth/authorization-flow)[

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/connect)[

](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/supported-tools)

# Connect to Tape MCP

> Add Tape to Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Gemini Enterprise or any other MCP client, and sign in with your Tape account.

Add Tape to your MCP client and sign in with your Tape account.

Every client connects to the same endpoint:

```text
https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp
```

Add this URL to your client as a remote MCP server. Sign in to Tape when the client asks. You don't create or paste a token: the client opens Tape in your browser, you [approve the connection](#how-signing-in-works), and the client does the rest.

Pick your client below, follow its steps, then [check the result](#verify-the-connection). Prefer to give the client a [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/connect-with-token)? Use a token for read-only access, for a server without a browser, or to limit the client to some of your workspaces.

## Claude

Use this in claude.ai, Claude Desktop and the Claude mobile apps. They share your connectors. Client documentation: [Custom connectors using remote MCP](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp).

1.  In Claude, open **Customize** → **Connectors**, select **\+ Add**, then **Add custom connector**.
2.  Name it `Tape` and enter `https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp` as the URL. If the dialog shows **Advanced settings**, leave them empty. If it asks you to review authentication settings instead, keep the recommended sign-in options and leave **Request headers** empty.
3.  Select **Add**, then **Connect**, and approve the connection in Tape.

On Claude's Team and Enterprise plans, members can't add a custom connector themselves. An owner adds Tape for the whole organization under **Organization settings** → **Connectors**, with the same name and URL. Members then select **Connect** under **Customize** → **Connectors** and sign in with their own Tape account.

To change a connector's settings later, remove it and add it again.

> Using Claude Desktop with a third-party model provider?
> 
> On these deployments, members can't add connectors themselves. The deployment's admin adds Tape as a managed MCP server with OAuth turned on ([extensions and MCP servers](https://claude.com/docs/third-party/claude-desktop/extensions)); each member then connects it and approves the connection in Tape. If Claude refuses the sign-in on the way back, the admin adds `tapeapp.com` to that server's `oauth.additionalRedirectReferrerHosts`.

## Claude Code

Client documentation: [Claude Code MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).

1.  Add the server:
    
    ```shell
    claude mcp add --transport http tape https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp
    ```
    
2.  In Claude Code, run `/mcp`, select **tape** and choose **Authenticate**.
    
3.  Approve the connection in the browser window that opens.
    

Options for `claude mcp add`:

-   `--scope user` makes the server available in every project.
-   `--scope project` writes it into the repository's `.mcp.json` so your team shares it. Each teammate signs in with their own Tape account.
-   `--callback-port` is needed only if something on your machine requires a fixed port. Claude Code receives the sign-in on a random local port, and Tape accepts any port.

## ChatGPT

Client documentation: [Add a custom MCP server](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/custom-mcp-server).

1.  In ChatGPT on the web, go to **Plugins**, select the plus button, then **Add custom MCP server**.
2.  Name it `Tape`. Under **Connection**, enter `https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp` as the **Server URL** and choose **OAuth** authentication.
3.  Review the warning, select **I understand and want to continue**, then **Create as a plugin**.
4.  Install the plugin, then sign in and approve the connection in Tape.

Your ChatGPT workspace permissions and security settings decide whether you can add and use custom MCP servers.

## Cursor

Client documentation: [Cursor MCP](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp).

1.  Create `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project with the content below. To use Tape in every project, create `~/.cursor/mcp.json` instead.
    
    *.cursor/mcp.json*
    
    ```json
    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "tape": {
          "url": "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
    
2.  Save the file and restart Cursor.
    
3.  Open **Customize** in the sidebar → **MCPs**, find Tape, follow the sign-in prompt, and approve the connection in Tape.
    

## VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Client documentation: [VS Code MCP servers](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers).

1.  Create `.vscode/mcp.json` in your workspace with:
    
    *.vscode/mcp.json*
    
    ```json
    {
      "servers": {
        "tape": {
          "type": "http",
          "url": "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp"
        }
      }
    }
    ```
    
    VS Code uses `servers` where most clients use `mcpServers`, and it needs `"type": "http"`.
    
2.  Open the Command Palette (`Cmd+Shift+P` / `Ctrl+Shift+P`), run **MCP: List Servers**, and start **tape**.
    
3.  Allow VS Code to sign in when it asks, and approve the connection in Tape.
    

To use Tape in every workspace, run **MCP: Open User Configuration** and add the same entry there.

    *~/.codex/config.toml*


## Gemini Enterprise

Client documentation: [Set up a custom MCP server](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/connectors/custom-mcp-server/set-up-custom-mcp-server).

Gemini Enterprise doesn't discover Tape's sign-in by itself. A Google admin sets up the connection once, with a client ID and secret that Tape issues for your organization.

1.  Email [team@tapeapp.com](mailto:team@tapeapp.com) to request a Gemini Enterprise client for your Tape organization. Say whether you use Gemini Enterprise in the Google Cloud console or Gemini Business.
    
2.  In Gemini Enterprise, add a *custom MCP server* with **OAuth 2.0** authentication:
    
    | Field | Value |
    | --- | --- |
    | MCP Server URL | `https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp` |
    | Authorization URL | `https://api.tapeapp.com/oauth/authorize` |
    | Token URL | `https://api.tapeapp.com/oauth/token` |
    | Client ID | The client ID Tape sent you |
    | Client Secret | The client secret Tape sent you |
    | Scopes | See below |
    
    In the Google Cloud console, also select **Enable PKCE Support**.
    
3.  In the Google Cloud console, wait until the data store is active. Then connect it to your Gemini Enterprise app.
    
4.  The admin, then each user, authorizes the connector once in the Gemini Enterprise web app and approves the connection in Tape.
    
5.  Only then, in the Google Cloud console, open the data store and select **Actions** → **Reload custom actions**. Select the Tape tools and select **Enable actions**. No action is enabled by default.
    

Gemini can't ask for more scopes later, so *the scopes you enter are all it ever gets*. Fill them in even where the form marks the field optional; left empty, the connector can only read apps and records. For the full set of Tape MCP tools, enter them on one line, separated by single spaces:

```text
organization:read workspaces:read workspaces:edit apps:read apps:edit records:read records:edit records.comments:read records.comments:edit automations:read automations:edit automations:run
```

Leave out `automations:run` if Gemini shouldn't start automations. It's the one capability whose effects can leave Tape. For a read-only connector:

```text
organization:read workspaces:read apps:read records:read records.comments:read automations:read
```

Keep these points in mind:

-   **Google Cloud console prerequisites.** The admin needs Google's Discovery Engine Editor role. The organization policy must allow custom MCP data stores, and the egress hosts `mcp.tapeapp.com` and `api.tapeapp.com` must be allowed. Users need Google Identity (Google Workspace or Cloud Identity) or workforce identity federation. See Google's guide.
-   **Gemini Business** can't edit a connector's OAuth settings afterwards. To change them, delete the connector and create it again.
-   **No yearly reconnect.** Connections through the client Tape issued last as long as Gemini uses them at least once every 90 days.

## Other MCP clients

Any client that supports *remote MCP servers with OAuth* can connect. Add a Streamable HTTP server with Tape's URL, and complete the sign-in when the client asks:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tape": {
      "url": "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Tape has no SSE endpoint. Wherever a client offers a transport, choose Streamable HTTP or plain "HTTP".

In Tape, select your profile picture, then select **Preferences** → **Tape MCP**. Select **Add an MCP client** to see the URL there too.

![Tape MCP page in the settings window with the Add an MCP client button and the clients ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Gemini Enterprise and Visual Studio Code](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/tape-mcp-add-client-5555696c5f000af9d5e05f253419e568.png)

**Clients that only run local servers** reach Tape through the [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote) bridge. This includes Claude Desktop's `claude_desktop_config.json`. The bridge runs on your computer, opens the sign-in in your browser, and needs Node.js.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tape": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

If the client can't sign in to remote servers either way, connect it with a token.

To test the endpoint by hand, point the [MCP Inspector](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector) at `https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp` and use its OAuth flow.

Building your own client? See [Build an MCP client](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/build-a-client).

## Check the result

1.  **Ask the assistant which Tape tools it has.** A populated tool list shows that the client reaches the server.
2.  **Ask it which Tape account it's connected as**, for example "Which Tape user and organization are you connected as?" The answer names your user and your organization.

The second step uses `tape-fetch` with `type: "self"`, which needs no capability and also lists which tools the connection can use. If the tool list appears and this step fails, the problem is the sign-in, not the connection. `tape-get-users` is a different tool: it finds *other* people by name.

From the shell, the health endpoint answers without any client:

```shell
curl https://mcp.tapeapp.com/health
```

*Response*

```json
{ "status": "ok" }
```

## How signing in works

1.  **Your client contacts the Tape MCP server** and learns that it needs to sign in. It finds Tape's sign-in by itself. You only give it the server URL.
    
2.  **Your browser opens Tape.** Sign in if you aren't signed in yet. If you belong to more than one *organization*, choose the one to connect; the connection reaches only that one. For another organization, connect again, in most clients by adding Tape a second time under another name.
    
3.  **Review the connection.** The screen reads **Connect with Tape MCP**. It says that the client respects your Tape permissions, acts on your behalf, and can:
    
    -   View your organization and its members
    -   Run your automations, which can send emails and call other services
    
    This short list stands for every capability the Tape MCP tools use. A client that asks for a different set sees one line for each capability instead, for example a Gemini Enterprise connector set up with the read-only scopes.
    
    Tape marks a client **Unverified** when it can't tie the client to a website, typically a self-registered client on your own computer. The screen doesn't show where your browser returns to. Continue only if you started the connection yourself from the client.
    
4.  **Select Continue.** Your browser returns to the client, and the Tape tools are ready to use.
    

The connection acts *as you*: it reaches only what you can reach in Tape, and everything it changes shows you as the author. One sign-in covers every capability the [Tape MCP tools](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/supported-tools) use. None of them manages members, shares records, manages webhooks or sends email; for a narrower connection, use a token.

**Who can connect.** Every member of a Tape organization can connect a client. Guests can't. Owners and admins of an organization can also [limit which clients members may connect](#for-organization-admins). If your organization does, the sign-in screen tells you why it can't continue.

**How long it lasts.** Your client renews its access in the background. A connection ends after 90 days unused, and one year after you approved it; the client then asks you to sign in again. [Gemini Enterprise](#gemini-enterprise) connections have no one-year limit.

Each client and each device gets its own connection, so connecting a second laptop doesn't disconnect the first. You can hold up to 10 connections to the same client; an eleventh ends the oldest.

## Manage your connections

**In Tape**, select your profile picture, then select **Preferences** → **Tape MCP** → **Connected**. The list shows each MCP client you connected, when you first connected it, and when it was last used. Tape lists clients by app: **Claude** covers claude.ai, Claude Desktop and Claude Code.

To disconnect a client on every device, select it and select **Remove**. It stops working on its next request.

![Connected tab of the Tape MCP page with the details of Claude, the dates First connected and Last used, and the Remove button](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/connected-client-remove-838adb20cf7e1cad3f302a068270d291.png)

**In the client**, removing the server or connector deletes the client's copy of your sign-in. Most clients don't tell Tape, so the connection stays listed in Tape until it expires after 90 days unused. Remove it in Tape as well to end it right away.

### For organization admins

Owners and admins manage clients for the whole organization under **Tape MCP** → **Manage**. There you choose which clients members can connect. Select **All MCP clients** to see every client; the per-client controls are in the **⋯** menu of a client's row.

**Which clients members can connect:** **All MCP clients** or **Approved MCP clients only**.

![Manage tab of the Tape MCP page with the setting Which clients members can connect open, showing All MCP clients and Approved MCP clients only](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/manage-which-clients-af8b316feb458c75d26833f119ffd510.png)

-   Switching to **Approved MCP clients only** disconnects no one. Tape approves every MCP client that someone in your organization is connected to at that moment. Review the **Approved MCP clients** list afterwards, and remove or restrict what you don't want.
-   Removing a client from that list disconnects everyone from it.
-   From then on, members can connect approved clients only.
-   Owners and admins can connect any client. When only approved clients are allowed, connecting a client approves it for the organization.
-   Limiting clients requires the Premium or Enterprise plan.

**In the ⋯ menu of a client's row:**

-   **Access** → **Owners and admins**: take a client away from members. The table then shows it as **Restricted**. Members' connections to it end immediately, and setting **Access** back to **Everyone** doesn't restore them.
-   **View members**: see who connected a client, and disconnect one of them.
-   **Disconnect all members**: disconnect everyone from one client, owners and admins included.

To disconnect everyone from Tape MCP at once, select **Disconnect all users**.

These controls apply to signed-in clients. A member can still connect a client with a personal access token.

## Troubleshooting

**The browser says Tape doesn't know the client registration.** Tape removes a self-registered client if no one connects it within 25 hours. Remove Tape from the client and add it again.

-   For `mcp-remote`, also delete its stored registrations with `rm -rf ~/.mcp-auth`.
-   In VS Code, run **Authentication: Remove Dynamic Authentication Providers**, select Tape, and connect again.
-   For Gemini Enterprise, the message means the client ID is wrong or no longer valid. Check it, or ask Tape for a new client.

**The sign-in page says "This request has expired".** Complete a sign-in soon after you start it, in the browser where the sign-in page first opened. The page also shows this message when the request was already answered, for example after you went back in the browser, or when you opened its address in another browser. Start the connection again from your client and complete it in one browser.

**The sign-in page doesn't let you continue.** It names the reason: guests can't connect clients, your organization allows only approved clients, or it limits this client to owners and admins. Ask an owner or admin of your organization.

**The sign-in page says the connection couldn't be completed, with reason `AUTHORIZE_SCOPE_UNKNOWN`.** A scope is misspelled or contains an invisible character. This happens when you type scopes by hand, as in Gemini Enterprise. Recreate the connector with the one-line list under [Gemini Enterprise](#gemini-enterprise).

**The client keeps asking you to approve more access.** A connection with fewer scopes asks again the first time a tool needs one it lacks. Approve it, and the client continues with a new connection that includes it.

**It worked, and now Tape refuses every call with `401`.** The connection has ended: you or an admin removed it in Tape, it expired, or your role changed. Sign in again from the client.

**Calls fail with `503` and a `Retry-After` header.** Tape couldn't check the connection at that moment. Wait a few seconds and retry. Your connection is unaffected.

**The client shows the server as failed, or reports an HTML or `405` error.** The URL probably lacks the `/mcp` path, or the client is configured for SSE. Tape serves JSON-RPC over `POST` at `https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp` and answers every other method with `405`. Opening that URL in a browser returns `405` by design.

**A tool returns `403` that names no capability.** Then the connection's capabilities aren't the cause. Your own access applies, and a connection never grants access you don't have. Some actions require a role: creating a workspace requires an organization role that permits it, and changing a workspace requires the **Admin** role in the workspace.

**Reading a workspace returns no apps.** Reading a workspace also returns its apps, which need `apps:read` on top of `workspaces:read`. Without it, you get the workspace back with `apps: null` and a reason, not an error. That `null` means Tape *didn't read the apps at all*, unlike `[]` (none you can see), so never report such a workspace as empty.

**A tool returns `404` for a record, app or automation you know exists.** Tape answers `404` on purpose, the same as for a resource that doesn't exist. Check that your Tape user can see the resource; with a token, also check its [content access](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/connect-with-token#troubleshooting-a-token-connection). For an *automation*, every automation route also requires the **Admin** role in the app's workspace.

**Requests start failing with `429`.** All your connections and tokens share one per-user Developer API budget, so a busy assistant competes with your other integrations that use your tokens or user API key. Using Tape in the browser doesn't count against it. See [Request limits](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/request-limits).

**Tape rejects large tool arguments.** Request bodies are capped at 128 KB. Split the work across several calls.

## FAQ

**Can I connect without signing in through a browser?** Yes. Connect with a personal access token. A token is also the way to give an assistant read-only access, or access to only some of your workspaces and apps.

**Can the assistant delete anything?** No. No tool removes a record, comment, app, workspace, automation, field or field option, and none is planned; a person removes them in the Tape app. A write can still overwrite: `tape-update-database` replaces a field's configuration as a whole, so Tape flags it as destructive even though it deletes nothing.

This limit applies to the *tools*, not to the *credential*. Most `:edit` capabilities permit deletion through any *other* client or script that uses the credential:

-   `records:edit` covers deleting records.
-   `apps:edit` covers deleting apps, fields and views.
-   `records.comments:edit` covers deleting your own comments.
-   `automations:edit` covers deleting automations.
-   `workspaces:edit` covers deleting a workspace and everything inside it.

The access token a client receives when you sign in is also valid at the Tape Developer API.

**How do I attach a file?** In two steps: `tape-create-file-upload` creates a short-lived upload URL, then the client POSTs the file to it directly, so the bytes never travel through the MCP server. The handle you get back goes into an attachment or image field like any other value. A client that can't make HTTP requests of its own can't perform the second step; add the file in the Tape web interface instead.

**Do the assistant's writes trigger automations and webhooks?** Yes, by default. A record or comment written through MCP behaves like one written by hand: it notifies followers, fires webhooks, and triggers automations, which can send email and make outbound HTTP calls. `tape-create-records`, `tape-update-record` and `tape-create-comment` accept `silent`, `no_webhook` and `no_workflow` to suppress each of these; all three default to `false`. See [Security best practices](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/security).

# Connect with a personal access token

> Connect an MCP client to Tape with a personal access token instead of signing in — for headless use, narrower access, or clients without OAuth support.

Connect an MCP client to Tape with a personal access token instead of [signing in](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/connect).

Point the client at the endpoint, and have it send the [personal access token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens) as a header on every request:

```text
https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp
```

```http
Authorization: Bearer tape_pat_0a1b2c3d...
```

## When to use a token

| Situation | Why a token |
| --- | --- |
| The assistant should reach only *some workspaces or apps* | You can limit a token to selected workspaces and apps. A sign-in reaches everything you can |
| The assistant should be *read-only*, or hold fewer capabilities | You pick a token's capabilities one by one. A sign-in grants every capability the Tape MCP tools use |
| It runs *without a browser*, for example on a server, in a CI job, or through the Claude API | Signing in needs a person at a browser. You configure a token once |
| The client can't sign in to remote MCP servers | A token only needs the client to send a header, or the [`mcp-remote`](#claude-desktop) bridge |

Guests can't connect an MCP client either way. They can't sign in from a client, and they can't create a personal access token. A token created before someone became a guest stops working until they're a member again.

A token connection and a signed-in connection see the same tools. A token limits them to the capabilities and content access you chose. When a capability is missing, a tool on a token fails and you create a new token; on a sign-in, your client asks you to approve more access.

## Step 1: Create a token

Create a token for this client as described in [Create a token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#create-a-token): select your profile picture, then select **Preferences** → **Developer** → **New token**. The token sets what the connection may do and reach.

-   **Token name:** for example "Read-only assistant".
-   **Content access:** keep **All** or select only the workspaces and apps the assistant may reach.
-   **Capabilities:** clear **All**, then select only what the assistant needs. For a read-only assistant, that's **Read apps** and **Read records** (`apps:read`, `records:read`). For more, see [Choose capabilities](#choose-capabilities).

Select **Create token** and copy the token. Tape shows it only once.

![New personal access token dialog named Read-only assistant with access to all content and 2 capabilities: one under Apps and Read records under Records](https://developers.tapeapp.com/assets/images/read-only-token-94c0245459305a969a7a4251a437e34d.png)

> Treat the token like a password
> 
> Keep the token out of the config file: use the environment variable or secret prompt shown for your client. Never commit a config file that contains a token, and revoke the token if it may have leaked.

## Step 2: Add Tape to your client

Pick your client below. Each one sends the token in the `Authorization` header.

### Claude Code

Client documentation: [Claude Code MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp).

```shell
claude mcp add --transport http tape https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer tape_pat_0a1b2c3d..."
```

Add `--scope user` to make the server available in every project. Add `--scope project` to write it into the repository's `.mcp.json`. Since your team shares that file, use an environment variable there instead of the token itself.

### Cursor

Client documentation: [Cursor MCP](https://cursor.com/docs/mcp).

1.  Create `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project, or `~/.cursor/mcp.json` to use Tape in every project.
2.  Paste the configuration below.
3.  Set `TAPE_PAT` in your shell profile instead of writing the token into the file.
4.  Save and *restart Cursor*. Tape then appears under **Customize** → **MCPs**.

*.cursor/mcp.json*

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tape": {
      "url": "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:TAPE_PAT}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Client documentation: [VS Code MCP servers](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/agent-customization/mcp-servers).

1.  Create `.vscode/mcp.json` in the workspace and paste the configuration below. The `inputs` block makes VS Code prompt for the token once and store it securely, so no secret goes into the file.
2.  Open the Command Palette (`Cmd+Shift+P` / `Ctrl+Shift+P`) and run **MCP: List Servers**.
3.  Start the Tape server. VS Code prompts for the token on first use.

*.vscode/mcp.json*

```json
{
  "inputs": [
    {
      "type": "promptString",
      "id": "tape-pat",
      "description": "Tape personal access token",
      "password": true
    }
  ],
  "servers": {
    "tape": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${input:tape-pat}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Desktop

Custom connectors in Claude Desktop and on claude.ai normally connect by signing in. To use a token instead and keep it on your own machine, bridge to the endpoint with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote). It runs locally over stdio and forwards to the HTTP endpoint with your header.

1.  Add the configuration below to your `claude_desktop_config.json`.
2.  Restart Claude Desktop.

*claude_desktop_config.json*

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tape": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "mcp-remote",
        "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp",
        "--transport",
        "http-only",
        "--header",
        "Authorization:${TAPE_AUTH_HEADER}"
      ],
      "env": {
        "TAPE_AUTH_HEADER": "Bearer tape_pat_0a1b2c3d..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Two details in this snippet are deliberate:

-   **`--transport http-only`.** Tape speaks Streamable HTTP and has no SSE endpoint, so the default SSE fallback finds nothing.
-   **`Authorization:${TAPE_AUTH_HEADER}` with no space, and `Bearer` inside the variable.** Claude Desktop on Windows and Cursor break arguments that contain spaces. Keeping the space inside the environment variable avoids this. On macOS and Linux, you can write `"Authorization: Bearer ${TAPE_PAT}"` directly.

The same configuration works in any other stdio-only client.

### Windsurf

Client documentation: [Windsurf MCP](https://docs.windsurf.com/windsurf/cascade/mcp).

1.  Open **Settings** → **Cascade** → **MCP servers** → **View raw config**. This opens `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`.
2.  Add the configuration below.
3.  Set `TAPE_PAT` in your shell profile.
4.  Save and *restart Windsurf*.

*mcp_config.json*

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tape": {
      "serverUrl": "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:TAPE_PAT}"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The header name must be exactly `Authorization`. The value must be `Bearer` followed by the token, with the space.

### Codex

Client documentation: [Codex MCP](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp).

Add the server to `~/.codex/config.toml`, or to `.codex/config.toml` for a single project. Codex reads the token from an environment variable when it connects and sends it as `Authorization: Bearer`.

*~/.codex/config.toml*

```toml
[mcp_servers.tape]
url = "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp"
bearer_token_env_var = "TAPE_PAT"
```

Export `TAPE_PAT` before you start Codex; if the variable is unset or empty, the server fails to start. Older Codex versions pick up stdio servers only: add `experimental_use_rmcp_client = true` under a `[features]` block above the server entry, or upgrade.

### Claude API

Client documentation: [MCP connector](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/mcp-connector).

The Messages API calls the Tape MCP server directly through its MCP connector. Declare the server and reference it from a toolset:

```json
{
  "model": "claude-opus-5-5",
  "max_tokens": 4096,
  "mcp_servers": [
    {
      "type": "url",
      "name": "tape",
      "url": "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp",
      "authorization_token": "tape_pat_0a1b2c3d..."
    }
  ],
  "tools": [{ "type": "mcp_toolset", "mcp_server_name": "tape" }],
  "messages": [{ "role": "user", "content": "Which of my apps have records created this week?" }]
}
```

Send the beta header `anthropic-beta: mcp-client-2025-11-20`. Both halves are required: the API rejects `mcp_servers` without a matching `mcp_toolset` entry.

### Any other MCP client

Configure a *remote Streamable HTTP server* with one custom header. Most clients accept a variation of:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "tape": {
      "url": "https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer tape_pat_0a1b2c3d..."
      }
    }
  }
}
```

If the client speaks stdio only, use the `mcp-remote` bridge shown under [Claude Desktop](#claude-desktop). There's no SSE endpoint to fall back to: Tape answers `GET` with `405`.

To test the endpoint by hand, point the [MCP Inspector](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/inspector) at `https://mcp.tapeapp.com/mcp` and add the `Authorization` header there.

## Step 3: Check the result

1.  **Ask the assistant which Tape tools it has.** A populated tool list shows that the client reaches the server.
2.  **Ask it which Tape account it's connected as**, for example "Which Tape user and organization are you connected as?" The assistant calls `tape-fetch` with `type: "self"`, which needs no capability. The answer names your user and organization.
3.  **Ask it which tools the token can use.** The tool list from step 1 shows every tool, whatever the token's capabilities. The `self` answer's `current_tool_access` marks each tool `available`, `partial` or `unavailable`, with the `missing_scopes` to add. `available` means the capabilities don't block the tool; content access and roles still apply.

Getting `401`, or does the client ask you to sign in? See [Troubleshooting a token connection](#troubleshooting-a-token-connection).

## Choose capabilities

Grant only what the assistant needs:

| You want the assistant to… | Grant |
| --- | --- |
| List apps, read views, and search | `apps:read` |
| Read records and their field values | `records:read` |
| List records shared with you | `records:read` |
| Create records | `apps:read` + `records:edit` |
| Update records | `records:read` + `records:edit` (+ `apps:read`) |
| Upload files | `records:edit` |
| Read comments and replies on records | `records.comments:read` |
| Post comments on records | `records.comments:edit` |
| Create apps (with their fields) and views | `apps:edit` |
| Change existing apps, or add fields to them | `apps:read` + `apps:edit` |
| Change an existing view | `apps:edit` |
| Look up other users in your organization | `organization:read` |
| Read the workspaces you belong to | `workspaces:read` |
| Create and rename workspaces | `workspaces:edit` |
| See automations, their setup and their run history, including credentials for connected systems | `automations:read` |
| Create, change, activate or pause automations | `automations:edit` |
| Trigger an automation manually | `automations:run` |

> Why does a write fail with only an edit capability?
> 
> [Editing doesn't include reading](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities#four-rules-worth-knowing), and most write tools read before they write. Pair them, as the table does.
> 
> Updating a record reads the app's schema only when you set a field that has no value yet. Without `apps:read`, a token updates many records and then fails on one.
> 
> Search [narrows its results instead of refusing](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities#four-rules-worth-knowing): with only `apps:read`, it returns no records and no error. Grant both if the assistant should search across everything.

> Why do automations still fail with the right capability?
> 
> `tape-run-automation` checks only `automations:run`. But automation IDs come only from `tape-get-automations`, and reading one uses `tape-fetch`. Both need `automations:read`, so pair them.
> 
> *Every* automation route also requires the **Admin** role in the app's workspace, which no capability replaces. Without it, `tape-get-automations` and `tape-get-runs` return an *empty page and no error* ("none you administrate", not "none exist"). Everything else, including `tape-fetch` with `type: "automation"` or `type: "automation_run"`, answers `404`.

A *read-only assistant* (`apps:read` and `records:read` only) can't read comments, see automations, list workspaces or look up colleagues: Tape *refuses these calls instead of answering partially*. Add `records.comments:read`, `automations:read`, `workspaces:read` and `organization:read` for whichever of these the assistant should reach.

> `workspaces:edit` reaches further than the MCP tools do
> 
> No MCP tool deletes, but `workspaces:edit` covers *deleting a workspace, and with it every app and record inside*, in any other client or script that uses the token. Grant it only to a token that needs to create or rename workspaces.
> 
> Creating a workspace also requires a token whose [content access](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#content-selection) is **All**, and an organization role that permits creating workspaces.

### Automations run as their owner

> `automations:run` reaches beyond the token
> 
> An automation runs with the rights of the person who owns it. Triggering one can change *and delete* data in apps outside your token's content access, send email in someone else's name, call external systems, and run custom code. The tool's arguments don't show what the automation does.
> 
> Grant it only when the assistant needs to trigger automations, and read the automation before you run it. A *paused automation can still run this way*: pausing stops only its trigger.
> 
> `automations:run` neither implies nor requires `automations:read` or `automations:edit`.

## Troubleshooting a token connection

**The client can't connect, reports `401`, or asks you to sign in to Tape even though you configured a token.** The `Authorization` header doesn't reach the server, so Tape answers `401` and invites the client to sign in. Don't complete that sign-in if you meant to use a token: it connects without the token's limits. Check these points:

-   The header name is exactly `Authorization`.
-   The value starts with `Bearer` , including the space.
-   If you used an environment variable, it's set in the environment the client was launched from. An unset variable leaves an empty `Bearer` value, which counts as no token. GUI apps often don't inherit a shell profile.

**`no active user for the given API key`, or a signature error.** The token is wrong, revoked, or was altered on the way. Send it *verbatim*, with the `tape_pat_` prefix in lower case.

**A tool returns `403` naming a missing capability.** The token lacks a [capability](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/capabilities) the tool needs, and capabilities are fixed at creation. Create a new token with the capability, switch the client over, and revoke the old one. See [Choose capabilities](#choose-capabilities).

**A tool returns `404` for a record, app or automation you know exists.** Check the token's [content access](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#content-selection) first: a resource outside it returns the same `404` as one that doesn't exist. For other causes, see [Troubleshooting](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/mcp/connect#troubleshooting).

## Revoking a token

Select your profile picture, then select **Preferences** → **Developer**, and revoke the token there; see [Revoke a token](https://developers.tapeapp.com/docs/api/personal-access-tokens#revoke-a-token). Revoking takes effect on the next request and never affects your other tokens or your signed-in connections.
